question: Argentina IMF EFF: Will the IMF Executive Board complete the second review and enable a disbursement between Oct 15 and Dec 31, 2025 (ART)?
background:
Context and status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- Program approval and size: On April 11, 2025, the IMF Executive Board approved a 48‑month Extended Fund Facility (EFF) arrangement for Argentina totaling about US$20 billion (SDR 15.267 billion).
- First review completed and disbursement: On July 31, 2025, the IMF Executive Board completed the first review of Argentina’s EFF arrangement, “enabling an immediate disbursement of SDR 1.529 billion (about US$2 billion).” This press release exemplifies the standard IMF phrasing used when a review is completed and a disbursement is enabled.
- Forward-looking constraints on review timing: Reporting on August 1, 2025 indicated that the IMF lowered Argentina’s net international reserve (NIR) accumulation targets through 2026 and removed a review that had been due before the country’s October legislative elections, with the next review due after those elections.
- What the EFF is and how reviews/disbursements work: The EFF supports countries facing medium‑term balance‑of‑payments problems due to structural weaknesses. Access to IMF resources is phased, and disbursements are conditional on policy performance assessed at periodic reviews.

Key definitions and references for forecasters:
- Extended Fund Facility (EFF): An IMF lending facility supporting multi‑year structural reform programs; periodic reviews assess performance and, when completed by the Executive Board, typically “enable” access to the next disbursement tranche.
- “Second review” (in this question): The second periodic program review under Argentina’s 48‑month EFF arrangement approved April 11, 2025.
- IMF Executive Board: The decision‑making body that formally completes reviews under IMF arrangements; see the Board phrasing and role as used in the July 31, 2025 Argentina press release (“Executive Board completed the first review … enabling … disbursement”).
- Argentina Time (ART): The official time in Argentina is UTC−03:00 year‑round (no daylight saving time). Buenos Aires observes ART.

Primary sources to monitor:
- IMF News/Press Releases related to Argentina (example press release format: PR25272 for the first review) and IMF Staff Country Reports pages on imf.org. A qualifying IMF publication will explicitly state that the Executive Board completed the second review and that this completion enabled/approved a (next) disbursement.
- For general program context: the April 11, 2025 approval release  and subsequent reporting on review timing and target adjustments.
resolution_criteria:
This is a binary question. It will resolve based on official IMF publications as follows:

Event window and time zone:
- Start: 2025-10-15 00:00:00 ART (UTC−03:00).
- End: 2025-12-31 23:59:59 ART (UTC−03:00).
- ART is Argentina Time, which is UTC−03:00 year‑round.

YES resolution:
- Resolve YES if, within the event window, there exists at least one official IMF publication on imf.org (e.g., a press release, Executive Board decision/statement, or the Staff Report page for the relevant review) that explicitly states both of the following for Argentina under the current 48‑month EFF arrangement approved on April 11, 2025 :
  1) “The Executive Board completed the second review” (or equivalent standard IMF phrasing such as “The IMF Executive Board completed today the second review …”).
  2) The completion “enabled” or “approved” a disbursement (typical phrasing includes “enabling an immediate disbursement of …” or “approving a disbursement of …”). The IMF’s standard language for completion/enabling a disbursement is exemplified in the July 31, 2025 press release on the first review.

NO resolution:
- Resolve NO if no such qualifying IMF publication dated within the event window can be found by the resolution deadline.

Source and dating rules:
- The authoritative source is the IMF website (imf.org). The publication must be publicly accessible on imf.org and clearly associated with Argentina’s EFF.
- For the purposes of determining whether the publication falls within the event window, use the publication date displayed on the IMF page (as shown on the press release or report page). If both an Executive Board meeting date and a separate publication date are listed, the publication date controls for this question’s timing.

Term clarifications:
- “Second review” refers to the second periodic review under Argentina’s 48‑month EFF arrangement approved on April 11, 2025.
- “Enable/approve a disbursement” means the IMF text explicitly states that a disbursement is made available as a consequence of completing the second review, using standard IMF phrasing such as “enabling an immediate disbursement of …” or “approving a disbursement of …”.

Examples (illustrative):
- A press release that states, “The IMF Executive Board completed the second review of the Extended Arrangement under the EFF for Argentina, enabling an immediate disbursement of SDR X” within the window would resolve YES.
- A staff report published within the window whose cover page or press release states the Board “completed the second review … enabling a disbursement” would resolve YES.
- If the Board completes the review but the IMF publication is dated outside the window, resolve NO under this question’s timing rule.

Fallback if imf.org is inaccessible at resolution time:
- If the IMF website is inaccessible for more than 24 consecutive hours at the resolution deadline, use reports from at least two of the following wire services: Reuters, Associated Press, or AFP, that clearly state the IMF Executive Board completed Argentina’s second EFF review and enabled/approved a disbursement, with at least one citing or linking to the IMF release. For timing, use the earliest datestamp among those reports; it must fall within the event window.

question: Will Türkiye’s headline CPI annual inflation (YoY) for November 2025, as published by TurkStat, be at or below 31.00%?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01
- What is being measured: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) tracks the average price level of a basket of goods and services purchased by households. The year‑over‑year (YoY) inflation rate is the annual percentage change in CPI, comparing a month’s CPI to the same month a year earlier. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consumer_price_index
- Who publishes the figure: The Turkish Statistical Institute (TUIK, commonly TurkStat) is Türkiye’s official government statistics agency responsible for publishing CPI. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_Statistical_Institute
- Latest official readings: Official annual CPI inflation was 33.52% in July 2025  and 32.95% in August 2025, with a 2.04% monthly increase in August.
- Near‑term expectations: A Reuters poll ahead of August’s release had a median YoY forecast of 32.6% (range 32.2–33.2%) and noted the release was scheduled at 0700 GMT on Sept 3. A Reuters poll for September pointed to 32.5% YoY (range 32.09–33.6%), and cited August’s official 32.95% YoY and 2.04% MoM figures.
- Policy/official forecasts: The Turkish government later forecast year‑end 2025 inflation at 28.5%. Earlier, Reuters reported analysts’ median end‑2025 forecast at 29.75%, above the central bank’s then‑forecast of 24%.
- Publication cadence: TurkStat publishes monthly CPI bulletins on its data portal; CPI is listed within the Inflation & Price category on the portal. Example: Reuters explicitly references the monthly release schedule (e.g., August data at 0700 GMT on Sept 3).

Why this threshold and timing
- The November 2025 CPI YoY will likely be published in early December, allowing resolution before December 31, 2025. Given the recent disinflation trend from July to August and poll medians for September in the low‑30s, a 31.00% threshold aims to balance difficulty and plausibility, yielding a non‑trivial forecasting problem.
resolution_criteria:
Question
Resolve YES if the headline all‑items CPI year‑over‑year (YoY) inflation rate for November 2025, as published by TurkStat (TUIK), is less than or equal to 31.00%. Resolve NO otherwise.

Precise definitions
- CPI: Consumer Price Index for all items (headline CPI), as defined and published by TurkStat. CPI is an index of the average price level of a consumer basket; the YoY rate is the annual percentage change in this index.
- YoY (year‑over‑year) CPI inflation: The percentage change in the CPI for November 2025 relative to November 2024, as reported by TurkStat in the monthly CPI bulletin for November 2025.
- Publisher/Source: Turkish Statistical Institute (TUIK/TurkStat), Türkiye’s official statistics agency. Primary source is the official November 2025 CPI bulletin (English or Turkish) on the TurkStat data portal under the Inflation & Price category ("Consumer Price Index (CPI)").
- Headline vs. core: Use the headline all‑items CPI (not any special/"core" or seasonally adjusted measures). If multiple CPI measures are presented, select the standard all‑items CPI headline YoY figure.

How to extract the number
- Use the headline YoY percentage for CPI (all items) for November 2025 as shown in the official bulletin page (English or Turkish). If both English and Turkish versions are available and differ due to rounding/display, prefer the English page. If the English page is unavailable, use the Turkish page and the “yıllık” (annual) percentage for TÜFE (CPI).
- Decimal handling and comparison: Compare the value exactly as displayed to two decimal places in the bulletin to the threshold 31.00%. “At or below 31.00%” means a displayed value of 31.00% or any lower number (e.g., 30.99%).

Time window and version control
- Relevant publication window: 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC through 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. Only the November 2025 CPI bulletin is eligible.
- Corrections/revisions: If TurkStat issues an official correction to the November 2025 CPI bulletin on or before 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, use the corrected value. Corrections or revisions dated after this cutoff are ignored.

Sources of truth for resolution
- Primary: TurkStat’s official November 2025 CPI bulletin (data.tuik.gov.tr). The CPI is published via monthly bulletins on the TurkStat data portal’s Inflation & Price category.
- Fallback (if the bulletin page is inaccessible or not publicly reachable by the resolver by the cutoff): Use contemporaneous reporting from major global wire services that explicitly cite TurkStat’s November 2025 CPI YoY figure, such as Reuters (examples of Reuters’ CPI coverage and schedule references: ).

Rationale for resolvability and timing
- TurkStat is the authoritative publisher of CPI. Reuters wires routinely report the official monthly CPI figures and scheduled release times. This ensures the YoY figure for November 2025 will be obtainable and verifiable before the 2025-12-31 UTC cutoff.

question: Will Pakistan’s PVARA issue at least one license to a Virtual Asset Service Provider (VASP) under the Virtual Assets Ordinance, 2025 between 2025-10-01 and 2025-12-31 (UTC)?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01
- SBP prohibitions (2018): The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) issued BPRD Circular No. 03 of 2018 on April 6, 2018, directing all Banks/DFIs/Microfinance Banks and PSOs/PSPs to refrain from processing, using, trading, holding, transferring value, promoting, or investing in virtual currencies/tokens, and not to facilitate customers in such transactions, stating such assets are not legal tender and that SBP had not authorized any issuance/sale/exchange/investment in them. A parallel FE Circular No. 03 of 2018 (April 18, 2018) applied similar prohibitions to Exchange Companies and Exchange Companies-B.
- SBP’s clarification (2025-05-30): SBP clarified that it advised regulated entities to avoid dealing in virtual assets due to the absence of a legal/regulatory framework, “not because it was declared illegal in the country,” and noted it is engaging with the Pakistan Crypto Council to develop an appropriate framework.
- New legal framework (mid-2025): Multiple sources indicate Pakistan promulgated the Virtual Assets Ordinance, 2025 in July 2025, establishing the Pakistan Virtual Asset Regulatory Authority (PVARA) to license, regulate, and supervise virtual asset service providers (VASPs). A Finance Division press release (PR No. 384) states the Ordinance was promulgated on July 8, 2025 and published in the Gazette on July 9, and that PVARA issued a call for Expressions of Interest (EoI) from global VASPs on September 13, 2025. Independent coverage similarly reports the Ordinance came into force on July 8, 2025 and that it established PVARA.
- Policy developments (late Aug 2025): Business Recorder reported PVARA’s first board meeting (Aug 26, 2025) deliberated withdrawing SBP’s 2018 circular and discussed an AI-driven licensing/regulatory roadmap; a draft licensing framework was shared with members for consultation.
- Additional context: Media report that Pakistan’s Pakistan Crypto Council signed an agreement with World Liberty Financial (WLF), a crypto firm reportedly majority-owned by the Trump family, outlining collaboration on sandboxes, stablecoin use, and tokenization, and that government officials signaled plans to announce comprehensive crypto policy; this highlights political momentum but is not directly dispositive for resolution.

Key definitions for this question
- Virtual asset (VA): As per FATF Glossary, a “digital representation of value that can be digitally traded, or transferred, and can be used for payment or investment purposes,” excluding digital representations of fiat currencies, securities, and other financial assets covered elsewhere.
- Virtual asset service provider (VASP): As per FATF Glossary, any person who as a business conducts one or more of the following for/on behalf of another: (i) exchange between VAs and fiat; (ii) exchange between one or more forms of VAs; (iii) transfer of VAs; (iv) safekeeping/administration of VAs or instruments enabling control; (v) participation in/provision of financial services related to an issuer’s offer/sale of a VA.

Why this question now
- As of early October 2025, Pakistan has created PVARA via the Virtual Assets Ordinance, 2025 and has begun outreach to potential licensees (EoI), but reporting indicates licensing rules and the status of SBP’s 2018 prohibitions are still being operationalized or reviewed. Whether at least one VASP can obtain a license in 2025 is uncertain and policy-contingent, making this a high-entropy forecast.

Pointers to primary sources for checking resolution
- SBP circulars page (historical prohibitions): BPRD Circular No. 03 of 2018 ; FE Circular No. 03 of 2018.
- Finance Division press releases (official announcements re: PVARA/Ordinance/licensing): Finance Division press releases index.
- Newswire coverage for cross-verification: Yahoo Finance article summarizing PVARA’s legal basis ; Arab News coverage of law/PVARA ; Business Recorder on PVARA Board actions.
- Definitions: FATF Glossary definitions of VA and VASP.
resolution_criteria:
Question:
- Resolve Yes if, between 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC (inclusive), Pakistan’s Pakistan Virtual Asset Regulatory Authority (PVARA) grants at least one license/authorisation/registration to operate as a Virtual Asset Service Provider (VASP) under the Virtual Assets Ordinance, 2025, evidenced by an official primary source as defined below. Resolve No otherwise.

Operational definitions and scope
- “Virtual Asset Service Provider (VASP)” uses the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) definition: a business that conducts one or more of the following for/on behalf of another—VA/fiat exchange; VA/VA exchange; transfer of VAs; safekeeping/administration of VAs; or services related to an issuer’s offer/sale of a VA.
- “License/authorisation/registration” means a formal grant of legal permission issued by PVARA pursuant to the Virtual Assets Ordinance, 2025 (or regulations made under it) that explicitly allows a named entity to operate as a VASP in or from Pakistan. The decision must be described with language such as “license,” “authorisation/authorization,” or “registration,” identify the licensee, and cite the legal basis (e.g., the Virtual Assets Ordinance, 2025). Provisional sandbox admissions, no-objection certificates (NOCs), MoUs, draft or proposed regulations, policy roadmaps, calls for EoIs, or press statements lacking an explicit grant of license/authorisation/registration do not count.
- “PVARA” refers to the autonomous regulator established by the Virtual Assets Ordinance, 2025 to license, regulate, and supervise VASPs.

Eligible time window
- Event must occur between 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, inclusive. The authoritative timestamp is the date/time shown on the official publication (see sources below). If the official record lists only a date (no time), it will be taken as occurring at 00:00:00 UTC on that date for inclusion purposes. If an undated page is updated, use the page’s listed publication/update date; if none is listed, use the earliest timestamp from credible archival snapshots during the window.

Primary resolution sources (in order of preference)
- The Gazette of Pakistan publication of a licensing notice (if applicable) or an official notification on a Government of Pakistan domain (e.g., finance.gov.pk) explicitly granting a VASP license under the Virtual Assets Ordinance, 2025.
- An official announcement posted by PVARA (e.g., on its official website or an official Government of Pakistan page) explicitly granting such a license.
- If neither of the above is available but a credible wire service (e.g., Reuters, Associated Press) reports the license and links to an official document, that will be accepted; if links are not provided, the report must include verbatim quotations that can be matched to an official notice posted on a government website during the eligible window.

Exclusions and clarifications
- The following do not count for resolution: draft rules, consultations, expression-of-interest calls, press interviews, policy speeches, or board deliberations (e.g., PVARA’s Aug 26, 2025 deliberations on withdrawing SBP’s 2018 circular) unless accompanied by an explicit licensing grant that meets the criteria above.
- The withdrawal/amendment of SBP’s 2018 circulars alone does not resolve the question; the criterion is issuance of at least one VASP license under the Virtual Assets Ordinance, 2025.
- Any license type that falls under VASP (exchange, broker, custodian, transfer, issuer-related services) counts, provided it is issued by PVARA under the Ordinance and explicitly labeled as a license/authorisation/registration.
- Subsequent suspension or revocation of a counted license does not negate a Yes resolution.

How to resolve on/after 2025-12-31
- On or after 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, check the Ministry of Finance press releases index and PVARA/Government of Pakistan official pages for any licensing announcement in the eligible window. If found, record the licensee name and publication date, and resolve Yes. If no eligible official licensing notice is found, resolve No.

Notes and references for resolvers
- Historical SBP circulars establishing the prior prohibitions are here for context. SBP’s 2025 clarification that prior actions were due to absence of a framework (not declaring VAs illegal) and engagement with Pakistan Crypto Council is here. The creation of PVARA via the Virtual Assets Ordinance, 2025 and EoI call are documented by the Finance Division press release (PR No. 384) , with corroborative reports from Yahoo Finance and Arab News.

question: Will the Sahm Rule recession signal be triggered for any 2025 month by December 31, 2025 (UTC)?
background: Context: The National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) dates U.S. recessions retrospectively, often with a lag; therefore, timely real-time proxies are useful to forecast whether recession-like conditions emerge within a calendar year. The Sahm Rule is a widely used real-time indicator of recession onset based on movements in the national unemployment rate. It is designed to identify the early months of a recession by detecting a sufficiently large rise in unemployment relative to its recent low. For a concise overview of the Sahm Rule, see Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahm_rule. The FRED series "Real-time Sahm Rule Recession Indicator (SAHMREALTIME)" operationalizes this measure using the seasonally adjusted national unemployment rate (U-3) and publishes monthly values: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/SAHMREALTIME. The U-3 unemployment rate is the official, seasonally adjusted national unemployment rate published monthly by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) in the Employment Situation report (overview: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm; series page: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/UNRATE). Forecasters should consult the FRED SAHMREALTIME page for the latest readings and historical values throughout 2025, noting that new monthly data are typically posted shortly after each BLS Employment Situation release.
resolution_criteria:
Start and end of observation window: This question concerns whether the Sahm Rule recession signal is triggered for any reference month in calendar year 2025, as determined and displayed by FRED, by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Definitions (authoritative links provided for clarity):
- Sahm Rule recession signal ("triggered"): The signal is considered triggered in any month m of 2025 if the Real-time Sahm Rule Recession Indicator value for month m is greater than or equal to 0.50 percentage points. The indicator is defined as the difference (in percentage points) between (a) the three-month moving average of the seasonally adjusted national unemployment rate (U-3) for month m and (b) the minimum of the three-month moving averages over the prior 12 months (months m−12 through m−1). See FRED series description: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/SAHMREALTIME and overview: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahm_rule.
- U-3 unemployment rate: The seasonally adjusted national unemployment rate published by BLS (overview: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm; series: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/UNRATE).
- Three-month moving average: The arithmetic mean of the U-3 unemployment rates for month m and the two preceding months (m−1, m−2), as used by the SAHMREALTIME series.
- Reference month: The month label shown on the SAHMREALTIME series for each observation on FRED.

Source of truth and measurement:
- Primary source: The FRED series page for "Real-time Sahm Rule Recession Indicator (SAHMREALTIME)": https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/SAHMREALTIME.

Resolution logic:
- Resolve YES if, as displayed on the FRED SAHMREALTIME page at or before 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, the series reaches or exceeds 0.50 for any reference month in 2025.
- Eligible months: January 2025 through November 2025 by default; include December 2025 only if its value is posted on the FRED SAHMREALTIME page by the resolution timestamp above.
- Resolve NO otherwise.

Tie and rounding rules:
- A value exactly equal to 0.50 counts as "triggered" (YES). Use the value displayed on FRED to two decimal places (or greater precision if shown) without additional rounding by the resolver.

Revisions and data availability:
- Use the values shown on the FRED SAHMREALTIME series page as of the resolution timestamp (2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC). If the FRED site is temporarily unavailable at that time, the resolver should use the first available snapshot thereafter and document the outage. No other sources will be used unless FRED is inaccessible for 72 consecutive hours spanning the resolution timestamp; in that case, the resolver may use the St. Louis Fed’s archived data service (ALFRED) for SAHMREALTIME or an official FRED API response reflecting the same series, with the chosen fallback documented.

Exclusions and clarifications:
- This market does not rely on an NBER recession announcement.
- Only the SAHMREALTIME series is used (not SAHMCURRENT or other variants).

question: U.S. core PCE year-over-year for November 2025 ≥ 2.8%?
background:
Definitions and measurement:
- Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index excluding food and energy ("core PCE"): A measure of prices paid by consumers for goods and services that omits food and energy to better reflect underlying inflation. BEA describes this series and its purpose on its data page and FAQ.
- Year-over-year (YoY) in BEA releases corresponds to the "12-month percent change" and is also presented as "Change from one year ago" in tables and bullets. This is the metric used for both the overall PCE price index and the core PCE index in monthly Personal Income and Outlays releases.

Release timing and source:
- The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) schedules "Personal Income and Outlays, November 2025" for December 19, 2025 at 10:00 AM; this monthly release contains the PCE price indexes and their 12-month percent changes. This BEA release page and its accompanying tables will be the primary source for resolution.

Status quo as of today (2025-10-01):
- In the latest available BEA release (August 2025), the 12-month percent change was 2.7% for the overall PCE price index and 2.9% for the PCE price index excluding food and energy (core). These values are stated in the August 2025 Personal Income and Outlays news release.
- The BEA core PCE data page currently shows recent "Change From Month One Year Ago" values for the core index of +2.9% (August 2025), +2.9% (July 2025), and +2.8% (June 2025).

Why this question:
- Core PCE YoY near year-end 2025 is policy-relevant and plausibly uncertain. The recent readings around 2.8–2.9% suggest meaningful two-sided risk for November 2025, making a 2.8% threshold non-trivial.

Eligible timeframe for forecasting context events (not for resolution data):
- Any contextual developments a forecaster considers may occur between October 15, 2025 00:00 UTC and December 31, 2025 23:59 UTC. Resolution itself will rely solely on the BEA publication referenced above.
resolution_criteria:
Resolve YES if the BEA "Personal Income and Outlays, November 2025" release lists the PCE price index excluding food and energy (core PCE) 12-month percent change (a.k.a. "From one year ago") for November 2025 as 2.8% or higher; resolve NO otherwise.

Operational details:
- Source of truth: The BEA news release page for "Personal Income and Outlays, November 2025" and/or the accompanying data tables posted with that release on bea.gov. The BEA core PCE data page (PCE price index excluding food and energy) is acceptable if it displays the November 2025 "Change From Month One Year Ago" value contemporaneously with the release.
- Use the first value published on the release date (December 19, 2025) for resolution. Subsequent revisions will not affect resolution.
- Use the percentage as published by BEA (to the precision they report; typically one decimal place). For avoidance of doubt: a published value of 2.8% counts as "2.8% or higher".
- Timezone for the resolution deadline: The question will be considered resolved as soon as the BEA release is published; if needed for administrative closure, the final deadline is December 31, 2025 at 23:59 UTC, but the value used is the one first published on December 19, 2025.

Key term references for adjudication:
- Core PCE definition (BEA): "personal consumption expenditures (PCE) prices excluding food and energy prices".
- BEA core PCE data page and its "Change From Month One Year Ago" presentation.
- Example of BEA release format showing 12-month percent change figures (August 2025 news release).

question: Between 2025-10-15 and 2025-12-31 (Asia/Jakarta), will OJK revoke the business license of at least one licensed fintech P2P lending operator (LPBBTI)?
background:
Context and status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- Regulatory scope and definitions: In Indonesia, Layanan Pendanaan Bersama Berbasis Teknologi Informasi (LPBBTI) refers to information-technology-based joint funding (commonly called fintech P2P lending). The governing regulation is OJK Regulation No. 10/POJK.05/2022, which defines LPBBTI, requires operators to obtain an OJK business license (izin usaha) before operating, and sets conditions under which OJK may impose administrative sanctions up to and including revocation of the business license (pencabutan izin usaha). See especially Article 1 (definitions) and Article 8(1) (licensing requirement); numerous subsequent articles outline violations that can lead to revocation (e.g., Articles 41, 49, 52, 59, 67, 82, 97, 98, 105, 107, 109, 112).
- Recent enforcement precedents in LPBBTI:
  • Investree (PT Investree Radika Jaya): OJK announced the revocation of Investree’s business license on 2024-10-21 via a press release stating that the revocation was due to minimum equity shortfalls and other violations under POJK 10/2022; the decision number is KEP-53/D.06/2024.
  • PT Ringan Teknologi Indonesia (“Ringan”): OJK published an announcement on 2025-05-06 noting that the business license had been revoked by OJK Decision KEP-17/D.06/2025 dated 2025-04-24; the announcement outlines post-revocation obligations and clarifies that the operator is prohibited from conducting LPBBTI business henceforth.
- Market size baseline: As of OJK’s directory per 2025-07-31, there are 96 licensed LPBBTI/fintech P2P lending operators (“penyelenggara … yang berizin di OJK”), providing a reference universe for potential enforcement actions in the remainder of 2025.

Why this is forecastable: OJK has shown willingness to revoke LPBBTI licenses in 2024–2025, and there remains a sizable population of licensed operators (96 as of end-July 2025). Whether at least one more revocation occurs in Q4 2025 is uncertain but plausible, creating a balanced regulatory-risk question that can be resolved via authoritative OJK publications.

Helpful links for forecasters:
- Governing regulation (POJK 10/POJK.05/2022): https://ojk.go.id/id/regulasi/Documents/Pages/Layanan-Pendanaan-Bersama-Berbasis-Teknologi-Informasi/POJK%2010%20-%2005%20-%202022.pdf 
- Example OJK press release (Investree): https://ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/siaran-pers/Pages/OJK-Cabut-Izin-Usaha-PT-Investree-Radhika-Jaya.aspx 
- Example OJK announcement (Ringan): https://ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/pengumuman/Pages/OJK-Cabut-Izin-Usaha-Penyelenggara-LPBBTI-PT-Ringan-Teknologi-Indonesia.aspx 
- OJK LPBBTI directory page (per 31 July 2025): https://ojk.go.id/id/kanal/iknb/data-dan-statistik/direktori/fintech/Pages/Direktori-Layanan-Pendanaan-Bersama-Berbasis-Teknologi-Informasi-Per-31-Juli-2025.aspx
resolution_criteria:
YES resolves if ALL of the following are true:
1) A revocation decision (pencabutan izin usaha) by OJK applies to at least one LPBBTI operator (“Penyelenggara Layanan Pendanaan Bersama Berbasis Teknologi Informasi” as defined in OJK Regulation 10/POJK.05/2022).
2) The revocation pertains to a licensed LPBBTI operator (i.e., an entity that had an OJK LPBBTI business license prior to the decision).
3) The OJK decision’s official date (the “tanggal” on the decision or as stated by OJK) falls between 2025-10-15 and 2025-12-31 inclusive, using the Asia/Jakarta (WIB; UTC+7) calendar date. If OJK’s publication includes both a publication date and a separate decision date, the decision date governs; if the decision date is not explicitly stated, the publication date on ojk.go.id is used instead (WIB).
4) The revocation is published on OJK’s official website (ojk.go.id) in an Announcement (Pengumuman) and/or Press Release (Siaran Pers) and/or as an attached OJK decision document (e.g., a “Keputusan …” with a KEP number) that explicitly states the business license has been revoked (“mencabut izin usaha” / “pencabutan izin usaha”). Examples of acceptable publication formats are demonstrated in OJK’s Investree press release (Siaran Pers) and Ringan announcement (Pengumuman).

NO resolves if no such OJK revocation decision meeting the above conditions is published.

Clarifications and edge cases:
- Voluntary license return followed by an OJK decision that revokes the business license still counts, provided OJK issues a formal decision stating the revocation (e.g., Ringan’s KEP-17/D.06/2025 language).
- Administrative sanctions short of “pencabutan izin usaha” (e.g., warnings, fines, business activity restrictions) do not count.
- Revocations affecting non-LPBBTI entities (e.g., banks, insurers, non-LPBBTI lenders) do not count.
- Multiple revocations within the window still resolve YES (the condition is “at least one”).
- Verification procedure: At resolution time, the resolver will search ojk.go.id for “pencabutan izin usaha” combined with LPBBTI operator names and/or review the OJK “Pengumuman” and “Siaran Pers” sections for Q4 2025 postings to identify any item explicitly stating the revocation and the decision date; examples of the phrasing and placement are shown in the Investree and Ringan items.

Time window:
- Start: 2025-10-15 00:00:00 (Asia/Jakarta; UTC+7), determined by the OJK decision date as printed/stated.
- End: 2025-12-31 23:59:59 (Asia/Jakarta; UTC+7), determined by the OJK decision date as printed/stated.

Definitions (authoritative):
- LPBBTI (Layanan Pendanaan Bersama Berbasis Teknologi Informasi): See definition in POJK 10/POJK.05/2022, Article 1.
- Business license (izin usaha) for LPBBTI and revocation (pencabutan izin usaha): The license required by Article 8(1); revocation is an administrative sanction authorized under POJK 10/2022 (see Articles cited in Background).
- Published by OJK: The item must be hosted on the ojk.go.id domain (e.g., in Pengumuman or Siaran Pers) and explicitly state that the LPBBTI business license has been revoked (examples: Investree press release; Ringan announcement).

question: Will Burnley be in the Premier League relegation zone (positions 18–20) at 23:59:00 UTC on 2025-12-31?

- Competition and definitions: The Premier League is the top division of English men’s association football, contested by 20 clubs, with the bottom three teams each season relegated to the EFL Championship. Throughout the season, teams are ordered in the league table by points, then goal difference, then goals scored; for ties affecting key outcomes (e.g., championship, relegation, qualification), head‑to‑head is considered (points in matches between tied teams, then away goals), and a playoff may be used if necessary. The official, authoritative public display of the current table is on the Premier League’s own website at its “Tables” page.
- Club in question: Burnley Football Club (Burnley) are competing in the 2025–26 Premier League after promotion from the Championship; Scott Parker was appointed head coach on a three‑year deal in July 2024, replacing Vincent Kompany. Early in the 2025–26 season, snapshots show Burnley around the bottom quartile: as of 2025‑09‑27 they had 4 points and were 18th; by 2025‑09‑29 they were listed 17th in the table.

These matches immediately precede the resolution timestamp and can materially move Burnley’s position around the relegation threshold.
- Time standard: Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) is the global time standard that does not observe daylight saving time; timestamps in this question refer to UTC.

Key terms and sources for forecasters:
- “Relegation zone,” “bottom three,” and “positions 18–20” are used interchangeably here to mean places 18th, 19th, and 20th in the 20‑team Premier League table.
- “Official Premier League table” refers to the standings as publicly displayed by the Premier League at https://www.premierleague.com/tables.

resolution_criteria:

Resolution steps:

2) Outcome:

- Resolve NO otherwise.
3) Definitions and tie‑breakers: Table positions are those displayed by the official Premier League site, which reflect the competition’s ordering rules (points, goal difference, goals scored, and applicable tie‑breaks per Premier League practice).
4) Fallbacks if the primary page is temporarily unavailable at that time: Use a contemporaneous, reputable public table such as the BBC Sport Premier League table page to read Burnley’s position; if any discrepancy is later clarified by the Premier League, the Premier League’s displayed position takes precedence for resolution.

Scope and timing details:
- Timezone: All times are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
- Season and competition: Only the English Premier League 2025–26 table is relevant; no other competitions or tables are considered.

question: Will a U.S. Act of Congress enacted between Oct 15 and Dec 31, 2025 rescind at least $2.0 billion in budget authority?
background:
Definitions and legal context as of Sep 30, 2025:
- Rescission (Impoundment Control Act context): GAO describes a rescission as the proposed cancellation of budget authority before that authority would otherwise expire, initiated via a presidential special message to Congress under the Impoundment Control Act (ICA). Congress must enact a rescission into law for the cancellation to take effect; otherwise the funds must be made available after the ICA’s time limits. ICA’s rescission procedure is codified at 2 U.S.C. § 683 (special messages and the 45-day continuous session rule).
- Budget authority: GAO defines budget authority as authority provided by federal law to enter into financial obligations that will result in immediate or future outlays of federal funds.
- Counting rescissions (definiteness rule): GAO guidance on rescission statistics indicates that rescissions comprising indefinite or uncertain amounts (e.g., “up to” or “not more than”) are not counted; if a law rescinds “not less than” a specific amount, that minimum can be counted; otherwise only definite amounts are included.

Status quo and recent activity:
- On May 28, 2025, the Administration transmitted a special message proposing approximately $9.4 billion in rescissions of budget authority.
- Congress subsequently enacted the Rescissions Act of 2025 as Public Law 119-28 on July 24, 2025, rescinding specified budget authority in multiple accounts (as reflected on Congress.gov’s public law page for H.R.4).
- On August 28, 2025, the Administration transmitted another special message proposing rescissions totaling $4,999,999,990 across various foreign assistance and international organization accounts. The White House characterized this late-August package as a “pocket rescission” totaling $5 billion near the end of the fiscal year. GAO has explained that “pocket rescissions” (withholding proposed rescissions until funds expire near FY-end) are illegal under the ICA because the Act does not permit withholding through expiration absent congressional action.

Why this matters for forecasting: A second-half‑2025 attempt to cancel billions in previously appropriated funds has created uncertainty about whether Congress will enact another significant rescission by year‑end. The ICA provides a pathway but also constrains timing. Political dynamics around foreign aid, public broadcasting, and separation-of-powers disputes add further uncertainty.

Useful references (for forecasters and resolvers):
- GAO ICA explainer: https://www.gao.gov/legal/appropriations-law/impoundment-control-act 
- Statute: 2 U.S.C. § 683 (LII): https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/2/683 
- GAO Glossary (budget authority definition excerpted): https://www.gao.gov/assets/a76916.html 
- GAO rescission counting note: https://www.gao.gov/products/b-330828 
- May 28, 2025 special message (~$9.4B): https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Proposed-Rescissions-of-Budgetary-Resources.pdf 
- H.R.4 public law page (example of how Congress.gov displays enacted rescissions): https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/4 
- Aug 28, 2025 special message (~$5.0B): https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Proposed-Rescissions-of-Budgetary-Resources-August-28-2025.pdf 
- White House “pocket rescission” press statement (late Aug 2025): https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefings-statements/2025/08/historic-pocket-rescission-package-eliminates-woke-weaponized-and-wasteful-spending/ 
- GAO blog on pocket rescissions’ illegality: https://www.gao.gov/blog/what-pocket-rescission-and-it-legal
resolution_criteria:
Question: Will at least one U.S. federal law enacted between Oct 15, 2025 00:00:00 UTC and Dec 31, 2025 23:59:59 UTC rescind (i.e., cancel via enacted legislation) definite amounts of budget authority totaling ≥ $2,000,000,000 (two billion U.S. dollars, nominal)?

Definitions for this question:
- “Rescinds” means enacted legislation that cancels previously provided budget authority, consistent with the ICA framework for rescission proposals and congressional enactment into law.
- “Budget authority” is as defined by GAO: authority provided by law to enter into obligations that will result in immediate or future outlays of federal funds.
- “Definite amounts” follow GAO’s counting guidance: only definite, specified dollar amounts in the law’s text count toward the total; amounts phrased as “up to,” “not more than,” or other indefinite formulations do not count. If the law rescinds “not less than” a specific amount, count that minimum amount.
- “U.S. federal law enacted” means a bill or joint resolution that has become a Public Law during the window, whether by presidential signature or congressional veto override, with an official enactment date within the window (as displayed on Congress.gov). The enactment date governs, not the effective date. Public Law format example and status display: Congress.gov page for Public Law 119-28 (H.R.4).
- “Totaling ≥ $2,000,000,000” means the sum of all definite rescinded amounts specified within a single enacted law. Multiple separate laws do not aggregate for this question; any one law must meet or exceed the threshold on its own.

Inclusions and exclusions:
- Include rescission provisions enacted in any law (standalone rescissions act, appropriations/omnibus, or other statute) so long as the law’s text rescinds definite dollar amounts of budget authority.
- Exclude proposed rescissions (special messages) that are not enacted into law.
- Exclude rescissions with indefinite amounts (“up to,” “not more than,” “such sums as may be necessary”); include “not less than” at the stated minimum.
- Exclude administrative withholdings or deferrals absent enacted rescission; ICA requires funds proposed for rescission be made available if Congress does not act within the statutory period.

Resolution:
- Resolve Yes if there exists at least one Public Law enacted within the window whose text rescinds definite amounts of budget authority summing to ≥ $2,000,000,000.
- Resolve No otherwise.

Primary resolution source and method:
- Use Congress.gov to identify laws enacted in the window and to access their text and Public Law status. Example format/reference: the Public Law page for H.R.4, which shows Public Law number and enactment date.
- Compute the total by summing the definite rescinded amounts in the enacted law’s text, applying GAO’s definiteness rules.

Secondary/confirmatory sources (if needed):
- White House/O.M.B. materials (special messages) to understand targeted accounts and amounts proposed, noting that only enacted text governs.
- GAO ICA explainer and 2 U.S.C. § 683 for process context and timeline constraints.

Edge cases:
- If a law rescinds amounts both definite and indefinite, count only the definite amounts.
- If a law states multiple rescissions across accounts, all definite rescinded amounts within that law are summed.
- If a veto override enacts a law on Dec 31, use the official enactment date/time in UTC as displayed on Congress.gov; enactment outside the window does not count even if effective date falls inside the window.

question: In EIA’s Electric Power Monthly, will coal’s share of U.S. net electricity generation for October 2025 be at least 16.00%?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30: The U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) publishes the Electric Power Monthly (EPM), typically with a two-month data lag. For example, the EPM page showed “Data for July 2025 — Release Date: September 23, 2025 — Next Release Date: October 24, 2025,” evidencing the cadence and lag. The September 2025 EPM issue includes monthly tables through July 2025 and states that values for 2024 and 2025 are preliminary and that coverage is the U.S. (50 states and DC).

Recent benchmarks: In Table 1.1 (“Net Generation by Energy Source: Total (All Sectors)”), coal’s share was 15.59% in October 2024 (coal net generation 50,933 thousand MWh; total 326,718 thousand MWh), and 17.96% in July 2025 (coal net generation 80,249; total 446,899). These shoulder- and summer-month shares suggest October’s coal share plausibly sits near the 16% threshold.

Key definitions: EIA defines net generation as gross generation minus the electricity consumed for station service/auxiliaries; energy storage can have negative net generation, but for share calculations, we use EIA-reported monthly net generation values. In EPM methodology, “Coal” generation includes anthracite, bituminous, subbituminous, lignite, waste coal, refined coal, synthetic coal, and coal‑derived synthesis gas.

Resolution source: The EPM main page hosts links to the current issue and tables (including Table 1.1) and indicates the release schedule; October 2025 data are expected to be published in late December 2025, consistent with the observed lag. The September 2025 EPM confirms that Table 1.1 provides monthly U.S. totals by energy source and lists methodological notes and coverage.
resolution_criteria:
Timeframe: The question resolves on or before 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Data window: Only October 2025 data count. The start date for eligible data is 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC and the end date is 2025-10-31 23:59:59 UTC, as represented in EIA’s October 2025 monthly entries.

Source of truth: EIA Electric Power Monthly (EPM) tables, specifically Table 1.1 “Net Generation by Energy Source: Total (All Sectors),” in the first EPM issue that includes October 2025 data and is publicly available by the resolution deadline.

Definitions (binding for resolution):
- Net generation: Use EIA’s definition (gross generation less station service/auxiliaries). Apply the figures as reported by EIA without adjustment.
- Coal generation: As categorized by EIA in EPM tables (includes anthracite, bituminous, subbituminous, lignite, waste coal, refined coal, synthetic coal, and coal‑derived synthesis gas).
- U.S. totals: Use the U.S. total (all sectors) row in Table 1.1, which covers the 50 states and the District of Columbia; territories are excluded.

Computation steps: From Table 1.1 for October 2025,
1) Read “Coal” net generation (thousand MWh).
2) Read “Total” net generation (thousand MWh).
3) Compute share = (Coal net generation / Total net generation) × 100%. Use the reported raw values; do not round intermediate values. Compare the exact computed share to 16.00%.

Outcome rule: Resolve Yes if the computed share is greater than or equal to 16.00%. Resolve No if it is less than 16.00%.

Versioning: If EIA revises October 2025 data after initial publication, use the first EPM issue that made October 2025 data available by the resolution deadline. If, contrary to expectations, October 2025 data are not published by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, the question should be treated as not resolvable under these criteria (organizer discretion), but based on EIA’s observed schedule, publication by late December 2025 is expected.

question: Will Box Office Mojo’s Domestic Opening Weekend figure for “Wicked: For Good” (tt19847976) be at least $105,000,000?
background:
Summary and current context (as of 2025-09-30):
- Film and release timing: The official site for the film states “In Theaters November 21, 2025,” confirming the U.S. theatrical release date for Wicked: For Good (Part Two). Wikipedia also lists November 21, 2025 as the scheduled U.S. theatrical release date, and notes that the film’s official title is Wicked: For Good (it was previously referred to as “Wicked Part Two” in some regions).
- Early screenings: Amazon has announced “Prime Early Screening” tickets to see Wicked: For Good on November 17, 2025, four days before the film’s wider release on November 21, 2025. These are select early screenings and not the general release.
- Resolution source availability: Box Office Mojo (BOM) already hosts the title page for Wicked: For Good at https://www.boxofficemojo.com/title/tt19847976/ and will display box office metrics there after release. On BOM title pages, the “Opening” field represents the domestic opening weekend gross; for example, Wicked (2024) shows “Opening $112,508,890” on its title page.
- Definitions used by BOM: BOM/IMDbPro defines “Weekend box office” as Friday through Sunday unless otherwise noted, with estimates posted Sunday and actuals posted Monday (Pacific Time). “Domestic” refers to North America (U.S., Canada, and Puerto Rico) unless otherwise noted.
- Benchmark from Part One: As context, Wicked (2024) recorded a domestic opening weekend of $112,508,890 and a domestic total of $473,231,120 on Box Office Mojo. This provides a relevant baseline for forecasting the sequel’s opening performance.

Why this is forecastable now:
- The film is scheduled to open on Nov 21, 2025, so the opening weekend (Fri–Sun) will conclude by Nov 23, 2025, well before the Dec 31, 2025 resolution deadline [87b05b; e239ce]. The title page exists and historically displays the requisite “Opening” figure [83c9fd; 141916].
- The threshold ($105M) is set close to Part One’s opening ($112.5M), where reasonable analysts can disagree given sequel dynamics, competition on the pre-Thanksgiving frame, word-of-mouth, and possible impacts (positive or negative) from early screenings [141916; 7578a6].
resolution_criteria:
- Question: Resolve “Yes” if Box Office Mojo’s Domestic Opening Weekend figure for the film “Wicked: For Good” (IMDb title ID tt19847976) is at least $105,000,000; otherwise resolve “No.”

- Primary resolution source: The Box Office Mojo title page for tt19847976 (https://www.boxofficemojo.com/title/tt19847976/). This page exists already and will display the needed metrics after release.

- What exact number to use:
  • Use the “Opening” (a.k.a. Domestic Opening Weekend) figure shown on the BOM title page for tt19847976. On BOM, the “Opening” field on a title page corresponds to the domestic opening weekend gross; e.g., Wicked (2024) lists “Opening $112,508,890” on its title page.
  • “Weekend box office” on BOM is Friday through Sunday unless otherwise noted; “Domestic” refers to North America (U.S., Canada, and Puerto Rico). This implicitly defines the opening weekend period for the purpose of this question.

- Time window and updates:
  • Opening weekend for Wicked: For Good is expected to be the first Friday–Sunday of its domestic release, which is scheduled for November 21–23, 2025, based on the official U.S. theatrical release date of November 21, 2025 [87b05b; e239ce].
  • Resolve based on the figure as displayed on BOM at or before 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. If the figure is revised on BOM before the deadline, use the value as of the deadline. Revisions after the deadline are ignored for resolution.

- Handling previews and early screenings:
  • Any preview grosses or special early screenings (e.g., Prime Early Screening on Nov 17, 2025) are handled according to how Box Office Mojo incorporates them into the “Opening” figure. No manual adjustments will be made; the value displayed by BOM governs the resolution [7578a6; e239ce].

- Title and identification:
  • The film is uniquely identified by IMDb title ID tt19847976 on BOM, which avoids ambiguity in case of an alternate or localized on-page title.

- Edge cases:
  • If, by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, Box Office Mojo does not display a Domestic Opening Weekend (“Opening”) figure for tt19847976 (e.g., due to a release delay or the film not opening domestically by that time), resolve “No.” This ensures the market resolves by the deadline [83c9fd; 87b05b].

- Currency and rounding:
  • The threshold is $105,000,000 (US dollars). No special rounding rules are applied beyond BOM’s standard presentation; the decision criterion is whether the BOM “Opening” value is greater than or equal to 105,000,000 exactly.

question: Will the Federal Reserve lower the federal funds rate target range midpoint by at least 100 basis points by 2025-12-31 (UTC), relative to 2025-09-15?
background: Context for forecasters: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) sets a target range for the federal funds rate, the interest rate at which depository institutions lend balances to each other overnight. Cuts in the policy rate are typically implemented in 25 basis point increments. Policy rates influence broader financing conditions, including commercial borrowing costs. This question operationalizes “a 100 bp cut” as a change in the midpoint of the FOMC’s target range of at least 1.00 percentage point between a fixed baseline date and the end date. Definitions: federal funds rate (see: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_funds_rate), basis point (see: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basis_point). Data used for resolution will come from the Federal Reserve Board’s monetary policy press releases and the St. Louis Fed’s FRED series for the Federal Funds Target Range Upper (DFEDTARU) and Lower (DFEDTARL). Forecasters should check those sources for the baseline (2025-09-15) and end-date (2025-12-31) values when forming priors.
resolution_criteria:
Start and end of measurement window: Baseline is the federal funds target range in effect at 2025-09-15 23:59:59 UTC. The end observation is the federal funds target range in effect at 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. The question resolves on the first business day after 2025-12-31 once sources are checked.

Quantity measured: Midpoint of the federal funds target range on each date, defined as (upper limit + lower limit)/2, in percentage points. If the FOMC targets a single point (no range) on either date, treat the upper and lower as equal to that point target.

Resolution rule: Resolve YES if the end-date midpoint is less than or equal to (baseline midpoint − 1.00). Otherwise resolve NO.

Primary sources (authoritative and recurring):
- Federal Reserve Board monetary policy press releases (FOMC statements): https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy.htm
- St. Louis Fed FRED series for Federal Funds Target Range – Upper Limit (DFEDTARU): https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DFEDTARU and Lower Limit (DFEDTARL): https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DFEDTARL

Measurement procedure:
1) Determine the upper and lower limits in effect at the two specified timestamps using the Fed press releases or the FRED DFEDTARU/DFEDTARL daily values for those calendar dates. If both are available and disagree, prefer the Federal Reserve Board press release text for the decision that set the range in effect at the timestamp.
2) Compute the midpoint for each date as (upper+lower)/2.
3) Compute change = baseline midpoint − end-date midpoint.
4) If change ≥ 1.00 percentage points (100 bps), resolve YES; else NO.

Edge cases and tie-breaking:
- If the policy target changes intraday on 2025-12-31, use the range in effect at 23:59:59 UTC on 2025-12-31.
- If sources are temporarily unavailable on the resolution date, use reputable wire services (e.g., Associated Press, Reuters, Bloomberg) or major newspapers (e.g., WSJ, NYT) reporting the announced target range; verify against archived copies when available.
- No rounding beyond the precision published by the Fed/FRED is applied; midpoints are calculated using the exact published upper and lower values.

question: Iran crude oil production in November 2025 (per OPEC secondary sources) ≥ 3,250 tb/d?
background:
Overview and status quo as of Sept 30, 2025 (UTC):
- Sanctions context: On Sept 27–28, 2025, United Nations nuclear-related sanctions on Iran were reinstated via the JCPOA “snapback” mechanism. Reporting noted the return of an arms embargo, travel bans, asset freezes and other measures; Iran recalled its ambassadors to the UK, France and Germany in response. On Sept 29, 2025, the Council of the European Union said it reimposed restrictive measures, including freezing assets of the Central Bank of Iran and major Iranian commercial banks, and restrictions affecting imports, purchase and transport of crude oil, natural gas, petrochemical and petroleum products, as well as certain transport limitations.
- OPEC data source: The OPEC Monthly Oil Market Report (MOMR) is OPEC’s recurring publication that “covers major issues affecting the world oil market and provides an outlook for crude oil market developments for the coming year” and serves as the canonical landing page for monthly issues and updates (https://www.opec.org/monthly-oil-market-report.html). Within MOMR, Table 5-7 is titled “DoC crude oil production based on secondary sources, tb/d” and lists country-level crude oil production for Declaration of Cooperation (DoC) participants (OPEC+), including the Islamic Republic of Iran; the table header explicitly shows the unit “tb/d”. The December MOMR historically includes November production data (e.g., the December 2024 MOMR header includes “Nov 24”).
- Current production baseline: Iran’s crude oil production (per OPEC secondary sources) was reported at 3,245 tb/d (3.245 million barrels per day) for July 2025, down 12 tb/d month-on-month, illustrating a recent baseline near the proposed threshold. Total DoC crude production figures and the unit “tb/d” are consistently used across MOMR issues.
- Definitions and units: A barrel (bbl) is a standard oil volume unit equal to 42 US gallons (about 159 liters) under API reference conditions; barrels per day (b/d) is the flow-rate unit used for oil production. The MOMR’s Table 5-7 uses “tb/d” (thousand barrels per day) in its title; this question relies on the figure as reported in that table. The “Declaration of Cooperation (DoC)” is OPEC’s cooperation framework with non-OPEC producers (commonly referred to as OPEC+).
Why this question is high-entropy and plausibly uncertain: Newly reimposed UN/EU nuclear-related sanctions could constrain Iran’s crude exports, financing and logistics, potentially influencing production decisions, while Iran may sustain or adjust output to maximize revenue or demonstrate resilience. With recent levels near 3,250 tb/d and policy uncertainty, November 2025 production could reasonably land above or below the threshold.
Timing: The December 2025 MOMR is typically published in mid-December; OPEC’s MOMR page is the authoritative source for the latest monthly issue.
resolution_criteria:
Question: Will the figure for the Islamic Republic of Iran in OPEC’s MOMR Table 5-7 (“DoC crude oil production based on secondary sources, tb/d”) for November 2025 be ≥ 3,250 tb/d?

Primary resolution source:
- Use the OPEC Monthly Oil Market Report (MOMR) published in December 2025, accessed via OPEC’s MOMR landing page (https://www.opec.org/monthly-oil-market-report.html). Locate Table 5-7 (or its successor explicitly titled “DoC crude oil production based on secondary sources, tb/d”) and read the entry for “IR Iran” for November 2025. If the reported value is ≥ 3,250 tb/d, resolve Yes; otherwise, resolve No.

Clarifications and definitions:
- “tb/d” means thousand barrels per day; rely on the unit shown in the OPEC table title (“tb/d”) and the value reported there. A barrel (bbl) is 42 US gallons and b/d denotes barrels per day; 3,250 tb/d equals 3.25 million barrels per day.
- “DoC” refers to the OPEC+ cooperation framework; Table 5-7 lists crude oil production for DoC participants, including Iran.
- “Secondary sources” is OPEC’s established methodology for country production estimates; the table title specifies “based on secondary sources”. This question uses OPEC’s reported figure as-is without further adjustment.

Versioning and timing:
- If OPEC publishes multiple versions of the December 2025 MOMR, use the latest official December 2025 MOMR available by 23:59 UTC on Dec 31, 2025.
- If, unexpectedly, the December 2025 MOMR is not posted by 23:59 UTC on Dec 31, 2025, defer resolution until the first MOMR that includes November 2025 country-level production data (Table 5-7 or successor). If no such MOMR is publicly available by Jan 31, 2026, flag for admin review.

Start and end of the forecasting window:
- Forecasting window: Events and publications relevant to resolution must occur between 00:00 UTC on Oct 15, 2025 and 23:59 UTC on Dec 31, 2025. The underlying production month being assessed is November 2025; only the OPEC-reported November 2025 figure for Iran in Table 5-7 counts toward resolution.

Notes for resolvers:
- Do not substitute other agencies’ estimates (e.g., IEA/EIA) or company/third-party datasets. Use OPEC’s MOMR Table 5-7 value for IR Iran, November 2025, as published.
- If Table 5-7 is renamed or renumbered, use the table explicitly labeled with DoC country “crude oil production based on secondary sources” in tb/d and containing monthly rows/columns including Nov 2025.

question: Will OPEC+’s official required-production sum for its eight participating countries be ≥250,000 bpd higher in December 2025 than in September 2025?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30:
- What is OPEC+? OPEC+ refers to the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries together with other cooperating oil‑producing countries, formed in late 2016 to coordinate production policy. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OPEC
- How OPEC+ states targets: In 2025 communications, OPEC press releases for a subgroup of eight participating countries have used the term “required production level” and announced month‑to‑month “production adjustments” relative to those required levels. The eight participating countries are Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman. OPEC has noted these adjustments can be paused or reversed depending on market conditions. Example PR (May 3, 2025): https://www.opec.org/pr-detail/563-03-may-2025.html
- 2024 baseline and unwind: On June 2, 2024, OPEC+ extended deep production cuts into 2025, including extending 3.66 mb/d of cuts to end‑2025 and phasing out 2.2 mb/d of voluntary cuts from October 2024 to September 2025, with the option to pause or reverse the unwind. Capacity target talks were pushed to November 2025.
- Developments in 2025: OPEC+ agreed to raise output by 137,000 bpd in October 2025, decided by eight members in an online meeting, while noting it could accelerate, pause, or reverse future hikes. Reuters reported earlier monthly boosts in mid‑2025 were larger (e.g., 411,000 bpd in June/July; 555,000 bpd in August/September), and that the October step represented a slowdown. The group also indicated it had begun unwinding a second tranche of cuts ahead of schedule. Reuters subsequently reported OPEC+ was likely to approve another production increase of at least 137,000 bpd for November 2025, to be decided at an October 5 meeting; that article did not mention December plans.
- Market outlook: The U.S. EIA stated on 2025-08-12 that OPEC+ announced it would unwind its cuts by September 2025 (a year ahead of the prior schedule), and the EIA expected supply to outpace demand, inventories to grow, and Brent to average below $60/bbl in Q4 2025.
- Where targets are published: OPEC’s Monthly Oil Market Report (MOMR) is a monthly analytical publication and is typically not the channel for announcing formal OPEC+ production targets; formal targets and “required production levels” for the eight‑country subgroup have appeared in OPEC press releases/communiqués. See MOMR: https://www.opec.org/monthly-oil-market-report.html
- Units: One oil barrel (bbl) equals exactly 42 U.S. gallons (approximately 159 liters). “bpd” denotes barrels per day. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barrel_(unit)
Why this is non‑trivial: As of late September 2025, an October +137 kbpd increase has been agreed and at least another +137 kbpd for November is anticipated, but OPEC+ retains flexibility to pause or reverse increases, leaving the net change between September and December 2025 uncertain. The EIA’s outlook suggests additional pressure to increase supply into late 2025, yet price dynamics might prompt caution.
resolution_criteria:
Outcome to resolve between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.
Definition of key terms and scope:
- OPEC+ means OPEC members plus cooperating non‑OPEC producers, as described here: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OPEC.
- Eight participating countries refers to the subgroup explicitly listed by OPEC in 2025 production‑adjustment press releases: Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, UAE, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman.
- Required production level is the official per‑country target level used in OPEC’s 2025 press releases when announcing month‑to‑month production adjustments for the eight participating countries (e.g., “a production adjustment of 411 thousand barrels per day in June 2025 from May 2025 required production level”). This terminology and approach are documented in OPEC’s May 3, 2025 press release.
- Barrel and bpd: One barrel (bbl) equals exactly 42 U.S. gallons; bpd = barrels per day. Calculations are done in bpd (not thousand bpd).
What is measured:
- Let S_sep be the sum of the required production levels (in bpd) for the eight participating countries applicable to September 2025.
- Let S_dec be the sum of the required production levels (in bpd) for the same eight countries applicable to December 2025.
Resolution rule:
- YES if S_dec − S_sep ≥ 250,000 bpd. NO otherwise.
Source hierarchy and how to determine S_sep and S_dec:
1) Primary sources: OPEC/OPEC+ official communications (press releases, meeting communiqués) that specify per‑country required production levels and/or month‑specific targets for the eight participating countries. Example of the relevant format and terminology: OPEC PR, May 3, 2025. OPEC official publications are hosted on https://www.opec.org/ (Press Releases section).
2) If a primary source specifying the exact per‑country required production levels for September 2025 and/or December 2025 is not publicly available by 2025‑12‑31 23:59:59 UTC, rely on reputable wire‑service reports that directly and unambiguously quote OPEC/OPEC+ official target figures or month‑on‑month adjustments from those official communications. Acceptable outlets include Reuters (Energy/OPEC section: https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/opec/), Bloomberg, or the Associated Press. For context on recent reporting style and substance, see: Reuters on October +137 kbpd  and on expected November +≥137 kbpd.
3) If multiple sources conflict, precedence is: OPEC communication(s) > Reuters > Bloomberg > Associated Press. Use the latest applicable document available by the resolution timestamp.
How to compute and handle units/rounding:
- Use the per‑country required production figures as stated. If a figure is provided in thousand bpd, convert to bpd by multiplying by 1,000. Sum the eight countries’ figures to obtain S_sep and S_dec. Compute S_dec − S_sep to the nearest barrel (no additional rounding beyond the source precision).
- Only targets/required production levels count; actual realized production does not affect resolution.
Temporal and eligibility notes:
- The question compares targets applicable to September 2025 and December 2025. For S_sep, use the last official required production levels applicable to September 2025 as of 2025‑09‑30 23:59:59 UTC. For S_dec, use the last official required production levels applicable to December 2025 available by 2025‑12‑31 23:59:59 UTC.
- Forecasting period: 2025‑10‑15 00:00:00 UTC through 2025‑12‑31 23:59:59 UTC. This window defines when the market participant is forecasting the outcome; it does not restrict use of earlier documents needed to establish September 2025 targets.
- If OPEC+ announces ranges rather than point targets for required production levels, use the clearly identified “required production level” point figure. If only a range exists and no point figure is identified by 2025‑12‑31, resolve using the lower bound of the range to define each country’s required production level for summation.
Why this is resolvable:
- OPEC’s 2025 press releases for the eight‑country subgroup explicitly reference “required production levels” and month‑to‑month adjustments, and note that increases can be paused or reversed. Reuters’ reporting documents both agreed and anticipated month‑specific increases and the eight‑member decision mechanism. The EIA documents the broader unwind timeline into September 2025. OPEC’s MOMR is monthly analysis (not the venue for the targets themselves). Together, these sources provide clear, authoritative, and timely documentation to establish S_sep and S_dec and compute the difference by the resolution deadline.

question: Will the U.S. unemployment rate (U-3, seasonally adjusted) for November 2025 be 4.5% or higher when the BLS publishes the Employment Situation on December 5, 2025?
background:
Overview and status quo as of September 30, 2025
- What is being forecast: The seasonally adjusted U.S. unemployment rate (U-3) for the reference month November 2025, as reported in the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) Employment Situation news release scheduled for Friday, December 5, 2025, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time (ET).
- Definitions (authoritative BLS sources):
  • U-3 (official unemployment rate): Total unemployed as a percent of the civilian labor force; calculated as (unemployed ÷ labor force) × 100.
  • Unemployed (CPS): People with no employment during the survey reference week, who were available for work (except for temporary illness), and who made specific efforts to find employment during the 4‑week period ending with the reference week.
  • Labor force: All people age 16+ classified as either employed or unemployed.
  • Seasonally adjusted: Statistical procedure removing normal seasonal effects (e.g., holidays, school schedules, weather) to better reveal underlying trends.
- Current status: The latest published headline unemployment rate (seasonally adjusted U-3) was 4.3 percent for August 2025, and the release noted the rate "changed little" in August. The next Employment Situation report (covering September 2025) is scheduled for Friday, October 3, 2025, at 8:30 a.m. ET.
- Where to find the data at resolution time: BLS Employment Situation release page (the canonical landing page for the monthly report): https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.htm. BLS’s release calendar confirms the Employment Situation for November 2025 is set for Friday, December 5, 2025, at 8:30 a.m. ET.
Why this question is non-trivial: The threshold (≥ 4.5%) is close to the recent reported level (4.3% for August 2025), making both “Yes” and “No” plausible depending on labor-market developments through November.
resolution_criteria:
How the question resolves
- Resolution window: This question resolves on the basis of the BLS Employment Situation news release published on Friday, December 5, 2025, at 8:30 a.m. ET, which covers the reference month November 2025.
- Exact test: "Yes" if the headline seasonally adjusted unemployment rate (U-3) for November 2025, as published in the BLS Employment Situation news release on that date, is greater than or equal to 4.5%. Otherwise, "No".
- What value to use: Use the seasonally adjusted U-3 unemployment rate for the United States, as presented in the December 5, 2025 Employment Situation news release (e.g., in the summary and accompanying tables). Do not use any later revisions, benchmarking updates, or corrections published after the initial release; resolution is based on the first official publication on December 5, 2025.
- Scope and definitions (for clarity):
  • "U-3" means the official unemployment rate: total unemployed as a percent of the civilian labor force.
  • "Unemployed," "labor force," and "seasonally adjusted" are defined per BLS Current Population Survey concepts.
  • "Reported by BLS" means posted on the BLS Employment Situation news release page: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.htm.
- Contingencies: If BLS reschedules the December 5, 2025 release, resolve using the first official Employment Situation news release that includes November 2025 data (i.e., the earliest publication that reports the November 2025 U-3). If multiple versions are posted the same day (e.g., corrected PDFs), use the earliest official publication time-stamped by BLS.
- Primary resolution sources:
  • BLS Employment Situation release page: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.htm.
  • BLS release calendar confirming date/time: https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/current_year.asp (entry: Employment Situation for November 2025 — Friday, December 5, 2025, 08:30 AM ET).

question: Will the IMF Executive Board approve any new financing for Malawi between October 15 and December 31, 2025?
background:
Summary of context as of 2025-09-30:
- IMF Executive Board: The IMF’s 25-member Executive Board conducts the day-to-day business of the IMF and is the decision-making body that approves financing arrangements and related reviews. See: https://www.imf.org/en/About/executive-board/eds-voting-power
- Status of Malawi’s 2023 IMF program: The Extended Credit Facility (ECF) arrangement approved in November 2023 for Malawi automatically terminated on May 14, 2025 because no program review was completed within 18 months, per IMF policy for low-income countries. See: IMF press release on the 2025 Article IV Board conclusion and Malawi FAQs, respectively. 
- Article IV (2025): The Executive Board concluded the 2025 Article IV consultation with Malawi in July 2025, noting high inflation, unsustainable fiscal and debt dynamics, FX shortages, and fuel scarcity, and emphasizing decisive policy action, fiscal consolidation, debt sustainability steps (including external restructuring), a market-clearing exchange rate, and governance reforms. 
- Macroeconomic snapshot (mid-2025): IMF staff reported real GDP growth projected at 2.4% in 2025, inflation averaging about 29% in 2025, very low reserves, a current account deficit near 22% of GDP, and that after the ECF’s expiry authorities were designing a homegrown reform program. The IMF country report further highlights persistent inflation and unsustainable fiscal/debt dynamics.
- How Board approvals are announced: IMF Board-approved financing is typically announced via IMF press releases with formulations such as “The Executive Board … approved a [X]-month arrangement under the Extended Credit Facility (ECF) for [country]” or “completed the [nth] review … making available ”. See also the Malawi country page, which aggregates country-specific news and documents.

Key facility definitions (for clarity):
- Extended Credit Facility (ECF): Medium-term concessional financing for PRGT-eligible low-income countries with protracted balance of payments needs. https://www.imf.org/en/About/Factsheets/Sheets/2023/Extended-Credit-Facility-ECF
- Stand-by Credit Facility (SCF): Concessional financing for short-term balance of payments needs; can be used on a precautionary basis. https://www.imf.org/en/About/Factsheets/Sheets/2023/Stand-by-Credit-Facility-SCF
- Rapid Credit Facility (RCF): Rapid, concessional financing for urgent balance of payments needs in LICs. https://www.imf.org/en/About/Factsheets/Sheets/2023/Rapid-Credit-Facility-RCF
- Rapid Financing Instrument (RFI): Rapid financing for urgent balance of payments needs for any member under the GRA. https://www.imf.org/en/About/Factsheets/Sheets/2023/Rapid-Financing-Instrument-RFI
- Extended Fund Facility (EFF): Medium-term financing to address structural balance of payments problems (often used by emerging/advanced economies). https://www.imf.org/en/About/Factsheets/Sheets/2023/Extended-Fund-Facility-EFF
- Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF): Longer-term financing to support reforms that reduce macro-critical risks (e.g., climate, pandemic preparedness). https://www.imf.org/en/About/Factsheets/Sheets/2023/Resilience-Sustainability-Facility-RSF
- Staff-Monitored Program (SMP): An informal staff-monitored arrangement without Executive Board endorsement and without financing; used to build track record. https://www.imf.org/en/About/Factsheets/Sheets/2023/Staff-Monitored-Program-SMP

Primary sources for resolution and situational awareness:
- IMF Malawi country page (aggregates press releases, reports): https://www.imf.org/en/Countries/MWI 
- IMF News press releases (typical locus for Board approval announcements): example of ECF approval phrasing ; Article IV Board conclusion for Malawi.
resolution_criteria:
Question and date window:
- This resolves to Yes if the International Monetary Fund (IMF) Executive Board approves any new financing for the Republic of Malawi between October 15, 2025 and December 31, 2025, inclusive, based on the Board decision date as stated in the IMF press release header (“Washington, DC – [Date]”). For this question, inclusion is determined by whether that stated Board decision date falls between 2025-10-15 and 2025-12-31, inclusive, using Washington, DC local date (US/Eastern). If multiple qualifying approvals occur, only one is required for a Yes. Otherwise, resolve No.

Definitions (all must be interpreted per IMF factsheets and press releases):
- IMF Executive Board: The 25-member body that conducts the day-to-day business of the IMF; it is the decision-making body that approves IMF financing arrangements and completes reviews.
- New financing (qualifying events): Any of the following events for Malawi announced by the IMF as an Executive Board decision during the window:
  1) Approval of a new financing arrangement under any IMF financing facility (e.g., ECF, SCF, EFF, RSF, or other IMF financing facility).
  2) Approval of a rapid financing disbursement (e.g., RCF or RFI).
  3) Completion of a review under an already-approved arrangement that “makes available” a disbursement (as stated in the press release), or an augmentation of access that increases available financing for Malawi within the arrangement period (as stated in the press release). Example of standard IMF announcement phrasing: “The Executive Board … approved …” or “completed the [nth] review … making available …”.

Non-qualifying events (explicit exclusions):
- Article IV consultations and their Board conclusions (surveillance only).
- Staff-Monitored Programs (SMPs), staff mission end-of-mission press releases, staff-level agreements, management approvals, press briefings, or any announcement that does not explicitly state an Executive Board decision to provide financing to Malawi.
- Announcements by Malawian authorities or third parties without corroborating IMF Board approval language.

Start and end of eligibility window (time standard):
- A decision counts if the IMF press release states that the Executive Board decision date (“Washington, DC – [Date]”) is on or after 2025-10-15 and on or before 2025-12-31 (US/Eastern date). No time-of-day is required since IMF press releases use date-only stamps.

Authoritative resolution sources and verification steps:
- Primary: IMF News press releases and/or the Malawi country page on imf.org. Confirm the presence of Board-approval phrasing and that the stated decision date falls within the window.
  • Example links: https://www.imf.org/en/News (filter for Malawi) and https://www.imf.org/en/Countries/MWI
