- “Intergovernmental Conference (IGC)”/“Accession Conference” refers to the formal meetings at which accession negotiations proceed and are publicly communicated by the Council; official Council press releases for these conferences constitute valid evidence.
- Timezone: All times are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
- Start date: 00:00 UTC on 15 October 2025. End date: 23:59 UTC on 31 December 2025.

Exclusions:
- Announcements of intent, proposals, or statements that a cluster is “ready” or “recommended” to open do not count unless they explicitly state that negotiations on a named cluster are opened.
- Technical steps such as completing screening, adopting roadmaps/benchmarks, or opening/closing individual chapters without an explicit statement that the cluster is opened do not count.
- Press reports without corroborating official Council/IGC documentation do not count by themselves; however, if consilium.europa.eu is temporarily inaccessible, credible wire services (e.g., Reuters, AP, AFP) contemporaneously reporting on the official EU action may be used as a backup to determine resolution.

If by 23:59 UTC on 31 December 2025 no eligible source shows that any negotiating cluster with Ukraine has been opened during the period, resolve NO.

question: EU BEV share (monthly): Will BEVs reach at least 18.0% of EU new passenger-car registrations in November 2025?
background:
Context and definitions as of 2025-09-30:
- Definition: A battery electric vehicle (BEV) is an electric vehicle powered exclusively by one or more electric motors using energy stored in onboard batteries and has no internal combustion engine. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battery_electric_vehicle
- Scope and data series: The European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association (ACEA) publishes monthly statistics press releases on EU new passenger-car registrations by power source (fuel type), with an accompanying PDF annex that includes EU totals and breakdowns by power source for the month and year-to-date (YTD). The annex tables typically include “New car registrations by market and power source – monthly” and “– year to date” for the EU, and sometimes also for EU+EFTA+UK; the EU scope is clearly delineated in the tables. See: https://www.acea.auto/press-release-calendar/
- Current status: ACEA reports that up to August 2025 (YTD), battery-electric cars accounted for 15.8% of the EU market share. See: https://www.acea.auto/pc-registrations/new-car-registrations-0-1-in-august-2025-year-to-date-battery-electric-15-8-market-share/
- Additional context (not used for resolution): JATO Dynamics reported that BEVs reached a record 20.2% market share in Europe in August 2025; the scope for this statistic is “Europe-28” (EU + EFTA + UK), which is broader than the EU-only scope ACEA uses for its core EU totals. See: https://www.jato.com/resources/media-and-press-releases/chinese-car-brands-outsell-renault-in-europe-in-august
- Publication schedule and resolvability: ACEA’s statistics press release calendar schedules the November 2025 “Passenger car registrations” release for Tuesday, 23 December 2025, ensuring the data will be available before year-end for question resolution. See: https://www.acea.auto/press-release-calendar/

Why this threshold: With EU BEV share at 15.8% YTD by August 2025  and recent month-level European data showing around 20% in the broader Europe-28 scope , a 18.0% threshold for a single month (November 2025) in the EU is challenging yet plausible, yielding high-entropy forecasting.

Key term clarifications to avoid ambiguity:
- “EU” refers to the European Union aggregate used by ACEA in its monthly registration tables; do not use EU+EFTA+UK aggregates for resolution.
- “New passenger-car registrations” are ACEA’s monthly counts of first-time registrations of new passenger vehicles; resolution will rely on the values as reported by ACEA in the November 2025 monthly tables.
- “BEV share” means the ratio of BEV registrations to total new passenger-car registrations in the EU for the month of November 2025, expressed as a percentage, as defined in the Resolution Criteria below.
resolution_criteria:
- Event window definition: “November 2025” means the calendar month from 2025-11-01 00:00:00 UTC through 2025-11-30 23:59:59 UTC.
- Source of truth: Resolve using ACEA’s official “Passenger car registrations” monthly statistics press release for November 2025 and/or its accompanying PDF annex, which ACEA schedules for publication on Tuesday, 23 December 2025. The annex provides EU totals and breakdowns by power source (including Battery Electric) for the month, enabling computation of the BEV share.
- Measurement scope: Use EU-only totals from ACEA’s tables. Do not use EU+EFTA+UK aggregates.
- Calculation: Compute the monthly EU BEV share for November 2025 as:
  BEV share = (EU BEV units registered in November 2025) / (EU total new passenger-car registrations in November 2025).
  Compare the exact (unrounded) ratio to the threshold 0.1800. Resolve Yes if the ratio is greater than or equal to 0.1800 (i.e., ≥ 18.0%), and No otherwise. If ACEA directly provides a monthly EU BEV percentage for November 2025, that figure may be used; if both unit counts and a percentage are present and inconsistent, precedence goes to the share computed from unit counts.
- Definitions for categories: “Battery Electric” refers to vehicles powered solely by electricity stored in onboard batteries with no internal combustion engine. Use ACEA’s standard power-source categories as presented in the November 2025 annex.
- Corrections and errata: If ACEA issues an official correction to November 2025 EU totals by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, use the latest corrected values available by that time; otherwise, use the initial release values.
- Verification timebox: A resolver should be able to verify the outcome within ~10 minutes by retrieving ACEA’s November 2025 press release and reading the EU monthly tables.

Resolution:
- Yes: The computed EU BEV share for November 2025 is ≥ 18.0%.
- No: The computed EU BEV share for November 2025 is < 18.0%.

question: Will the Ohio Power Siting Board issue an “Opinion, Order, and Certificate” approving PowerConneX II (OPSB Case 25-302-EL-BGN) by December 31, 2025?
background:
Summary of what’s being forecast
- This question concerns whether the Ohio Power Siting Board (OPSB) will approve the PowerConneX II New Albany Energy Center project by issuing its final approval order—titled “Opinion, Order, and Certificate”—for OPSB Case 25-302-EL-BGN by the end of 2025. Under Ohio law, a “certificate” means a certificate of environmental compatibility and public need issued by the OPSB pursuant to Section 4906.10 of the Ohio Revised Code (definition at ORC 4906.01(D): https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-4906.01).

Project and case details as of 2025-10-01 (status quo)
- Project: PowerConneX II New Albany Energy Center (OPSB Case 25-302-EL-BGN). It is a proposed natural gas–fired power generation facility with a capacity up to 216 MW, located in New Albany, Ohio.
- Hearings scheduled: A local public hearing is scheduled for October 29, 2025 at 6:00 p.m. (Eastern) and an evidentiary hearing is scheduled for November 6, 2025 at 10:00 a.m. (Eastern). The local public hearing is at New Albany City Hall; the evidentiary hearing is at the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio, Hearing Room 11-C, 180 East Broad Street, Columbus, OH 43215. The OPSB event page also lists a local public hearing for Oct. 29, 2025 at 6:00 p.m. (Eastern) for this case.
- Where to track filings and any eventual order(s):
  • OPSB case page for 25-302-EL-BGN: https://opsb.ohio.gov/cases/25-302-el-bgn.
  • OPSB event page for the case’s Local Public Hearing: https://opsb.ohio.gov/wps/portal/gov/opsb/events/25-302-el-bgn-LPH.
  • The OPSB commonly titles final approval documents “Opinion, Order, and Certificate,” as evidenced in other EL-BGN cases (e.g., Madison Fields Solar).

Legal definitions and how OPSB approves projects
- “Certificate” is explicitly defined in Ohio law (ORC 4906.01(D)), and is the authorization issued by the OPSB for constructing and operating a major utility facility (ORC 4906.01 definition section: https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-4906.01). The Board’s final approval order is typically styled “Opinion, Order, and Certificate”.

Additional context
- In April 2025, the OPSB authorized PowerConneX, Inc. to seek an accelerated review for a 120 MW natural-gas plant in New Albany, Licking County (case number referenced there was 25-90-EL-BGN). This item provides general context on similar PowerConneX development activity in the same area but does not itself determine the outcome of Case 25-302-EL-BGN.

Why this may resolve within the timeframe
- The local public hearing (Oct. 29, 2025) and evidentiary hearing (Nov. 6, 2025) are scheduled before year-end, after which the OPSB could issue a final order. The issuance, however, is not guaranteed by year-end—hence the uncertainty suitable for forecasting.
resolution_criteria:
Question
- Resolve whether the OPSB issues its final approval order granting a certificate for OPSB Case 25-302-EL-BGN (PowerConneX II New Albany Energy Center) on or before 2025-12-31 (date on the order), with the observation window beginning 2025-10-15. Specifically, the question resolves YES if, between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 (inclusive, using the document’s stated date), the OPSB issues a final order that grants a certificate of environmental compatibility and public need for Case 25-302-EL-BGN. Otherwise, resolve NO.

What counts as a qualifying approval
- A qualifying approval is an OPSB final order for Case 25-302-EL-BGN titled “Opinion, Order, and Certificate,” or a substantively equivalent order that explicitly grants a “certificate of environmental compatibility and public need” pursuant to ORC 4906.10 for the project identified as PowerConneX II New Albany Energy Center (Case 25-302-EL-BGN).

Timing and date conventions
- The controlling date is the date shown on the signed OPSB order as posted in the official case docket for 25-302-EL-BGN. The date must be on or after 2025-10-15 and on or before 2025-12-31. If the order shows only a date (no time), that date will be used. If both date and time are provided, use the date component only.

What does NOT count
- Any order that denies, dismisses, remands, or otherwise does not grant a certificate of environmental compatibility and public need for Case 25-302-EL-BGN does not count.
- Meeting agendas, press releases, news articles, or staff reports are not sufficient on their own; the qualifying criterion is the presence of a signed OPSB order in the case docket that grants the certificate.
- Orders in other cases (e.g., Case 25-90-EL-BGN) do not count for this question.

Source of truth and how to verify (10-minute check)
- Primary source: OPSB case page for 25-302-EL-BGN (https://opsb.ohio.gov/cases/25-302-el-bgn) where orders and certificates are posted. Look for a document titled “Opinion, Order, and Certificate,” or an order that explicitly grants the certificate for this case.
- Secondary source if needed: The OPSB events page for the case (https://opsb.ohio.gov/wps/portal/gov/opsb/events/25-302-el-bgn-LPH) provides official scheduling context but is not used for resolution.

Definitions (with links)
- “Certificate” means a certificate of environmental compatibility and public need issued by the OPSB under ORC 4906.10 (definition: ORC 4906.01(D), https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-4906.01).
- “Opinion, Order, and Certificate” is the standard title used by OPSB for final approvals in EL-BGN cases (example on an OPSB case page for another project).

Start and end dates
- Eligible issuance period: 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC through 2025-12-31 (inclusive) as determined by the date on the OPSB’s order posted to the case docket.

question: Will the U.S. FDA approve topical ocular reproxalap (Aldeyra Therapeutics) for the treatment of dry eye disease on or before December 31, 2025?
background:
As of October 1, 2025, Aldeyra Therapeutics reports that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has accepted for review the resubmitted New Drug Application (NDA) for topical ocular reproxalap for the treatment of dry eye disease (DED) and assigned a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date of December 16, 2025. Earlier in 2025, the FDA issued a Complete Response Letter (CRL) stating that the NDA failed to demonstrate efficacy in adequate and well-controlled investigations; the CRL did not identify safety or manufacturing (CMC) issues. Aldeyra stated its intent to resubmit the NDA mid‑year 2025. Reproxalap is described by the sponsor as a small‑molecule modulator of reactive aldehyde species (RASP) being developed for DED and allergic conjunctivitis.

Key definitions and context for forecasters:
- FDA: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is the federal agency responsible for evaluating NDAs for safety and efficacy. NDA approval means FDA has determined the drug is safe and effective for its proposed use(s), labeling is appropriate, and manufacturing and quality controls are adequate.
- NDA: A New Drug Application is the formal request by a sponsor for FDA approval to market a new pharmaceutical in the U.S..
- PDUFA: The Prescription Drug User Fee Act authorizes FDA to collect user fees to help expedite drug reviews; the current authorization (PDUFA VII) covers fiscal years 2023–2027.
- Dry eye disease (DED): A multifactorial disease of the ocular surface characterized by tear film instability, hyperosmolarity, ocular surface inflammation and damage, and neurosensory abnormalities.
- Topical ocular (eye drops): Administration of liquid drops directly to the eye’s surface.

Primary resolution source: FDA’s Drugs@FDA database (“FDA‑Approved Drugs”) will be used to verify approval status and dates for the relevant NDA.
resolution_criteria:
Time window: Eligible events must occur between 2025‑01‑01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025‑12‑31 23:59:59 UTC (inclusive).

Question to resolve: Will the FDA grant approval of an NDA for topical ocular reproxalap (regardless of final trade name) for the indication of treating dry eye disease (DED) within the time window?

Definitions (for resolution):
- “Approve” or “approval” means the FDA issues an approval action for an NDA, such that the product is authorized for marketing for the specified indication in the U.S., consistent with FDA’s definition of NDA approval (i.e., FDA has determined the drug is safe and effective for its proposed use(s), labeling is appropriate, and manufacturing/quality controls are adequate).
- “Topical ocular reproxalap” refers to the small‑molecule drug candidate known as reproxalap, administered as eye drops, sponsored by Aldeyra Therapeutics, and submitted to FDA for DED.
- “Dry eye disease (DED)” is as defined in the background above.

Resolution rules:
- Resolve Yes if, by the end of the time window, either of the following is true for the DED indication:
  (a) The relevant entry in FDA’s Drugs@FDA database shows an Approval action for reproxalap’s NDA for DED; or
  (b) The FDA publishes an official announcement (e.g., press release or announcement page) stating that FDA has approved reproxalap for DED.
- Resolve No if neither (a) nor (b) occurs within the time window, or if the FDA issues a Complete Response Letter, Refuse-To-File, or other non‑approval action only, or if any approval pertains solely to a different indication (e.g., allergic conjunctivitis) or a non‑topical ocular formulation.

Primary source of truth: FDA’s Drugs@FDA database entry for the product/indication. If Drugs@FDA has not yet updated by the end date, resolution may rely on an official FDA announcement as described above. Supporting context on the NDA and current review timeline derives from Aldeyra’s public communications and FDA background sources.

question: By December 31, 2025, will Italy publish a law in the Gazzetta Ufficiale that reallocates at least 6 of the 7 voting seats on RAI’s Board of Directors to be elected by Parliament, with those elections in at least one round requiring no more than an absolute majority in each chamber?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30:
- Current legal framework: Under Article 63 of Italy’s Consolidated Law on Audiovisual Media Services (TUSMA; D.Lgs. 8 November 2021, n. 208), RAI’s Board of Directors (Consiglio di amministrazione) consists of seven members. Two are elected by the Chamber of Deputies, two by the Senate (both using limited vote to one candidate), two are designated by the Council of Ministers (on proposal of the Minister of Economy and Finance), and one is designated by RAI employees. The board president is chosen by the board, with a favorable two‑thirds opinion by the Parliamentary Oversight Commission. The mandate lasts three years, with various eligibility and incompatibility provisions.
- EMFA timing: The European Media Freedom Act (EMFA) entered into force in May 2024, with full applicability in Italy starting 8 August 2025, while select provisions applied earlier (e.g., Article 3 from 8 November 2024; parts of Articles 4 and 6 and Articles 7–13 from 8 February 2025; Articles 14–17 from 8 May 2025).
- Reform proposals in 2025: A unified draft bill (testo unificato) dated 29 July 2025 proposes reallocating six of the seven voting board seats to Parliament—three elected by the Chamber of Deputies and three by the Senate—while one voting seat would be designated by RAI’s permanent employees. For the six parliamentary seats, the draft sets a two‑thirds threshold in the first two ballots and an absolute majority of the members (maggioranza assoluta dei componenti) from the third ballot onward. It removes government‑appointed voting seats and introduces some non‑voting participants. The board would elect the President and CEO. Terms would be extended to five years, among other changes.

Why this is forecast‑worthy now: Whether a reform of this structure is enacted and published by year‑end is uncertain but salient, especially given EMFA applicability since August 2025 and active parliamentary discussion of RAI governance. The specific threshold and allocation features are checkable in the statutory text (Gazzetta Ufficiale), enabling a crisp, unambiguous resolution.

Helpful definitions and references:
- RAI (Radiotelevisione italiana S.p.A.): Italy’s public service broadcaster. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RAI
- Parliament: Bicameral legislature comprising the Chamber of Deputies (Camera dei deputati) and the Senate of the Republic (Senato della Repubblica). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_Italy
- Absolute majority of members (maggioranza assoluta dei componenti): More than half of the total members of the chamber (not merely votes cast). See also Italian parliamentary practice glossary (general concept). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_majority
- Simple majority of votes cast: More than half of valid votes cast in a vote (abstentions not counted among valid votes).
- Board of Directors (Consiglio di amministrazione) and current composition rules: as defined in TUSMA Art. 63.
- Gazzetta Ufficiale (Italy’s official journal of record): https://www.gazzettaufficiale.it/
resolution_criteria:
Binary resolution (Yes/No). All times and dates in UTC.

Start date: 2025-09-30 00:00:00 UTC. End date: 2025-12-31 22:59:59 UTC (which corresponds to 23:59:59 CET on 2025-12-31).

Question: Will there be a law of the Italian Republic, published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale by the end date, that—within its operative provisions—does both of the following for RAI (Radiotelevisione italiana S.p.A.) governance?
A) Allocates at least 6 of the 7 voting seats on the RAI Board of Directors (Consiglio di amministrazione) to be elected by Parliament, defined as the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate; and
B) Specifies that, for the election of those parliamentary seats, in at least one ballot round in each chamber the threshold to elect each member is no higher than an absolute majority of the members of that chamber (maggioranza assoluta dei componenti). A rule that allows election by a simple majority of votes cast (maggioranza semplice dei votanti) also satisfies this condition.

Key definitions and clarifications:
- Voting seats: Seats on the RAI Board of Directors with voting rights. Non‑voting participants or observers, if any, do not count toward the 7.
- Parliament: The Chamber of Deputies (Camera dei deputati) and the Senate of the Republic (Senato della Repubblica).
- Elected by Parliament: Selected through voting procedures conducted by the Chamber and/or the Senate as prescribed in the law (e.g., parliamentary ballots), as opposed to designation by the Government (Council of Ministers), the Ministry of Economy and Finance, or RAI employees.
- Absolute majority of the members: More than half of the chamber’s total members (maggioranza assoluta dei componenti). Simple majority of votes cast is more than half of valid votes cast, excluding abstentions.
- Board size: This question targets the 7‑member board structure. If a law changes the board size from 7, then condition A is evaluated literally (“at least 6 of the 7 voting seats”). If the law does not define a 7‑member board (e.g., increases to 9), the condition A will not be satisfied and the market resolves No.

Resolution procedure:
1) Primary source: The text of the law as published in Italy’s Gazzetta Ufficiale within the time window. The resolver will locate any enacted law that amends RAI governance (notably Article 63 of D.Lgs. 208/2021 (TUSMA) or equivalent provisions) and check whether both condition A and condition B are met in the published statutory text.
2) If multiple laws are published in the window affecting RAI governance, the final state as of the end date governs. If any single law meeting both A and B is published by the deadline (regardless of later effective dates), resolve Yes. Otherwise resolve No.
3) If needed for interpretation (e.g., to identify current composition rules), the resolver may consult TUSMA Article 63 in force as baseline. For EMFA timing context, see. For an example of a 2025 draft illustrating 6 parliamentary seats and an absolute‑majority fallback threshold, see the unified draft dated 29 July 2025. Only the enacted law text in the Gazzetta Ufficiale will control the final decision.

Examples to guide resolution (non‑binding):
- Yes example: A law published on 2025‑12‑15 states that the RAI Board has 7 voting members; 3 are elected by the Chamber and 3 by the Senate; after two ballots at two‑thirds, from the third ballot the members are elected by absolute majority of the components in each chamber. Employees elect 1 member. This meets A and B [structure mirrors 4f9a85].
- No examples: (i) A law keeps the board at 7 but leaves only 4 or 5 seats to parliamentary election; (ii) A law assigns 6 seats to Parliament but requires a two‑thirds majority for all ballots, with no absolute‑majority or simple‑majority fallback; (iii) The only relevant texts published by the deadline are draft bills, committee reports, or communications, not laws published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale.

Authoritative references for baseline and context: TUSMA Article 63 (current governance) ; EMFA applicability timeline in Italy ; 29 July 2025 unified draft bill proposing 6 parliamentary seats with an absolute‑majority fallback.

question: Will the United States raise the universal reciprocal tariff baseline (for non‑listed partners) above 10% between 00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025?
background:
Summary of current policy as of October 1, 2025: Executive Order (EO) 14257 established an additional ad valorem duty (“reciprocal tariff”) that applies universally at 10% to imports, except where otherwise provided, and set country‑specific rates for trading partners enumerated in Annex I; implementation occurs via modifications to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS) and publication in the Federal Register. Subsequent Presidential actions modified partner‑specific rates and procedures but, as of July 31, 2025, confirmed that goods from foreign trading partners not listed in the then‑current Annex I remain subject to the universal 10% rate unless expressly provided otherwise. Other actions in mid‑2025 adjusted timelines, suspended or extended certain headings, or addressed PRC‑specific measures, without changing the universal baseline rate for non‑listed partners.

Key definitions and authoritative references:
- “Ad valorem duty”: A tariff calculated as a percentage of the value of the goods. See general definition: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ad_valorem_tax. EO 14257 imposes “an additional ad valorem rate of duty of 10 percent” on imports, except as otherwise provided.
- “Universal reciprocal tariff baseline”: The additional ad valorem duty rate applicable to imports from foreign trading partners not enumerated in the most current Annex I (i.e., not assigned a partner‑specific rate), as established by EO 14257 and any subsequent amendments.
- “Listed partner” vs. “non‑listed partner”: “Listed” refers to foreign trading partners enumerated in Annex I of EO 14257 or successor Annexes with partner‑specific rates; “non‑listed” refers to any foreign trading partner not so enumerated at the relevant time.
- “HTSUS”: The Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States, maintained by the U.S. International Trade Commission (USITC), provides tariff classifications and rates; EO 14257 and subsequent actions modify HTSUS (including Chapter 99) to implement reciprocal tariffs. Reference: https://hts.usitc.gov/.
- “Federal Register”: The official journal for U.S. government rules, proposed rules, and notices; reciprocal tariff EOs and implementing notices are published here. Reference: https://www.federalregister.gov/.
- “White House Presidential actions”: Official EOs and proclamations are posted here: https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/.

Status quo details (for forecasting context):
- EO 14257 states: “all articles imported into the customs territory of the United States shall be, consistent with law, subject to an additional ad valorem rate of duty of 10 percent,” except as otherwise provided; and partner‑specific rates apply to “trading partners enumerated in Annex I”. EO 14257 also authorizes further modifications to increase or decrease duties in response to retaliation, alignment, or changes in manufacturing capacity, and delegates implementation authority to modify HTSUS via Federal Register notice.
- The July 31, 2025 action “Further Modifying the Reciprocal Tariff Rates” maintained the 10% ad valorem rate for foreign trading partners not listed in Annex I, while reorganizing HTSUS headings to facilitate partner‑specific rates; it explicitly states unlisted partners remain at 10% under EO 14257, as amended.
- A July 10, 2025 Federal Register notice extended a temporary suspension related to certain headings and timelines without altering the universal baseline rate above 10%.
- An August 14, 2025 Federal Register action continued PRC‑specific suspensions/adjustments and did not change the universal baseline for non‑listed partners.
- A September 10, 2025 Federal Register action modified scope, procedures, and annexes (e.g., updating lists of excluded goods and steps to implement agreements), while signaling potential future adjustments but not changing the universal baseline rate at that time.

Why this question is high‑entropy and non‑trivial: As of October 1, 2025, the universal baseline remains 10%, but EO 14257 explicitly provides authority and processes to modify duties in response to evolving trade, security, and economic conditions (including retaliation or alignment by trading partners), making a near‑term increase plausible yet uncertain. Recent actions show active management of partner‑specific rates and HTSUS structure, indicating potential for further changes before year‑end. Forecasters must assess political and economic drivers, negotiation dynamics, and administrative timelines for promulgating and making effective any change above 10%.

Suggested verification sources on resolution date: Federal Register entries for EO 14257 and subsequent modifications (search by EO number and keywords like “reciprocal tariff,” “Annex I,” “HTSUS Chapter 99”), and White House Presidential actions for any EO/proclamation modifying the universal baseline rate. See examples of relevant entries: EO 14257 in the Federal Register ; White House action on July 31, 2025 ; FR notices on July 10, August 14, and September 10, 2025.
resolution_criteria:
Resolve YES if, between 00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, there is a formally enacted and effective Presidential action (e.g., Executive Order or Proclamation) and/or implementing Federal Register notice that sets the universal reciprocal tariff baseline (the additional ad valorem duty applicable to goods from foreign trading partners not listed in the then‑current Annex I) strictly greater than 10.000% as of 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025. Resolve NO otherwise.

Operational details:
- “Formally enacted and effective” means the measure is published (White House Presidential actions and/or Federal Register) and has taken effect per its stated effective date (e.g., with respect to goods entered for consumption on or after a specified date/time). Announced intent without effective implementation does not count.
- The determination hinges on the baseline rate applicable to non‑listed partners at resolution time. Partner‑specific rate changes, temporary suspensions of particular headings, or PRC‑only adjustments do not count unless they explicitly change the universal baseline rate for non‑listed partners.
- If multiple actions exist, the latest action in force as of 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025 governs. Verify by checking the most recent White House Presidential actions and Federal Register notices modifying EO 14257, its annexes, or HTSUS Chapter 99 notes.
- Primary resolution sources: Federal Register (https://www.federalregister.gov/) and White House Presidential actions (https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/). EO 14257 and subsequent modifications explicitly state that HTSUS modifications and notices will be published in the Federal Register, enabling unambiguous verification.

question: Between 2025-01-01 and 2025-12-31 (UTC), will the European Commission formally open at least one Article 258 TFEU infringement procedure against an EU Member State that cites Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the “AI Act”) as a legal basis?
background:
Context
- What this question is about: Whether the European Commission will take the first formal step (the letter of formal notice) to open an infringement procedure under Article 258 TFEU against at least one EU Member State in 2025 for alleged non-compliance with obligations in the EU Artificial Intelligence Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the “AI Act”). The Commission uses the infringement procedure to address Member State failures to fulfil obligations under EU law; the first formal step is the letter of formal notice.

- The AI Act and applicability timeline: The AI Act was published in the Official Journal on 12 July 2024 and entered into force on 1 August 2024. Its provisions apply in stages over 6–36 months. Relevant 2025 milestones include: bans on “unacceptable-risk” AI systems applying six months after entry into force (early February 2025), codes of practice applying nine months after entry into force (May 2025), and certain general-purpose AI (GPAI) transparency obligations applying 12 months after entry into force (August 2025). The European Parliament’s topic page highlights that the ban on unacceptable-risk systems began to apply on 2 February 2025 and that codes of practice apply nine months after entry into force.

- What counts as “AI Act obligations”: The AI Act’s official designation is Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of 13 June 2024. It lays down harmonised rules for AI in the Union, including prohibitions on specific AI practices, requirements for high‑risk AI systems, and transparency obligations for certain AI systems. This question treats any obligation arising under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as an “AI Act obligation.”

- Enforcement actors and venues: Infringement procedures under Article 258 TFEU are actions by the European Commission against EU Member States for alleged breaches of EU law; the formal stages are (i) letter of formal notice, (ii) reasoned opinion, and (iii) referral to the Court of Justice of the European Union. Information about Commission infringement decisions is published online and can be searched by country, policy area, date, and (importantly here) by legal basis. Separately, within the Commission, the European AI Office plays a key role in implementing and enforcing AI Act requirements for general‑purpose AI models; however, its supervision of providers is distinct from Article 258 infringement procedures against Member States.

Why this is uncertain and interesting
- 2025 is the first year in which several AI Act obligations bite, including the bans on unacceptable‑risk AI systems and initial GPAI transparency requirements, while Member States must ramp up governance and enforcement capacity. Whether the Commission will escalate to a formal Article 258 action against any Member State before year‑end is uncertain and potentially sensitive, making for a non‑trivial forecast that depends on legal readiness, national implementation efforts, and observed compliance signals.
resolution_criteria:
Question
- Resolve Yes if, between 2025-01-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, the European Commission formally opens at least one infringement procedure under Article 258 TFEU against an EU Member State in which Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the “AI Act”) is cited as a legal basis or the alleged breach explicitly concerns obligations under that Regulation. Otherwise resolve No.

Definitions (authoritative references provided)
- Infringement procedure (Article 258 TFEU): The Commission’s process against a Member State for failure to fulfil obligations under EU law. The formal stages are: (i) letter of formal notice; (ii) reasoned opinion; (iii) referral to the Court of Justice. The sending of a letter of formal notice is the first formal step and constitutes the “formal opening” of an infringement case.
- Letter of formal notice: A formal Commission letter requesting information and inviting the Member State to comply, typically with a two‑month deadline to respond. Its dispatch by the Commission marks the formal opening of an infringement procedure.
- AI Act / Regulation (EU) 2024/1689: “Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 June 2024 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence … (Artificial Intelligence Act).” It introduces prohibitions on certain AI practices, requirements for high‑risk systems, and transparency obligations, among others.
- Time zone: All dates/times are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

What qualifies for a Yes
- Any case where the Commission sends a letter of formal notice to an EU Member State during the eligibility window and where: (a) the Commission’s official publication (database entry or press release) lists Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 among the legal bases for the case, or (b) the publication text explicitly states that the alleged breach concerns obligations under the AI Act.

What does NOT qualify
- Actions not involving EU Member States (e.g., supervision or penalties imposed by the European AI Office on AI providers).
- Steps taken outside the eligibility window.
- Cases that do not cite the AI Act as a legal basis and do not explicitly allege breaches of obligations arising from the AI Act.

Primary resolution sources
- European Commission’s official infringement information portal, which publishes and allows search of infringement decisions by country, policy area, date, and legal basis. The presence of at least one case in 2025 whose legal basis includes Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 or whose description explicitly alleges AI Act non‑compliance will be sufficient to resolve Yes.
- European Commission “News and media” press releases announcing monthly “infringements packages.” A press release announcing that the Commission has sent a letter of formal notice to a Member State for alleged breaches of the AI Act within the eligibility window is sufficient to resolve Yes.

Ties and edge cases
- If a reasoned opinion or Court referral occurs in 2025 but the letter of formal notice for that same case was sent in 2024, the question resolves No (the formal opening was outside the window).
- If a press release announces a letter of formal notice on 2025-12-31 (UTC) but the database entry appears later, resolve Yes based on the press release.
- If multiple press releases or database entries exist, any single qualifying case is sufficient for Yes.

Contextual notes for forecasters
- Entry-into-force and staged applicability: The AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024, with bans on unacceptable‑risk systems applying from early February 2025, codes of practice from May 2025, and GPAI transparency obligations from August 2025.
- Governance: The European AI Office supports implementation and enforces certain AI Act requirements for GPAI models within the Commission structure, which may influence Commission awareness of national-level compliance but is separate from Article 258 actions.

question: Will CoreWeave publish a statement that its Active Power is at least 900 MW between Oct 15 and Dec 31, 2025 (UTC)?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30:
- Company and current metrics: CoreWeave, Inc. (Nasdaq: CRWV) reported that it ended Q2 2025 with approximately 470 MW of Active Power and increased total Contracted Power by ~600 MW to 2.2 GW, via its Q2 2025 press release and earnings materials.
- Management guidance toward year-end: On the August 12, 2025 earnings call, management said they were “on track to deliver over 900 megawatts of active power before the end of the year,” and reiterated a plan to “end the year with over 900 megawatts of active power.” These statements are forward-looking guidance rather than confirmations of current levels.
- M&A and power footprint context: On July 7, 2025, CoreWeave announced an agreement to acquire Core Scientific, stating that through the acquisition it would own approximately 1.3 GW of gross power across Core Scientific’s footprint, with over 1 GW of potential additional gross power for expansion; the transaction was expected to close in Q4 2025. Note that “gross power” in this context includes capacity supporting both HPC contracts (~840 gross MW) and crypto mining (~500 gross MW) and is not the same as CoreWeave’s “Active Power” metric.

Why this question: The company’s Q2 status (~470 MW Active Power) and management guidance (targeting >900 MW by year-end) set up meaningful uncertainty about both execution and whether CoreWeave will publish an official, unambiguous statement of having reached ≥900 MW of Active Power before the end of 2025. Construction timelines, interconnects, potential acquisition close, and disclosure practices introduce real execution and communication risk.

Key definitions and clarifications:
- Active Power: For the purpose of this question, “Active Power” means the specific metric labeled “Active Power” as reported by CoreWeave in its official investor communications (e.g., press releases, investor presentations, SEC filings, or earnings call transcripts posted on CoreWeave’s Investor Relations site). We do not infer or convert other power metrics to Active Power unless CoreWeave itself labels them as such. If a document uses “Active Power,” we take that term at face value as CoreWeave’s own metric. CoreWeave’s Q2 2025 materials report ~470 MW of Active Power but do not provide a formal definition beyond the label.
- Contracted Power: A separate CoreWeave-reported metric referring to contracted capacity (~2.2 GW as of Q2 2025) which is not interchangeable with Active Power.
- Gross power (Core Scientific context): Refers to the aggregate gross power across Core Scientific’s footprint (including crypto mining capacity) per the acquisition announcement and is not the same as Active Power.
- Power units: Megawatt (MW) and Gigawatt (GW). 1 GW = 1,000 MW. See general definitions for watt and multiples (e.g., https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watt#Multiples). Unit conversions are allowed for resolution (e.g., “0.9 GW” equals 900 MW).
- Acceptable phrasings: “≥ 900 MW,” “at least 900 MW,” “over 900 MW,” “more than 900 MW,” “0.9 GW or greater,” or a specific number that is ≥ 900 MW. For this market, statements using “approximately X MW” will be interpreted as X MW for threshold comparison (e.g., “approximately 910 MW” counts as 910; “approximately 900 MW” counts as 900).

Current status data points forecasters may use:
- Active Power as of Q2 2025: ~470 MW.
- Contracted Power as of Q2 2025: ~2.2 GW.
- Management guidance for year-end 2025: on track to deliver/end the year with over 900 MW Active Power (forward-looking as of Aug 12, 2025).
- Acquisition backdrop: Agreement to acquire Core Scientific; ~1.3 GW gross power cited; expected Q4 2025 close; conversion of crypto facilities to HPC is a potential future action and not indicative of current Active Power.
resolution_criteria:
Question: Will CoreWeave publish a statement that its Active Power is at least 900 MW between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC?

Start and end dates (UTC):
- Start: 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC
- End: 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC

Resolve Yes if, within the above window, CoreWeave publishes any eligible document that contains a statement satisfying ALL of the following:
1) It explicitly references “Active Power.”
2) It unambiguously indicates Active Power is ≥ 900 MW (e.g., “≥ 900 MW,” “at least 900 MW,” “over 900 MW,” “more than 900 MW,” “0.9 GW or greater,” or a specific figure ≥ 900 MW). Unit substitutions are allowed with 1 GW = 1,000 MW.
3) It is stated as a present or past fact (e.g., “we now have…,” “as of [date] we had…,” “we ended  with…,” “we have surpassed 900 MW”), not solely as a future plan, target, or expectation (e.g., “on track to deliver,” “targeting,” “expect to reach” will NOT count on their own).
4) It pertains to CoreWeave’s consolidated business (including subsidiaries). If the Core Scientific acquisition closes, any consolidated Active Power figure is eligible provided it is labeled “Active Power.”

Eligible document types and sources:
- CoreWeave Investor Relations site (investors.coreweave.com), including: press releases, investor presentations/slide decks, earnings call transcripts posted on the IR site, and SEC filings linked from the IR site.
- CoreWeave corporate newsroom (coreweave.com/newsroom), specifically official press releases.
- SEC’s EDGAR (sec.gov) filings by CoreWeave (e.g., 8-K, 10-Q, 10-K) if they contain the qualifying statement and are filed within the window.

Interpretation clarifications:
- “Approximately”: For threshold comparison, “approximately X MW” will be interpreted as X. Thus “approximately 900 MW” is treated as 900 MW; “approximately 910 MW” is treated as 910 MW.
- Metrics that do NOT count: Statements solely about “Contracted Power,” “Gross Power,” “Nameplate,” or similar capacity measures do not count unless the statement explicitly labels the metric as “Active Power.”
- Forward-looking-only statements do not count: E.g., “on track to deliver over 900 MW” without an accompanying present/past statement at or above the threshold will not satisfy the criteria.
- Conflicting statements: If multiple statements within the window conflict, the most recent-dated statement within the window prevails for resolution.
- Accessibility: If the original source is temporarily unavailable, archived copies (e.g., via Internet Archive or the IR site’s CDN mirror) of eligible sources are acceptable if they clearly show publication within the window.

Resolution:
- Yes if at least one eligible document within the window satisfies all criteria.
- No if no eligible document within the window satisfies all criteria (including if CoreWeave provides only forward-looking statements or only non-Active Power metrics during the window, or provides no applicable disclosure at all).

Primary sources to check at resolution time:
- investors.coreweave.com (Financials > Quarterly Results; News)
- coreweave.com/newsroom
- sec.gov EDGAR filings for CoreWeave (CRWV)

Reference data points supporting background and scope come from CoreWeave’s Q2 2025 press release and earnings materials and related communications , and the Core Scientific acquisition press release.

question: Between 2025-10-15 and 2025-12-31 (inclusive), will Great Britain’s National Energy System Operator (NESO) issue at least one Electricity Margin Notice (EMN)?
background:
Context and definitions as of 2025-09-30:

• What is NESO? The National Energy System Operator (NESO) is Great Britain’s publicly owned, independent system operator, launched on 2024-10-01 and responsible for planning and operating GB’s energy system. It replaced National Grid’s Electricity System Operator, with expanded strategic functions.

• What is an Electricity Margin Notice (EMN)? An EMN is a formal message issued by NESO when the normal safety margin for operating the electricity system is tighter than desired and cannot be addressed through standard mechanisms. It is a routine tool used to signal the market to provide a larger cushion of spare capacity and does not mean supply is at risk. EMN is a Grid Code modification that replaced the earlier “Notice of Inadequate System Margin (NISM)” and indicates a High Risk of Demand Reduction (HRDR). Market communication channels historically include BMRS, websites, and other market-facing mechanisms.

• How EMNs differ from Capacity Market Notices (CMNs): Both use similar underlying system data, but CMNs are automatically triggered based on predefined margin thresholds at four hours ahead, while EMNs are manually issued by the control room using operational and engineering judgment. They can therefore occur independently and at different times.

• Recent example (for context): In January 2025, NESO issued an EMN on 2025-01-07 at 20:30 for the period 16:00–19:00 on 2025-01-08, due to low temperatures and high demand; the EMN was cancelled at 16:15 on 2025-01-08 after requirements were met. Reuters also reported that NESO posted the cancellation and confirmed the time window, illustrating that EMNs are publicly signalled and covered by national media.

• Winter 2025 outlook: NESO signalled a de-rated margin of 6.6 GW in its early 2025 winter outlook (highest since 2019/20), while noting there can still be tight days, most likely in early December or mid-January. This suggests non-trivial uncertainty whether an EMN will be needed during late 2025.

Why this question has genuine uncertainty and clear resolution: EMNs are not issued every winter day but can occur during tight conditions and are publicly communicated. The 2025 outlook implies reasonable capacity but acknowledges potential tightness, making issuance between mid-October and year-end uncertain, yet observable via NESO market messages or credible media.
resolution_criteria:
How the question resolves

• Time window and timezone: The question resolves based on whether at least one EMN is issued between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC (inclusive), using UTC timestamps.

• Definitions
  – “Electricity Margin Notice (EMN)”: A formal market message, defined in the Grid Code, issued by NESO when operating margins are tighter than desired and standard mechanisms are insufficient, used to signal the market to increase available capacity; EMN replaced NISM and indicates a High Risk of Demand Reduction.
  – “Issue/issued”: For this question, an EMN is considered “issued” at the time NESO (the GB system operator) publishes or publicly confirms the EMN via an official channel (see Sources of Truth).
  – “Publish or publicly confirm”: Any of the following qualify: (a) NESO posts the EMN or its cancellation/activation on an official NESO web page (e.g., news/updates or system-notices explainer pages), (b) NESO transmits the EMN as an official market message via recognized market platforms (e.g., BMRS/Elexon), or (c) credible national media (e.g., Reuters, BBC) directly cites NESO’s posted market message or official confirmation with the EMN explicitly named and a time window described.
  – Distinction from CMN: Capacity Market Notices (CMNs) are automated four-hours-ahead signals and do not count toward this question unless a separate EMN is also issued; only EMNs count.

• What counts
  – YES if at least one EMN is issued (even if later cancelled) within the time window defined above.
  – NO if no EMN is issued within the time window defined above.
  – If multiple EMNs occur, any single confirmed EMN suffices for YES.

• Sources of truth (verifiable by a human within ~10 minutes)
  – NESO official communications: NESO “energy 101” and news/updates pages where system notices and explanations are posted.
  – Market platform postings: EMN market messages published to BMRS/Elexon or other established market channels noted in Grid Code documentation.
  – Credible national media citing NESO: Reuters coverage of EMNs and cancellations with explicit time windows has historically provided clear public confirmation.

• Examples for verification (illustrative only, outside this question’s window):
  – NESO’s January 2025 EMN issuance and cancellation and accompanying explanations.
  – Reuters’ report explicitly confirming an EMN and its cancellation window.

Notes

• Cancellation does not negate issuance; an EMN that is issued and later cancelled still counts as a Yes event within the window.
• Great Britain’s system operator scope and EMN definition are taken from official sources, ensuring clarity of terms for resolution.

question: Will Pakistan’s General CPI YoY inflation for November 2025 be at least 3.8% according to PBS?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01:
- Source and cadence: The Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) publishes monthly Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation press releases and monthly reviews, with a consistent pattern of releasing a given month’s CPI in the following month (e.g., November data is typically released in early December).
- Definition used by PBS: PBS reports “CPI inflation General” (the overall CPI at the National level) on a year‑over‑year (YoY) basis, phrased as “November [year] over November [prior year] (Year on Year)” and shows a National “General” row in its tables. The CPI is compiled on Base Year 2015‑16, with National CPI calculated as a weighted average of Urban and Rural CPI.
- Recent readings: PBS reported YoY General CPI at 4.86% for November 2024. In mid‑2025, PBS reported YoY General CPI at 3.2% for June 2025  and 2.99% for August 2025. These indicate a marked deceleration through 2025 from late‑2024 levels.

Key term definitions and links:
- Consumer Price Index (CPI): A measure that examines weighted average prices of a basket of consumer goods and services (see: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consumer_price_index). In this question, “General CPI” refers to the overall CPI at the National level as published by PBS (not Urban or Rural sub‑indices).
- Year‑over‑year (YoY): The percentage change of a metric relative to the same month in the previous year (see: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Year-over-year). PBS uses this terminology explicitly in its CPI press releases and tables.
- Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS): The official statistical authority of Pakistan; CPI press releases are accessible at https://www.pbs.gov.pk/press-releases and monthly CPI reviews/datasets at https://www.pbs.gov.pk/cpi.

Why this threshold: With YoY General CPI near ~3%–4% in recent months (4.86% Nov 2024; 3.2% Jun 2025; 2.99% Aug 2025), a 3.8% cutoff for November 2025 is intended to maximize uncertainty and disagreement among forecasters about whether inflation will re‑accelerate or remain subdued by late‑2025.
resolution_criteria:
Primary proposition:
- Resolve YES if PBS’s official November 2025 CPI figure for “General” at the National level (Year‑over‑Year, i.e., November 2025 over November 2024) is at least 3.8% (≥3.8%) as reported by PBS; resolve NO otherwise.

Primary source hierarchy:
1) PBS press release for November 2025 hosted on pbs.gov.pk (e.g., PBS “Press Releases” page: https://www.pbs.gov.pk/press-releases). Use the YoY General CPI figure as presented by PBS, typically stated as “CPI National … increased by X% over [same month of prior year]” and shown in the “Yearly Analysis (November 2025 over November 2024)” table under the “General” row.
2) If the November 2025 press release is not available by the deadline, use PBS’s “Monthly Review on Price Indices” for November 2025 from https://www.pbs.gov.pk/cpi. Use the YoY General CPI figure stated as “CPI inflation General, … on year‑on‑year basis” or the YoY table’s “General” row.

Clarifications:
- “General CPI” means the overall CPI at the National level; Urban‑only or Rural‑only figures do not count.
- Use the exact percentage as PBS reports (do not recalculate). If multiple values appear due to rounding differences, take the figure in the YoY table’s “General” row. If a press release and monthly review both exist and disagree, the press release takes precedence.
- Base year and methodology: PBS compiles CPI on Base Year 2015‑16; National CPI is a weighted average of Urban and Rural CPI.
- Timing: Evaluate sources as of 2025‑12‑31 23:59:59 UTC. Any revisions published after this cutoff are ignored for resolution.
- Start date and scope: The question pertains solely to the YoY General CPI for the month of November 2025 (November 2025 over November 2024) as reported by PBS; other months or metrics are out of scope.

Outcome:
- YES: PBS reports YoY General CPI for November 2025 ≥ 3.8%.
- NO: PBS reports YoY General CPI for November 2025 < 3.8%.

question: Will Rotterdam advertise a bid or award a contract for Water District No. 5 transmission main (“Phase 3”) replacement by Dec 31, 2025?
background:
Context as of Sep 30, 2025:
- Rotterdam (Schenectady County, NY) is executing a multi-phase Water District No. 5 (WD5) Comprehensive Water System Improvement Project funded in part by a $34 million authorization (Bond Resolution 268.22; capital project line H134 established Mar 12, 2025).
- In August 2025, the Town Board awarded “Water District No. 5 Water System Improvements – Contract No. 2 – Valve & Hydrant Replacement” to Birdsall Excavation and Construction, LLC, for an amount not to exceed $1,016,746, per the Aug 13, 2025 agenda/resolution materials. Local reporting likewise described the contract’s scope (hydrant and valve replacements) and timing, and noted that a third phase would involve replacing transmission lines that could be put out to bid later in 2025.
- Earlier in 2025, WD5 work also included leak detection survey activities (Phases 3, 4, and 5 of the leak survey, not construction) and various bid calls for related equipment/supplies; Town procurement notices are typically posted to the Town’s official newspaper and to the Empire State Purchasing Group on BidNet (bidnetdirect.com/townofrotterdam). Many New York public entities also post solicitations to the New York State Contract Reporter (NYSCR), the state’s official procurement opportunity website.

Why this question: The Town has publicly indicated interest in moving a third phase focused on WD5 transmission main (“transmission line”) replacement to bidding later in 2025, but timing and funding logistics were not guaranteed, creating genuine uncertainty while being objectively checkable via official postings or a contract award. This question targets that clear procurement milestone.

Key status points for forecasters:
- Funding framework in place (capital line H134; prior $34M authorization).
- Recent award covered hydrant/valve replacements (not transmission mains).
- Town has established channels for bid advertising (official newspaper; BidNet) and could also use NYSCR.
resolution_criteria:
This resolves Yes if, between 00:00:00 ET on Jan 1, 2025 and 23:59:59 ET on Dec 31, 2025, ANY of the following occurs:
1) Bid advertised: An official, public bid advertisement/solicitation is published by the Town of Rotterdam (or its authorized agent) that explicitly identifies both (a) Water District No. 5 (WD5) and (b) transmission main work, using any of the following accepted terms in the title or scope: “transmission main,” “transmission line” (in the context of water mains), or “trunk main” replacement. Publication venues that qualify include any of the following:
   - The Town’s procurement postings on the Empire State Purchasing Group (BidNet: bidnetdirect.com/townofrotterdam) or the Town’s official website; or
   - The Town’s official newspaper public notice; or
   - The New York State Contract Reporter (NYSCR).

2) Contract award: The Rotterdam Town Board adopts and publicly posts a resolution awarding a construction contract whose title or scope explicitly identifies both (a) Water District No. 5 and (b) transmission main work, with accepted terms as above, and the adopted resolution, agenda, minutes, or resolution text is published on the Town’s official website.

Definitions and clarifications:
- Water District No. 5 (WD5): The Town of Rotterdam’s WD5 service area as used in Town Board resolutions and project documentation.
- Transmission main/line/trunk main (for purposes of this question): Any bid or award document text that uses these terms to denote large-diameter water mains conveying water within WD5. To prevent ambiguity, the document itself must include the term(s) “transmission main,” “transmission line” (water), or “trunk main” in its title or scope statement.
- Advertise a bid/solicitation: Publicly post the invitation to bid with scope, instructions, and due date on one of the qualifying venues listed above (Town website/BidNet, official newspaper, or NYSCR).
- Award a contract: Adoption by the Rotterdam Town Board of a resolution that accepts and awards a construction contract meeting the WD5 transmission main scope as defined above, evidenced by published agendas, minutes, or resolutions on the Town’s website (as with the Aug 13, 2025 contract award for hydrant/valve work).

What does not count:
- Postings or awards for design-only or consulting work (e.g., preliminary engineering reports, studies) without a construction scope focused on transmission main replacement.
- Work limited to hydrants, valves, leak detection, general maintenance, materials-only procurements, or tank siting that does not explicitly include WD5 transmission main replacement.

Primary resolution sources (any one is sufficient):
- Town of Rotterdam official postings: Town Board agendas, minutes, or resolutions; Town procurement postings on BidNet (bidnetdirect.com/townofrotterdam). Examples of such documents are captured in prior Town agendas/resolutions.
- NYS Contract Reporter posting if used by the Town.
- Reputable local media (e.g., The Daily Gazette) may be used for corroboration, but in case of discrepancy, official Town documents will govern.

If none of the qualifying advertisements or awards occur within the period, resolve No.

Time zone: All times Eastern Time (ET).

question: Between 2025-10-15 and 2025-12-31 (UTC), will the European Commission adopt any formal State aid decision under Council Regulation (EU) 2015/1589 concerning Hungary’s Paks II project?
background:
Context and status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- What is Paks II? Paks II refers to Hungary’s project to add two new nuclear power reactor units (commonly described as VVER‑1200 Generation III+ units, Units 5 and 6) at the existing Paks Nuclear Power Plant site. The beneficiary entity is MVM Paks II (Paks II Nuclear Power Plant Development Private Company Limited by Shares). Key features, including technology type, ownership/beneficiary, and financing arrangements, are described in the European Commission’s 2017 state‑aid decision and general descriptions of the plant and expansion.
- Prior Commission decision: On 6 March 2017, the European Commission adopted Commission Decision (EU) 2017/2112 in State aid case SA.38454, approving investment aid that Hungary intended to grant for the development of two new reactors at the Paks II nuclear power station.
- Court annulment in 2025: On 11 September 2025, the Court of Justice of the European Union, in Case C‑59/23 (Austria v Commission, Paks II), set aside the General Court’s prior judgment and annulled the Commission’s 2017 decision approving the aid. The Court held that the Commission could not confine itself to state‑aid compatibility but also had to ascertain whether the direct award of the construction contract complied with EU public‑procurement rules; it also found the Commission’s reasoning insufficient on that point. This judgment removes the legal effect of the 2017 approval and implies that any future Commission decision on the aid would need to address procurement‑law compliance in a reasoned manner.
- How Commission state‑aid decisions are defined and published: Under Council Regulation (EU) 2015/1589, the Commission adopts formal “decisions” at various stages: (i) Article 4(2) (decision that a notified measure does not constitute aid); (ii) Article 4(3) (decision not to raise objections—compatibility at preliminary stage); (iii) Article 4(4) (decision to initiate the formal investigation procedure); and (iv) Article 9(2)–(5) (decisions closing the formal investigation: no‑aid finding; positive/conditional decision; negative decision). Decisions to open or close the formal investigation are published in the Official Journal, and summary notices are published for certain Article 4 decisions; publication rules and timelines are set out in Article 32 of Regulation 2015/1589.
- Where decisions are announced/tracked: The Commission regularly communicates the adoption of state‑aid decisions via official press releases (e.g., its “State aid latest news” page), which list dated entries for adopted decisions and describe the measure, Member State, and decision type. Formal texts of decisions are published on EUR‑Lex and/or in the Official Journal (example: Decision (EU) 2017/2112 for SA.38454).

Key definitions for this question:
- “Paks II project” means the Hungarian measure to support the development of two new nuclear reactor units at the Paks site, as described in the Commission’s 2017 decision in case SA.38454 and general references to the expansion project (including references to “Paks II,” “MVM Paks II,” “Paks II Nuclear Power Plant Development Private Company Limited by Shares,” “Units 5 and 6,” and “VVER‑1200” reactors).
- “European Commission decision” means a formal act adopted by the European Commission under Council Regulation (EU) 2015/1589 in a state‑aid procedure. For the purposes of this market question, qualifying decisions are limited to: Article 4(2) decisions (no aid), Article 4(3) decisions (no objections), Article 4(4) decisions (to initiate the formal investigation), and Article 9(2)–(5) decisions (closing the formal investigation: no‑aid, positive, conditional, or negative decisions). Decisions outside these provisions (e.g., information injunctions, suspension/recovery injunctions, or other procedural steps) do not qualify.
- “New” in this question explicitly excludes the 6 March 2017 Commission Decision (EU) 2017/2112 and requires an adoption date within the question’s observation window.
- “Adopt” refers to the formal adoption by the Commission (College) of one of the qualifying decision types above; for resolution, the adoption date will be the date stated in the Commission’s decision text or, if not yet available there, the adoption date stated in an official Commission press release.

Why this is forecast‑relevant now: The 2017 approval has been annulled by the EU’s top court, creating a need—and uncertainty—around if and when the Commission will adopt a fresh state‑aid decision on Paks II. The Commission could, for example, (i) re‑open the case via a new Article 4(4) decision, (ii) issue a new no‑objections decision under Article 4(3), or (iii) adopt a decision closing a formal investigation under Article 9—any of which would qualify under this market question. The timing between mid‑October and end‑December 2025 is uncertain given procedural, evidentiary, and political considerations.
resolution_criteria:
Question: Between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, will the European Commission adopt any qualifying state‑aid “decision” concerning Hungary’s Paks II project as defined below?

Eligible decisions (must be “new,” i.e., not Decision (EU) 2017/2112):
- A decision under Article 4(2) (no aid), Article 4(3) (no objections), or Article 4(4) (to initiate the formal investigation) of Council Regulation (EU) 2015/1589; or
- Any decision closing the formal investigation under Article 9(2)–(5) of Regulation (EU) 2015/1589 (no‑aid decision; positive decision; conditional decision; negative decision).

Scope and identification of the case:
- The decision must clearly concern the Paks II project (as defined), whether under State aid case SA.38454 or any successor SA case number that explicitly refers to the Paks II nuclear expansion, MVM Paks II, and/or Units 5 and 6 at Paks.

Evidence required for resolution (any one is sufficient):
1) An official European Commission press release (e.g., on the Commission “State aid latest news” page or Press Corner) stating that the Commission has adopted a qualifying decision concerning Paks II, with an adoption date within the observation window.
2) An EUR‑Lex/Official Journal entry showing a Commission decision concerning Paks II (as defined) and stating an adoption date within the observation window (the EUR‑Lex entry for Decision (EU) 2017/2112 is provided here as an example of such a listing, but that 2017 decision is excluded by definition).

Adoption date and time zone:
- If sources disagree, the adoption date printed inside the Commission decision text (EUR‑Lex/Official Journal) prevails over any press release date. If only a press release is available by 2025‑12‑31, its stated adoption date is used. All date/time references are in UTC.

Exclusions (do not count as qualifying decisions):
- Procedural acts outside Articles 4(2)–(4) and 9(2)–(5), including information requests, injunctions (e.g., suspension/recovery), or other non‑decision procedural steps.
- The original Commission Decision (EU) 2017/2112 of 6 March 2017 (outside the window and specifically excluded).

Resolution:
- Resolve “Yes” if at least one qualifying decision concerning Paks II is adopted within the observation window and evidenced as above. Resolve “No” otherwise.

Notes and references for resolvers:
- Background facts about Paks II and the 2017 Commission approval are in Decision (EU) 2017/2112 (SA.38454)  and general descriptions of the Paks plant/expansion.
- The CJEU judgment annulling the 2017 decision (Case C‑59/23, 11 Sep 2025) is summarized with key holdings affecting future Commission action.
- Decision typology and publication rules are defined in Regulation (EU) 2015/1589.
- Commission state‑aid decisions are routinely communicated via dated press releases on the “State aid latest news” page, suitable for timely resolution checks.

question: Will U.S. “general imports” (customs value) of HS heading 4202 from France in October 2025 be at least 10% lower year-over-year?
background:
Status quo and context as of September 30, 2025:

- What is HS heading 4202? HS (Harmonized System) codes are internationally standardized at 6 digits, with countries often extending them to 8–10 digits for national use. HS heading 4202 covers trunks, suitcases, handbags, traveling bags and similar containers; the heading scope and an Additional U.S. Note defining “travel, sports and similar bags” are specified in Chapter 42 of the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS).
- What is measured here? The U.S. Census Bureau’s trade statistics define “Customs value” and “General imports.” Customs value is the value of imports as appraised by U.S. Customs and Border Protection under the Tariff Act of 1930—generally the price actually paid or payable for the merchandise, excluding U.S. import duties, freight, insurance, and other charges to bring the goods to the U.S.. “General imports” measure total physical arrivals of merchandise from foreign countries, whether entering consumption channels immediately or being entered into bonded warehouses or Foreign Trade Zones.
- Data availability and release timing: The FT900 “U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services” press release schedule lists October 2025 data as releasing on December 4, 2025 at 8:30 a.m. Eastern, ensuring availability before year-end. The Census International Trade API provides Monthly International Trade Datasets (MITD) for HS-based imports, including variables GEN_VAL_MO (General imports, total value), CTY_CODE/CTY_NAME, I_COMMODITY (HS code), COMM_LVL (aggregation level), and a time parameter; datasets are updated with the most recent month after the FT900 morning release. France’s Schedule C country code in Census trade data is 4279 (ISO code FR).
- Recent figures: From the Census International Trade API, France’s General imports (customs value) of HS 4202 in October 2024 were 129,527,936 (GEN_VAL_MO). As of the latest available month (July 2025), the value was 117,736,516.
- Macro backdrop: On July 27, 2025, the U.S. and EU announced a framework deal imposing a broad 15% tariff on most EU goods, replacing a previously threatened higher rate; implementation timing aligned with August 2025 start, affecting EU exporters, with sectoral impacts under discussion. Bain & Company’s June 19, 2025 luxury outlook projected a continued slip in personal luxury goods in 2025, with a full-year contraction of roughly 2–5% amid economic headwinds and weakening pricing power.

Why this question is non-trivial: October is a key shipping month for holiday retail, tariffs may reduce flows or shift sourcing, and luxury demand has softened—yet brands could mitigate via pricing, inventory balancing, or customs strategies. The threshold (≥10% YoY decline) appears plausible either way given recent data and policy changes.

Key definitions and references:
- HS heading 4202 scope: see HTSUS Chapter 42 description and note ; HS structure overview.
- Customs value and General imports definitions: U.S. Census foreign trade reference.
- Schedule C country code for France: 4279; ISO FR.
- Release timing for October 2025 data: FT900 schedule (December 4, 2025, 8:30 a.m. Eastern).
- Census International Trade API variables and update cadence: Guide to International Trade Datasets.

Helpful data source links (for forecasters):
- FT900 release schedule: https://www.census.gov/foreign-trade/schedule.html 
- Census International Trade API HS imports variables: https://api.census.gov/data/timeseries/intltrade/imports/hs/variables.html 
- HS 4202 description (HTSUS, Ch.42 archival reference): https://www.usitc.gov/tata/hts/archive/9200/920c420.pdf 
- Harmonized System overview: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harmonized_System 
- Country code list (France 4279): https://www.census.gov/foreign-trade/schedules/c/countryname.html 

Current benchmark values (from Census API):
- October 2024: GEN_VAL_MO = 129,527,936 (France, HS4=4202) 
- July 2025: GEN_VAL_MO = 117,736,516 (France, HS4=4202)
resolution_criteria:
Question: Will the U.S. “general imports” (customs value) of HS heading 4202 from France in October 2025 be at least 10% lower than October 2024?

Measured item:
- Series: Census International Trade API, Monthly HS imports endpoint: https://api.census.gov/data/timeseries/intltrade/imports/hs 
- Variables: GEN_VAL_MO (General imports, total value), CTY_CODE/CTY_NAME, I_COMMODITY (HS code), COMM_LVL, MONTH, YEAR (or time) 
- Filters: I_COMMODITY=4202, COMM_LVL=HS4, CTY_CODE=4279 (France) 
- Definitions applied:
  - “Customs value” and “General imports” per U.S. Census definitions.
  - HS heading “4202” scope per HTSUS (handbags, travel goods, similar containers) ; HS code structure per HS overview.

Timeframe and timezone:
- Target months: October 2024 (baseline) and October 2025 (evaluation). Use the API “time” parameter values 2024-10 and 2025-10, respectively.
- Resolution will use the first official values published in the API after the FT900 October 2025 release at 8:30 a.m. Eastern on December 4, 2025; values available no later than 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025 will be considered.

Computation:
- Let V2024 = GEN_VAL_MO for I_COMMODITY=4202, COMM_LVL=HS4, CTY_CODE=4279, time=2024-10.
- Let V2025 = GEN_VAL_MO for I_COMMODITY=4202, COMM_LVL=HS4, CTY_CODE=4279, time=2025-10.
- Compute YoY% = ((V2025 − V2024) / V2024) × 100.

Resolution:
- Resolve Yes if YoY% ≤ −10.0000% (i.e., V2025 is at least 10% lower than V2024). Resolve No otherwise.

How to retrieve:
- Example API calls (JSON):
  - Baseline: https://api.census.gov/data/timeseries/intltrade/imports/hs?get=CTY_CODE,CTY_NAME,GEN_VAL_MO,MONTH,YEAR,I_COMMODITY,COMM_LVL&time=2024-10&COMM_LVL=HS4&I_COMMODITY=4202&CTY_CODE=4279 
  - Evaluation: https://api.census.gov/data/timeseries/intltrade/imports/hs?get=CTY_CODE,CTY_NAME,GEN_VAL_MO,MONTH,YEAR,I_COMMODITY,COMM_LVL&time=2025-10&COMM_LVL=HS4&I_COMMODITY=4202&CTY_CODE=4279 
- If the API is temporarily unavailable, resolution may be made using the same dataset accessed via USA Trade Online (the Census interface) after the October 2025 FT900 release; but the primary resolution source is the API endpoint above.

Documentation:
- The resolver will record V2024, V2025, the computed YoY%, the exact API responses (or screenshots from USA Trade Online), the date/time of retrieval, and the FT900 release reference.

Notes:
- This question uses “General imports” (not “Imports for consumption”) and “Customs value” (not CIF value), per Census definitions.
- France is identified by CTY_CODE 4279 per Schedule C.
- HS heading 4202 includes handbags, travel goods, and similar containers; this forecast concerns the aggregated HS4 level (all HS6/HS10 under 4202).
- Rationale for uncertainty: The July 2025 value (117,736,516) vs October 2024 (129,527,936) indicates a recent decline ahead of tariff effects, but October flows may be influenced by holiday-season shipping, pricing adjustments, and sourcing shifts, making ≥10% YoY decline plausible but uncertain.

question: Between 00:00 UTC Oct 15 and 23:59 UTC Dec 31, 2025, will Russia or Belarus publish a signed intergovernmental document that explicitly sets a timeline or staged plan to establish a “common gas market” of the Union State?
background:
Context as of Sep 30, 2025:
- What is the Union State: The Union State of Russia and Belarus is a supranational union aimed at deeper economic and defense integration between the two countries.
- Recent energy integration milestone: On Dec 6, 2024, Russia and Belarus signed the Treaty on the Unified Electricity Market of the Union State at a Supreme State Council meeting in the Kremlin. This is frequently cited by leaders as the starting point for broader energy market integration.
- Leaders’ statements on next steps: On Sep 15, 2025, President Alexander Lukashenko said the signed electricity market agreement is only the beginning and that the Union State must “move further: create a common gas market, establish unified rules for the oil market, ensure fair prices… and equal operating conditions” for entities in both countries. He did not set concrete deadlines in those remarks.
- Gas supply vs. market integration: On Sep 26, 2025, Putin and Lukashenko held talks in Moscow; their published readout discussed Belarus’s nuclear plant reducing gas demand but continued gas purchases from Gazprom, with no mention of a common gas market document or timeline. News reports the same day noted a five-year gas supply deal replacing short-term arrangements, without detailing a Union State common gas market framework.
Why this question: Leaders have publicly prioritized moving from a unified electricity market toward a common gas market, but as of mid-Sep 2025, there were no public, signed, time-bound roadmaps or intergovernmental acts initiating such a gas market framework. Whether a formal document will be adopted and published by year-end is policy-contingent and uncertain.
Key definitions and scope:
- Union State: As defined above.
- “Common gas market” (English) / “single gas market” is interpreted as the establishment of a unified market framework for natural gas trade, transmission/access, pricing methodology, and/or market operation across Russia and Belarus under the Union State. For unambiguous resolution, the qualifying document must explicitly refer to a Union State “common gas market” (accepted terms in Russian: “единый рынок газа” and/or “единый газовый рынок”, or Belarusian equivalents) in the context of the Union State. If the document refers to a “common energy market” without specifically naming gas, it does not qualify.
- “Intergovernmental document” means a treaty, agreement, protocol, program, action plan, or roadmap formally adopted and signed by authorized representatives of Russia and/or Belarus in the Union State context (e.g., documents akin to the Dec 6, 2024 Unified Electricity Market treaty ).
- “Roadmap” means an official, signed plan that sets out steps with at least one date-bound milestone or staged implementation timeline. Mere statements of intent without dates do not count.
- “Published” means the full text or a scan of the signed document is made publicly available on an official government or Union State website.
Examples of official publication sources (non-exhaustive):
- Russia: en.kremlin.ru; government.ru; minenergo.gov.ru; official site of the Union State Standing Committee (xn--c1anggbdpdf.xn--p1ai/en/).
- Belarus: president.gov.by; government.by; energy.gov.by (or the Belarus Ministry of Energy’s current official domain); the Union State information portal soyuz.by.
Notes:
- A bilateral gas supply contract (prices/volumes) without an explicit Union State “common gas market” framework and dated milestones does not qualify.
- Drafts, unsigned communiqués, and speeches do not qualify.
resolution_criteria:
Time window for eligible documents: 00:00:00 UTC on Oct 15, 2025 through 23:59:59 UTC on Dec 31, 2025.
Primary resolution rule (Yes): Resolve Yes if, during the time window, an official Russian, Belarusian, or Union State site publishes a signed intergovernmental document (treaty/agreement/protocol/program/action plan/roadmap) that:
1) Explicitly refers to establishing a Union State “common gas market” (accepted terms include: English “common gas market” or Russian “единый рынок газа/единый газовый рынок”; Belarusian equivalents are also acceptable) in the Union State context; and
2) Sets a timeline or staged implementation plan (i.e., includes at least one dated milestone or phase) toward creating that market.
Secondary rule (language): The document may be in Russian, Belarusian, or English; the presence of the accepted term in any of these languages and the Union State context is required.
