Publication requirement: The full text or a scanned copy must be publicly accessible on an official government or Union State website (examples: en.kremlin.ru; government.ru; minenergo.gov.ru; president.gov.by; government.by; Belarus Ministry of Energy’s official domain; Union State Standing Committee official site xn--c1anggbdpdf.xn--p1ai/en/; soyuz.by). If multiple official sources publish the same document, any one suffices.
Exclusions (Resolve No):
- Documents signed outside the time window (before Oct 15, 2025 or after Dec 31, 2025).
- Documents that discuss energy integration generally or “common energy market” but do not explicitly name the Union State “common gas market.”
- Documents lacking any dated milestones or staged implementation timeline (i.e., pure statements of intent).
- Pure gas supply contracts (pricing/volumes) without the Union State common gas market framework/timeline.
- Speeches, interviews, or press releases without a signed document.
Verification steps for resolvers:
- Check the official portals listed above for publications between Oct 15 and Dec 31, 2025.
- Confirm the document is signed and identifies the Union State “common gas market” explicitly, and that it includes at least one date-bound milestone or staged plan.
- If conflicting reports exist, prioritize the text of the signed document on official sites over media reports.
- For background on prior energy integration and the Union State, see.

question: Will the SQM–Codelco Salar de Atacama partnership reach final closing between Oct 15 and Dec 31, 2025?
background:
Status quo and key facts as of October 1, 2025:
- On September 22, 2025, Chile’s development agency CORFO submitted the terms of a modified lease with SQM through 2030 and a new 2031–2060 lease for the SQM–Codelco joint venture to Chile’s Comptroller General; Reuters reported that “the approval of Chinese antitrust regulators” remained “the last condition to finalize the deal,” with the parties expected to finalize the partnership in 2025.
- Chile’s competition authority (Fiscalía Nacional Económica, FNE) approved the SQM–Codelco association in April 2025, in Phase 1 and subject to mitigation measures; Codelco’s April 24 press release noted this approval and highlighted remaining steps including indigenous consultation led by CORFO and authorizations from the Chilean Nuclear Energy Commission (CCHEN). The release added that most international antitrust approvals had been obtained and that China was the only remaining international antitrust approval at that time.
- The partnership’s official site outlines prerequisites/conditions precedent and milestones for effectiveness, including: indigenous consultation run by CORFO; authorizations from CCHEN; approval by the Comptroller General of the Republic to formalize the contracts; and antitrust approvals in Chile and abroad. It also specifies that the association becomes effective once all legal, technical, environmental, and consultation requirements are met, after which operations were intended to begin in 2025.
- Definitions of key terms and authorities:
  • Joint venture (JV): a business entity formed by two or more parties with shared ownership, returns/risks, and governance.
  • China’s antitrust regulator: the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), a ministerial-level agency under China’s State Council responsible for market supervision and antitrust enforcement; “Chinese antitrust approval” refers to SAMR clearing the transaction (with or without remedies).
  • Chile Standard Time (CLST) in late 2025 is UTC−03:00. This offset applies from the Sunday after the first Saturday of September 2025 until the Sunday after the first Saturday of April 2026.

What remains uncertain: As of late September 2025, the key unresolved condition reported publicly was SAMR’s antitrust clearance. Domestic non-antitrust approvals and procedural steps (indigenous consultation, CCHEN authorizations, Comptroller authorization and formalization of contracts) were also cited by official and partnership sources as conditions precedent to effectiveness.

Useful sources for resolution checking:
- Official press releases and investor communications from Codelco (newsroom), SQM (newsroom/investor relations), CORFO, and the partnership site (https://acuerdocodelcosqm.cl/).
- Chile’s competition authority (FNE) decision page (for context on the JV approval already granted) and any subsequent monitoring/enforcement notes.
- Credible wire services (e.g., Reuters) reporting on closing or SAMR clearance.
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves to Yes if, between 00:00 CLST (UTC−03:00) on October 15, 2025, and 23:59 CLST (UTC−03:00) on December 31, 2025, at least one of the following occurs and can be independently verified:

A) An official announcement by Codelco, SQM, and/or CORFO states that “closing” (or “final closing,” “consummation,” “effectiveness,” “entry into force,” or equivalent) of the SQM–Codelco Salar de Atacama partnership has occurred, and that all conditions precedent have been satisfied, such that the definitive agreements governing the modified 2025–2030 lease and the 2031–2060 JV/lease are in effect, and the association/JV has been materialized (e.g., via the merger of subsidiaries Minera Tarar and SQM Salar as contemplated).

B) Authoritative regulatory or contractual evidence indicates that closing/effectiveness has occurred, including BOTH:
   1) Publication/confirmation of SAMR’s antitrust clearance for the transaction (approval with or without remedies counts as approval) , AND
   2) Confirmation that Chilean non-antitrust conditions cited by official sources are met (indigenous consultation completion by CORFO, CCHEN authorizations, and authorization/registration by the Comptroller General to formalize the contracts), with the partnership declared effective per an official source.

Resolution sources and verification hierarchy:
- Primary: Official press releases or filings by Codelco, SQM, CORFO, or the partnership site (acuerdocodelcosqm.cl). If multiple official sources conflict, prefer the most recent formal filing/press release and corroborate with regulator notices where applicable.
- Secondary: Credible wire services (e.g., Reuters) directly reporting that closing has occurred or that all conditions precedent have been satisfied (including SAMR approval).

If no eligible closing/effectiveness is publicly confirmed by 23:59 CLST on December 31, 2025 (02:59 UTC on January 1, 2026), resolve No.

Clarifications and definitions for unambiguous resolution:
- “Closing/effectiveness” means the point at which the definitive agreements for the SQM–Codelco Salar de Atacama partnership become legally effective and enforceable, following satisfaction of conditions precedent identified by the parties and official sources (including but not limited to SAMR clearance, CCHEN authorizations, Comptroller authorization/formalization, and completion of CORFO-led indigenous consultation).
- “Chinese antitrust approval” refers specifically to clearance by China’s State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) under China’s Anti-Monopoly Law; approval may be unconditional or conditional (with remedies) and both count as approval.
- “Joint venture (JV)” is used in the ordinary corporate sense of a jointly owned entity with shared governance, risks, and returns.
- Time window and timezone: Eligible events must occur between 00:00 CLST (UTC−03:00) on October 15, 2025, and 23:59 CLST (UTC−03:00) on December 31, 2025; this corresponds to 03:00 UTC on October 15, 2025, through 02:59 UTC on January 1, 2026.

Edge cases:
- If SAMR clears the deal but the parties have not declared closing/effectiveness and any Chilean condition precedent cited by official sources remains unmet by the deadline, resolve No.
- If the parties declare closing/effectiveness but subsequent credible reporting or official regulator statements within the window indicate a material unsatisfied condition (e.g., SAMR has not cleared, or Comptroller authorization has not been granted), do not resolve Yes unless the deficiency is cured within the window; otherwise resolve No.

question: Italy BEV share: Will battery-electric vehicles be at least 6.5% of new passenger-car registrations in Italy in November 2025?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30:
- Italy’s battery-electric vehicle (BEV) market share has been volatile in 2025, with UNRAE reporting 4.9% BEV share in July 2025 (118,493 total passenger-car registrations; BEV down from 6.0% in June) and 4.9% in August 2025, with a year-to-date BEV share of 5.2% through August. UNRAE attributed market softness and delayed EV purchases partly to pending incentives that were announced but not yet operational as of early September 2025, which “froze the market” while buyers waited.
- UNRAE publishes monthly Italian passenger-car (autovetture) registration datasets, including breakdowns by “alimentazione” (powertrain) in the Struttura del mercato tables and model rankings. These datasets typically post on or about the first day of the following month and include BEV as a distinct category with both volumes and share (“quota %”) for the month and year-to-date.
- As a separate official source, the Italian Ministry’s “Il Portale dell’Automobilista” provides monthly statistics on passenger-car registrations with filters by fuel type (including electric), with complete statistics for the previous month available from the second working day of the current month.

Definitions and scope for this question:
- Battery-electric vehicle (BEV): A road vehicle powered solely by one or more electric motors using energy stored in rechargeable batteries; no internal combustion engine. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battery_electric_vehicle.
- Passenger-car registrations (“immatricolazioni di autovetture”): First registrations of passenger cars (autovetture) in Italy during the calendar month. For our primary source (UNRAE), this refers to autovetture (passenger cars) as reported in UNRAE’s Struttura del mercato datasets. See general concept of vehicle registration: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_registration.
- BEV share (for November 2025): The percentage equal to 100 × (BEV autovetture registrations in November 2025) ÷ (total autovetture registrations in November 2025). If UNRAE publishes a “quota %” for Elettriche (BEV) for November 2025, that figure is the primary value used; otherwise compute from the published monthly volumes.
- Timezone and period: November 2025 refers to registrations dated from 2025-11-01 00:00:00 to 2025-11-30 23:59:59 Europe/Rome (CET, UTC+1). Data are taken as published by the resolution sources for the month of November 2025.
- Scope exclusions: Commercial vehicles, industrial vehicles, motorcycles, and other vehicle types not classified as autovetture are excluded; plug-in hybrids (PHEV) and other electrified but non-BEV powertrains do not count toward BEV.

Why this threshold: Recent monthly BEV shares have hovered around ~5% with a June spike to 6.0% and policy changes potentially affecting year-end demand. A 6.5% threshold sits above recent monthly levels but within plausible reach if incentives or year-end deliveries lift BEV uptake, creating meaningful uncertainty for forecasters.
resolution_criteria:
Primary source and computation:
- Use UNRAE’s official “Immatricolazioni” page to access the November 2025 autovetture Struttura del mercato dataset (Per alimentazione). Expected publication is around December 1, 2025. Verify that “Elettriche (BEV)” appears as a category with volumes and “quota %” for November 2025.
- If the November 2025 Struttura del mercato table includes a BEV “quota %” for the month, resolve using that percentage. Otherwise, compute BEV share as: 100 × (BEV autovetture registrations for November 2025) ÷ (total autovetture autovetture registrations for November 2025) using the same UNRAE document’s monthly volumes. Use at least two decimal places in the calculation and compare to the 6.5% threshold without rounding.

Fallback source (if UNRAE November 2025 autovetture data are not available by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC):
- Use the Italian Ministry’s Il Portale dell’Automobilista statistics page. Select autovetture and filter by month (November 2025) and by “Alimentazione” to obtain (a) total autovetture registrations in November 2025 and (b) BEV/electric autovetture registrations in November 2025. Compute BEV share as above. Complete statistics for the previous month are available from the second working day of the current month, so November 2025 should be available by early December 2025. If both UNRAE and the Ministry’s portal are available and disagree, prefer UNRAE.

Resolution rule:
- Resolve Yes if the November 2025 BEV share (as defined above) is ≥ 6.5%; resolve No otherwise.

Timing and revisions:
- Use the latest official figures published on the source pages as of 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. If UNRAE revises November 2025 data before that cutoff, use the latest revision; disregard revisions published after the cutoff.

Source navigation links (for human verifier):
- UNRAE Immatricolazioni (monthly datasets, including Struttura del mercato and Per alimentazione): https://unrae.it/dati-statistici/immatricolazioni. Example of Struttura del mercato format with “Per alimentazione” and BEV category: April 2025 PDF structure.
- UNRAE press releases providing recent context and typical publication cadence: July 2025 market shares (BEV 4.9%; 118,493 registrations) ; August 2025 market (BEV 4.9%; YTD BEV 5.2%; incentive commentary; published Sep 1, 2025).
- Ministry portal statistics and timing: https://www.ilportaledellautomobilista.it/web/portale-automobilista/statistiche-immatricolazioni-autovetture (complete stats available from the second working day of the current month).

question: Will India’s PMD all‑India average retail onion price be at least ₹40/kg on any calendar day between 2025-10-15 and 2025-11-15 (IST)?
background:
Context and status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- India’s Department of Consumer Affairs’ Price Monitoring Division (PMD) monitors daily retail and wholesale prices for essential commodities and publishes them on its website; onions are among the monitored items. PMD’s reporting network has expanded over time and uses cross‑verification with FCI and NAFED to validate daily prices.
- A publicly described onion retail price dataset historically referenced 75 market centres; PMD’s scope has since expanded substantially, and current daily prices are reported on the PMD website.
- As a price‑stabilization measure ahead of the festive season, the Government of India launched subsidised retail sales of onions at ₹24/kg via NCCF/NAFED mobile vans on 2025‑09‑04 in cities including Delhi, Mumbai, and Ahmedabad, with the stated goal of keeping food inflation in check.
- For daily figures, PMD provides “Daily Prices”, “Daily Summary”, and “Daily Retail & Wholesale Prices” report pages on its official dashboard (fcainfoweb.nic.in), which are used by forecasters to see the “All India Average Retail Price (₹/Kg)” by commodity and date.

Why this question has non‑trivial uncertainty:
- The government’s calibrated interventions at ₹24/kg aim to dampen prices, while seasonal supply dynamics (harvest cycles, storage, logistics) can still induce short‑term spikes. The outcome between the Diwali window (mid‑Oct to mid‑Nov) is plausibly neither obviously below nor above ₹40/kg, creating genuine forecasting uncertainty.

Key term references for clarity:
- Onion: the common bulb onion, scientific name Allium cepa, widely used as a culinary vegetable.
- Currency: the Indian rupee (INR), symbol ₹, official currency of India.
- Time zone: Indian Standard Time (IST) is UTC+05:30; India does not observe daylight saving time.
- PMD reporting: PMD monitors daily prices and publishes them on its website; onions are covered. The Department’s “Price Monitoring” page lists “Daily Prices” and “Daily Summary” dashboards on fcainfoweb.nic.in.
resolution_criteria:
Resolution window and time zone:
- Eligible dates are calendar days from 2025‑10‑15 00:00 to 2025‑11‑15 23:59, Indian Standard Time (IST; UTC+05:30). A “calendar day” means the 24‑hour period from 00:00 to 23:59 IST on the labeled date.

What counts for resolution:
- Resolve Yes if, on any eligible calendar day, the Department of Consumer Affairs Price Monitoring Division’s (PMD) official dashboard displays an All India Average Retail Price for Onion with unit “1 Kg” that is greater than or equal to ₹40.00 (forty rupees per kilogram). Resolve No otherwise.

Definitions and measurement details:
- Onion: refers to the common bulb onion, Allium cepa.
- Unit: 1 kilogram (kg), as labeled on PMD commodity tables.
- Currency: ₹ (Indian rupee).
- “All India Average Retail Price (₹/Kg)”: the exact value published by PMD on its official daily price report pages for the commodity “Onion” and unit “1 Kg”. No transformations or external averaging are applied—the resolver uses the value as displayed by PMD for the relevant date.
- Date attribution: Use PMD’s own date label for the daily report (e.g., “As on <date>” or “Date: <dd/mm/yyyy>”). A day qualifies if its PMD‑labeled date falls within 2025‑10‑15 to 2025‑11‑15 (inclusive).

Primary sources of truth:
- PMD official dashboard pages on fcainfoweb.nic.in that show daily all‑India average retail prices by commodity and date. The Department’s “Price Monitoring” page lists the authoritative links: Daily Prices (commodity‑wise), Daily Summary, and Daily Retail & Wholesale Prices. PMD’s mandate to publish daily prices is described by the Department.

Source precedence and tie‑breaking:
- If multiple PMD official pages display differing all‑India average retail prices for Onion (1 Kg) for the same date, the value shown on the “Daily Prices” commodity‑wise page (the page titled “Daily Average Retail Prices of Essential Commodities”) will prevail for resolution.

Exclusions and clarifications:
- Intraday market movements, city‑level prices, wholesale prices, or any non‑PMD sources do not affect resolution. Only PMD’s published all‑India average retail price for Onion (1 Kg) counts.
- Rounding: Use the value as displayed by PMD. If PMD shows decimals, the threshold comparison is against the displayed number (e.g., 39.99 is below threshold; 40.00 or higher meets threshold).

How a resolver will decide quickly:
1) Navigate to the Department’s Price Monitoring page and follow the links to the PMD dashboard (fcainfoweb.nic.in) to access “Daily Prices” or “Daily Summary”.
2) Locate Onion (1 Kg) in the All India Average Retail Price tables and review the values for dates 2025‑10‑15 through 2025‑11‑15 (IST).
3) If any date’s value is ≥ ₹40.00, resolve Yes; if none are, resolve No.

Supporting context:
- PMD’s daily monitoring, expanded reporting network, and cross‑verification with FCI/NAFED underpin the reliability of the daily all‑India average figures.
- Government interventions at ₹24/kg during Sept 2025 underscore active price management ahead of the festive season, a factor forecasters may weigh when forming probabilities.

question: Will Nigeria’s year-on-year headline inflation rate for November 2025 be at or below 19.5%, as reported by the National Bureau of Statistics?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30: Nigeria’s National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) reported that headline inflation eased to 20.12% year-on-year (YoY) in August 2025, down from 21.88% in July 2025, with month-on-month (MoM) inflation moderating to 0.74% from 1.99% in July. The Central Bank of Nigeria’s (CBN) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) Communique No.159 (Sept 23, 2025) highlighted sustained disinflation for five consecutive months into August, attributing the deceleration to monetary policy actions, exchange rate (FX) stability, increased capital inflows, robust external reserves, and harvest-season effects; the MPC reduced the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) by 50bps to 27.00% while signaling staff projections for continued disinflation into late 2025.

Definitions and measurement: 
- Consumer Price Index (CPI): A statistical estimate tracking the average price level of a basket of consumer goods and services over time; the annual percentage change in CPI is commonly used as the headline measure of inflation. 
- Inflation: A general increase in the average price level of goods and services; commonly measured as the annualized percentage change in a price index such as CPI. 
- Headline inflation (YoY) in NBS publications: For the purposes of this question, “headline inflation (year-on-year)” refers to the YoY percentage change in the All-Items CPI for a given month (e.g., November 2025 vs. November 2024), using the exact figure labeled as “headline inflation (year-on-year)” in the official NBS “CPI and Inflation Report” for that month. NBS publishes a monthly “CPI and Inflation Report” series on its eLibrary and NADA microdata portals, which consistently host monthly CPI reports across years, including multiple months of 2025 (e.g., February–August 2025).

Data sources and publication practice: NBS’s eLibrary page shows recurring monthly “CPI and Inflation Report” releases with a track record of publication around mid-month for prior years, and the NBS microdata catalog (NADA) hosts monthly CPI reports and data files for 2025, indicating consistent availability of monthly CPI documentation. Given August 2025 YoY at 20.12% and recent disinflation drivers (policy stance, FX stability, harvest season, PMS price moderation), forecasters should assess risks affecting food prices, FX liquidity, fuel costs, and output, as well as any policy or supply-side shocks that could push November’s YoY headline inflation above or below 19.5%.
resolution_criteria:
- Question scope: This question concerns Nigeria’s “headline inflation (year-on-year)” for November 2025.
- Start date and timezone: The eligible statistic is the YoY headline inflation for the calendar month of November 2025; resolution will occur upon publication of the official NBS report. All times are referenced in UTC.
- What is measured: Use the precise “headline inflation (year-on-year)” figure for November 2025 as stated in the official NBS monthly “CPI and Inflation Report” (All-Items CPI YoY).
- Resolution rule: 
  • Answer Yes if the NBS-reported YoY headline inflation for November 2025 is less than or equal to 19.5%. 
  • Answer No if it is greater than 19.5%.
- Primary resolution source: The official NBS “CPI and Inflation Report” for November 2025, accessible via the NBS eLibrary CPI category (https://www.nigerianstat.gov.ng/elibrary/search/cpi) and/or the NBS NADA microdata catalog, CPI collection (https://microdata.nigerianstat.gov.ng/index.php/catalog/154). Use the first official NBS publication that includes the November 2025 headline inflation figure.
- Timing: Resolve as soon as the November 2025 CPI and Inflation Report is published by NBS, which is typically in December (mid-month based on historical postings).
- Fallback: If, exceptionally, NBS has not published the November 2025 headline CPI by 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, resolve immediately upon the first subsequent official NBS release that includes November 2025’s headline CPI YoY figure.
- Tiebreakers/ambiguities: If multiple NBS documents present the November 2025 headline inflation, use the figure in the main CPI and Inflation Report document for November 2025. If an erratum is issued by NBS prior to resolution, use the corrected figure. If NBS presents both provisional and final figures, use the latest figure available at the moment of resolution. If NBS publishes multiple base-period CPI series, use the series explicitly labeled as headline (All-Items) inflation (YoY) in the CPI and Inflation Report.
- Exclusions: Do not use third-party estimates (media, analysts, other agencies) unless they directly reproduce an official NBS figure from the specified report; in case of discrepancy between third-party reporting and NBS documents, defer to the NBS report.

question: Between January 1 and December 31, 2025 (UTC), will Ghana’s Parliament approve—and will the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration implement—a reduction of the regular 32‑page passport application fee to GHS 350 for new applications?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30: Ghana began the mass roll-out of chip‑embedded passports on April 28, 2025. At that announcement, Cabinet stated it had approved reducing the passport application fee from GHS 500 to GHS 350, but the reduction was expressly noted as “awaiting parliamentary approval.” The Ministry also highlighted processing times of 15 working days for regular applications and 5 working days for expedited services.

What is being measured and why it’s uncertain: In Ghana, changes to government fees typically require parliamentary approval and subsequent implementation (e.g., publication and operationalization by the responsible ministry/agency). The policy change therefore has two steps that both must occur for the fee to be “in effect”: (1) parliamentary approval of the reduced fee, and (2) the Passport Office/MFA charging GHS 350 for eligible new applications in practice. The timing and sequencing of these steps—and whether both happen by year-end—are uncertain.

Key terms and definitions used in this question:
- Ghanaian cedi (GHS): Ghana’s currency. For clarity, GHS 350 means three hundred and fifty Ghana cedis; amounts may be written as “GH₵350,” “GHS 350,” or “350 Ghana cedis,” which shall be treated as equivalent.
- Ordinary 32‑page passport booklet (regular service): The default booklet type for adult applicants. “Regular service” refers to the standard processing option, distinct from expedited services; the MFA has communicated regular processing in 15 working days and expedited in 5 working days.
- New application: An application initiated after the effective date of the new fee (if any) via Ghana’s official Passport Office/MFA channels (e.g., the official online application portal or in‑person Passport Office), where the applicant pays the base fee at the time of submission. Renewals and first‑time applications both count as “new applications” if initiated after the effective date; applications initiated prior to the effective date do not count, even if payment is completed later.
- Approved by Parliament: A public record that Parliament has passed legislation or an instrument that explicitly sets or authorizes the passport application fee for the ordinary 32‑page booklet (regular service) to be GHS 350. Acceptable evidence includes Parliament’s official website (e.g., Act passage notice, Hansard, or an official parliamentary release) or publication in the official Ghana Gazette issued by Ghana Publishing Company.
- In effect: The Passport Office/MFA is actively charging GHS 350 as the base fee for the ordinary 32‑page booklet under regular service for new applications (see definition of “new application”). Acceptable evidence includes the official MFA or Passport Office website/portal showing the GHS 350 fee and/or an official MFA/Passport Office notice stating that the GHS 350 fee is currently applicable for new applications.

Authoritative sources to check at resolution:
- Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration (MFA) website: https://mfa.gov.gh/
- Ghana Passport Office application portal: https://passport.mfa.gov.gh/ (or the current official portal used by MFA/Passport Office)
- Parliament of Ghana website: https://www.parliament.gh/
- Ghana Gazette (via Ghana Publishing Company): https://ghanapublishing.gov.gh/
- The MFA’s announcement of chip‑embedded passports and the proposed fee reduction (for status context): https://mfa.gov.gh/index.php/ghanas-chip-embeded-passport-rollout-begins/ 

Status quo indicators: As of the April 28/May 2, 2025 MFA communication, the fee reduction to GHS 350 was proposed by Cabinet and awaiting parliamentary approval; regular and expedited processing times were stated as 15 and 5 working days, respectively. Forecasters should monitor Parliament’s proceedings and MFA/Passport Office updates to assess whether both approval and implementation occur by year‑end.
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves based on the situation at 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025.

Start date for eligible events: 00:00:00 UTC on January 1, 2025. Events before this start date do not count.

Resolution: 
- Resolve “Yes” if BOTH of the following are true by the resolution time:
  1) Approved by Parliament: There is an official, public record that Parliament has passed legislation or an instrument that explicitly sets or authorizes the passport application fee for the ordinary 32‑page booklet (regular service) to GHS 350; and
  2) In effect for new applications: The Passport Office/MFA is charging GHS 350 as the base fee for the ordinary 32‑page booklet under regular service for new applications (as defined). Evidence may include the official online portal fee display, an MFA/Passport Office fee schedule, or an official notice stating the fee is currently applicable.

- Resolve “No” if either condition 1) or 2) above is not met by the resolution time.

Evidence standards and acceptable sources:
- Parliamentary approval can be evidenced by:
  • Parliament of Ghana’s official website (e.g., Act passage notice, Hansard, or a formal parliamentary communication), or
  • Publication in the Ghana Gazette issued by Ghana Publishing Company. 
- “In effect” can be evidenced by:
  • The official MFA website or the Passport Office portal showing GHS 350 as the base fee for the ordinary 32‑page booklet (regular service), or
  • An official MFA/Passport Office announcement stating the GHS 350 fee is currently applicable for new applications.

Clarifications:
- The exact figure must be GHS 350 for the ordinary 32‑page booklet under regular service. Fees for expedited services, courier delivery, or other booklet sizes (e.g., 48‑page) are excluded. 
- If multiple fee schedules are published, the latest official schedule in effect as of the resolution time governs.
- Alternate currency notations are acceptable if they unambiguously represent 350 Ghana cedis.
- If the Parliament approval occurs but the fee is not yet being charged for new applications (e.g., implementation date set after Dec 31, 2025), resolve “No.”

Key status source for context (not sufficient alone for “Yes” unless updated to meet criteria): MFA’s announcement of the chip‑embedded passports and proposed fee reduction, which stated Cabinet approval and that parliamentary approval was pending at the time.

question: Argentina CPI (IPC): Will INDEC report that November 2025 national “Nivel general” monthly change is ≤ 2.2%?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01:
- INDEC (Argentina’s national statistics institute) publishes a monthly technical report (“Informe técnico”) for the national Consumer Price Index (Índice de precios al consumidor, IPC). The August 2025 report shows the national monthly variation (variación mensual del Nivel general del IPC, Total nacional) was 1.9%, with year-to-date (acumulado en el año) at 19.5% and interannual (YoY) at 33.6%. The July 2025 report also showed a 1.9% national monthly change, with year-to-date 17.3% and YoY 36.6%.
- The IMF staff report for Argentina (First Review under the EFF, published 2025-08-01) projects end-of-period inflation in 2025 to fall to around 20–25%. This disinflation path implies monthly headline CPI in the low single digits, but shocks could move November’s reading above or below 2.2%.
- INDEC’s diffusion calendar schedules the publication of the November 2025 IPC in December 2025; specifically, it is listed for December 11, 2025.
- Definitions and methodology: INDEC’s IPC (base December 2016=100) produces national results (“Total nacional”) by aggregating regional indices; the “Nivel general” is the highest aggregation level of the index, and the monthly variation (“variación mensual”) is computed as ((Index_t / Index_{t−1}) − 1) × 100, i.e., the month-over-month percentage change. INDEC’s IPC measures the evolution of prices representative of household consumption expenditure in urban areas, with coverage across 39 urban agglomerations nationwide; national results are representative of total households in urban areas.
Why this threshold could be non-trivial: Recent monthly readings have been 1.9% , and the IMF projects year-end disinflation. November’s outcome around the 2%–3% range is plausibly uncertain given potential movements in administered prices, exchange rates, and seasonal effects, making ≤ 2.2% a meaningful, high-entropy cut.
resolution_criteria:
How we will resolve:
- Event window: This question concerns the November 2025 observation of INDEC’s national headline CPI (IPC) and will resolve when INDEC publishes the November 2025 IPC “Informe técnico” on indec.gob.ar, or by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC at the latest.
- Source of truth: INDEC’s official “Índice de precios al consumidor (IPC) – Informe técnico” for November 2025 posted on indec.gob.ar. The report format is standard and includes the national “Nivel general” monthly variation; see, e.g., the August 2025 IPC report for the typical presentation.
- Exact measure used: “Variación mensual del Nivel general del IPC. Total nacional” as printed in the November 2025 IPC Informe técnico. Use the numeric percentage value published by INDEC for the national headline (Total nacional) “Nivel general” monthly change.
- Comparison rule: If the reported national monthly variation is ≤ 2.2%, resolve Yes; if it is > 2.2%, resolve No.
- Rounding and format: INDEC reports percentages using the Spanish decimal comma (e.g., 2,2%); interpret 2,2% as 2.2%. Use the value as printed in the November 2025 IPC Informe técnico. If the report contains multiple instances of the national monthly variation, use the value shown in the main table/section for “Nivel general — Total nacional” (the figure that INDEC highlights as the national headline monthly change), consistent with the August 2025 report’s standard format.
- Revisions: If INDEC publishes the November 2025 IPC Informe técnico on or before 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC and subsequently revises the figure, resolve using the value in the first November 2025 IPC Informe técnico available by the deadline. If INDEC does not publish the November 2025 IPC Informe técnico by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, resolve No.
Definitions (authoritative):
- “Índice de precios al consumidor (IPC)”: INDEC’s national CPI index (base December 2016=100), with national results (“Total nacional”) constructed by weighted aggregation of regional indices.
- “Nivel general”: The highest level of aggregation of the IPC index; national “Nivel general” is computed from regional indices with consumption-expenditure weights.
- “Variación mensual”: Month-over-month percentage change in the index value, computed as ((Index_t / Index_{t−1}) − 1) × 100.
- Coverage: The IPC measures price evolution for a set of goods and services representative of household consumption in urban areas, with national coverage across 39 urban agglomerations; national results are representative of total urban households.
Citations: INDEC IPC August 2025 report ; INDEC IPC July 2025 report ; IMF staff report projection ; INDEC diffusion calendar (2nd semester 2025) ; INDEC IPC methodology (base Dec 2016).

question: Will a legally effective 100% ad valorem U.S. import duty apply to any brand‑name prescription drugs on December 31, 2025?
background:
Status quo as of early October 2025
- Announcement and planned start: On Sep 25, 2025, President Trump announced that brand‑name or patented pharmaceutical products would face a 100% tariff, initially stated to begin Oct 1, 2025. An ad valorem tariff is a duty charged as a percentage of the price/value of the good.
- Delay/paused implementation: As of Oct 1, 2025, the administration did not implement the triple‑digit duties, instead pausing to negotiate drug price concessions. Reporting indicates the tariffs did not take effect on Oct 1 and were delayed as leverage while negotiations with drugmakers continued.
- Example deal and leverage: Around this timeline, Pfizer publicly agreed to lower certain U.S. drug prices and invest in U.S. manufacturing; in exchange it was said to receive relief or a grace period from contemplated tariffs, underscoring the administration’s use of the tariff threat to drive price cuts.
- Legal/policy pathway: Earlier in 2025, the Commerce Department initiated a Section 232 national security investigation into imports of pharmaceuticals and pharmaceutical ingredients, covering finished drugs (generic and non‑generic), APIs, and key starting materials; this investigation provides a plausible legal pathway for imposing tariffs on pharmaceuticals if the President so decides.
- Trade implementation context: When the U.S. implements tariff changes, they are formalized via Federal Register notices and reflected in the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS), with operational guidance often issued to importers via U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) Cargo Systems Messaging Service (CSMS). Recent examples include U.S.–EU tariff adjustments on autos and parts, which were confirmed in government notices and implemented with CBP CSMS guidance detailing HTSUS changes and effective dates.

Key definitions and scope for this market
- Brand‑name drug: A drug marketed under a proprietary, trademark‑protected name (FDA glossary).
- Ad valorem tariff: A tariff rate charged as a percentage of the price of the imported good (WTO glossary).

Why this is forecasting‑relevant now
- As of Oct 1, 2025, the threatened 100% tariff on brand‑name pharmaceuticals had not been legally implemented, but negotiations and the Section 232 pathway keep the possibility live through year‑end. The outcome depends on policy decisions, legal steps (e.g., Presidential proclamations or rules), industry negotiations, and potential court challenges, making it genuinely uncertain whether a legally effective 100% tariff will actually be in force on Dec 31, 2025.
resolution_criteria:
Question
- Resolve Yes if, as of 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, at least one legally effective U.S. measure (e.g., Presidential proclamation, USTR/BIS rule or notice) published in the Federal Register imposes an additional 100% ad valorem import duty on any brand‑name (also described in such measures as “brand‑name,” “branded,” “patented,” “innovator,” or equivalent) prescription pharmaceutical products, and that measure is operative (in effect) and not enjoined or stayed by a U.S. federal court at that time.
- Resolve No otherwise.

Operational details and sources of truth
- “Legally effective” and “operative” mean the measure has been published in the Federal Register with an effective date on or before Dec 31, 2025 and is in force at 23:59:59 UTC that day (i.e., entries made then would be subject to the 100% rate). If a measure exists but is subject to a court‑ordered stay, temporary restraining order, preliminary injunction, or similar order preventing its enforcement at that time, it shall be considered not operative for resolution.
- “100% ad valorem import duty” means a tariff rate set as 100% of customs value (ad valorem). The measure must specify a 100% rate; lower capped rates (e.g., 15%) do not satisfy this criterion.
- “Brand‑name prescription pharmaceutical products” refers to finished prescription drug products described in the operative measure as brand‑name/branded/patented/innovator (or equivalent) and classifiable as pharmaceutical products under U.S. tariff law. We accept the scope and product coverage as defined in the operative Federal Register notice or proclamation; it is not necessary for the measure to distinguish by individual trademarks so long as it targets branded/patented prescription drugs consistent with the FDA’s concept of brand‑name drugs (marketed under a proprietary, trademark‑protected name).
- Exemptions or carve‑outs (e.g., for particular countries under trade frameworks or for firms meeting conditions) do not negate a Yes outcome so long as the 100% rate applies to at least one non‑exempt subset of covered brand‑name prescription drugs for at least one country of origin at the resolution timestamp.
- Primary resolution sources: (1) Federal Register (to verify the existence, scope, and effective status of any 100% pharmaceutical tariff measure); (2) CBP CSMS and the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS) as implemented, to confirm operational status if needed (e.g., Chapter 99 provisions and effective dates). Recent analogous implementations (e.g., U.S.–EU tariff adjustments) are typically reflected through these sources.

Notes
- Background context on the September 2025 announcement, delayed implementation as of Oct 1, 2025, and leverage via negotiations is provided for situational awareness only and does not affect resolution. Announcement of intent alone without a legally effective, operative measure does not count.

question: Will the European Commission adopt a DMA non-compliance decision imposing a fine on Alphabet (Google) between 00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30:
- Digital Markets Act (DMA). The DMA is Regulation (EU) 2022/1925, an EU law that sets obligations for designated “gatekeepers” and empowers the European Commission to enforce compliance, including via non‑compliance decisions and fines.
- Alphabet designated as a gatekeeper. On September 6, 2023, the Commission designated six gatekeepers under the DMA: Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, ByteDance, Meta, and Microsoft. Designated gatekeepers had six months to ensure compliance with DMA obligations for their core platform services.
- Investigations into Alphabet’s compliance. On March 25, 2024, the Commission opened non‑compliance investigations into Alphabet under the DMA, including: (i) Google Play “steering” restrictions; and (ii) self‑preferencing in Google Search. The Commission indicated it intended to conclude these proceedings within 12 months; if it finds an infringement, it can impose fines up to 10% of total worldwide turnover (or up to 20% for repeated infringement).
- Preliminary findings to Alphabet. On March 19, 2025, the Commission sent two sets of preliminary findings to Alphabet under the DMA concerning Google Search and Google Play, noting that preliminary findings do not prejudge the outcome of the investigation.
- Enforcement precedents in 2025. On April 23, 2025, the Commission adopted DMA non‑compliance decisions against Apple and Meta and announced fines of €500 million and €200 million, respectively. This confirms the Commission’s practice of publishing formal non‑compliance decisions that include fines on the official DMA portal and press communications.
- Official publication venue. The Commission publishes DMA information, updates, and decisions on its official Digital Markets Act portal at digital‑markets‑act.ec.europa.eu.
- Corporate identification. Alphabet Inc. is the parent holding company of Google LLC; Google LLC is Alphabet’s largest subsidiary operating services such as Google Search and Google Play.

Why this question is non‑trivial now: The Commission has advanced Alphabet cases through formal investigations and preliminary findings, and has issued non‑compliance decisions with fines to other gatekeepers in 2025. Whether Alphabet (Google) will receive a formal non‑compliance decision imposing a monetary fine during the specified window remains uncertain, creating a high‑entropy policy forecasting problem linked to ongoing enforcement dynamics.

Key definitions and links:
- Digital Markets Act (DMA): Regulation (EU) 2022/1925. Official text: EUR‑Lex CELEX:32022R1925 (link: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/1925/oj/eng).
- Gatekeeper: An undertaking designated under Article 3 of the DMA to which DMA obligations apply; Alphabet is one of the six gatekeepers designated on 2023‑09‑06.
- Non‑compliance decision: An implementing act adopted by the Commission under Article 29 DMA establishing that a gatekeeper failed to comply with obligations (e.g., Articles 5–7) or measures specified in enforcement decisions; it orders the gatekeeper to cease non‑compliance and can follow preliminary findings and consultation steps.
- Fine (under the DMA): A monetary penalty imposed by the Commission pursuant to Article 30 DMA. For infringements of Articles 5–7, fines may be up to 10% of total worldwide turnover, and up to 20% for repeated infringements within eight years; Article 30 also provides other fine types for specified procedural infringements.
- Alphabet (Google): For this question, “Alphabet (Google)” refers to Alphabet Inc. and its subsidiary Google LLC (and any legal entity in the Alphabet group that is the addressee of the relevant DMA decision). Background references: Alphabet Inc. overview (Wikipedia) and Google LLC overview (Wikipedia).
- Official publication source: European Commission DMA portal (https://digital-markets-act.ec.europa.eu) and Commission press releases/press corner; the portal is the Commission’s official site for DMA information.

Additional context on Alphabet’s current DMA enforcement status:
- Open proceedings and preliminary findings specifically identify suspected issues in Search and Play; the Commission’s stated 12‑month intention to conclude proceedings provides a temporal marker but does not guarantee timing or outcome.
- Recent non‑compliance decisions with fines against other gatekeepers show fines are being used in DMA enforcement, but each case is fact‑specific and outcome‑dependent.
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves based on whether, during the period from 00:00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 through 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, the European Commission publishes an official DMA non‑compliance decision that imposes a fine on Alphabet (Google), as defined below.

Event window and timezone:
- Eligible events must occur and be published between 00:00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025.

Definitions for resolution:
- “Non‑compliance decision” means an implementing act adopted by the European Commission pursuant to Article 29 of Regulation (EU) 2022/1925 (DMA) that establishes a gatekeeper’s failure to comply with DMA obligations or measures, and orders the gatekeeper to cease non‑compliance.
- “Fine” means a monetary penalty imposed by the European Commission under Article 30 of the DMA. For the purpose of this question, the decision must impose a fine under Article 30 in relation to non‑compliance with Articles 5–7 or other specified measures (as enumerated in Article 30(1)); fines for purely procedural infringements (e.g., failure to supply information) also constitute “fines” under Article 30, but they only resolve this question if they are imposed within a non‑compliance decision under Article 29.
- “Alphabet (Google)” means Alphabet Inc., Google LLC, or another Alphabet group legal entity that is the addressee of the relevant DMA decision; Alphabet is a designated DMA gatekeeper.
- “Published” means that the European Commission makes the decision or an official press communication explicitly stating the adoption of a DMA non‑compliance decision imposing a fine available on its official websites (the DMA portal and/or Commission Press Corner/Newsroom). The Commission’s DMA portal is the official site for DMA information.

What counts (Yes):
- A European Commission non‑compliance decision under Article 29 DMA against Alphabet (Google) published within the event window, where the Commission explicitly states in the decision or an accompanying official press communication that a fine has been imposed (e.g., “has fined” with an amount specified), consistent with Article 30 DMA.

What does not count (No):
- A non‑compliance decision published outside the event window.
- A non‑compliance decision without a fine (e.g., ordering remedies but imposing no monetary penalty).
- A fine imposed outside an Article 29 non‑compliance decision (e.g., a standalone procedural fine not tied to a non‑compliance decision).
- Preliminary findings, opening of proceedings, statements of objections, consultations, or workshop materials that do not constitute an adopted Article 29 non‑compliance decision.
- Reporting solely by third‑party media without an official Commission publication.

Primary resolution sources (verification steps):
1) Check the European Commission’s DMA portal for Alphabet‑related enforcement pages and decisions: https://digital-markets-act.ec.europa.eu.
2) Check Commission Press Corner/news releases for DMA decisions and fines during the window (e.g., pages similar to the April 23, 2025 Apple/Meta decisions): confirmation language typically includes “found [X] in breach” and “has fined [X] €…”.

Resolution:
- Resolve Yes if an official Commission publication during the window clearly indicates the adoption of an Article 29 DMA non‑compliance decision that imposes a fine against Alphabet (Google), per definitions above; otherwise resolve No.

Notes and edge cases:
- If the Commission adopts such a decision during the window but delays web publication until after December 31, 2025, the question resolves No (publication within the window is required).
- If the decision names a specific Alphabet group legal entity (e.g., Google LLC) as addressee, it qualifies, provided it is within the Alphabet group as defined.
- If multiple relevant decisions are published during the window, any single qualifying decision suffices to resolve Yes.
- If the Commission publishes only preliminary findings or opens additional proceedings during the window without adopting a non‑compliance decision imposing a fine, resolve No.

question: PEF 2026: Will OPD IMSS‑Bienestar’s approved 2026 allocation be at least 172,492.4 mdp?
background:
Definitions and context (as of 2025-10-01):
- IMSS‑Bienestar: Officially “Servicios de Salud del Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social para el Bienestar,” a decentralized public body (organismo público descentralizado, OPD) of the Federal Public Administration, non‑sectorized, with legal personality, its own assets, and technical/operational/management autonomy, created to provide free comprehensive medical and hospital care (including medicines and associated inputs) to people without social security affiliation. Common abbreviation: IMSS‑Bienestar.
- mdp: Abbreviation for “millones de pesos.” Government usage note: quantities in thousands of millions of pesos use mmdp; tables present quantities in millions of pesos (mdp) unless noted otherwise. In this question, 1 mdp = 1,000,000 Mexican pesos (MXN).
- Budget process and timing: The Executive sends the Initiative of the Revenue Law and the Project of the Expenditure Budget (PPEF) by September 8, and the Chamber of Deputies must approve the Presupuesto de Egresos de la Federación (PEF) by November 15. The PEF is published as an official decree in the Diario Oficial de la Federación (DOF) and includes annex tables with detailed allocations; for example, the PEF 2025 decree and annex structure were published in DOF on December 24, 2024, demonstrating the existence and format of the source of truth.
- Proposed 2026 allocation to IMSS‑Bienestar (for forecaster context): In the PPEF 2026 Project of Decree, Annex 1 (“Gasto neto total (pesos)”), under Section B: Ramos Administrativos, Ramo 56 “Servicios de Salud del Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social para el Bienestar” is listed with 172,492,400,589 pesos, which equals 172,492.4 mdp. Note this is a proposal, not yet the approved PEF.
- Health sector context: Independent analysis of PPEF 2026 reports proposed total health spending of about 996,528 mdp (≈2.6% of GDP) and highlights distributional concerns; per capita spending for the population without social security is projected to decline from $4,609 in 2025 to $4,412 in 2026, while IMSS per‑capita rises, indicating pressures and potential equity debates around allocations to IMSS‑Bienestar.

Why this question is non‑trivial: The threshold matches the Executive’s proposed figure; the Chamber may adjust line items during approval. Political commitments to expand coverage for uninsured populations weigh against overall fiscal constraints. Outcome uncertainty arises from possible increases, decreases, or reclassification of the OPD’s allocation during the legislative process.
resolution_criteria:
Event window and time zone:
- Eligible event window: 2025-10-15 00:00:00 to 2025-12-31 23:59:59 (UTC).

Operational definitions for resolution:
- Entity to evaluate: The decentralized public body defined as IMSS‑Bienestar (“Servicios de Salud del Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social para el Bienestar”), as described in. In the PEF tables it is currently labeled as Ramo 56 under Ramos Administrativos.
- Metric to compare: The amount shown for this entity in Annex 1 (“Anexo 1. Gasto neto total (pesos)”) of the approved Presupuesto de Egresos de la Federación 2026 (PEF 2026). This is the net total expenditure allocation in pesos for the ramo/entity as published in the final decree and annex tables.
- Threshold and units: 172,492.4 mdp, where 1 mdp = 1,000,000 MXN. For avoidance of rounding ambiguity, the threshold in pesos is 172,492,400,000 MXN.

Resolution rule:
- Resolve Yes if the approved PEF 2026 (final decree) allocates ≥172,492,400,000 MXN to IMSS‑Bienestar in Anexo 1 under the label that corresponds to this OPD (e.g., “Servicios de Salud del Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social para el Bienestar,” currently Ramo 56).
- Resolve No if the allocation in Anexo 1 is <172,492,400,000 MXN, or if the OPD does not appear as a distinct entity/ramo in Anexo 1 of the approved PEF 2026 (i.e., no separate line corresponding to IMSS‑Bienestar).

Source of truth and how to verify (must be unambiguous by the resolution date):
- Primary source: The published PEF 2026 decree and annex tables in the Diario Oficial de la Federación (DOF). Precedent confirms PEF decrees and annex tables are formally published and accessible (e.g., PEF 2025).
- Fallback if DOF publication lags beyond the resolution date: The official PEF 2026 text and annexes published on the Cámara de Diputados “Leyes Biblio” site (same repository that hosts PEF 2025).

Notes:
- “Approved” refers to the final PEF 2026 decree as enacted and published, consistent with the constitutional process and timeline for approval by the Chamber of Deputies (deadline November 15).
- We compare the peso figure in Anexo 1 to the threshold; conversion to mdp uses the 1 mdp = 1,000,000 MXN convention.
- The PPEF 2026 proposal lists the entity as Ramo 56 and proposes 172,492,400,589 pesos (172,492.4 mdp) for forecaster baseline context; the approved PEF may differ.

question: SEEPEX Day-Ahead (Serbia): In November 2025, will the average daily Peak price exceed the average daily Base price by at least 10.00 €/MWh?
background:
Overview and context as of 2025-09-30:
- Market and data availability: SEEPEX, the Serbian power exchange, publishes Day-Ahead market data with daily fields labeled Price Base and Price Peak, and provides monthly trading reports summarizing the Day-Ahead market. An August 2025 monthly report PDF is hosted on the official SEEPEX site, illustrating the regular publication pattern (monthly PDFs in /wp-content/uploads/YYYY/MM/). Trade press citing SEEPEX reported that in August 2025, the average daily base price was 81.06 €/MWh and the average daily peak price was 59.07 €/MWh, highlighting that the peak–base relationship can vary by season.
- Products and hours: SEEPEX defines standard block products for the Day-Ahead auction, including Baseload (hours 1–24) and Peakload (hours 9–20). Off-Peak blocks cover hours 1–8 and 21–24. These hours are in local time; in November, Serbia observes Central European Time (CET, UTC+01:00).
- Units: Prices are quoted in euros per megawatt-hour (€/MWh). One megawatt-hour is a unit of energy equal to 1,000 kilowatt-hours.
- Current snapshot examples: The SEEPEX market-data page displays recent daily values for Price Base and Price Peak (e.g., for delivery day 2025-10-01: Price Base 145.83 €/MWh, Price Peak 164.55 €/MWh), illustrating how base and peak are reported at the daily level.
Why this question is plausibly uncertain: Summer 2025 saw peak below base on average, but winter conditions (higher daytime demand, potential constraints) can invert that relationship; whether the November spread reaches at least 10 €/MWh is uncertain and driven by weather, fuel prices, interconnector availability, and hydro conditions. The necessary figures are directly reported by SEEPEX, enabling unambiguous resolution.
resolution_criteria:
Scope and timeframe:
- Eligible period: November 2025 is defined as the calendar month from 2025-11-01 00:00 CET through 2025-11-30 24:00 CET (Serbia observes CET in November; CET is UTC+01:00).
Definitions (as used for context; resolution uses SEEPEX’s published monthly figures):
- Base refers to Baseload hours (1–24) and Peak refers to Peakload hours (9–20) in the SEEPEX Day-Ahead market; Off-Peak covers 1–8 and 21–24.
- Price units: €/MWh; 1 MWh = 1,000 kWh.
Primary resolution rule:
- Let P_peak be the numerical value labeled “Average daily Peak price” (or “Avg Daily Price – Peak”) for the Day-Ahead market in the official SEEPEX Monthly Report for November 2025. Let P_base be the numerical value labeled “Average daily Base price” (or “Avg Daily Price – Base”) for the Day-Ahead market in the same report. Compute D = P_peak – P_base using the values as published (two-decimal precision as reported). Resolve Yes if D ≥ 10.00 €/MWh; resolve No otherwise.
Sources of truth and retrieval:
- Primary source: The SEEPEX “Monthly Report – November 2025” published on seepex-spot.rs (example pattern: monthly report PDFs are hosted under /wp-content/uploads/YYYY/MM/, e.g., “SEEPEX-Monthly-Report-August-2025.pdf”).
- Where to find it: SEEPEX News posts link to each Day-Ahead monthly report (e.g., “Trading monthly report for August 2025”) and the site’s reports/downloads pages list monthly PDFs.
- Fallback (if the November 2025 monthly report PDF is not available on the SEEPEX site by 2025-12-31 23:59 UTC): Use a SEEPEX webpage that explicitly lists the November 2025 Day-Ahead monthly average base and peak prices. If no official SEEPEX page with November monthly averages is available by that time, use figures reported by credible trade press that explicitly cite SEEPEX as the source (e.g., Serbia Energy’s monthly trading reports).
Operational notes:
- Use the latest version of the official SEEPEX November 2025 monthly report available on the SEEPEX site as of the resolution cutoff. If multiple versions exist, use the version with the latest publication date prior to the cutoff.
- No alternative calculations (e.g., reconstructing averages from daily data) should be performed; rely solely on the labeled monthly figures published by SEEPEX.

question: By 11:59:59 pm Eastern Time on December 31, 2025, will an official source confirm that definitive agreements to implement the U.S.-majority TikTok joint venture have been executed?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- Legal posture: On January 17, 2025, the U.S. Supreme Court upheld the federal law requiring TikTok (owned by ByteDance) to be sold to an American entity or face a U.S. ban, establishing that continued operation in the U.S. depends on effectuating a qualifying divestiture.
- Enforcement timing: On September 16, 2025, a Presidential Executive Order further extended the pause on federal enforcement of the law until December 16, 2025. On September 25, 2025, the White House published a Presidential action describing a framework for a “qualified divestiture,” and directed the Attorney General not to enforce the Act for 120 days to permit completion of the contemplated divestiture; the document also notes the framework would be effectuated “once its implementation agreements are executed”. A same-day White House fact sheet emphasized the 120-day non-enforcement window to allow completion and described key governance and ownership parameters.
- What the contemplated U.S.-majority TikTok joint venture (JV) entails: According to official White House materials, the U.S. TikTok application would be operated by a newly established U.S.-based joint venture that is majority-owned and controlled by U.S. persons, with ByteDance owning less than 20% of the JV’s equity and holding only one of seven board seats (Americans to hold six of seven seats). The materials indicate that algorithm/control and content-moderation decisions would be under the JV, addressing national security concerns, with the framework becoming effective when implementation agreements are executed.
- Deal status as of late September 2025: Reuters reporting contemporaneous with the White House announcements indicated that while a framework was approved, the transaction details were not yet finalized; investor stakes were subject to change and “numerous details need to be fleshed out,” signaling that definitive agreements had not been signed. Additional reporting described that structural elements were still under discussion, and ByteDance would remain a significant minority shareholder with roles delineated between the JV and ByteDance-affiliated operations, reinforcing that final implementation documents were pending.
- Likely resolution sources: If a U.S.-listed investor party enters into material definitive agreements, the company would typically disclose entry into such agreements in a Form 8‑K within four business days under Item 1.01, providing a clear, time-stamped regulatory record. The White House publishes official statements at whitehouse.gov, and TikTok’s official newsroom hosts company press releases and statements.

Why this question is uncertain: The framework exists, enforcement has been paused to permit completion, and reporting suggests active negotiations—but execution of definitive/implementation agreements remained outstanding as of late September 2025. Execution by year-end is plausible but not assured, creating genuine uncertainty suitable for forecasting.
resolution_criteria:
Time window and timezone:
- Eligible announcements must be first published between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC (inclusive) and 2026-01-01 04:59:59 UTC (inclusive), which corresponds to 11:59:59 pm Eastern Time on 2025-12-31.

Question subject:
- “U.S.-majority TikTok joint venture” refers to the U.S.-based entity described in official White House materials as the vehicle to operate TikTok’s U.S. application, majority-owned and controlled by U.S. persons, with ByteDance owning less than 20% and Americans holding six of seven board seats, and with algorithms/content-moderation under the JV’s control. The announcement must unambiguously refer to this JV construct (or a materially equivalent structure explicitly identified by the White House as the qualified divestiture).

What counts as “definitive/implementation agreements” and “executed”:
- “Definitive/implementation agreements” are the binding transaction agreements that implement and establish the JV described above (e.g., joint venture agreement/operating agreement, equity subscription/sale agreements, IP/technology license and operational agreements), as opposed to preliminary, non-binding documents such as term sheets, memoranda of understanding, or agreements in principle. For publicly listed parties, the execution of a “material definitive agreement” as defined under SEC Form 8‑K Item 1.01 constitutes sufficient evidence that a definitive agreement has been executed.
- “Executed” means signed by duly authorized representatives of the relevant parties such that the agreement(s) are binding. For SEC filings, the disclosure of entry into a material definitive agreement under Item 1.01 within four business days is acceptable confirmation.

What qualifies as a “publicly announce”/acceptable sources:
- Any one of the following, published within the time window, qualifies:
  1) An official White House publication on whitehouse.gov (e.g., Presidential actions, fact sheets, press statements) explicitly stating that the definitive/implementation agreements establishing the U.S.-majority TikTok JV have been executed.
  2) An official press release or statement posted on TikTok’s official newsroom (newsroom.tiktok.com) explicitly stating that such agreements have been executed.
  3) An official press release/statement posted on the official website of the new U.S. JV (if operational) explicitly stating execution of such agreements.
  4) A regulatory filing on the SEC’s EDGAR system by any U.S.-listed company that is a party to the transaction (e.g., an investor or partner), disclosing entry into a material definitive agreement under Item 1.01 that unambiguously pertains to executing the agreements that establish the JV described above.
  5) A report by Reuters or the Associated Press that contains an on-the-record, attributed statement by a named official of the White House, TikTok, or a party to the agreements, explicitly confirming that such definitive/implementation agreements have been executed. Reports relying solely on anonymous sources do not qualify.

Qualifying language (examples):
- Phrases such as “the parties have executed definitive agreements to establish the U.S.-majority TikTok joint venture,” “implementation agreements have been signed,” or “entered into binding definitive agreement(s) to form the JV described by the White House framework” qualify. Phrases like “agreement in principle,” “framework agreement,” “non-binding term sheet,” “letter of intent,” “intends to,” or “will pursue” do not qualify.

Resolution:
- Resolve YES if at least one qualifying announcement (as defined above) is published within the time window explicitly stating that the definitive/implementation agreements to establish the U.S.-majority TikTok JV have been executed. Otherwise, resolve NO.

Tie-breakers and conflicts:
- If conflicting reports exist, prioritize official publications (White House, TikTok newsroom, JV official site) and regulatory filings over media reports. If a qualifying source issues a correction or retraction before the deadline that makes it clear the agreements were not executed, resolve NO.

Notes for verifiers:
- The White House framework and enforcement delays are detailed in Presidential materials dated September 16 and September 25, 2025.
- Board composition and ownership constraints cited above come from official and wire reports.
- Reuters reporting indicates the deal was not finalized as of late September 2025, supporting that resolution was still open as of the start of the window.

question: Will the U.S. government publicly certify that TikTok has executed a “qualified divestiture” under the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act by December 31, 2025?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30:
- Statutory framework: The Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (Pub. L. 118-50) restricts distribution/maintenance of “foreign adversary controlled applications,” and provides that if a “qualified divestiture” is executed, the prohibition does not apply or ceases to apply to that app (§2(c)). “Qualified divestiture” means a divestiture or similar transaction that the President determines, through an interagency process, (A) would result in the app no longer being controlled by a foreign adversary, and (B) precludes any operational relationship between the U.S. operations of the app and formerly affiliated entities controlled by a foreign adversary, including cooperation on a content recommendation algorithm or any data-sharing agreement (§2(g)(6)). The Act expressly includes “TikTok” in the definition of “foreign adversary controlled application” (§2(g)(3)(A)(ii)) and defines when an entity is “controlled by a foreign adversary” (§2(g)(1)). Congress.gov text: https://www.congress.gov/bill/118th-congress/house-bill/7521/text [link provided for convenience; authoritative claims above are sourced to the Act as summarized].
- Enforcement timing and delays: The Act’s prohibitions as applied to TikTok became effective in January 2025, but Executive Order 14166 suspended enforcement for 75 days to allow orderly consideration, with DOJ directed not to enforce or penalize conduct during that period or prior to the order. Subsequent presidential actions further delayed enforcement, including an extension until December 16, 2025. On September 25, 2025, a further presidential action (“Saving TikTok While Protecting National Security”) directed the Attorney General not to enforce the Act for 120 days from that order and described criteria the President evaluated regarding a contemplated divestiture.
- Status of a potential TikTok divestiture: The September 25 Federal Register publication states that, following an interagency process, the President determined a contemplated Framework Agreement would, once implementation agreements are executed, constitute a “qualified divestiture” under the Act, outlining criteria such as: U.S.-based joint venture with less than 20% ownership or control by foreign adversary persons, U.S. control of algorithms and code and content-moderation decisions, storage of sensitive U.S. user data in a U.S.-run cloud, and intensive monitoring/retraining of recommendation models by trusted U.S. security partners. These statements pertain to a proposed/anticipated transaction; they do not themselves certify that a qualified divestiture has been executed. Separately, contemporaneous reporting described a U.S.–China framework, investor lineup, and stated enforcement would be delayed further, though some details remained unresolved.

Why this question is forecastable: A final, public certification that TikTok has executed a qualified divestiture (as defined in the Act) is a binary, verifiable event that could plausibly occur before year-end but is not yet known. It depends on legal, regulatory, and transactional milestones that remain uncertain as of September 30, 2025.
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves using publicly available, authoritative U.S. government sources. Time zone is UTC.

Resolution window: From 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC through 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, inclusive.

Operationalized question: Resolve YES if, during the resolution window, an official U.S. government publication on a federal.gov domain explicitly states that TikTok has executed a “qualified divestiture” under the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act and that the President has determined/certified that condition pursuant to §2(g)(6) of the Act; otherwise resolve NO.

Accepted forms of evidence (in order of precedence):
- A notice, executive order, presidential memorandum, determination, or other presidential action published on FederalRegister.gov that explicitly states the President has determined/certified that TikTok has executed a “qualified divestiture” under the Act.
- A presidential action or statement on WhiteHouse.gov that explicitly states the same.
- An official determination or certification posted on a relevant federal agency’s.gov site (e.g., Department of Justice) that explicitly states the same.

Key term definitions (for resolution):
- “TikTok”: the application specifically listed in §2(g)(3)(A)(ii) of the Act.
- “Qualified divestiture”: as defined in §2(g)(6) of the Act; the President must determine, through an interagency process, that the transaction (A) results in TikTok no longer being controlled by a foreign adversary and (B) precludes any operational relationship between TikTok’s U.S. operations and formerly affiliated entities controlled by a foreign adversary, including cooperation on a content recommendation algorithm or any data-sharing agreement.
- “Operational relationship” (for avoidance of doubt): includes, at minimum, cooperation regarding content recommendation algorithms and data-sharing agreements, per the Act’s illustrative examples in §2(g)(6)(B).
- “Publicly certify” (for this market’s purposes): an explicit statement in an official U.S. government publication (as enumerated above) that the President has determined/certified that TikTok has executed a qualified divestiture under the Act. Media reports, company press releases, leaks, or statements lacking explicit certification language do not count.

Inclusions and exclusions:
- Inclusion: A public document that explicitly states that the qualified divestiture “has been executed” and that the President has determined/certified that the resulting structure satisfies §2(g)(6). If such a certification document also states (or a companion official document states) that, under §2(c), the prohibition does not apply or ceases to apply to TikTok, that supports but is not required for a YES, provided the certification criteria above are met.
- Exclusion: Documents that only state a proposed or contemplated transaction “would” or “will, once executed, constitute” a qualified divestiture do not count (e.g., characterizations like those in the September 25, 2025 Federal Register publication describing a framework agreement).
- Exclusion: Publications posted before 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC (even if still live on a government site) do not count toward a YES; the certification must be newly published within the resolution window.

If conflicting publications exist, resolve based on the most authoritative source per the precedence above, favoring FederalRegister.gov over WhiteHouse.gov, and those over other.gov publications. If multiple qualifying publications appear, use the earliest qualifying publication time stamp within the window for resolution. If no qualifying publication appears within the window, resolve NO.

Primary reference texts for verification and definitions: the statutory definitions and mechanics in the Act as published on Congress.gov ; relevant presidential actions on FederalRegister.gov and WhiteHouse.gov documenting enforcement delays and contemplated divestiture criteria.

question: Hillman Solutions (HLMN): Will Q3 2025 net sales be at least $425.0 million?
background:
Company and fiscal calendar context
- Hillman Solutions Corp. (Nasdaq: HLMN) reports on a 52–53 week fiscal year ending on the last Saturday in December; in a 52‑week year, each quarter consists of 13 weeks. The company recognizes revenue when control transfers to customers and presents “Net sales” as its GAAP top‑line. Monetary amounts in financial tables are stated as “dollars in thousands” (USD).
- In 2025, Hillman’s Q1 covered the thirteen weeks ended March 29, 2025, and Q2 covered the thirteen and twenty‑six weeks ended June 28, 2025; by convention, Q3 follows as a 13‑week period ending in late September (e.g., Q3 2024 ended September 28, 2024).

Recent results and guidance relevant to forecasting Q3 2025
- Q1 2025 net sales were $359.3 million, up 2.6% year over year (thirteen weeks ended March 29, 2025).
- Q2 2025 net sales were $402.8 million, up 6.2% year over year (thirteen weeks ended June 28, 2025).
- Management updated full‑year 2025 net sales guidance to a range of $1.535–$1.575 billion in the Q2 2025 release.
- For seasonality context, Q3 2024 net sales were $393.3 million (down 1.4% YoY) for the thirteen weeks ended September 28, 2024, and Q4 2024 net sales were $349.6 million (thirteen weeks ended December 28, 2024).
- Hillman typically issues a press release for Q3 results in early November; for example, Q3 2024 results were released on November 5, 2024 at 7:30 a.m. ET.

Why the $425.0 million threshold?
- Given the updated FY2025 net sales guidance range of $1.535–$1.575 billion (midpoint $1.555 billion) and reported H1 2025 net sales totaling $359.3m + $402.8m = $762.1m, the implied H2 requirement spans roughly $772.9m–$812.9m to meet the low end through midpoint. With Q4 2024 at $349.6m for reference, a Q3 outcome around the mid‑$400m range would keep multiple full‑year scenarios in play, making $425.0m a balanced and uncertain threshold for Q3 2025.
resolution_criteria:
Question
- Between 00:00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, will Hillman Solutions Corp. report GAAP “Net sales” for its fiscal third quarter of 2025 that are greater than or equal to $425,000,000 (USD)? Resolve YES if ≥ $425.0 million; NO otherwise.

Definitions and scope
- “Fiscal third quarter of 2025” (Q3 2025) means Hillman’s 13‑week period that immediately follows Q2 2025 (which ended June 28, 2025) and precedes Q4 2025, consistent with the company’s 52/53‑week fiscal calendar ending the last Saturday in December.
- “Net sales” refers to Hillman’s GAAP revenue line as presented in its consolidated financial statements, recognized when control of goods or services transfers to customers; sales taxes are excluded, and discounts/rebates are netted in determining net sales.
- Currency and units: All amounts are in U.S. dollars. If the primary source presents financial tables labeled “(dollars in thousands),” the authoritative figure is the exact GAAP Net sales amount from those tables (i.e., the thousands figure multiplied by 1,000). If a narrative headline figure differs from the financial tables, the tables take precedence.
- Synonyms: If the press release or filing uses “Revenue” interchangeably with “Net sales” for the quarter’s top‑line GAAP amount, treat it as equivalent for resolution purposes, but prefer the labeled “Net sales” line where both appear.

Primary resolution source (use the earliest available in this order of precedence)
1) Hillman’s Q3 2025 earnings press release on the company’s Investor Relations News page (e.g., prior Q3 releases are posted there), or on the Investor Relations Financial Results page for the relevant quarter.
2) The Form 10‑Q for the thirteen‑week period comprising Q3 2025, filed with the U.S. SEC and accessible via EDGAR and/or Hillman’s IR site.

Timing and contingencies
- The market‑moving event (publication of the Q3 2025 results) is expected to occur within the resolution window based on historical practice (e.g., Q3 2024 released Nov 5, 2024). If both a press release and a Form 10‑Q are available and present differing GAAP Net sales for Q3 2025, use the Form 10‑Q figure.
- If Hillman issues a correction or restatement of the Q3 2025 net sales figure before 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, resolve using the latest corrected figure available by that deadline. Corrections issued after this deadline will be ignored for resolution.

Scoring
- YES if GAAP Net sales for Q3 2025 are ≥ $425,000,000 as per the sources above. NO if they are < $425,000,000.

question: Will FEMA’s listed Public Assistance obligations for DR-4827-NC be at least $950,000,000 as of 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC?
background:
Context and status quo (as of today)
- Disaster and scope: DR-4827-NC is FEMA’s designation for North Carolina’s Major Disaster associated with Tropical Storm Helene; the official FEMA disaster page for DR-4827 is https://www.fema.gov/disaster/4827.
- Current total obligations: The FEMA DR-4827 page lists Public Assistance (PA) “Dollars Obligated” by work type. As of late September 2025, it shows: Total PA Grants Dollars Obligated ≈ $784,000,491.00, with Emergency Work (Categories A–B) $398,645,876.63 and Permanent Work (Categories C–G) $354,433,855.52. This indicates substantial obligated funding already recorded, with room for additional obligations and potential deobligations before year-end.
- What is FEMA Public Assistance (PA)?
