FEMA’s PA program provides supplemental grants to state, tribal, territorial, and local governments, and certain private nonprofit organizations, for eligible emergency work and permanent work following a presidential disaster declaration. FEMA processes PA funding by “categories of work”: Emergency Work (A: Debris removal; B: Emergency protective measures) and Permanent Work (C: Roads and bridges; D: Water control facilities; E: Public buildings and equipment; F: Public utilities; G: Parks, recreational, and other facilities).
- What does “obligated” mean here? FEMA states that it “obligates funds to the Recipient based on the eligible total of an approved project. The Recipient then disburses funding to the Applicant.” Obligations are tied to specific approved project worksheets and can occur over time; emergency work is generally to be completed within six months and permanent work within 18 months, subject to time extensions.
- Data sources and caveats: The FEMA DR-4827 page provides the headline totals used in this question. As a backup, OpenFEMA provides the Public Assistance Funded Projects Details dataset listing obligated PA projects (project worksheets) with financial fields including federalShareObligated and identifiers such as disasterNumber and stateAbbreviation; the dataset documentation notes financial information is derived from FEMA grants systems and is not intended for official federal reporting and may differ slightly from other sources. The “Public Assistance Grant Award Activities (EMMIE)” dataset further explains that obligations can include additions and subtractions (deobligations) over the life of a project, which helps explain why totals can move in either direction as projects evolve.

Why this threshold and timeframe?
- As of late September 2025, total PA obligations for DR-4827-NC were about $784.0M. Whether they will be at or above $950.0M by the end of 2025 depends on the pace of additional project approvals and any deobligations, creating meaningful uncertainty for forecasters.

Key definitions (with sources)
- DR-4827-NC: FEMA’s disaster number and page for North Carolina Tropical Storm Helene (https://www.fema.gov/disaster/4827).
- Public Assistance categories A–G: A (Debris removal), B (Emergency protective measures); C (Roads and bridges), D (Water control facilities), E (Public buildings and equipment), F (Public utilities), G (Parks, recreational, and other facilities).
- Obligations: “FEMA obligates funds to the Recipient based on the eligible total of an approved project. The Recipient then disburses funding to the Applicant.”.
- OpenFEMA PA Funded Projects Details datasets: Documentation describing fields such as disasterNumber, stateAbbreviation, and federalShareObligated, and noting financial data caveats and update mechanics.

Links to resolution sources
- FEMA DR-4827 page: https://www.fema.gov/disaster/4827 
- FEMA Public Assistance process and categories: https://www.fema.gov/assistance/public/process 
- OpenFEMA Public Assistance Funded Projects Details dataset pages: v1 https://www.fema.gov/openfema-data-page/public-assistance-funded-projects-details-v1 ; v2 https://www.fema.gov/openfema-data-page/public-assistance-funded-projects-details-v2
resolution_criteria:
Primary resolution rule (authoritative source):
- Resolve YES if, as of 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, the FEMA DR-4827 page (https://www.fema.gov/disaster/4827) displays Total Public Assistance Grants Dollars Obligated (i.e., the sum across Categories A–G, which are shown as Emergency Work A–B and Permanent Work C–G) greater than or equal to $950,000,000.00. Resolve NO otherwise.

How to read the FEMA page:
- Use the Public Assistance section of the DR-4827 page where “Dollars Obligated” are shown, typically separated into “Emergency Work (Categories A–B)” and “Permanent Work (Categories C–G).” The total “Public Assistance Grants Dollars Obligated” reported there is the value to compare against the $950,000,000.00 threshold.
- Currency and rounding: Use the exact dollar figure displayed (including cents if present). The threshold is $950,000,000.00; values equal to or greater than this amount resolve YES; values below resolve NO.
- Timing: The evaluation time is 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. If necessary, an archived capture (e.g., from the Internet Archive) closest to and not later than this timestamp may be used to evidence what the FEMA page displayed at the resolution time.

Backup resolution rule (if the FEMA DR-4827 page is unavailable or does not display a Total PA “Dollars Obligated” figure on or within 24 hours after the resolution timestamp):
- Use OpenFEMA’s Public Assistance Funded Projects Details dataset. Sum the field federalShareObligated for all records with disasterNumber = 4827 and stateAbbreviation = “NC”. If this aggregate is greater than or equal to $950,000,000.00 as of a dataset snapshot whose lastRefresh (or equivalent dataset-level timestamp) is on or before 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, resolve YES; otherwise resolve NO.
- Dataset references: v1 page (https://www.fema.gov/openfema-data-page/public-assistance-funded-projects-details-v1) and v2 page (https://www.fema.gov/openfema-data-page/public-assistance-funded-projects-details-v2). Note that the OpenFEMA documentation cautions this data is not intended for official federal reporting and may differ slightly from other sources; in case of discrepancy with the FEMA DR-4827 page, the FEMA page prevails.

Definitions and scope for resolution:
- “Public Assistance categories A–G” are defined by FEMA as Emergency Work (A, B) and Permanent Work (C, D, E, F, G).
- “Obligated” means FEMA has obligated funds to the Recipient for approved projects; totals can change over time due to additional obligations and deobligations across project versions.
- This question is resolved purely by the value at the resolution timestamp (not whether the total “ever” exceeded the threshold earlier).

question: Will the U.S. Import Price Index for “Pharmaceutical products (HS 30)” be at least 2.5% higher in November 2025 than in September 2025?
background:
What is being measured: The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) International Price Program (IPP) publishes monthly U.S. Import and Export Price Indexes (MXP) that track price changes for nonmilitary goods and services the U.S. imports and exports. BLS publishes merchandise goods price indexes using multiple classification systems, including a Harmonized System (HS) product-category table that explicitly lists “Pharmaceutical products (30)” for imports and exports. The HS (Harmonized Commodity Description and Coding System) is the internationally standardized product classification maintained by the World Customs Organization; HS Chapter 30 covers pharmaceutical products.

Where to find the series: In each monthly U.S. Import and Export Price Indexes news release on bls.gov, BLS includes a table titled “U.S. Import Price Indexes by Harmonized System,” under which “Pharmaceutical products (30)” appears with index levels and percent changes. The existence of that HS-based import table, and the inclusion of the “Pharmaceutical products (30)” line, is demonstrated in 2025 releases.

Release schedule relevant to resolution: According to BLS’s release schedule, the September 2025 U.S. Import and Export Price Indexes are scheduled for release on October 17, 2025, at 8:30 a.m. ET. The November 2025 U.S. Import and Export Price Indexes are scheduled for release on December 16, 2025, at 8:30 a.m. ET. This ensures both months needed for comparison will be published before the resolution date.

Recent context and status quo as of September 30, 2025: On September 25, 2025, President Trump announced a 100% tariff on imports of branded or patented pharmaceutical products effective October 1, 2025, with an exemption for companies building manufacturing plants in the United States (i.e., if construction has started). In response, the European Commission and Japan stated they had secured limits (caps) via joint statements with the U.S., indicating an all-inclusive 15% tariff ceiling for EU pharmaceuticals and comparable treatment for Japan. These policies create uncertainty for measured import prices by late 2025.

Latest available “Pharmaceutical products (HS 30)” import index levels and recent changes: In the August 2025 release, the HS-based import table shows “Pharmaceutical products (HS 30)” index levels of 156.4 in July 2025 and 158.0 in August 2025, with a 1.0% monthly increase from July to August. Earlier in mid-2025, the same HS-based import table showed index levels of 155.2 in April and 156.0 in May, alongside monthly changes of -0.3%, -0.3%, +1.4%, and +0.5% across early 2025. These figures suggest recent modest monthly movements with occasional upticks, making a two-month cumulative change of 2.5% plausible but not certain.

Definitions for clarity:
- U.S. Import Price Indexes (MXP): The official BLS series measuring changes in the prices of goods and services imported into the U.S..
- Harmonized System (HS): The WCO-maintained international product classification; Chapter 30 covers pharmaceutical products.
- “Pharmaceutical products (HS 30)” import index: The specific HS-category line in the BLS “U.S. Import Price Indexes by Harmonized System” table for imports that corresponds to HS Chapter 30 and is labeled “Pharmaceutical products (30)”.
- Index level: The numeric index value printed by BLS for a given month in the HS-based import table (e.g., 158.0), used directly for the calculation.

Why this forecast is non-trivial: The measured import prices for pharmaceuticals could be influenced by the new tariff policy, exemptions for companies building U.S. plants, and potential caps for EU/Japan-origin goods. At the same time, past monthly changes for HS 30 have typically been modest, so whether November 2025 will be at least 2.5% above September 2025 is uncertain and requires analysis of policy implementation, supply chain adjustments, and negotiation outcomes.
resolution_criteria:
Resolution date/time: The question will be resolved using data available no later than December 31, 2025 at 23:59 UTC.

Outcome determination:
- Identify the “Pharmaceutical products (30)” line in the “U.S. Import Price Indexes by Harmonized System” table within the BLS U.S. Import and Export Price Indexes news releases for September 2025 and November 2025.
- Extract the index levels printed for September 2025 and November 2025 on bls.gov.
- Compute the percent change as: (Index_Nov_2025 – Index_Sep_2025) / Index_Sep_2025.
- Resolve “Yes” if the computed percent change is greater than or equal to 0.025 (i.e., at least +2.5%); otherwise resolve “No.” Use the index levels as printed in the BLS release (to the precision provided there) for this computation.

Primary resolution source:
- BLS U.S. Import and Export Price Indexes news release page (where the HS tables are posted): https://www.bls.gov/news.release/ximpim.htm. The existence of the HS-based table including “Pharmaceutical products (30)” is evidenced in 2025 releases.

Publication schedule confirmation:
- September 2025 data release: October 17, 2025, at 8:30 a.m. ET.
- November 2025 data release: December 16, 2025, at 8:30 a.m. ET.

Contingencies:
- If November 2025 HS-based import data are not published on bls.gov by December 31, 2025 due to an official delay, resolve using October 2025 vs September 2025 with the same computation and threshold, relying on the October 2025 U.S. Import and Export Price Indexes release (scheduled November 18, 2025, 8:30 a.m. ET).
- If neither October nor November 2025 HS-based import data are available on bls.gov by December 31, 2025 due to an official delay, the question will be marked No Answer.

Notes:
- Only the import series for “Pharmaceutical products (HS 30)” is to be used; the export series is excluded.
- Later revisions published after December 31, 2025 will not be considered for resolution; use the first-published values available on bls.gov by the resolution cutoff.
- Time zones: Release times given in Eastern Time; resolution cutoff specified in UTC.

question: Will parties outside both the NDA and the INDIA bloc collectively win at least 10 seats in the 2025 Bihar Legislative Assembly election?
background:
Context and status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- The Bihar Legislative Assembly has 243 seats; 122 are needed for a majority. The 2025 Bihar Assembly election is expected to be held in October–November 2025 and conducted by the Election Commission of India (ECI).
- Major alliances in Bihar for 2025 (as currently described):
  • NDA (Bihar): Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), Janata Dal (United) [JD(U)], Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) [LJP(R)], Hindustani Awam Morcha [HAM(S)], Rashtriya Lok Morcha [RLM].
  • INDIA bloc / Mahagathbandhan (Bihar): Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD), Indian National Congress (INC), Communist Party of India (Marxist–Leninist) Liberation [CPI(ML)L], Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)], Communist Party of India [CPI], Vikassheel Insaan Party [VIP].
  • Definitions: The National Democratic Alliance (NDA) is a big-tent, multi-party political alliance led by the BJP. The Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance (INDIA) is a big-tent, multi-party opposition alliance led by the Indian National Congress.
- Parties outside these alliances have indicated they will contest, increasing uncertainty:
  • Jan Suraaj Party (JSP), founded by Prashant Kishor on 2024-10-02, intends to contest all 243 seats.
  • Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), and Plurals Party (founded by Pushpam Priya Choudhary) have also announced contest intentions.
- Recent baseline: In the 2020 Bihar Assembly election, seat distribution was NDA 125 (BJP 74; JD(U) 43; VIP 4; HAM(S) 4), MGB/INDIA 110 (RJD 75; INC 19; CPI(ML)L 12; CPI 2; CPM 2), and other parties/independent seats included AIMIM 5, BSP 1, LJP 1, Independent 1. This shows that non-NDA/non-INDIA parties winning a meaningful number of seats is plausible but not guaranteed.
- Resolution source: The ECI’s official results portal (results.eci.gov.in) publishes party-wise results for state assembly elections.
resolution_criteria:
Eligible period and time zone: The question concerns the 2025 Bihar Legislative Assembly general election. It will be resolved based on official results available between 00:00:00 UTC on 2025-10-15 and 23:59:59 UTC on 2025-12-31.

Definitions:
- “Seat” means a legislative assembly constituency in Bihar; the assembly has 243 seats. A “seat won” means a candidate declared elected for that constituency in the ECI’s official results (i.e., the ECI’s final party-wise tally).
- “Party-wise results” refers to the ECI’s published tally of seats won by each named political party for the Bihar Assembly election (as displayed on results.eci.gov.in for the relevant election).
- “NDA (Bihar)” members (for the purpose of this question, fixed for classification) are: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), Janata Dal (United) [JD(U)], Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) [LJP(R)], Hindustani Awam Morcha [HAM(S)], Rashtriya Lok Morcha [RLM].
- “INDIA bloc/Mahagathbandhan (Bihar)” members (for the purpose of this question, fixed for classification) are: Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD), Indian National Congress (INC), Communist Party of India (Marxist–Leninist) Liberation [CPI(ML)L], Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)], Communist Party of India [CPI], Vikassheel Insaan Party [VIP].
- “Outside both the NDA and INDIA bloc” means any political party that is not listed among the NDA (Bihar) members or INDIA/Mahagathbandhan (Bihar) members defined above. Independent candidates are not “parties” and do not count toward the total.

Resolution steps:
1) On or after the ECI’s declaration of results for the 2025 Bihar Assembly election and no later than 23:59:59 UTC on 2025-12-31, navigate to the ECI results portal (results.eci.gov.in) and open the party-wise results page for the Bihar Assembly election.
2) Identify the number of seats won (as shown on the ECI party-wise page) by each party that is “outside both alliances” per the fixed lists above. Do not include seats won by parties listed under NDA or INDIA blocs (per the above lists), and do not include independent winners.
3) Sum those seat counts. Resolve “Yes” if the sum is greater than or equal to 10; otherwise resolve “No.”

Edge cases and clarifications:
- Alliance classification is fixed to the member lists enumerated above to ensure unambiguous resolution, regardless of any changes in alliances or seat-sharing after this question is published.
- If the ECI has not published party-wise results for Bihar by 23:59:59 UTC on 2025-12-31, resolve “No.”
- If there are recounts or court-ordered changes after 2025-12-31, ignore them; use the ECI party-wise tally as it stood at 23:59:59 UTC on 2025-12-31.

Primary source of truth: ECI party-wise results for the 2025 Bihar Assembly election (results.eci.gov.in). Supporting context on alliances and election timing: 2025 Bihar Legislative Assembly election page ; NDA definition ; INDIA definition. Baseline historical performance: 2020 Bihar Assembly results.

question: EU to adopt a binding measure curtailing or penalizing Druzhba pipeline crude to Hungary/Slovakia by year-end 2025
background:
Context and status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- Druzhba pipeline and relevant flows: The Druzhba (Friendship) pipeline is one of the world’s longest oil pipeline networks, originating in Russia and splitting into a northern and a southern branch. The southern branch runs through Ukraine, splitting to supply Slovakia and Hungary, serving refineries in those countries.
- EU publication and legal act definitions: EU binding legal acts are published in the Official Journal (OJ) L series, which contains EU legislation. Regulations are binding in their entirety and directly applicable in all Member States; decisions are also binding in their entirety (both under Article 288 TFEU).
- Commodity and customs classifications: For EU sanctions and trade measures, "crude oil" corresponds to Combined Nomenclature (CN) code 2709 00; "petroleum products" correspond to CN code 2710 (distinct from crude).
- Definitions of trade measures that may be considered: A tariff is a tax or duty imposed on imports, paid by the importer. An import quota is a trade restriction that sets a physical limit on the quantity of a good that can be imported in a given period.
- Current EU stance and pipeline exemptions: Following the EU’s ban on seaborne Russian crude, EU Russian oil imports were cut by about 90%. Hungary and Slovakia still import Russian oil via pipeline.
- Latest reporting (Sept 2025): The EU is considering trade measures specifically targeting remaining Russian oil imports via the Druzhba pipeline to Hungary and Slovakia. Political context includes public pushback by Slovakia against pressure to reduce Russian energy purchases, citing cost and contractual constraints.
- Resolution sources: The OJ L series provides the authoritative publication of adopted EU legal acts. Council press releases are official announcements of adopted measures and can confirm adoption details.

Why this question is interesting/high-entropy: There is active consideration of measures aimed at pipeline crude flows to Hungary and Slovakia, but the form (tariff, cap, ban), scope, and political coalition remain uncertain, creating genuine forecasting uncertainty by Q4 2025.
resolution_criteria:
Start and end time window:
- Eligible acts must be adopted and published between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) is the global time standard used to regulate clocks and time zones.

Definitions and scope:
- "Druzhba pipeline crude to Hungary/Slovakia" means crude oil (CN code 2709 00) delivered by pipeline via the Druzhba southern branch into Hungary and/or Slovakia (i.e., pipeline flows into those Member States via the southern leg described in the Druzhba pipeline entry). Imports via other pipelines (e.g., non-Druzhba networks) or seaborne deliveries are excluded.
- "Binding legal act" means a Regulation or a Decision of the European Union (as defined under Article 288 TFEU) that is binding in its entirety; directives, recommendations, notices, guidelines, proposals, and communications do not count for resolution purposes.
- "Curtails, penalizes, or conditions imports" means the legal act explicitly applies to crude oil under CN 2709 00 delivered by pipeline via Druzhba into Hungary and/or Slovakia and imposes at least one of the following on those specific flows:
  (a) a non-zero import duty/tariff ;
  (b) a quantitative import cap/"import quota" limiting volumes during a defined period ;
  (c) a prohibition or suspension of purchase, import, or transfer of such crude;
  (d) a tariff-rate quota combining a quantitative cap and tariff.

Resolution (Yes/No):
- Resolves Yes if, within the time window, the EU adopts and publishes in the Official Journal L series a binding Regulation or Decision that explicitly targets crude oil (CN 2709 00) delivered by pipeline via the Druzhba southern branch into Hungary and/or Slovakia and imposes one or more of the measures listed above.
- Resolves No otherwise.

Clarifications (what does and does not count):
- The act must clearly identify the covered flows—for example, by referencing pipeline deliveries, the Druzhba southern branch, and/or imports into Hungary and/or Slovakia by pipeline—and must apply to crude oil (CN 2709 00). Measures that only address petroleum products (CN 2710) or that do not clearly apply to the Druzhba pipeline flows into Hungary/Slovakia do not count.
- General, EU-wide measures that apply to all Russian crude or all energy imports without specific language identifying pipeline deliveries into Hungary and/or Slovakia (or the Druzhba southern branch) do not count for this question, even if they incidentally affect those flows.
- Non-binding instruments (e.g., proposals, guidelines, notices to operators, communications, roadmaps) do not count.

Verification sources:
- Primary: Publication in the Official Journal L series (OJ L), which contains EU legislation and authentic texts of adopted Regulations and Decisions.
- Secondary (if OJ L publication is delayed but the act is adopted within the time window): An official Council press release explicitly announcing adoption of the act, including its formal identifier (e.g., Regulation (EU) YYYY/NNN or Decision (EU) YYYY/NNN), will be accepted for resolution purposes.

Notes for resolvers:
- The forecast window is designed to align with recent reporting that the EU is weighing measures targeting Druzhba pipeline flows to Hungary and Slovakia. The background provides current status and definitions to verify scope: ongoing pipeline imports by Hungary and Slovakia despite a 90% reduction in EU Russian oil imports from the seaborne ban , and the commodity classification distinctions (CN 2709 vs. 2710) that determine whether a measure targets crude or refined products.

question: Between 2025-04-24 and 2025-12-31 (UTC), will the European Commission adopt and publish an additional DMA non-compliance decision and/or impose a DMA fine on Meta that explicitly concerns its advertising model (beyond the 2025-04-23 decision)?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01:
- On 2025-04-23, the European Commission adopted a non-compliance decision against Meta under the Digital Markets Act (DMA) and imposed a €200 million fine. The decision found Meta’s prior “consent or pay” advertising model non-compliant because it did not give users the required specific choice to opt for a service that uses less of their personal data but is otherwise equivalent. The Commission stated it is assessing Meta’s updated option introduced in November 2024 that allegedly uses less personal data for ads. Commission materials from the same date also describe the breach as failing to give consumers the choice of a service that uses less personal data.
- The 2025-04-23 decision explicitly limited its scope to Meta’s original “Consent or Pay” advertising model for the period March–November 2024 and noted this was without prejudice to the Commission’s ability to investigate Meta’s “Additional Ads” (i.e., less-personalized ads) option later.
- In November 2024, Meta announced a free “Less Personalized Ads” (LPA) option in the EU/EEA and Switzerland, describing it as relying on less data (primarily contextual signals from a current session plus minimal data such as age, location, gender, and ad engagement) and noting that ad breaks would be introduced in this low-data mode. Meta also reduced the price of the “Subscription for No Ads” at that time.
- Subsequent reporting indicated Meta was unlikely to propose further changes to its model in mid-2025 despite Commission warnings of potential daily fines, and suggested new EU antitrust/DMA charges could be likely, underscoring ongoing enforcement risk in 2025.

Why this is forecastable: The Commission has said it is assessing Meta’s updated ads option  and expressly left open further action beyond its April 2025 decision. However, follow-on decisions or fines are uncertain in timing and substance, making year-end 2025 a plausible but non-trivial window.

Key definitions and scope for this question:
- European Commission: The EU’s executive institution responsible for enforcing the DMA. For resolution, we rely on official Commission publications (Press Corner, Digital Strategy DMA pages) and the Official Journal/EUR-Lex.
- Digital Markets Act (DMA): Regulation (EU) 2022/1925 on contestable and fair markets in the digital sector.
- Meta: Meta Platforms, Inc. (provider of Facebook and Instagram in the EU/EEA).
- Advertising model (for this question): Meta’s approach to serving ads to users of Facebook and/or Instagram in the EU/EEA, including but not limited to: (a) the “consent or pay”/“pay or consent” model found non-compliant on 2025-04-23; and (b) the “Less Personalized Ads” (also referred to as “Additional Ads” or “less-personalized ads”) option introduced in November 2024, which Meta describes as relying primarily on contextual signals from a user’s current session and a minimal set of data (age, location, gender, and ad engagement), potentially with unskippable ad breaks.
- Non-compliance decision (for this question): A formal Commission decision under the DMA finding that Meta has not complied with one or more DMA obligations, akin to the decision adopted on 2025-04-23 against Meta’s “Consent or Pay” model.
- Fine (for this question): A pecuniary penalty imposed by the Commission under the DMA within a decision, distinct from periodic penalty payments. Only fines count for a YES outcome; periodic penalty payments do not count.

Status quo summary as of 2025-10-01:
- Meta has one DMA non-compliance decision and fine already adopted on 2025-04-23 regarding its earlier model.
- The Commission has publicly stated it is assessing Meta’s November 2024 less-personalized ads option , and the April 2025 decision’s scope suggests further action could target the updated model.
- Media reporting in July 2025 suggested the Commission warned of possible daily fines and that additional charges were likely, while Meta was unlikely to make further changes at that time.
resolution_criteria:
Resolution timing: This question resolves based on information available up to 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. Eligible actions must occur between 2025-04-24 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Question: Will the European Commission adopt and publish an additional DMA non-compliance decision and/or impose a DMA fine on Meta that explicitly concerns Meta’s advertising model within the eligibility window?

Operational rules:
- “Additional” means beyond the Commission decision adopted on 2025-04-23 concerning Meta’s advertising model (document number C(2025) 2091; scope limited to March–November 2024). Any new decision must be a separate decision adopted on or after 2025-04-24.
- “Adopt and publish” is satisfied if, by the resolution timestamp, at least one of the following is publicly accessible for the new action: (a) a Commission Press Corner press release describing the adoption of the decision; (b) a Commission Digital Strategy/DMA news post describing the adoption; (c) the decision or its summary notice in the Official Journal/EUR-Lex (e.g., a C-series summary). Examples of such sources for the April 23 action are available on Commission sites and EUR-Lex.
- “Explicitly concerns Meta’s advertising model” means the decision text and/or official Commission communication states that the subject matter pertains to Meta’s ads model on Facebook and/or Instagram (e.g., “pay or consent,” “less personalized ads,” “Additional Ads,” or equivalent references to ad personalization/data use in the EU/EEA). Decisions focused on unrelated conduct (e.g., Marketplace tying under antitrust law) do not count.
- What counts for YES: Any of the following adopted and published within the window: (1) a new DMA non-compliance decision against Meta that concerns its advertising model (fine included or not); or (2) a Commission decision under the DMA imposing a fine on Meta that the Commission states concerns its advertising model (even if combined with a non-compliance decision). Periodic penalty payments alone do not count as a “fine.”
- What does NOT count: (a) Informal statements, speeches, leaks, or media reports without an adopted decision; (b) actions under other legal frameworks (e.g., DSA, GDPR, antitrust) unless expressly stated by the Commission as a DMA decision; (c) periodic penalty payments without an accompanying fine; (d) any decision adopted before 2025-04-24 or after 2025-12-31 UTC.

Resolution sources and precedence:
- Primary sources: European Commission official publications (Press Corner and Digital Strategy DMA news pages) describing the adoption of the decision/fine.
- Secondary/backup: The Official Journal/EUR-Lex publication of the decision or its summary (e.g., C-series).
- If primary and secondary sources conflict, the decision text/summary on EUR-Lex prevails.
- If needed for confirmation of adoption timing or scope, reputable wire services (e.g., Reuters) may be used as supporting evidence, but cannot substitute for the absence of an adopted Commission decision.

Adjudication:
- YES if, by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, such an additional DMA non-compliance decision and/or DMA fine concerning Meta’s advertising model has been adopted and published as defined above. NO otherwise.

Notes:
- The Commission’s April 23, 2025 decision and €200m fine regarding Meta’s earlier model are excluded from counting for this question; they are background only.
- The April 2025 decision’s stated scope (March–November 2024 original model) and the Commission’s ongoing assessment of the November 2024 “less personalized ads” option motivate the plausibility of further action in 2025.

question: Between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, will an official financing arrangement for Iran’s Sirik nuclear power project be publicly disclosed beyond the headline $25 billion figure?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- On 2025-09-26, Iran and Russia announced a $25 billion agreement for four nuclear power units to be built in the Sirik region of Iran’s southern Hormozgan province, totaling roughly 5 GW of capacity (about 1,255 MW per unit). Early reports name the parties as Iran Hormoz Company (on behalf of the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran, AEOI) and Rosatom (Russia’s state nuclear corporation). These reports did not disclose specific financing terms (e.g., lenders, loan amounts, interest rates, tenors, or export credit commitments).

What counts as “financing arrangements” in this question:
- For clarity, the question is about whether concrete financing details for the Sirik nuclear project are publicly disclosed during the specified window. Typical elements include, but are not limited to: a signed intergovernmental loan, a loan agreement (see definition: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loan_agreement), a credit line, export credit agency support/guarantee (see definition: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Export_credit_agency), payment terms (e.g., deferred payment schedule), interest rate/benchmark, tenor/maturity, grace period, or sovereign guarantee terms.

Project definition and parties:
- “Sirik nuclear project” refers to the four nuclear power units in Sirik, Hormozgan, associated with the $25 billion agreement announced on 2025-09-26, with an aggregate capacity near 5 GW and approx. 1,255 MW per unit.
- “Either party” refers to Rosatom (including subsidiaries) and the AEOI (including Iran Hormoz Company).

Why this is uncertain and decision‑useful:
- Large nuclear projects frequently involve complex financing structures (e.g., intergovernmental loans, export credit guarantees, or staged payment terms). However, initial announcements often omit financing specifics, and sanctions/political dynamics can delay disclosure. There is a plausible chance that concrete terms emerge within the next ~2.5 months, but it is far from guaranteed, making this a non-trivial forecast.

Key term definitions (for unambiguous resolution):
- “Publicly disclosed” means published in a publicly accessible official channel, such as an official website or official government gazette (see “Government gazette”: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_gazette), or an official press release (see “Press release”: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Press_release) or an official report posted by the relevant entity. See acceptance criteria below for specifics.
- “Specific financing arrangement” means a disclosure that includes at least one concrete financing element tied to the Sirik project, such as: identity of lender(s) or guarantor(s), a numerical loan amount and currency, tenor/maturity, interest rate formula (e.g., SOFR/EURIBOR plus margin), existence/amount of an export credit guarantee, or defined payment terms (e.g., % milestone payments, grace period, repayment schedule). General statements that financing “will be arranged” or that the deal is “worth $25bn” do not count.

Current public reporting baseline:
- Initial coverage confirms the agreement’s value and scope but notes no financing specifics have been made public as of the announcement date.

Suggested places to check during the resolution window (non-exhaustive):
- Rosatom press center/news pages and official documents.
- AEOI and Iran Hormoz Company official publications.
- Official government channels in Iran and Russia (e.g., ministries of finance/economy, central banks, state export credit agencies, official gazettes).
- Credible wire services or state media that reproduce/cite primary official documents (e.g., IRNA, TASS, Reuters, Xinhua, AP, Bloomberg) when they directly quote or link to official documents. Ultimately, the resolution depends on the acceptance criteria below, not on any single outlet.

Cited sources establishing the status quo and project definition:
- Xinhua English coverage detailing four units in Sirik (~1,255 MW each, total ~5,020 MW), parties (Iran Hormoz Company and Rosatom project company), and that financing terms were not disclosed.
- Al Jazeera coverage noting the $25bn amount, four units in Sirik, total capacity ~5 GW, and no financing specifics mentioned.
- POWER Magazine coverage reporting four plants in Sirik with unit capacity ~1,255 MW and stating no financing terms or timeline were specified.
resolution_criteria:
What resolves “Yes”:
- Resolve “Yes” if, between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC (inclusive), there is a public disclosure that meets all of the following:
  1) Source: The disclosure appears in at least one of the following channels:
     - An official website, official report, official government gazette, or official press release of Rosatom (or subsidiaries), the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran (AEOI), Iran Hormoz Company, or a relevant national government entity (e.g., finance/economy ministry, central bank, sovereign wealth fund, or export credit agency) of Russia or Iran; OR
     - A credible news/wire or state-media article that reproduces or explicitly cites such an official document/press release/gazette entry (e.g., by quoting from it and identifying it as the source) and provides enough detail to verify the financing terms. If relying on such reporting, the resolver must be able to identify the underlying official document or direct quotation.
  2) Content: The disclosure includes at least one concrete financing element for the Sirik project, such as: lender/guarantor identity; a numerical loan amount and currency; tenor/maturity; interest rate formula (fixed or floating benchmark plus margin); grace period; sovereign guarantee terms; export credit agency support/guarantee with amounts or limits; or specific payment terms (e.g., milestone payment percentages or repayment schedule).
  3) Project linkage: The disclosure explicitly ties the financing element(s) to the Sirik nuclear project defined in Background (the four-unit, ~$25bn project in Sirik, Hormozgan announced on 2025-09-26).

What does NOT count:
- Restatements of the total deal value (~$25bn) without any financing elements.
- Generic language like “financing will be arranged” or “to be determined,” or references to “banking facilities” without lender identity or amounts.
- Anonymous or speculative media reports not citing a primary official document or official press statement.
- Disclosures published before 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC or after 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC (all times UTC).

Time window and timezone:
- Only disclosures published between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC (inclusive) are eligible. Times are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

Resolution process:
- The resolver will verify whether at least one qualifying disclosure exists within the time window that satisfies the Source, Content, and Project linkage requirements above. If yes, resolve “Yes”; otherwise, resolve “No.”

Notes:
- Definitions used: Loan agreement (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loan_agreement); Export credit agency (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Export_credit_agency); Press release (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Press_release); Government gazette (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_gazette).
- The project scope and absence of financing specifics at announcement are established by cited coverage.

question: By 2025-12-31, will OJK report year-over-year growth in outstanding financing for Indonesia’s fintech P2P lending (LPBBTI) sector for September 2025 of at least 22.0%?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01:
- Metric and recent levels: Otoritas Jasa Keuangan (OJK) has been reporting year-over-year (YoY) growth rates for the fintech peer-to-peer lending sector, which it variously refers to as Layanan Pendanaan Bersama Berbasis Teknologi Informasi (LPBBTI) and “Pinjaman Daring (Pindar).” For example, OJK’s August 2025 RDKB press release states: “Pada industri Pinjaman Daring (Pindar), outstanding pembiayaan di Juli 2025 tumbuh 22,01 persen yoy (Juni 2025: 25,06 persen yoy)”. Earlier in 2025, OJK reported 31.06% YoY in February 2025 and 29.94% YoY in January 2025 for outstanding financing in the fintech P2P sector. These points indicate deceleration through mid-2025 from very high YoY rates early in the year to ~22% in July 2025.
- Terminology and sector scope: OJK’s formal name for the P2P lending sector is LPBBTI. OJK defines LPBBTI as a financial service that connects lenders and borrowers to enter into loan agreements in rupiah directly through electronic systems; OJK also refers to this as Peer-to-Peer Lending/Pinjaman Online (i.e., fintech P2P lending). OJK’s RDKB press releases sometimes use the synonym “Pinjaman Daring (Pindar)” alongside LPBBTI when citing this sector’s statistics.
- What YoY means: Year-over-year (YoY) compares a value for a given period to the same period one year earlier. A standard formula is (current period’s value ÷ prior-year same period’s value) - 1, expressed in percent; financial publications commonly present YoY as a percentage change. In OJK documents, “yoy” denotes this year-on-year percentage change.
- Data source and publication pattern: OJK publishes monthly “Statistik P2P Lending” as downloadable files (often Excel); e.g., the “Statistik P2P Lending Periode Desember 2024” page links to an XLSX file and shows a publication date of 2025-03-04, implying a lag of roughly 2 months or more for monthly statistical spreadsheets. OJK also publishes monthly RDKB (Rapat Dewan Komisioner Bulanan) press releases that summarize sector indicators and have included LPBBTI/Pindar YoY growth for outstanding financing (e.g., July 2025 at 22.01% YoY). For timely resolution within 2025, the RDKB press release(s) are expected to be the primary source for the September 2025 YoY figure.

Why this threshold and month: With YoY growth around 22% in July 2025 (down from ~31% in February), a 22.0% threshold for September 2025 sits near the recent trajectory, plausibly allowing either outcome (≥22.0% or <22.0%) by late 2025 given macroeconomic conditions, regulatory developments, and risk appetite in the sector.

Definitions (for clarity and consistency):
- OJK (Otoritas Jasa Keuangan): Indonesia’s Financial Services Authority, a government agency regulating and supervising financial services.
- LPBBTI (Layanan Pendanaan Bersama Berbasis Teknologi Informasi): The P2P lending sector as formally defined by OJK (also called Peer-to-Peer Lending/Pinjaman Online/fintech P2P).
- Outstanding financing (outstanding pembiayaan): The stock of loans outstanding in the LPBBTI sector, as referenced by OJK when it reports YoY growth (e.g., “outstanding pembiayaan … tumbuh … yoy”).
- Year-over-year (YoY) growth: The percentage change of a metric for a period compared to the same period one year prior; e.g., for September 2025, the comparison is to September 2024.
resolution_criteria:
Question: By 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, will OJK report that the year-over-year (YoY) growth in outstanding financing (outstanding pembiayaan) for the LPBBTI (fintech P2P lending) sector for September 2025 is at least 22.0%?

- What counts as “report”: Any official OJK publication hosted on the ojk.go.id domain (including, but not limited to, Siaran Pers RDKB press releases, accompanying OJK infographics, or OJK statistical pages) that explicitly states the YoY growth percentage for outstanding financing in the LPBBTI/P2P/Pinjaman Daring (Pindar) sector for September 2025. Examples of the type of qualifying sources include RDKB press releases that state “outstanding pembiayaan … tumbuh … yoy” for a given month ; monthly “Statistik P2P Lending” pages also qualify if they explicitly present the September 2025 YoY figure and are published by the deadline.
- Exact metric to use: Use OJK’s explicitly stated YoY percentage for outstanding financing in the LPBBTI/P2P/Pinjaman Daring sector for September 2025, as written by OJK. Do not recompute or re-round the figure.
- Threshold interpretation: “At least 22.0%” means greater than or equal to 22.0% based on the percentage number as published by OJK. For example, 22.0% or 22.01% qualifies as YES; 21.99% does not.
- Synonyms allowed: Treat LPBBTI, “fintech P2P lending,” “P2P Lending,” and “Pinjaman Daring (Pindar)” as the same sector for resolution purposes, consistent with OJK usage. The phrase “outstanding pembiayaan … tumbuh … yoy” is the target statistic.
- Priority among multiple OJK publications: If multiple OJK documents published on or before 2025-12-31 provide a September 2025 YoY figure and they conflict, use the one with the latest OJK publication date. If they are consistent, any one suffices.
- Resolution source expectation: OJK frequently reports LPBBTI/Pindar YoY growth in monthly RDKB press releases (e.g., 22.01% YoY for July 2025). If, contrary to expectation, no OJK publication available by 2025-12-31 includes the September 2025 YoY figure, resolve this question as NO (because the question specifically asks whether OJK reports such a figure by that date, not whether the true value meets the threshold).
- Timezone: All deadlines in this section are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

How to resolve:
1) Search OJK’s official site (ojk.go.id) for RDKB press releases and/or infographics published between 2025-10-01 and 2025-12-31 that mention LPBBTI/P2P/Pinjaman Daring and present the September 2025 YoY figure for outstanding financing. If found, read the exact percentage.
2) If step 1 fails, check the “Statistik P2P Lending Periode [Month Year]” pages to see if an entry published by 2025-12-31 includes the September 2025 YoY figure (noting that such pages are often published with a lag).
3) Apply the threshold rule to the OJK-published percentage and resolve YES if ≥ 22.0%, NO otherwise.

Background sources cited in this criterion are examples of qualifying RDKB press releases and monthly statistic pages and establish the expected format and phrasing. The definition of YoY and sector terminology are provided for clarity and consistency.

question: Brazil: Will PL 4501/2024 be received by the Finance and Taxation Committee (CFT) between 2025-10-15 and 2025-12-31 (BRT)?
background:
Overview and current status (as of 2025-10-01)
- Proposition: PL 4501/2024 (Projeto de Lei 4501/2024), idProposicao 2471228, proposes creating a Sovereign Strategic Bitcoin Reserve (“Reserva Estratégica Soberana de Bitcoins”) held by the Federal Government.
- Author and regime: Authored by Deputy Eros Biondini (PL-MG). It is under ordinary regime and subject to conclusiva (final) decision by committees per Art. 24 II of the RICD.
- Committees designated in despacho: The current despacho (10/12/2024) sent the bill to the committees of Desenvolvimento Econômico (CDE), Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação (CCTI), Finanças e Tributação (CFT), and Constituição e Justiça e de Cidadania (CCJC). This establishes that CFT (Comissão de Finanças e Tributaçāo) is one of the committees tasked with analyzing the bill.
- Recent 2025 actions in CDE: A favorable rapporteur opinion (Parecer do Relator) in CDE was posted on 06/06/2025; the bill was placed “Pronta para Pauta” in CDE; and on 27/08/2025, a Requerimento de Retirada de Pauta was approved, withdrawing it from that day’s agenda.

What forecasters should know about how progress is recorded
- Source of truth page: The Câmara dos Deputados “Ficha de Tramitação” (progress docket) for PL 4501/2024 shows the despacho and a chronological “Tramitação” table of actions and the órgão (body) responsible for each action. The despacho dated 10/12/2024 reads: “Às Comissões de Desenvolvimento Econômico; Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação; Finanças e Tributação (Mérito e Art. 54, RICD) e Constituição e Justiça e de Cidadania (Art. 54 RICD)”.
- Where “arrival at CFT” would appear: Movement to CFT will be reflected by a dated entry in the Tramitação table indicating the proposition has been transmitted to or received by CFT, typically showing the órgão as CFT and/or an action text indicating receipt/distribution to the Comissão de Finanças e Tributação. The despacho that lists intended committees (10/12/2024) does not, by itself, evidence that the bill has actually reached CFT.

Links for definitions/context (non-exhaustive)
- PL 4501/2024 Ficha de Tramitação (official docket): https://www.camara.leg.br/proposicoesWeb/fichadetramitacao?idProposicao=2471228 
- Comissão de Finanças e Tributação (CFT): https://www.camara.leg.br/commissoes?tri=finan%E7as-e-tributa%E7%E3o (authoritative committee portal). Note: this link is provided for context; the forecast resolves strictly to the Ficha de Tramitação for PL 4501/2024.
resolution_criteria:
Question
- Resolve Yes if PL 4501/2024 is recorded as having reached the Comissão de Finanças e Tributação (CFT) between 2025-10-15 00:00 and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 Brasília time (BRT; UTC−03:00), inclusive. Resolve No otherwise.

Operational definitions
- “Reached CFT” means there exists at least one entry on the official Câmara dos Deputados Ficha de Tramitação for PL 4501/2024 (https://www.camara.leg.br/proposicoesWeb/fichadetramitacao?idProposicao=2471228) with a date within the time window and either:
  1) the órgão listed as “CFT” (Comissão de Finanças e Tributação), or
  2) the action text clearly indicating transmission to or receipt by CFT (e.g., “À CFT”, “Recebido na Comissão de Finanças e Tributação”, “Distribuição para CFT”). 
- The despacho dated 10/12/2024 that generically sends the bill “Às Comissões de Desenvolvimento Econômico; Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação; Finanças e Tributação; e Constituição e Justiça e de Cidadania” does not count as having reached CFT for purposes of this question; only a subsequent Tramitação entry evidencing arrival at or receipt by CFT counts.

Time window and timezone
- Eligible entries must be dated between 2025-10-15 and 2025-12-31, inclusive, where the date used is the date displayed on the Ficha de Tramitação entry (interpreted in Brasília time, BRT; UTC−03:00). If an entry includes a specific time-of-day, that time is interpreted as BRT.

Source of truth and resolution
- Primary and sufficient source: the Câmara dos Deputados Ficha de Tramitação for PL 4501/2024 at https://www.camara.leg.br/proposicoesWeb/fichadetramitacao?idProposicao=2471228.
- The question resolves immediately to Yes upon such an entry appearing within the window; otherwise it resolves to No at 2025-12-31 23:59:59 BRT.
- If the Ficha page is temporarily unavailable at resolution time, resolution should be based on the first accessible state of the page captured no later than 2026-01-07 23:59:59 BRT (e.g., via cached/archived copy), provided it reflects the official Ficha content as of the deadline. The despacho listing the committees on 10/12/2024 alone is insufficient evidence of reaching CFT.

question: On 2025-12-31 (IRST), will Bonbast’s USD “Sell” rate be ≤110,000 toman (i.e., ≤1,100,000 rials) per USD?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30:
- Currency units and codes. The Iranian rial is Iran’s official currency (ISO 4217 code: IRR). In everyday usage and on Bonbast.com, prices are often quoted in toman; Bonbast’s archive explicitly states: “All prices are in Iranian Toman (1 Toman = 10 Rials)”. Iran Standard Time (IRST) is UTC+03:30, and Iran abolished daylight saving time in September 2022, so IRST is observed year-round.
- Free-market vs. official rate. Bonbast clarifies that foreign exchange in Iran has an official government rate and a free-market rate; it displays free-market rates. The official rate is stated as 42,000 rials (4,200 toman) per USD and has little practical use for individuals; most everyday transactions reference the free-market rate.
- Current/recent levels (late September 2025). Bonbast’s archive for 2025-09-29 shows USD Sell=110,850 toman and Buy=110,750 toman. The AlanChand USD page lists the market price at roughly 1,135,000 rials per USD on 2025-09-30. Multiple outlets reported the rial near a record low around 1.12 million rials per USD on 2025-09-28, citing Bonbast and AlanChand. Earlier in 2025, Reuters reported a record low around 1,039,000 rials per USD, attributing its source to Bonbast.com, which “gathers live data from Iranian exchanges”.
- Why this threshold? As of late September 2025, the free-market USD rate is hovering around 111–114 thousand toman (1.11–1.14 million rials) per USD. A threshold of 110,000 toman sets the question near the current level, increasing uncertainty and forecast value.

Key definitions and links for forecasters:
- Iranian rial (IRR): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iranian_rial 
- Iranian toman: colloquial unit; Bonbast quotes in toman; Bonbast archive note: “1 Toman = 10 Rials” https://www.bonbast.com/archive 
- Free-market vs official rate on Bonbast: https://www.bonbast.com/faq 
- Iran Standard Time (IRST, UTC+03:30): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_Standard_Time 
- Bonbast live/archives: https://www.bonbast.com/ and https://www.bonbast.com/archive 
- Additional context on recent levels: AlanChand USD page https://alanchand.com/en/currencies-price/usd ; late-Sept reporting citing Bonbast and AlanChand ; Reuters March 2025 note on Bonbast sourcing.
resolution_criteria:
Primary resolution (single source of truth):
- Resolve YES if the Bonbast.com Archive page for the date 2025-12-31 lists the USD “Sell” price as less than or equal to 110,000 (toman). Resolve NO if it lists the USD “Sell” price as greater than 110,000. All Bonbast prices are in toman; by Bonbast’s own notation, 1 toman = 10 rials. The “USD” row and the “Sell” column on that Archive page are the only values used for resolution (ignore the “Buy” column). The relevant page is: https://www.bonbast.com/archive.

Interpretation and definitions:
- “USD ‘Sell’ price” means the number in the “Sell” column for the “USD” row as presented by Bonbast on the Archive entry for 2025-12-31. This value is denominated in toman, not rials; for reference only, ≤110,000 toman corresponds to ≤1,100,000 rials at 1 toman = 10 rials.
- Date and time zone: The Archive is date-based. Use the entry dated 2025-12-31 on Bonbast’s Archive, which reflects Iran local date (IRST, UTC+03:30).

Fallbacks (only if strictly necessary):
1) If the Bonbast Archive entry for 2025-12-31 is not available by the time of adjudication, use a capture of the Bonbast homepage or Archive for 2025-12-31 obtained from a credible public web archive (e.g., Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine) or a timestamped screenshot by the resolver, reading the USD “Sell” value as displayed (still in toman). The goal is to recover the USD “Sell” value that Bonbast displayed for 2025-12-31.
2) If Bonbast is entirely inaccessible on 2025-12-31 and no credible capture exists, use AlanChand’s USD page for 2025-12-31 to read the free-market USD price in rials/toman, provided that page clearly states a date of 2025-12-31; convert to toman/rial as needed and resolve against the same ≤110,000 toman threshold. If both Bonbast and AlanChand are unavailable for that date, the question is unresolved until one is accessible.

Out-of-scope and clarifications:
- Official exchange rates (e.g., 42,000 rials per USD) are not used for resolution; this question specifically concerns the free-market rate as tracked by Bonbast.
- Intraday fluctuations or other times of day are irrelevant; only the value Bonbast records for the date 2025-12-31 (Archive) is used.
- No rounding is needed; compare the exact integer displayed by Bonbast in the Archive “Sell” column to the integer threshold 110,000. If the Archive displays a range or multiple entries for the date, use the value that Bonbast presents in the Archive table for USD/Sell (if multiple are shown, use the last listed USD/Sell value for that date).

question: By December 31, 2025 (23:59:59 UTC), will a signed definitive agreement be publicly announced to transfer the right to operate TikTok’s U.S. service to a U.S.-organized entity in which ByteDance and its affiliates will own less than 20% on a fully diluted basis at closing?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-09-30:
- On Sept 25, 2025, the U.S. President signed an order stating that a proposed deal framework for TikTok’s U.S. operations satisfies statutory requirements, with enforcement of the earlier divest-or-ban law delayed to allow completion. Reporting indicates the plan envisions ByteDance owning under 20% of the new U.S. venture, with the algorithm controlled in the U.S..
- The New York Times reported the envisioned U.S. TikTok company at about a $14 billion valuation and noted negotiators were given until mid-January to finalize the deal.
- Reuters reported that Americans would hold six of seven board seats in the new U.S. TikTok entity, with ByteDance choosing one, and that the recommendation algorithm would be secured, retrained, and operated in the U.S. outside ByteDance’s control.
- Additional analysis suggested a joint venture may handle data security and algorithm licensing/management, with ByteDance as a significant minority stakeholder (around 20%) in that JV and potentially receiving substantial licensing or other fees tied to U.S. profits; the exact structure remains fluid.

Why this is forecastable and uncertain:
- There is clear political and regulatory momentum toward a divestiture that brings TikTok’s U.S. operations into compliance with U.S. law, paired with a specific ownership threshold (<20%) and U.S. control provisions.
- However, material deal details (e.g., which entity precisely holds U.S. operating rights, the precise ByteDance stake across layered entities, and final algorithm control/licensing arrangements) were still being negotiated as of late September 2025 , creating genuine uncertainty about whether a definitive, binding agreement meeting all criteria will be signed and publicly announced by year-end.

Key concepts and where to find evidence:
- For public companies, “entry into a material definitive agreement” is disclosed on Form 8‑K, Item 1.01, typically within four business days; these filings are accessible on the SEC’s EDGAR system. 8‑K is a current report intended to disclose timely, material events, and Item 1.01 covers material agreements not in the ordinary course of business.
- Definitions used below are standard in U.S. securities and tax contexts: “affiliate” and “control” per SEC Rule 405 ; “U.S.-organized entity” (i.e., domestic corporation) per IRS guidance ; examples of “definitive agreements” in M&A include stock/asset purchase agreements and merger agreements. Ownership measured “on a fully diluted basis” includes all shares that could be created by convertible securities, options, warrants, etc..

Primary sources likely to provide resolution evidence include official company press releases and SEC filings (e.g., Form 8‑K Item 1.01 by any public company party), with corroboration by wire services and major outlets such as Reuters or the New York Times.
resolution_criteria:
Time window and scope:
- Start: 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC
- End: 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC
- Geography/time standard: All dates/times are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

Resolution:
- Resolve Yes if, between the start and end times above, a signed definitive agreement is publicly announced by at least one principal party (e.g., ByteDance, TikTok, the acquirer/investor consortium, or a public-company party via a Form 8‑K Item 1.01) that satisfies all conditions below. Otherwise resolve No.

Conditions that must all be satisfied:
1) Definitive agreement signed: There is a written, legally binding, fully executed agreement to consummate the transaction (e.g., stock purchase agreement, asset purchase agreement, merger agreement, or equivalent). Non‑binding term sheets, memoranda of understanding (MOUs), or letters of intent (LOIs) do not qualify. If any public company is a party, an Item 1.01 Form 8‑K would typically be filed within four business days of entry and can serve as evidence.

2) Transfer of the right to operate TikTok’s U.S. service: The agreement (or the accompanying official announcement/SEC filing) assigns, conveys, or otherwise grants to a U.S.-organized entity (as defined below) the exclusive right to operate the TikTok app for users located in the United States and exclusive control over U.S. user data and the content-recommendation operations for the U.S. service, whether via ownership or exclusive license. Wording consistent with reported policy goals—i.e., the algorithm is secured/retrained/operated in the U.S. outside ByteDance’s control—meets this criterion if stated in the agreement or official filing/press release.

3) U.S.-organized entity: The entity that will hold the rights in (2) is organized under the laws of the United States, a U.S. state, or the District of Columbia (i.e., a domestic corporation or LLC).

4) ByteDance ownership threshold: The agreement (or accompanying official announcement/SEC filing) explicitly states that ByteDance and its affiliates will collectively own strictly less than 20.000% of the equity of the entity identified in (3) as of the closing contemplated by that agreement, measured on a fully diluted, as‑converted basis (including all outstanding and reserved shares, options, warrants, convertible securities, and similar instruments). Ownership includes both direct and indirect holdings by ByteDance and its “affiliates.” “Affiliate” and “control” are as defined in SEC Rule 405 (affiliate means a person that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with the specified person; control means the power to direct management and policies through ownership, contract, or otherwise).

Evidence required and acceptable sources:
- Primary evidence can be: (a) an SEC Form 8‑K (Item 1.01) by any public-company party describing entry into the material definitive agreement, including the required summary of material terms; and/or (b) an official press release or transaction announcement posted on a principal party’s website that clearly states all relevant points for conditions (2)-(4).
- If the exact percentage ownership or rights are not stated in the agreement text publicly available but are specified in an Item 1.01 8‑K summary or official press release, that is sufficient. In the absence of these, corroboration by at least two reputable outlets (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, WSJ, NYT) reporting the signed definitive agreement and the <20% ByteDance stake and U.S. control arrangements will be accepted, provided their reporting is consistent with any available primary disclosures.

Clarifications and edge cases:
- Multiple-entity structures: If a layered structure is used (e.g., one entity for U.S. operations, a separate JV for data/algorithm), the relevant entity for measuring the <20% threshold is the U.S.-organized entity that, per the agreement/official disclosure, will hold the exclusive rights in condition (2)—i.e., exclusive right to operate TikTok’s U.S. app, exclusive control over U.S. user data, and control/operation of the U.S. recommendation algorithm.
- Announcement timing: The signing must be publicly announced (via SEC filing and/or official press release) within the resolution window. Agreements signed but not publicly announced within the window do not count.
- Amendments: If an agreement is signed within the window but later amended, the initial signing counts for timing. However, to resolve Yes, the version signed within the window must already satisfy conditions (2)-(4).
- Non-qualifying disclosures: LOIs, term sheets, framework agreements, or conditional government approvals without a binding, signed transaction agreement do not qualify.

Context references (for forecasters):
- Ownership threshold and U.S. control elements have been publicly described in late Sept 2025 reporting. Some reporting suggests alternative structures with ByteDance at or near 20% in certain JVs and substantial licensing economics, underscoring uncertainty about meeting the strict <20% criterion by year-end.

question: Will Ferrari finish ahead of Mercedes in the 2025 Formula One Constructors' Championship?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-10-01: According to the official Formula 1 results page for the 2025 Teams’ (Constructors’) standings, Mercedes have 290 points and Ferrari have 286 points, a four-point gap. There are six Grands Prix remaining between mid-October and early December: United States (Austin, Oct 17–19), Mexico City (Oct 24–26), São Paulo (Nov 7–9), Las Vegas (Nov 20–22), Qatar (Nov 28–30), and Abu Dhabi (Dec 5–7).

Definitions and scoring:
- Constructors’ Championship: One of two annual championships in Formula One, awarded to the team (constructor) that accumulates the most championship points over the season. Team totals are the sum of points scored by all cars entered by the team across the season.
- Points system in 2025: Grand Prix points for the top 10 finishers remain 25-18-15-12-10-8-6-4-2-1. Sprint points are awarded 8-7-6-5-4-3-2-1 to the top eight finishers. The fastest-lap bonus point has been removed for 2025 and is not awarded this season.
- Teams referred to in this question: “Mercedes” means Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team, and “Ferrari” means Scuderia Ferrari. The official F1 teams page lists teams competing in 2025 (link for reference: formula1.com/en/teams). 

Tiebreakers: If two constructors finish the season level on points, the FIA uses countback to rank them: most wins, then most second places, then most third places, and so on until a difference is found.

Why this may be uncertain: With only a small points gap and six race weekends remaining (some of which may include Sprint sessions), reliability, upgrades, driver performance, and incidents can swing results. The question resolves on the official standings, which incorporate any penalties or adjustments recognized by the FIA and reflected on Formula1.com before the resolution cutoff.
resolution_criteria:
Time window: Eligible events are those contributing to the official 2025 Formula One World Constructors’ Championship. The question resolves based on the final official standings as displayed on the Formula 1 2025 Teams’ standings page at or before 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Primary source of truth: Formula 1 official 2025 Teams’ standings page: https://www.formula1.com/en/results/2025/team. This page is the authoritative standings reference used to resolve this question.

Resolution: Resolve “Yes” if Ferrari’s final position in the official 2025 Constructors’ standings is higher (i.e., ranked above) Mercedes; otherwise resolve “No”. “Finish ahead” means ranked in a strictly higher finishing position on the official standings page referenced above.

Tie-handling: If Mercedes and Ferrari finish equal on points, use the FIA’s countback method (more wins, then more second places, then more third places, and so on) to determine who is ranked higher, as reflected on the official standings page. If (extremely unlikely) the official page displays them as an exact tie with no higher/lower rank between them, resolve “No” (Ferrari did not finish ahead).

Post-event adjustments: If the standings are adjusted by the FIA (e.g., due to penalties or appeals) after the final race but before the cutoff, use the standings as they appear on the official page at the resolution cutoff time. Changes occurring after 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC are ignored for resolution purposes.

Clarifications: 
- The points system used for ranking includes Grand Prix points and Sprint points per 2025 rules; no fastest-lap bonus point is awarded in 2025.
- No additional sources are required beyond the official Formula 1 standings page unless it is unavailable; in that unlikely case, credible wire services (e.g., AP, Reuters) reporting the final official constructors’ ranking may be used as backup verification.

question: Between October 15, 2024 and December 31, 2025 (UTC), will the IMF Executive Board approve a new IMF-supported program for Tunisia?
background:
Context and status quo as of 2025-09-30:
- Tunisia reached a staff-level agreement with IMF staff on October 15, 2022 for a 48-month Extended Fund Facility (EFF) of about US$1.9 billion, explicitly subject to subsequent Executive Board approval; no Board approval was announced at that time. Staff-level agreements are not Executive Board approvals.
- EBRD’s Transition Report 2024–25 notes slow progress on agreeing an IMF-supported program for Tunisia, despite external funding, and highlights vulnerabilities and a financing gap.
- As of mid-2025, the IMF’s Tunisia country page provides general information and outstanding purchases/loans but does not show a new Board-approved arrangement during 2024–2025; forecasters should monitor this page for updates.
- Tunisia’s macro backdrop in 2025: EBRD reported growth of 2.4% in H1 2025 (up from 1.6% in 2024), average inflation of 5.6% Jan–Jul 2025 (down from peaks above 10% in early 2023), fiscal deficit improvement (7.6% of GDP in 2023 to 6% in 2024), current account deficit at 1.5% of GDP in 2024, and international reserves of about US$8.5 billion in Aug 2025 (over three months of imports). These conditions shape the likelihood of reaching program approval by end-2025.
- For historical context, Tunisia received Board-approved emergency financing via the Rapid Financing Instrument (RFI) in April 2020, which was a one-off disbursement to address the COVID-19 shock; this illustrates the distinction between emergency financing and multi-year arrangements.

Definitions (authoritative sources provided):
- IMF-supported program (for purposes of this question): A “new arrangement” for Tunisia formally approved by the IMF Executive Board between 2024-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC under any of the following instruments: Extended Fund Facility (EFF), Stand-By Arrangement (SBA), Precautionary and Liquidity Line (PLL), Flexible Credit Line (FCL), Short-term Liquidity Line (SLL), Extended Credit Facility (ECF), Standby Credit Facility (SCF), or the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF).
  - EFF: Medium-term arrangement supporting structural reforms to address protracted balance of payments problems; typically 3–4 years; arrangements are approved by the Executive Board.
  - SBA: Short-to-medium term arrangement addressing balance of payments needs; typical duration 12–24 months (up to 36 months); arrangements are approved by the Executive Board.
  - PLL: Precautionary arrangement for members with sound fundamentals; Board-approved, as evidenced by Morocco’s PLL press releases.
  - RSF: Longer-term financing to support resilience and sustainability reforms; arrangements are approved by the Executive Board (e.g., Rwanda).
  - The IMF Lending toolkit outlines these instruments and distinguishes emergency instruments (e.g., RFI/RCF) and non-financial signaling instruments (e.g., PCI, SMP).

- “Approve”: For this market question, “approve” means that the IMF publishes an official press release or Executive Board decision stating that the Executive Board approved an arrangement for Tunisia under one of the instruments listed above (e.g., press releases that use the formula “IMF Executive Board Approves …”).
- “New”: Not previously approved before the start date (2024-10-15 00:00:00 UTC). Renewals/successor arrangements approved within the window count as “new” for this question.

Exclusions (to avoid ambiguity):
- Staff-level agreements (SLAs) without Executive Board approval do not count.
- Article IV consultations, Staff-Monitored Programs (including PMBs) and Policy Coordination Instruments (PCI) do not count, as they are not Board-approved lending arrangements.
- Emergency one-off disbursements under the Rapid Financing Instrument (RFI) or Rapid Credit Facility (RCF) do not count as “programs” for the purpose of this question, even though they are Board-approved, because this question’s definition of “IMF-supported program” is restricted to the instruments listed above.
resolution_criteria:
Outcome determination at 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC:
- Resolve YES if, between 2024-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, the IMF officially publishes a press release or Executive Board document stating that the Executive Board approved a new arrangement for Tunisia under any of the following instruments: EFF, SBA, PLL, FCL, SLL, ECF, SCF, or RSF.
- Resolve NO otherwise.

Primary resolution sources:
- IMF official press releases and Executive Board documents (e.g., press releases clearly titled “IMF Executive Board Approves …”, which are regularly published on imf.org).
- IMF’s Tunisia country page, which aggregates official IMF materials and may link to Board decisions and press releases relevant to Tunisia.

Verification procedure:
- A resolver should search imf.org for Tunisia-specific press releases and Executive Board documents dated within the window and confirm that the text explicitly states Executive Board approval of one of the qualifying instruments. The presence of phrases like “IMF Executive Board Approves [instrument] for Tunisia” is sufficient.

Notes:
- SLAs without Board approval do not satisfy the criterion.
- Emergency RFI/RCF disbursements, Article IV consultations, PCI, SMP/PMB do not satisfy the criterion.

Examples of qualifying evidence (for illustration):
- “IMF Executive Board Approves US$2.97 billion for Morocco Under the Precautionary and Liquidity Line” (PLL).
- “IMF Executive Board Approves 48-month US$20 billion Extended Arrangement for Argentina” (EFF).
- “IMF Executive Board Approves $319 Million Arrangement for Rwanda Under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility” (RSF).

Rationale for entropy:
- As of late 2025, Tunisia has made only slow progress toward an IMF-supported program, yet macro indicators improved modestly in 2025; program approval hinges on domestic reforms and external negotiations, making the outcome uncertain and suitable for forecasting.

question: Ecuador: Will Executive Decree No. 126 on automotive diesel pricing be repealed or materially amended between 2025-10-15 and 2025-12-31?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-10-01
- Executive Decree No. 126 was signed on September 12, 2025, elevating the retail price of automotive diesel (“diésel premium automotriz”) to USD 2.80 per gallon, effective from 00:00 on September 13, 2025, through December 11, 2025. Beginning December 12, 2025, the decree establishes a monthly price stabilization mechanism (“bandas”) with a maximum monthly increase of 5% and a maximum monthly decrease of 10% relative to the previous month, and sets a minimum floor price of USD 2.23 per gallon before VAT. The mechanism references US Gulf Coast international prices, import costs (transport, insurance, local infrastructure), and a supplier margin tied to international financial indicators.
- In response, the Confederación de Nacionalidades Indígenas del Ecuador (CONAIE) demanded the “derogatoria” (repeal) of Decree 126 and called for an “immediate and indefinite” national strike on September 18, 2025, citing the elimination of the diesel subsidy and the increase to USD 2.80/gal among the reasons.
- The Registro Oficial is the State of Ecuador’s official gazette and publishes binding legal norms, including executive decrees and laws. It is administratively attached to the Constitutional Court and serves as the authoritative channel for promulgation and public access to such norms.

Useful links (for definitions and verification)
- Registro Oficial (Official Gazette): https://www.registroficial.gob.ec/ 
- Presidency’s Minka decrees portal (for promulgated executive decrees): https://minka.presidencia.gob.ec/ (official portal link; used for verification alongside Registro Oficial)
- Background reading on the decree’s pricing provisions and mechanism caps/floor: El Comercio explainer; Primicias coverage 

Why this question is forecastable
- The outcome depends on political negotiations, protest dynamics, and fiscal constraints. CONAIE has explicitly demanded repeal, while the government has structured a mechanism it may wish to preserve. Either repeal/material change or retention without material change is plausible by year-end 2025.
resolution_criteria:
Question
- Resolve YES if, between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 (Ecuador mainland time, ECT, UTC−5), there is a promulgated executive decree or law that (a) explicitly repeals (“deroga”) Executive Decree No. 126, or (b) materially amends any of the decree’s operative pricing provisions listed below.
- Resolve NO otherwise.

Definitions (to eliminate ambiguity)
- Executive Decree No. 126 operative pricing provisions (as described in reputable press summaries of the decree text):
  1) The fixed retail price of USD 2.80 per gallon for automotive diesel (“diésel premium automotriz”) in effect from 00:00 on 2025-09-13 through 2025-12-11.
  2) The monthly price stabilization mechanism effective from 2025-12-12, including: (i) a max +5% monthly increase and max −10% monthly decrease versus the prior month; and (ii) a minimum floor price of USD 2.23 per gallon before VAT; and (iii) calculation inputs referencing US Gulf Coast international prices, import costs (transport, insurance, local infrastructure), and a supplier margin.
- Materially amends means any promulgated legal act that alters, suspends, removes, or replaces one or more of the above provisions (1)–(2). Examples that count include: changing the USD 2.80 price or its date range; changing the 2025-12-12 start date of the mechanism; changing the ±5%/±10% monthly caps; changing the USD 2.23/gal (pre-VAT) floor; removing or suspending the stabilization mechanism; or replacing its specified calculation inputs with a different structure.
- Not counted (non-material changes): editorial errata that do not change the meaning of (1)–(2); decrees that address only compensation programs, enforcement, or administrative matters without altering (1)–(2); or changes limited to other fuels (e.g., gasoline).
- Promulgated executive decree or law: a legal act published in the Registro Oficial (official gazette) or, if not yet in the gazette by the deadline, posted on the Presidency’s official Minka decrees portal with an issuance date within the eligibility window. If both sources exist, precedence for verification is the Registro Oficial.

Eligibility window and time zone
- Eligible acts must be dated and promulgated between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 and 2025-12-31 23:59:59, Ecuador mainland time (ECT, UTC−5). Dates will be interpreted according to the date shown on the official source (Registro Oficial or Minka portal).

Verification and sources of truth
- Primary source: Registro Oficial website (https://www.registroficial.gob.ec/). The resolver will search for publications explicitly repealing or amending Decree No. 126 and review the text to determine whether (1)–(2) are affected.
- Secondary source: Presidency’s Minka decrees portal (https://minka.presidencia.gob.ec/) to verify issuance and content if a relevant act appears there within the eligibility window but has not yet appeared in the Registro Oficial by the deadline. If a conflict arises, the Registro Oficial publication will control.

Edge cases
- If multiple acts occur and at least one meets the material amendment conditions, resolve YES.
- If an act is signed within the window but neither published in Registro Oficial nor posted on the Minka portal by the deadline, resolve NO.
- If an act partially amends Decree 126 but does not touch (1)–(2), resolve NO.

Citations: Factual background on Decree 126 and its mechanism caps/floor and timing ; protest demand for repeal and strike call ; role of the Registro Oficial as Ecuador’s official gazette.

question: Will U.S. core PCE inflation (YoY) for November 2025 be at or below 2.8% in the BEA’s December 19, 2025 Personal Income and Outlays release?
background:
Overview and current status (as of 2025-10-01)
- What is being measured: The “core PCE price index” is the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index excluding food and energy. BEA describes this as a measure that removes two categories with more volatile price swings to better show underlying inflation; it is released monthly as part of Personal Income and Outlays. BEA’s tables label the 12‑month rate as “Change From Month One Year Ago”.
- When/where it is reported: The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) lists a news release titled “Personal Income and Outlays, November 2025” scheduled for December 19, 2025 (release code BEA 25-55).
