- Primary confirmation that specifies amount, timing, nature of the funds (principal derived from immobilised Russian assets), and the receiving vehicle, from at least one of: (a) European Commission/Council Press corner releases or legal acts; (b) Euroclear press releases or financial statements; (c) official statements or filings by the receiving vehicle or participating governments. Examples of typical sources include the European Commission press releases announcing proceeds transfers  and Euroclear’s periodic disclosures of sanctioned‑asset‑related figures.
- Plus corroboration by at least one reputable international wire service (e.g., Reuters). See recent Reuters explainer/coverage for context on holdings and proposals [13bcdc; eddda0; 8d6501; 35c49f].

If sources disagree, prioritize primary official documents and Euroclear disclosures; resolve “No” unless there is clear, explicit evidence meeting the above requirements.

question: Will at least 64 SME IPOs list on BSE SME or NSE EMERGE between 2025-10-01 and 2025-12-31 (inclusive, IST)?
background:
Context and definitions (as of 2025-10-01)
- SME IPOs in India list on the SME platforms of the two major exchanges: BSE SME (Bombay Stock Exchange’s SME platform) and NSE EMERGE (National Stock Exchange’s SME platform). BSE SME is a specialized stock trading platform operated by BSE for small and medium enterprises to list and raise capital. NSE EMERGE is described by NSE as a credible marketplace providing capital-raising opportunities for fast-growing businesses not yet large enough for the main board. An initial public offering (IPO) is a public offering in which shares of a company are sold to investors and listed on one or more stock exchanges, transforming a private company into a public company.
- What sources show listing dates? Exchange listing notices/circulars explicitly state the effective listing date. For BSE SME, a typical BSE listing notice states: “Trading Members of the Exchange are hereby informed that effective from <DATE> the equity shares of <Company> are listed and admitted to dealings…” (example: JD Cables Ltd.). For NSE EMERGE, listing approval letters archived on NSE state that “the equity shares of the company are listed and admitted to dealings on the EMERGE SME platform … w.e.f. <DATE>” (example: Active Infrastructures Limited, effective March 28, 2025).
- Public aggregators provide day-by-day SME IPO listing dates and cross-checks. Chittorgarh’s “SME IPOs Listing 2025” page lists each SME IPO’s “IPO Listing Date” for 2025, supporting rapid verification and counting. Chittorgarh’s SME IPO dashboard indicates that, as of 2025-09-30, there were 211 SME IPOs in 2025 and also tracks ongoing/upcoming deals, underscoring high activity levels.

Why this threshold and time window
- We target a Q4 2025 window (Oct–Dec) to make the question timely and resolvable on or before 2025-12-31. The threshold (64) is chosen to be plausibly close to the central expectation given the high SME IPO activity observed year-to-date (211 by 2025-09-30) while leaving meaningful uncertainty for forecasters.

Links for quick reference (also cited above):
- BSE SME overview/definition (Chittorgarh): https://www.chittorgarh.com/faq_pg/what-is-bse-sme/4813/ 
- NSE EMERGE overview: https://www.nseindia.com/products-services/emerge-platform-about-sme 
- IPO definition (Wikipedia): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial_public_offering 
- BSE listing notice exemplar (shows “effective from” listing date language): https://m.bseindia.com/MAnnDet.aspx?newsid=ca869af7-29a8-4c8d-8420-553b14b8defb&Form=STR&scrpcd=544524 
- NSE EMERGE listing admission exemplar (shows “listed and admitted … w.e.f.” language): https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SHRADHA_28032025110412_updateonlistingapprovalactive.pdf 
- Aggregator listing-date page (for cross-checking): https://www.chittorgarh.com/report/ipo-listing-date-check-status-price-bse-nse/25/sme/?year=2025 
- SME IPO dashboard (activity snapshot): https://www.chittorgarh.com/ipo/ipo_dashboard.asp?a=sme
resolution_criteria:
Outcome
- Resolve YES if at least 64 unique companies have their equity shares first listed on either BSE SME or NSE EMERGE with an official listing effective date between 2025-10-01 and 2025-12-31 inclusive, measured in India Standard Time (IST; UTC+05:30). Otherwise, resolve NO.

Key definitions (with sources)
- SME platforms: “BSE SME” (BSE’s small and medium enterprises platform) and “NSE EMERGE” (NSE’s SME platform). Authoritative descriptions are available from BSE/NSE and industry references.
- IPO: An initial public offering is a public offering of shares that results in listing on a stock exchange.
- Listing date (the date used for counting): The “effective from” date stated in the exchange’s listing notice/circular confirming that the equity shares “are listed and admitted to dealings.” Examples: BSE notices that say “effective from <DATE> the equity shares … are listed and admitted to dealings” , and NSE EMERGE listing admission letters stating shares “are listed and admitted to dealings … w.e.f. <DATE>”.
- Unique companies: Distinct corporate issuers. If the same company lists equity shares on both SME platforms during the window (rare), count it once, based on the earliest listing date in the window.

Inclusions
- Only first-time listings of a company’s equity shares on BSE SME or NSE EMERGE pursuant to an IPO, as evidenced by an exchange listing circular or listing admission letter that uses the “listed and admitted to dealings … effective from” (or “w.e.f.”) language.

Exclusions (non-exhaustive but prioritized for common edge cases)
- Main-board listings (BSE/NSE main board) are excluded; only SME platforms count.
- Follow-on public offers (FPOs), offers for sale (OFS) without a new equity listing event, rights issues, preferential allotments, SPACs, REITs/InvITs, debt-only listings.
- Migrations (e.g., SME→main board) and re-listings of previously listed securities.
- Symbol changes, name changes, or additional securities of an already-listed SME issuer.

Eligible time window and timezone
- Start: 2025-10-01 00:00:00 IST (UTC+05:30)
- End: 2025-12-31 23:59:59 IST (UTC+05:30)
- Counting is based on the calendar date in IST printed or implied in the official listing notice/letter.

Primary resolution sources (and precedence)
- BSE SME: BSE corporate announcements/listing circulars that explicitly state the equity shares “are listed and admitted to dealings … effective from <DATE>.” Example form and language: JD Cables Ltd. notice.
- NSE EMERGE: NSE-issued listing admission letters or circulars archived on nsearchives.nseindia.com confirming the equity shares “are listed and admitted to dealings … w.e.f. <DATE>.” Example form and language: Active Infrastructures Limited letter.
- If there is any discrepancy between aggregator sites and exchange documents, exchange documents prevail.

Secondary cross-checks (non-binding)
- Chittorgarh “SME IPOs Listing 2025” page provides per-IPO listing dates and can be used to identify candidates for verification. Its SME dashboard provides activity snapshot context but is not used for resolution.

Procedure
1) After market close on 2025-12-31 (IST), compile all SME listings with effective dates within the window from BSE/NSE documents.
2) Deduplicate by issuer to ensure each company is counted once.
3) Tally the total. If the total is ≥64, resolve YES; otherwise, NO.

Notes
- If an exchange listing document is published slightly before or after the effective date, the effective date in the document controls the inclusion.
- If conflicting dates appear across documents, use the latest official exchange document that explicitly states the effective listing date; if still conflicting, prefer the exchange’s dedicated listing circular over company communications.

Citations: BSE SME definition and context ; NSE EMERGE platform overview ; IPO definition ; Chittorgarh listing-date report page and its date-field structure ; SME IPO activity snapshot as of 2025-09-30 ; BSE “effective from” listing notice exemplar ; NSE EMERGE “listed and admitted … w.e.f.” exemplar.

question: They Call Him OG: Will Sacnilk’s India Net (all languages) reach ≥ ₹200.0 crore by 23:59 IST on 31 December 2025?
background:
Summary of the subject and current status (as of 2025-09-30):
- Film: They Call Him OG is a 2025 Indian Telugu-language action crime film written and directed by Sujeeth and produced by D. V. V. Danayya; it stars Pawan Kalyan (lead) and Emraan Hashmi (antagonist). It released theatrically worldwide on 25 September 2025.
- Early box office context: The film held paid premieres in India on 24 September 2025 and opened strongly; by the end of its first Monday (day 5), industry/media reports citing Sacnilk put its India net at about ₹147.65 crore, with an estimated ₹7.45 crore on Monday alone and paid previews totaling roughly ₹21 crore.
- Sacnilk status: Sacnilk, a widely used Indian box office tracker, lists an India Net total for the title. On Sacnilk’s “Recent Movies Collection” page, They Call Him OG shows India Net ₹147.6 crore (with Worldwide ₹237.3, India Gross ₹176.8, Overseas ₹60.5). Sacnilk’s dedicated news page for the film presents an all-language day-wise India Net breakdown that sums to ₹147.6 crore through day 5 (Day 0 paid previews ₹21.0 cr; Day 1 ₹63.75 cr; Day 2 ₹18.45 cr; Day 3 ₹18.5 cr; Day 4 ₹18.5 cr; Day 5 ₹7.4 cr) and explicitly uses the “India Net” label.
- Key definitions referenced in this question: A crore denotes ten million (10,000,000) in the Indian numbering system; ₹200.0 crore equals ₹2,000,000,000 (two billion rupees). Indian Standard Time (IST) is UTC+05:30 and does not observe daylight saving time.

Why this is forecast-relevant: As of late September 2025, the Sacnilk-listed India Net total is around ₹147.6 crore, implying the film would need roughly another ₹52.4 crore in domestic net collections to reach ₹200.0 crore by year-end. Uncertainty stems from weekday holds, festival boosts (e.g., Dasara/Diwali), competition, and potential expansions or declines in screen count and ticket pricing—all affecting whether the cumulative India Net crosses the threshold by the deadline.
resolution_criteria:
Operationalization and scope:
- Outcome: YES if Sacnilk shows They Call Him OG with India Net (all languages combined) ≥ ₹200.0 crore as of 23:59:59 IST (UTC+05:30) on 31 December 2025; otherwise NO.
- Counting window: This refers to the cumulative India Net that Sacnilk maintains for this title from its India paid previews/theatrical start in September 2025 through the deadline. No currency conversions or adjustments are required; use figures exactly as displayed in Indian rupees.
- What “India Net” means for this question: Use the figure labeled “India Net” as displayed by Sacnilk for this film. Sacnilk’s pages explicitly use the "India Net" label for this title and present an all-language cumulative total; this question defers to Sacnilk’s labeling and value rather than any external definition.

Primary resolution source (single source of truth):
- Sacnilk’s “Box Office Collection of Recent Movies” page, row for “They Call Him OG,” India Net column: https://www.sacnilk.com/entertainmenttopbar2/RecentMoviesCollection. This page labels an “India Net” column and currently lists the film with that field.

Secondary/tertiary sources (only if the primary page is inaccessible or does not render for the resolver at the decision time):
- Sacnilk’s film-specific box office news page that uses the "India Net" label and aggregates all-language totals: https://www.sacnilk.com/news/OG_2024_Box_Office_Collection_Day_Wise_Worldwide.
- Sacnilk’s dedicated movie page for the title, if it displays an “India Net” total at resolution time: https://www.sacnilk.com/movie/OG_2024.

How to read the number and handle rounding:
- Use the value as displayed on Sacnilk. If the displayed India Net is rounded to one decimal place, evaluate against the threshold using the displayed rounded figure. Examples: 200.0 → YES; 199.9 → NO.

Archival and outage handling (to ensure determinism):
- If the relevant Sacnilk page(s) are temporarily unavailable at 23:59:59 IST on 31 December 2025, use a verifiable archived snapshot from the Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine (https://web.archive.org) of the applicable Sacnilk page(s).
- Snapshot selection order: Prefer a snapshot time-stamped at or before the deadline (≤ 23:59:59 IST on 31 Dec 2025). If none exists, use the earliest available snapshot captured after the deadline. Apply the same page-priority order as above (RecentMoviesCollection first; then the news page; then the movie page).

Discrepancies between Sacnilk pages:
- If multiple Sacnilk pages are accessible and show different India Net totals at the decision time, resolve using the value on the primary page (RecentMoviesCollection). Only if that page is inaccessible should you fall back to the secondary page, and then the tertiary page in that order.

Term and time references:
- Crore definition: ten million (10,000,000) in the Indian numbering system.
- IST definition: Indian Standard Time, UTC+05:30, no daylight saving.

Start date and end date in timezone:
- Start: From the film’s India paid previews/theatrical start in September 2025 as incorporated by Sacnilk’s cumulative “India Net” tracking (this includes day 0 paid previews).
- End: 23:59:59 IST on 31 December 2025.

Notes:
- This question is not about worldwide gross or India gross; only Sacnilk’s India Net field for this title is relevant.
- If the film title appears with minor styling variations (e.g., “OG” vs “They Call Him OG”), match by Sacnilk’s canonical entry for the film linked above.

question: Will UNRWA publicly announce that it will not disburse 100% of December 2025 staff salaries by December 31, 2025 (UTC)?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01: The United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) is the UN agency providing services to Palestine refugees across Gaza, the West Bank, Jordan, Lebanon and Syria; it is funded largely by voluntary contributions (overview: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNRWA). In 2025, UNRWA has repeatedly warned of a severe funding and cashflow crisis. In a September 2025 finance and fundraising update presented to its Subcommittee, UNRWA stated: “Currently forecasted income projects that UNRWA will be able to cover only 2 days of operations in November” and that it “will likely face a minimum US$ 200m financial deficit between the end of this year and beginning of next year (Q4 2025 and Q1 2026)”. The same slide deck noted that “In the first half of 2025, we managed to make payroll every month,” but only through “financial emergency measures in April and May,” and reiterated that UNRWA needs “approx. US$ 60m to operate per month! Or US$ 2m per day”.

In an official statement delivered on 2025-06-25, Commissioner-General Philippe Lazzarini said the projected shortfall for the 2025 Programme Budget was approximately USD 200 million and stressed that UNRWA “cannot carry a large deficit into 2026 – unlike in previous years,” given the loss of major donors, warning of an acute cashflow crisis if pledges were not disbursed on time. On 2025-09-25, Lazzarini further reported that austerity and cost control measures in 2025 amounted to USD 150 million and that the projected shortfall between Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 “exceeds 200 million USD,” with projected income in Q1 2026 “far too low to absorb any deficit from 2025”. These statements indicate material risk to continuity of operations and payroll in late 2025.

Why this question: Salary delays or partial disbursements are a clear, publicly verifiable indicator of cashflow stress. UNRWA has experienced such measures in past crises (e.g., deferred payroll reported in earlier annual operational reports), and current shortfall and cashflow projections create uncertainty around December 2025 payroll. This question focuses on a specific, unambiguous trigger—an official announcement about December 2025 staff salaries not being fully disbursed by the end of December—rather than broader, more ambiguous notions of “service continuity.”

Key definitions:
- UNRWA staff: Employees on UNRWA’s payroll (both “area staff” and “international staff”), excluding contractors, vendors, daily workers, or volunteers. General agency overview provided above; staff categories are established internally by UNRWA regulations.
- Staff salaries: The ordinary monthly payroll amounts due to UNRWA staff for the month of December 2025, exclusive of routine statutory deductions (e.g., taxes, pension contributions). “Full salary” for an employee means 100% of that ordinary monthly amount is disbursed as per UNRWA’s payroll (i.e., not a reduced or deferred portion).
- Publicly announce: An official communication accessible without login, published by UNRWA via one of the following: its Newsroom pages (Official Statements or News Releases) at https://www.unrwa.org/newsroom, or posts from UNRWA’s verified X (Twitter) account (@UNRWA) at https://x.com/UNRWA. These are standard official channels for UNRWA communications.
resolution_criteria:
Time window: Events eligible for resolution must be announced between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Resolution sources: Primary resolution will be based on official UNRWA communications published on:
- UNRWA Newsroom – Official Statements or News Releases (https://www.unrwa.org/newsroom)
- UNRWA’s verified X (Twitter) account (@UNRWA) at https://x.com/UNRWA
If UNRWA’s primary channels are inaccessible at resolution, secondary sources may include credible international news agencies (e.g., AP, Reuters, BBC) quoting named UNRWA officials; however, preference is given to primary sources.

How this resolves:
- YES if, within the time window, UNRWA publicly announces that 100% of December 2025 staff salaries will NOT be disbursed by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, OR publicly announces that December 2025 staff salaries will be paid at less than 100% in December (with any remaining portion deferred to a later date). Either formulation counts as a clear indication that full December payroll will not be completed by end-December.
- NO if no such announcement is made within the time window.

What counts as an announcement:
- Examples that count (any one is sufficient):
  - “UNRWA will issue only 60% of December salaries in December and defer the remainder to January.”
  - “UNRWA will be unable to pay December salaries in full by the end of December.”
  - “Payment of December salaries is delayed beyond December 31.”
- Examples that do not count:
  - General statements of financial stress or funding appeals without explicit reference to December 2025 salaries.
  - Third-party rumors or media reports without an explicit official UNRWA confirmation.

Additional clarifications:
- Scope: Any explicit announcement affecting any staff category (area staff or international staff) is sufficient for YES. If UNRWA announces partial or delayed payment for only one category of staff (e.g., area staff), that still counts as YES.
- Conflicting communications: If conflicting messages occur, the most recent official UNRWA communication within the time window prevails.
- Timezone: All timestamps are evaluated in UTC.

Status quo references: UNRWA’s September 2025 finance and fundraising update and official statements provide the current context for funding shortfalls and cashflow risk.

question: Will the UK PIPR 12-month change reported in the ONS “Private rent and house prices, UK: November 2025” bulletin be at least 5.6%?
background:
What is being forecast: This question asks whether the Office for National Statistics (ONS) will report a United Kingdom (UK) year-over-year (YoY) increase in average monthly private rents of at least 5.6% in the “Private rent and house prices, UK: November 2025” statistical bulletin.

Key definitions and references:
- United Kingdom (UK): The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, comprising England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.
- Price Index of Private Rents (PIPR): An ONS official statistic in development that measures the change in the price of renting residential property from private landlords. It is a monthly “stock” measure intended to reflect price changes across all privately rented properties, including both new and existing tenancies, and is compiled using administrative rental data (VOA, Scottish Government, Welsh Government, NIHE) with a hedonic double imputation methodology.
- 12-month change as used in ONS bulletins: In the monthly bulletin, ONS states the annual percentage change with wording such as “Average UK monthly private rents increased by X% in the 12 months to [month] (provisional estimate).” For example, the September 2025 bulletin states, “Average UK monthly private rents increased by 5.7% … in the 12 months to August 2025 (provisional estimate)”. This question will use that exact UK percentage as published in the November 2025 bulletin (which should refer to “the 12 months to October 2025”).
- Revisions: Because Northern Ireland rental data are delivered with a two‑month lag, the UK series imputes the two most recent months and revises them when data arrive; ONS expects these UK revisions to be minor. Every month ONS revises the two most recent UK estimates.
- Time standard: All dates/times in this question refer to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

Recent context (status quo as of 2025-09-30):
- Mar 2025: ONS reported “Average UK monthly private rents increased by 7.7% … in the 12 months to March 2025 (provisional estimate)”.
- May 2025: “7.0% … in the 12 months to May 2025 (provisional estimate)”.
- Jul 2025: “5.9% … in the 12 months to July 2025 (provisional estimate)”.
- Aug 2025: “5.7% … in the 12 months to August 2025 (provisional estimate)”.
- Release cadence example: The September 2025 bulletin was released on 17 September 2025, and noted the next release date as 22 October 2025.

Why this is forecastable and non-trivial: PIPR is a timely national measure of private rent inflation that has been decelerating through 2025, but remains elevated versus pre‑2022 norms. The November 2025 bulletin will reflect the “12 months to October 2025” reading, which is plausibly near the current 5–6% range, making a 5.6% threshold a high‑entropy target given recent momentum and revision practices.
resolution_criteria:
Question: Will the UK PIPR 12-month change reported in the ONS “Private rent and house prices, UK: November 2025” bulletin be at least 5.6%?

Operationalization:
- Metric to extract: The percentage value appearing in the sentence within the November 2025 ONS bulletin that states the UK annual change, in the style “Average UK monthly private rents increased by X% … in the 12 months to October 2025 (provisional estimate).” The UK value (not England, not Great Britain) is the target. This wording and placement are consistent with prior bulletins.
- Threshold test: Resolve YES if X ≥ 5.6%; resolve NO if X < 5.6%.
- Rounding: Use the percentage exactly as published in that sentence (ONS typically presents one decimal place). Do not adjust for any implied additional precision.
- Revisions: Use the first value published in the initial release of the “Private rent and house prices, UK: November 2025” bulletin. If, and only if, ONS issues a formal correction/erratum to that bulletin before 23:59:59 UTC on 31 December 2025, use the corrected value. Regular month‑to‑month revisions to the two most recent UK estimates due to Northern Ireland data lags are expected and documented by ONS, but for the purposes of this market, only the value in the initial November 2025 bulletin (or its official correction, if any) will be used.
- Source of truth: The ONS statistical bulletin “Private rent and house prices, UK: November 2025” on ons.gov.uk. Recent bulletins and phrasing examples are visible in the August and September 2025 releases. If the November 2025 bulletin is published on a different URL structure, the most directly comparable ONS page bearing that bulletin title will be used.
- Timing: Resolution will occur upon publication of that bulletin (initial release) and in any case no later than 23:59:59 UTC on 31 December 2025. All times UTC.

Outcomes:
- YES if the extracted UK annual percentage (12 months to October 2025) is ≥ 5.6%.
- NO if the extracted UK annual percentage is < 5.6%.

Notes for verifiers:
- Examples of the exact sentence structure and UK figures appear in: April 2025 (7.7%; 12 months to March) ; June 2025 (7.0%; 12 months to May) ; August 2025 (5.9%; 12 months to July) ; September 2025 (5.7%; 12 months to August; released 17 Sep 2025; next release 22 Oct 2025). These provide the template for locating the November 2025 UK value.
- Definition and revision practices for PIPR are documented in the PIPR QMI.

question: Will Blue Origin’s New Glenn launch NASA’s ESCAPADE mission between 00:00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025?
background:
Summary of status quo as of 2025-09-30:
- Vehicle status: Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket conducted its maiden flight (NG-1) on January 16, 2025, lifting off at 2:03 a.m. EST (0703 UTC) from Space Launch Complex 36 (SLC-36) at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station and reaching orbit.
- Mission overview: NASA’s ESCAPADE (Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers) is a twin-spacecraft heliophysics mission to study how the solar wind interacts with Mars’ magnetic environment, managed by UC Berkeley’s Space Sciences Laboratory with NASA partners; it will use two identical spacecraft for simultaneous observations.
- Current launch plan for NG-2/ESCAPADE: As of late September 2025, NASA and Blue Origin state that New Glenn’s second mission (NG-2) carrying ESCAPADE is targeted for “later this fall” from SLC-36, Cape Canaveral. NASA’s ESCAPADE blog reported the spacecraft returned to Florida in September 2025 to prepare for launch, scheduled no earlier than this fall on New Glenn. Independent reporting indicates the launch is now expected in late October or early November 2025, with NASA’s Launch Services Program citing “very late in October, maybe the first week in November,” and noting trajectory flexibility that allows ESCAPADE to launch virtually any day in 2025 before heading to Mars in 2026. Space.com further reports Blue Origin is targeting mid-October for NG-2, with pre-launch milestones including vehicle movement and a hotfire test anticipated mid-month.
Why this is non-trivial: New Glenn has flown once, and NG-2 involves interplanetary payload integration and pre-launch testing that commonly slip. The publicly stated windows span mid-October through early November 2025, leaving meaningful uncertainty about whether liftoff will occur within the specified forecasting window.
Key references a forecaster may monitor:
- NASA ESCAPADE mission page and blog for schedule/status updates.
- NASA news releases regarding ESCAPADE launch media accreditation and date targeting.
- Blue Origin’s official New Glenn mission pages and press releases (e.g., NG-1 precedent).
- Reputable industry reporting on schedule updates (SpaceNews, Space.com).
resolution_criteria:
Outcome determination window: Events must occur between 00:00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025.
Definitions and scope:
- “New Glenn” refers to Blue Origin’s orbital-class heavy-lift launch vehicle operating from SLC-36 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station; it successfully flew NG-1 on January 16, 2025.
- “ESCAPADE mission” refers to NASA’s twin-spacecraft heliophysics mission to study Mars’ magnetic environment and solar wind interaction, as described by NASA Science.
- “Launch” (for resolution) means liftoff: the moment the New Glenn rocket carrying the ESCAPADE payload leaves the launch pad under its own power. Static fire tests, wet dress rehearsals, rollouts, or scrubs do not count. An abort after liftoff still counts as a launch for the purposes of this question. Blue Origin’s NG-1 press materials exemplify how liftoff times are recorded and publicly reported (e.g., “engines ignited at 2:03 a.m. EST”).
- “Carrying the ESCAPADE payload” means the launched New Glenn vehicle has the ESCAPADE spacecraft integrated and manifested for the mission, as confirmed by NASA or Blue Origin. The mission is widely described as New Glenn’s second flight (NG-2).
Resolution rule:
- Resolve Yes if an officially confirmed liftoff of New Glenn with the ESCAPADE payload occurs within the window defined above.
- Resolve No if no such liftoff occurs within the window.
Accepted resolution sources:
- Primary: Official confirmation from NASA (e.g., NASA Science ESCAPADE blog/mission page or NASA news releases) and/or Blue Origin’s official press releases/news posts.
- Secondary (if primary is unavailable or delayed): Reputable, independent reporting with live coverage or post-event confirmation (e.g., SpaceNews, Space.com, Reuters).
How to verify quickly on resolution date:
- Check NASA’s ESCAPADE blog/mission page for a launch update or post.
- Check Blue Origin’s newsroom for an NG-2 launch press release (NG-1 precedent shows timely publication).
- Cross-check timing within UTC window using the timestamp provided by NASA/Blue Origin or corroborated by reputable outlets.

question: Will the EIA-reported U.S. average retail price for regular gasoline be below $3.10/gal in the last weekly reading with a Monday date in December 2025?
background:
Context and status quo as of 2025-10-01
- What series we mean: The U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) publishes a weekly national average retail gasoline price series commonly referenced as “Weekly U.S. Regular All Formulations Retail Gasoline Prices (Dollars per Gallon)” and disseminated on EIA’s Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Update portal. The same national series is republished by FRED as GASREGW with metadata indicating frequency “Weekly, Ending Monday” and units “Dollars per Gallon”.
- What “regular gasoline” means: EIA table definitions define “Regular gasoline” as gasoline with an antiknock index (average of research octane number and motor octane number) greater than or equal to 85 and less than 88.
- What the published retail price represents: EIA’s methodology states the weekly survey collects the cash price at the pump, including taxes, and that estimates are published at approximately 5:00 p.m. ET Monday (Tuesday on government holidays) but still represent Monday’s prices.
- How the national average is constructed: EIA’s weekly price estimates are calculated as volume‑weighted averages at the national, regional, and selected city/state levels, based on a stratified sample of retail outlets.
- Recent levels: As a reference point for forecasters, the FRED GASREGW series (sourced from EIA) shows recent U.S. weekly values (dollars per gallon): 2025‑09‑22: 3.173; 2025‑09‑15: 3.168; 2025‑09‑08: 3.192; 2025‑09‑01: 3.177.
- Known data issues: EIA noted misclassifications affecting some weekly motor gasoline formulation data between 2023‑09‑18 and 2023‑11‑06 and stated the published prices would not be changed; this is historical context and does not alter 2025 methodology or current series usage.
Why this is forecastable now: Late‑year gasoline prices reflect crude oil movements, refining margins, seasonal demand, and tax/regulatory factors. As of late September 2025, the national average is modestly above $3.10/gal, and late‑December often exhibits seasonal softening—creating plausible uncertainty around a $3.10 threshold. Primary source for resolution: EIA’s Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Update and the EIA national weekly series page.
resolution_criteria:
Yes/No event definition
- Question: Will the last weekly U.S. national average retail price for regular gasoline with a Monday reference date in December 2025 be strictly less than $3.10 per gallon?
- Series to use: EIA’s national weekly series “Weekly U.S. Regular All Formulations Retail Gasoline Prices (Dollars per Gallon)” (commonly republished by FRED as GASREGW; frequency Weekly, Ending Monday). The landing page for these weekly prices is the EIA Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Update portal, which links to the national U.S. series.
- What counts as the “last weekly reading in December 2025”: The observation in this series whose reference date is the final Monday that falls within December 2025 (U.S. Eastern Time). EIA states the weekly estimates represent Monday’s prices and are typically published around 5:00 p.m. ET Monday, or Tuesday on government holidays while still representing Monday’s prices.
- Units and inclusions: Use the value as published by EIA for the national “regular gasoline” series, in dollars per gallon, which reflects the cash price at the pump including taxes.
- Threshold and comparison: Resolve “Yes” if the EIA‑published value for that observation is strictly less than $3.10; resolve “No” otherwise. Determination is based on the value as displayed by EIA (typically to three decimal places) at the time of publication of that observation.
- Timing window: This market question is intended to resolve once the last December‑dated weekly observation is published, which under EIA’s schedule should occur on Monday, December 29, 2025 (or Tuesday, December 30, 2025 if delayed by a federal holiday) and therefore before 2025‑12‑31 23:59 UTC.
- Source(s) of truth and verification: The resolver will verify the outcome directly on EIA’s Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Update portal and/or the specific EIA weekly national series page for regular gasoline. If needed for cross‑check, the FRED GASREGW series (sourced from EIA) may be used to confirm the same weekly value and date labeling (“Weekly, Ending Monday”).
- Scope clarifications:
  • Regular gasoline definition follows EIA’s table definitions (antiknock index >=85 and <88).
  • Prices include all taxes and represent the cash pump price observed on Monday.
  • The national average is a volume‑weighted estimate based on EIA’s sampling methodology.
  • Historical 2023 misclassification notice does not alter the 2025 national series definition or the use of the published national value for resolution; no retroactive changes to those weeks were made per EIA.
- Edge cases:
  • If EIA publishes multiple December observations on the same date due to schedule adjustments, use the one whose reference (Monday) date is latest in December 2025.
  • If, contrary to expectations, EIA does not publish the final December 2025 observation by 2025‑12‑31 23:59 UTC, the market will remain open until the observation is published; however, based on EIA’s standard schedule this is not anticipated.

Key references (for definitions, schedule, and recent levels): EIA Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Update landing page ; EIA weekly gasoline price methodology (publication timing, inclusion of taxes) ; EIA table definitions for “regular gasoline” ; methodology note on volume‑weighted national averages ; 2023 misclassification notice ; recent weekly observations and series metadata via FRED GASREGW.

question: Will Eli Lilly’s 2025 year-to-date tirzepatide (Mounjaro + Zepbound) revenue exceed Novo Nordisk’s 2025 year-to-date semaglutide (Ozempic + Wegovy + Rybelsus) revenue for the nine months ended 2025-09-30 (UTC)?
background:
Context and scope: This question compares revenue from specific, clearly defined products to avoid ambiguity about company segment definitions.
- Eli Lilly and Company markets tirzepatide for type 2 diabetes as Mounjaro and for obesity as Zepbound. Tirzepatide is a dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist; see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tirzepatide and brand pages https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mounjaro and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zepbound.
- Novo Nordisk markets semaglutide for type 2 diabetes as Ozempic (injectable) and Rybelsus (oral), and for obesity as Wegovy; see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semaglutide, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozempic, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rybelsus, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wegovy.
- “Revenue” here means the companies’ reported worldwide product sales (also called net sales or revenue from product sales) for each named product, as presented in official quarterly press releases, financial workbooks, or investor presentations.
- Novo Nordisk reports in Danish kroner (DKK), while Eli Lilly reports in U.S. dollars (USD). For comparability, this question defines a specific, authoritative exchange-rate source and method (see Resolution Criteria) to ensure an unambiguous comparison. Federal Reserve H.10 daily rates: https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h10/.
- Status quo as of 2025-09-22 (UTC): Both companies publicly report quarterly product-level revenue for these drugs on their investor relations sites. This question refrains from asserting any current figures to avoid biasing forecasts and to keep the resolution purely mechanical using Q3 2025 publications.
- Resolution timing: Q3 2025 results (covering the nine months ended 2025-09-30) are typically published before year-end, enabling resolution before 2025-12-31 (UTC).
resolution_criteria:
Start date/time for eligibility: Forecasting runs from 2025-09-22 00:00 UTC until resolution no later than 2025-12-31 23:59 UTC. Measurement period for the compared revenues is fixed as 2025-01-01 through 2025-09-30 (inclusive).

Question resolves YES if the sum of Eli Lilly’s reported worldwide net product revenue for Mounjaro + Zepbound for the nine months ended 2025-09-30 exceeds the sum of Novo Nordisk’s reported worldwide net sales for Ozempic + Wegovy + Rybelsus for the same period, after currency conversion defined below. Otherwise, resolves NO.

Definitions and inclusions/exclusions:
- Included products and only these:
  - Eli Lilly: Mounjaro and Zepbound (both are tirzepatide). Exclude Trulicity (dulaglutide) and all other Lilly products.
  - Novo Nordisk: Ozempic, Wegovy, and Rybelsus (all are semaglutide). Exclude Saxenda and Victoza (liraglutide) and all other Novo Nordisk products.
- “Reported worldwide net product revenue/sales” means the figures explicitly presented by the companies for each product in their official Q3 2025 materials (press release, financial workbook, or investor presentation). Use the most granular, product-level figures provided; if a nine-month (YTD) figure is not presented for a product, sum that product’s Q1+Q2+Q3 2025 reported quarterly revenues from the same sources.
- Geography: Use worldwide totals as reported (sum of U.S. and international if only regional figures are presented). Exclude any royalty, collaboration, or non-product “other” revenue.

Currency conversion and computation:
- Base currency for comparison: USD.
- Convert Novo Nordisk’s DKK product sales to USD using the arithmetic average of the Federal Reserve H.10 daily Danish krone per U.S. dollar rates (DKK per USD) for every calendar day from 2025-01-01 through 2025-09-30 (UTC). Compute the mean of all available daily observations in that window. Convert DKK to USD by dividing DKK amounts by this mean DKK-per-USD rate. Use at least 6 decimal places for the exchange rate and do calculations to full precision before the final comparison.
- If H.10 does not publish a rate for specific days (e.g., weekends/holidays), use the available daily series as-is; do not interpolate. If H.10 daily rates are unavailable for the period, use the H.10 monthly average rates for Jan–Sep 2025 weighted equally by month (simple average of the nine monthly averages) as a fallback.

Primary resolution sources:
- Eli Lilly investor relations: Quarterly results page containing Q3 2025 press release/financial workbook with product sales tables: https://investor.lilly.com/financial-information/quarterly-results
- Novo Nordisk investor relations: Financial results page containing Q3 2025 materials with product sales tables: https://www.novonordisk.com/investors/financial-results.html
- Federal Reserve H.10 daily exchange rates: https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h10/

Procedural notes and edge cases:
- Use the latest officially published figures available as of 2025-12-31 23:59 UTC if any company issues a correction or restatement before that time.
- If any one of the three Novo Nordisk products or either of the two Eli Lilly products is not separately reported for the 9M 2025 period, sum their reported quarterly product revenues for Q1, Q2, and Q3 2025 from official materials. If a necessary quarterly product figure is not provided in any official Q1–Q3 2025 material by 2025-12-31, resolve the market N/A (void).
- “Exceeds” means strictly greater than (after conversion) by any positive amount; comparisons are made on unrounded values. If the computed totals are exactly equal, resolve NO.
- Timezone: All dates/times in this criterion are in UTC.

question: Will at least five natural persons be added to the EU’s Venezuela restrictive measures list between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01: On 10 January 2025, the Council of the European Union prolonged its restrictive measures on Venezuela until 10 January 2026 and adopted sanctions against 15 additional individuals, bringing the total number of individuals subject to EU sanctions under this regime to 69. The Council formalizes such actions through legal acts published in the Official Journal of the European Union (OJ), notably amending the Venezuela regime’s foundational instruments: Council Decision (CFSP) 2017/2074 and Council Regulation (EU) 2017/2063. For example, Council Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/44 of 9 January 2025 added 15 persons to the list by amending Annex IV to Regulation (EU) 2017/2063. In parallel, Council Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/42 of 9 January 2025 updated entries for 14 already-listed persons, illustrating that not all acts published change the count of listed individuals.

Definitions and legal structure:
- Council of the European Union (“the Council”): One of the EU’s legislative bodies composed of national ministers; it adopts CFSP decisions and regulations relevant to sanctions.
- Official Journal of the European Union (OJ): The EU’s official gazette. Only legal acts published in the OJ are binding; since July 2013, the electronic OJ via EUR-Lex has legal value.
- Venezuela restrictive measures regime: The EU sanctions framework concerning the situation in Venezuela, established by Council Decision (CFSP) 2017/2074 and Council Regulation (EU) 2017/2063. These acts include arms and equipment embargoes, travel bans, and asset freezes, and provide procedures for listing/delisting persons.
- List of sanctioned persons: In the Regulation, natural persons are listed in Annex IV (consolidated text reference), which is amended by subsequent acts to add, update, or remove entries.
- Natural person: A human being, as distinguished from a legal person such as a corporation or governmental body.

Why this is forecastable: Whether the Council will add at least five natural persons to the Venezuela regime in Q4 2025 depends on developments in Venezuela and EU foreign policy decisions. The Council’s timeline notes significant 2024–2025 political developments and the January 2025 listing action, underscoring ongoing dynamics that could plausibly lead to further listings but do not make them certain.

Data sources and how listings appear: New listings are enacted by Council legal acts (CFSP decision and implementing regulation) that amend the Annex listing persons; the acts are published in the OJ L series and typically use operative language such as “Annex IV to Regulation (EU) 2017/2063 is amended as set out in the Annex,” with the Annex enumerating added persons.
resolution_criteria:
Time window and timezone: Eligible additions are those whose adding legal act is published in the OJ between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC (inclusive). The question resolves based on UTC timestamps.

What counts as an “addition”: Count each unique natural person who is newly listed (i.e., included) in the Venezuela regime’s list of persons by virtue of an EU legal act published in the OJ L series during the time window. Specifically, count persons added to the list by amendments to Annex IV of Council Regulation (EU) 2017/2063 (and the corresponding annex to Council Decision (CFSP) 2017/2074) where the act’s Annex explicitly introduces new entries. Do not count acts that only update existing entries (e.g., change details) without adding new persons, nor acts that solely delist persons. If a person was not on the list immediately prior to the act’s publication and is included by the act, that person counts as an addition. If the same person is added more than once during the window (e.g., due to a clerical correction), count them once.

How to resolve:
1) Using EUR-Lex, list all OJ L series publications between the start and end timestamps that amend the Venezuela regime lists (search for acts amending Council Regulation (EU) 2017/2063 and/or Council Decision (CFSP) 2017/2074). Open each act and inspect the operative clause and its Annex. Identify whether the Annex enumerates newly added persons and count them. Acts whose annexes only revise existing entries (as with 2025/42’s updates) contribute zero to the addition count. Acts that add new entries (as with 2025/44) contribute the number of newly listed persons specified in the Annex.
2) Sum all additions across eligible acts. Resolve Yes if the total is ≥5; otherwise No.

Primary source of truth: Official Journal of the European Union (EUR-Lex) OJ L series. The OJ is binding and authoritative; the electronic OJ has legal value. Council press releases can be used for corroboration but the OJ governs resolution.

Notes:
- Legal framework references: Council Decision (CFSP) 2017/2074 defines the regime and procedures, and Council Regulation (EU) 2017/2063 (consolidated) contains Annex IV listing persons; both are amended by subsequent acts published in OJ L.
- Examples: Council Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/44 added 15 persons to Annex IV (illustrative of how additions are published) ; Council Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/42 updated entries without adding new persons.

Ambiguity reduction:
- “Between” is inclusive of both endpoints in UTC.
- “Added” is determined solely by OJ L acts’ Annexes introducing new entries; updates or delistings do not count. If an act both adds new persons and delists others, only the newly added persons contribute to the count.
- “Natural persons” excludes legal persons (entities/corporations), per legal definition.

question: By December 31, 2025 (UTC), will ACEA EU‑27 data show Tesla’s new passenger car registrations for January–November 2025 at least 30% lower than January–November 2024?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01: ACEA (the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association) publishes monthly press releases on “New passenger car registrations in Europe,” with EU‑27 figures and breakdowns that include manufacturer-level data; August 2025’s release demonstrates the cadence of these monthly, year-to-date updates, and ACEA states it provides registrations broken down by country, fuel type, and manufacturer. Reuters reported that for January–August 2025, Tesla’s sales (i.e., new registrations) in the European Union were down 42.9% year-over-year, and down 32.6% in Europe as a whole, indicating a substantial decline through late summer even as some individual markets began to show monthly rebounds. ACEA’s statistics press release calendar lists the publication date for the November 2025 passenger car registrations release (which will include January–November cumulative data) as Tuesday, 23 December 2025, ensuring availability before year-end.

Key definitions and scope:
- European Union (EU‑27): The 27 member states of the European Union; see EU entry for country list and membership. Link: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_state_of_the_European_Union (reference link only; scope in this question follows ACEA’s EU‑27 usage in its passenger-car registrations releases) [concept; ACEA monthly EU scope indicated in 4eb73f].
- New passenger car registration: The first-time registration of a new passenger vehicle, corresponding to EU vehicle category M1 (vehicles designed and constructed for the carriage of passengers, with no more than eight seats in addition to the driver’s seat). Link: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_classification#European_Union (reference link). In ACEA statistics, “passenger car registrations” refer to new passenger car registrations and exclude commercial vehicles; ACEA publishes these monthly for the EU.
- Tesla: The automotive marque of Tesla, Inc., as reported in ACEA’s by‑manufacturer registration tables. Link: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc (reference link).
- Periods compared: “January–November 2025” means registrations with registration dates from 2025‑01‑01 00:00:00 to 2025‑11‑30 23:59:59 (calendar months Jan through Nov); “January–November 2024” means registrations from 2024‑01‑01 00:00:00 to 2024‑11‑30 23:59:59. Times are expressed in UTC for clarity; ACEA aggregates by calendar month.
- Europe vs EU: This question uses EU‑27 only (ACEA’s EU scope). Figures that include EFTA and/or the UK (“Europe as a whole”) are out of scope.

Why this threshold and timing: Through Jan–Aug 2025, Tesla’s EU registrations were down 42.9% YoY, but late‑year performance (Sep–Nov) could narrow the gap, leaving realistic uncertainty around whether the full Jan–Nov decline will be ≥30%. Using Jan–Nov avoids year‑end lags in full‑year publications while capturing most of the annual cycle. The ACEA calendar shows the November release will be published on 23 December 2025, allowing resolution before year‑end.
resolution_criteria:
Yes if ACEA’s EU‑27 cumulative Tesla new passenger car registrations for January–November 2025 are at least 30% lower than the ACEA EU‑27 cumulative Tesla new passenger car registrations for January–November 2024; No otherwise.

Operationalization:
- Source of truth: The ACEA “New passenger car registrations in Europe” press release for November 2025 (published 23 December 2025 per ACEA’s calendar), together with its accompanying ‘by manufacturer’ EU‑27 table or annex, will be used to extract Tesla’s EU‑27 brand totals for Jan–Nov 2025 and Jan–Nov 2024. The monthly press releases and their YTD framing (e.g., the August 2025 release) establish the reporting cadence and EU scope.
- Computation: Let R2025 be Tesla’s EU‑27 new passenger car registrations cumulative for Jan–Nov 2025 and R2024 be Tesla’s EU‑27 cumulative for Jan–Nov 2024, as reported in ACEA’s by‑manufacturer EU‑27 table. Compute percentage change as (R2025 − R2024) / R2024. Resolve Yes if this is ≤ −30.0%; resolve No otherwise. Equivalently, Yes if R2025 ≤ 0.70 × R2024.
- Scope constraints: Use EU‑27 totals only; exclude non‑EU countries (e.g., EFTA, UK). Use passenger cars only; exclude commercial vehicles (LCVs, trucks, buses), consistent with ACEA’s passenger‑car statistics. Use Tesla brand totals; do not include other marques.
- Timing: Resolution occurs upon publication of November 2025 ACEA passenger‑car registrations (EU‑27) and its by‑manufacturer table, expected on 2025‑12‑23 per ACEA’s press release calendar; in any case, resolution will be made using the latest available ACEA November 2025 EU‑27 passenger‑car registrations data as of 2025‑12‑31 23:59:59 UTC.

Notes on validation: Background context on the 2025 YTD decline comes from Reuters’ report citing January–August 2025 declines for Tesla in the EU and Europe as a whole; this context is for forecasting background only and is not used directly in resolution. ACEA’s reliable statistics page affirms availability of manufacturer‑level registration breakdowns, and the August 2025 press release demonstrates monthly YTD reporting and EU scope.

question: Will BEA’s third estimate report real U.S. GDP growth (SAAR) for Q3 2025 at or above 3.6% on December 19, 2025?
background:
Context as of October 1, 2025:
- Scheduled release: The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) lists “Gross Domestic Product, 3rd Quarter 2025 (Third Estimate), GDP by Industry, and Corporate Profits (Revised)” for Friday, December 19 at 8:30 AM on its news release schedule. December is within Eastern Standard Time (EST), which is UTC−5 (Eastern Time in winter months).
- What is a “third estimate”? BEA publishes quarterly GDP estimates in three vintages—advance, second, and third—released near the end of the first, second, and third months after the quarter, based on progressively more comprehensive source data. The “third estimate” is the third and final vintage in the regular quarterly cycle.
- Definitions used in resolution:
  • Real GDP: BEA’s real (chain-type index/chained-dollar) estimates remove the effects of price changes to show changes in output or spending over time. See BEA’s concepts/methods and NIPA Handbook for details (links provided in Resolution Criteria).
  • SAAR (Seasonally Adjusted Annual Rate): BEA expresses monthly and quarterly values at seasonally adjusted annual rates; levels and changes are calculated on this SAAR basis.
- Recent GDP context: BEA’s third estimate for Q1 2025 reported real GDP at −0.5% SAAR. BEA’s third estimate for Q2 2025 reported real GDP at +3.8% SAAR, an upward revision of 0.5 percentage point from the second estimate. As of September 26, 2025, the Atlanta Fed’s GDPNow model estimate for Q3 2025 was 3.9%, with the next update scheduled for October 1.
- Why the 3.6% threshold? To maximize forecast uncertainty (entropy), the threshold is set close to recent outcomes and nowcasts: Q2 2025 third estimate was 3.8% , and the late-September GDPNow nowcast was 3.9% , making ≥3.6% a plausible but nontrivial cutoff.

Key terms and links:
- BEA release schedule: https://www.bea.gov/news/schedule 
- Eastern Time Zone (EST = UTC−5 in December): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone 
- BEA overview of GDP vintages: https://www.bea.gov/sites/default/files/2024-12/gdp3q24-3rd.pdf (see notes on advance/second/third estimates) 
- Real GDP methodology and chained-dollar/chain-type indexes: https://www.bea.gov/help/faq/79 
- SAAR usage by BEA: https://www.bea.gov/news/pio-release-additional-information 
- Recent BEA GDP releases for context: Q1 2025 third estimate https://www.bea.gov/news/2025/gross-domestic-product-1st-quarter-2025-third-estimate-gdp-industry-and-corporate-profits ; Q2 2025 third estimate https://www.bea.gov/news/2025/gross-domestic-product-2nd-quarter-2025-third-estimate-gdp-industry-corporate-profits 
- GDPNow (contextual nowcast): https://www.atlantafed.org/cqer/research/gdpnow 

Start and end of forecasting window:
- The event being forecast is the specific BEA publication at 13:30 UTC (8:30 AM EST) on December 19, 2025. The question resolves upon that release; any corrections posted after 23:59 UTC on December 19, 2025 are ignored for resolution purposes.
resolution_criteria:
Primary source and timing:
- Resolve using the BEA news release published on Friday, December 19, 2025, at 8:30 AM Eastern Standard Time (EST; UTC−5) titled “Gross Domestic Product, 3rd Quarter 2025 (Third Estimate), GDP by Industry, and Corporate Profits (Revised)” listed on BEA’s release schedule (https://www.bea.gov/news/schedule). 

What to read and the exact figure:
- Identify the real GDP growth rate (seasonally adjusted annual rate, SAAR) for Q3 2025 as shown in Table 1 of the release package (the table typically labeled “Real gross domestic product (GDP): percent change from preceding quarter”) or, if Table 1 is unavailable, use the percentage stated in the headline text of the release. “Real GDP” refers to BEA’s chain-type quantity indexes/chained dollars (i.e., inflation-adjusted output) , and “SAAR” means the percent change expressed at a seasonally adjusted annual rate per BEA practice. 

Decision rule:
- YES if the BEA’s reported Q3 2025 real GDP percent change from the preceding quarter (SAAR) is ≥ 3.6% in the December 19, 2025 third estimate release; NO if it is < 3.6%.

Timezone and versioning:
- Use the values as displayed in the BEA’s December 19 publication as of 23:59 UTC on December 19, 2025. If there are multiple posted versions on that day, use the latest version available before 23:59 UTC.

Contingencies:
- If the December 19, 2025 third-estimate release is postponed, resolve using the first BEA publication of “Gross Domestic Product, 3rd Quarter 2025 (Third Estimate), GDP by Industry, and Corporate Profits (Revised)” that appears on or before 23:59 UTC December 31, 2025 on bea.gov. If no such BEA third-estimate release for Q3 2025 is posted by 23:59 UTC December 31, 2025, resolve NO.

Reference documents for definitions and schedule:
- BEA release schedule: https://www.bea.gov/news/schedule 
- Eastern Time Zone (EST = UTC−5 in December): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone 
- Definition/methods for real GDP (chain-type/chained dollars): https://www.bea.gov/help/faq/79 
- SAAR usage by BEA: https://www.bea.gov/news/pio-release-additional-information 
- BEA description of GDP estimate vintages (advance/second/third): https://www.bea.gov/sites/default/files/2024-12/gdp3q24-3rd.pdf

question: By October 31, 2025, will President Irfaan Ali publish a Presidential Proclamation appointing the date, time, and place for the first sitting of Guyana’s new National Assembly?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-09-30: Multiple Guyanese outlets reported that the Clerk of the National Assembly, Sherlock Isaacs, is awaiting a Presidential Proclamation that appoints the time, date, and place for the first sitting of the new Parliament; he stated that at that sitting MPs will take their oaths and a Speaker will be elected. In Guyana, a new Parliament is summoned by a proclamation issued by the President which appoints the place and hour of the first sitting; the Clerk reads this proclamation at the first meeting, after which the roll of members is called and the Speaker and Deputy Speaker are elected, followed by swearing-in of Members. The President issued Proclamation No. 1 of 2025 dissolving Parliament on July 3, 2025, and such proclamations are publicly disseminated through official channels (e.g., the Department of Public Information). Proclamations and subsidiary legislation are also published in the Official Gazette of Guyana (the government’s public journal) and on the Parliament’s publications portal (Proclamations are listed under Subsidiary Legislation). As an example of how first sittings are publicly announced, the Parliament released details for the first sitting of the Twelfth Parliament (held at the Arthur Chung Conference Centre at 10:00 a.m. on September 1, 2020). Time zone: Guyana uses Guyana Time (GYT), which is UTC−4 year-round with no daylight saving time.

Key definitions and sources forecasters should know:
- Presidential Proclamation: For this market, a formal instrument issued by the President of Guyana that summons Parliament and appoints the time, date, and place for the first sitting of the National Assembly of the new Parliament. In Guyanese practice, proclamations are recognized and published as subsidiary legislation by Parliament and appear in the Official Gazette (often as Extraordinary Gazettes).
- First sitting of the National Assembly: The first meeting day of the National Assembly of the new Parliament, at which the proclamation is read, the Speaker and Deputy Speaker are elected, and members are sworn in, per the Parliament’s manual of rules.
- Authoritative publication channels: The Official Gazette of Guyana (https://officialgazette.gov.gy/), Parliament of Guyana’s website (https://parliament.gov.gy/), and official government communications such as the Department of Public Information or Office of the President (e.g., DPI article carrying Proclamation No. 1 of 2025).

Why this is non-trivial: As of late September 2025, no proclamation setting the first sitting had yet been published and stakeholders were publicly waiting on it; while proclamations are routine, there can be timing and political considerations around convening the new Parliament, making the issuance before a specific cut-off uncertain.
resolution_criteria:
This resolves to Yes if, between the start and end times below (inclusive), a Presidential Proclamation explicitly appointing all three of: (a) the date, (b) the time, and (c) the place for the first sitting of the National Assembly of the Parliament summoned after the July 3, 2025 dissolution is published by an authoritative channel (defined below). Otherwise, No.

Date window and time zones:
- Start: 2025-07-03 00:00:00 GYT (UTC−4) = 2025-07-03 04:00:00 UTC 
- End: 2025-10-31 23:59:59 GYT (UTC−4) = 2025-11-01 03:59:59 UTC 

What counts as a qualifying proclamation and publication:
- The document must be explicitly identified as a “Proclamation” issued by the President of Guyana, appointing the date, time, and place for the first sitting of the National Assembly of the new Parliament (i.e., the Parliament constituted following Proclamation No. 1 of 2025 dissolving the prior Parliament on July 3, 2025).
- “Published” means publicly accessible on any of the following authoritative channels: the Official Gazette of Guyana website (including Ordinary or Extraordinary Gazette PDFs); the Parliament of Guyana’s official website (e.g., its Proclamations or media releases sections); or an official government site such as the Department of Public Information or the Office of the President where the proclamation itself is posted or reproduced (including numbered proclamation references).
- The content must specify all three elements (date, time, and place). Proclamations that omit any one of these (e.g., appointing a date/place but not a time) do not qualify.
- If multiple proclamations are issued, the earliest one within the window that first appoints all three elements qualifies.

Preferred resolution sources to check on or after End:
1) Official Gazette of Guyana (https://officialgazette.gov.gy/) for Proclamation listings and Gazette PDFs.
2) Parliament of Guyana publications: Subsidiary Legislation → Proclamations, and/or Media Centre press releases.
3) Official government communications (e.g., Department of Public Information; Office of the President) that publish the proclamation (by title/number and full text).

Clarifications:
- This question does not require that the first sitting actually occurs by the End; it only requires publication of the proclamation appointing its date/time/place.
- Media-only reports without a posted proclamation on an authoritative channel do not count; media may be used as corroboration when they link to or reproduce the proclamation issued by an authoritative channel.
- Time zone definitions: Guyana Time (GYT) is UTC−4 year-round with no daylight saving time; all times herein are both in GYT and UTC for clarity.

question: Will Singapore’s reported LNG bunker sales reach at least 50,000 tonnes in any single month during October–November 2025 (counting December 2025 only if published by the deadline)?
background:
Context for forecasters (status quo as of 2025-10-01):
- Official data source: The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) publishes “Bunker Sales Breakdown, Monthly” on data.gov.sg. The dataset “shows the monthly bunker sales by type in tonnes” and states that “latest month figures are preliminary estimates.” It is updated monthly and is the intended single source of truth for monthly volumes by fuel type. MPA also provides a public-facing “Bunkering Statistics” page noting that it gives regular monthly updates for bunker sales volumes in port, corroborating that monthly figures are routinely published.
- Recent figures: In 2024, Singapore’s total bunker sales reached 54.92 million tonnes; sales of alternative bunker fuels exceeded one million tonnes to reach 1.34 million tonnes, including 0.88 million tonnes of biofuel blends and 0.46 million tonnes of LNG. These headline figures (from MPA’s media centre) provide recent context for LNG bunkering scale and growth into 2025.

Definitions and measurement scope:
- Liquefied natural gas (LNG): Natural gas (predominantly methane) cooled to a liquid for non-pressurized storage/transport. This general definition is provided for clarity and to anchor the meaning of the LNG category in the dataset.
- Bunkering / bunker sales: Bunkering is the process of supplying fuel to ships; “bunker fuel” refers to fuels used to power ships. For this question, “bunker sales” specifically refers to the monthly sales volumes as reported in MPA’s “Bunker Sales Breakdown, Monthly” dataset, disaggregated by fuel type; the relevant category is LNG.
- Tonne (metric ton): A unit of mass equal to 1,000 kilograms. The dataset reports volumes in tonnes; thresholds in this question use the same unit.

Why this question: LNG bunkering in Singapore grew significantly in 2024 (to 0.46 million tonnes), but month-to-month LNG bunkering volumes can vary with vessel calls, price spreads, fuel availability, and fleet uptake. A 50,000-tonne threshold for a single month in late 2025 is plausibly achievable yet uncertain, creating a non-trivial forecasting target anchored to an official, regularly updated dataset.

Useful links (for verification and ongoing tracking):
- MPA “Bunker Sales Breakdown, Monthly” on data.gov.sg: https://data.gov.sg/datasets/d_4f5abbf4486bf8e52bbed3be56dde562/view 
- MPA Bunkering Statistics page: https://www.mpa.gov.sg/port-marine-ops/marine-services/bunkering/bunkering-statistics 
- LNG definition: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquefied_natural_gas 
- Tonne definition: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonne 
- Bunkering definition: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bunker_fuel
resolution_criteria:
Outcome determination (binary):
- YES if, as of the resolution deadline, the MPA “Bunker Sales Breakdown, Monthly” dataset on data.gov.sg reports a value greater than or equal to 50,000 tonnes for the LNG category in at least one of the following calendar months of 2025: October or November. December 2025 may also count, but only if the dataset includes a December 2025 LNG value by the resolution deadline (see below). Otherwise, NO.

Scope and measurement details:
- Eligible period: Calendar months October 2025 and November 2025 are always eligible. December 2025 is eligible only if a December 2025 LNG value is present on the dataset by the resolution deadline. The start date for eligible months is 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC; the end of the eligible window is 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.
- Data source (single source of truth): “Bunker Sales Breakdown, Monthly” dataset published by MPA on data.gov.sg. Use the LNG (liquefied natural gas) category row/field in that dataset; accept the exact category label as presented by MPA (e.g., “Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG)”) to identify LNG. Use the value reported in tonnes. Latest-month figures may be preliminary; preliminary figures are acceptable for resolution.
- Units and threshold: “50,000 tonnes” means 50,000 metric tons, where 1 tonne = 1,000 kilograms. Compare the dataset’s LNG monthly value(s) against 50,000 to determine if any eligible month meets or exceeds the threshold.

Resolution timing and method:
- Resolution deadline: Check the dataset as it appears on 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. The most recent values visible on the dataset at or before this timestamp are used. If December 2025 is not yet displayed on the dataset by that time, it does not count; if it is displayed, it may count even if marked preliminary.
- Handling revisions: If the dataset shows multiple versions or has been revised, use whatever LNG monthly values are visible on data.gov.sg at the resolution timestamp; subsequent revisions after the deadline are ignored for resolution purposes.

Adjudication notes:
- If data.gov.sg is temporarily unavailable at the deadline, resolve using the first available snapshot thereafter that can be verified to reflect the state as of the deadline (e.g., archived page or API results with retrieval timestamp). If verification of the exact as-of state is not possible, use the earliest retrievable state after the deadline and document the retrieval time; this fallback is only to protect against transient outages and does not change the substantive rule that only months visible by the deadline count.

Informational support (non-binding for resolution): MPA’s Bunkering Statistics page indicates MPA provides regular monthly bunker sales updates, corroborating that timely monthly figures exist, but the formal source for resolution is the data.gov.sg dataset.

References for definitions and context: LNG definition ; tonne definition ; bunkering definition ; 2024 totals and alternative fuels breakdown ; dataset description and preliminary status.

question: Will Shanghai remove numerical home-purchase caps inside the Outer Ring Road (外环线以内) between Oct 15 and Dec 31, 2025?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30:
- On Aug 25–26, 2025, Shanghai issued a joint notice titled “关于优化调整本市房地产政策措施的通知” (沪建房管联〔2025〕417号). It explicitly removed the cap on the number of homes eligible resident families can purchase outside the Outer Ring Road (外环线以外), stating purchases there are “不限套数.” The notice also clarifies adult single individuals are treated as families for the purpose of these rules, and references the qualification verification mechanisms used in Shanghai’s housing policy administration. Reuters reporting the same day summarized that Shanghai removed restrictions on the number of homes eligible families can buy outside the city’s outer ring road and noted the change took effect Aug 26, 2025. A Shanghai Housing Administration site index page also lists this notice by number and effective date.
- Beijing, earlier in Aug 2025, eased suburban purchase restrictions, lifting curbs for qualified buyers outside its Fifth Ring Road while keeping curbs within the Fifth Ring, as reported by Reuters.
- Definition of the “Outer Ring Road”: In Shanghai, the S20 Outer Ring Expressway encircles the inner districts and is commonly used as the geographic demarcation between inner and outer areas; “outside the Outer Ring Road” refers to areas beyond this ring and “inside” (外环线以内) refers to areas within the area enclosed by S20.
Status quo: Shanghai’s Aug 2025 policy relaxation applied specifically to areas outside the Outer Ring Road and did not announce the removal of numerical purchase caps for areas inside the Outer Ring Road. This question asks whether Shanghai will take the further step of removing the numerical home-purchase cap for any area inside the Outer Ring Road by year-end 2025.
Why this should be forecastable: The Aug 2025 move created a clear policy pathway and precedent (removing caps outside the Ring), but whether authorities will extend similar easing to inner areas remains uncertain and depends on market conditions, fiscal/financial constraints, and central guidance.
resolution_criteria:
Question: Between 2025-10-15 00:00 and 2025-12-31 23:59 China Standard Time (CST, UTC+8), will the Shanghai municipal government publish an official notice that removes the numerical cap on the number of residential units a resident family may purchase within the area inside the S20 Outer Ring Road (外环线以内)?

Definitions and what counts:
- Inside the Outer Ring Road (外环线以内): The area enclosed by the S20 Shanghai Outer Ring Expressway. This ring expressway encircles the inner districts and serves as the boundary used in the Aug 2025 notice.
- Numerical home-purchase cap (套数限制): Policy restrictions that limit the number of residential units a family/household may purchase. “Removal of the cap” means official language indicating “不限套数” (no limit on the number of homes) or equivalent language that clearly removes the numerical purchase limit for the covered inner-area geography.
- Resident family (居民家庭): As used in Shanghai’s housing purchase rules, i.e., “符合本市住房购买条件的居民家庭,” which include categories defined by the municipality (e.g., local hukou families, non-local families meeting social insurance/tax requirements, and adult single individuals treated as families). For the purpose of this question, it is sufficient if the removal of the numerical cap applies to any subset of resident families as defined in the notice (e.g., local hukou families or adult singles), as long as the covered homes are inside the Outer Ring Road.
- Official notice: A formal document published by Shanghai municipal authorities responsible for housing policy (e.g., Shanghai Municipal Commission of Housing and Urban-Rural Development and/or Shanghai Municipal Housing Administration Bureau, potentially as a joint notice with related agencies), posted on official municipal websites such as the Shanghai Housing Administration (fgj.sh.gov.cn) under sections like 政策文件/通知 or the dedicated policy/“阅办联动” index. The notice must explicitly cover areas inside the Outer Ring Road and must clearly remove the numerical purchase cap there.

Resolution:
- Resolve Yes if between the stated CST times, an official Shanghai municipal notice is published that explicitly removes the numerical purchase cap (expressed as “不限套数” or equivalent) for residential purchases inside the Outer Ring Road, citywide or in any named inner-area geography (e.g., a district, subdistrict, or project area located inside the S20). The change may apply to either new commercial housing, existing homes, or both; any one of these categories suffices.
- Resolve No otherwise (including if easing occurs only outside the Outer Ring Road; if the notice is published before 2025-10-15 or after 2025-12-31 CST; or if the inner-area easing does not remove the numerical cap but merely adjusts other parameters like down payments or qualification criteria without removing 套数限制).

How to verify:
1) Check the Shanghai Housing Administration website (fgj.sh.gov.cn), especially the policy document sections and the “阅办联动专栏” index that lists such notices, for any publication between the stated dates containing language removing 套数限制 for 外环线以内.
2) If the official site is temporarily inaccessible, corroborate using credible outlets that report and quote the official notice text and/or document number (e.g., Reuters), ensuring the article explicitly states that the removal applies inside the Outer Ring Road and that the notice was published within the time window. The primary source of truth remains the official municipal publications.

question: Will Ulta Beauty report Q3 FY2025 comparable sales growth of at least 5.0%?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30:
- Metric and definition: Ulta Beauty reports “comparable sales” as a key operating metric. In recent press releases, Ulta defines comparable sales as “sales for stores open at least 14 months and e-commerce sales”. Ulta’s 2025 Form 10-K further clarifies that comparable sales include retail sales, salon services, and e-commerce; stores are included beginning on the first day of the 14th month of operation; remodeled stores remain in the comp base unless closed for part of the period; and in 53-week fiscal years the 53rd week is included, with the following year’s comparison shifted by one week to align comparable calendar weeks. Ulta’s fiscal year consists of 52 or 53 weeks ending on the Saturday closest to January 31. For additional general context, same-store/comparable sales in retail refers to the revenue change of existing outlets over a period compared to the same period a year earlier, excluding new or closed outlets.
- Latest results: In Q2 FY2025 (thirteen weeks ended August 2, 2025), Ulta reported comparable sales growth of 6.7% year-over-year and raised its full-year FY2025 comparable sales guidance to 2.5%–3.5%.
- Disclosure timing: Ulta’s IR calendar lists a “Q3 2025 Ulta Beauty Earnings Conference Call” on December 4, 2025, indicating Q3 FY2025 results will be released and discussed on or around that date.
Why this is interesting: Q2 comps were robust (+6.7%), but the full-year guide (2.5%–3.5%) implies more modest run-rate growth, and Q3 spans early holiday activity where promotional intensity and demand can swing outcomes. This makes a 5.0% threshold plausibly uncertain for Q3 FY2025.
resolution_criteria:
Resolve Yes if Ulta’s Q3 FY2025 press release states that comparable sales for the quarter increased by at least 5.0% year-over-year; resolve No if it states a figure below 5.0%.

Key definitions and rules:
- “Comparable sales” means Ulta’s company-reported comparable sales metric, which includes retail, salon services, and e-commerce; stores enter the comp base on the first day of the 14th month of operation; remodeled stores remain unless closed for part of the period; 52/53-week rules apply as described in Ulta’s filings. Ulta press releases describe this as “sales for stores open at least 14 months and e-commerce sales”.
- “Q3 FY2025” refers to Ulta’s third fiscal quarter of FY2025 as defined by the company’s fiscal calendar (a 52/53-week fiscal year ending on the Saturday closest to January 31).
- “At least 5.0%” means greater than or equal to 5.0%. The determination will use the percentage exactly as presented in the source document. If Ulta reports the figure to one decimal place, that displayed rounded figure governs. If a more precise figure is presented (e.g., in tables), that precise figure governs if it clearly refers to the overall company comparable sales for the quarter.
- If multiple comparable-sales-related figures are given (e.g., by channel, transactions, ticket), only the overall company “comparable sales” percentage for the quarter is used. Do not use year-to-date figures.
- Corrections: If Ulta issues an official correction to the press release or filing by 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, the corrected figure governs.

Primary source of truth:
- Ulta Beauty’s Q3 FY2025 earnings press release posted on the company’s Investor Relations website on or around December 4, 2025.

Fallback sources (used only if the press release is not available or is ambiguous by 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025):
1) Ulta’s Form 10-Q for Q3 FY2025 filed with the U.S. SEC (EDGAR), using the overall company comparable sales percentage for the quarter as defined above.
2) If neither the press release nor the 10-Q is available by the resolution deadline, use credible mainstream reporting (e.g., Reuters, AP, Bloomberg, WSJ) that directly quotes Ulta’s reported Q3 FY2025 comparable sales percentage.

Timing and timezone:
- The question resolves upon the first eligible source’s publication, with any corrections through 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025 considered. All dates/times are in UTC.

Notes to forecasters:
- As of Q2 FY2025, comparable sales growth was 6.7%, and full-year FY2025 comparable sales guidance was 2.5%–3.5%. Q3 FY2025 results are scheduled to be discussed on December 4, 2025 per Ulta’s IR calendar.

question: Will Colombia’s Superintendencia Nacional de Salud order any formal special measure on SANITAS EPS S.A.S. between 00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025?
background:
Context and status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- Superintendencia Nacional de Salud (Supersalud) is Colombia’s health-sector supervisory authority and publishes its administrative acts (resoluciones) on its official website; its “Resoluciones” page serves as the public repository for resolution PDFs.
- In Colombia, an Entidad Promotora de Salud (EPS) is the organization responsible for affiliating and registering insured persons in the public health system and managing contributions for healthcare providers (IPS).
