- Quota: The number of votes necessary for election; for this single-winner election it is defined as fifty percent of valid votes plus one, as calculated and applied by the PRO.
Primary sources for resolution include: the PRO’s results page and any associated official notices/declarations on https://www.presidentialelection.ie/. RTÉ provides an authoritative procedural overview and timing of count commencement (09:00 on 25 October).
resolution_criteria:
Question: Will any candidate be elected on the first count in Ireland’s 2025 presidential election between 00:00 UTC on 15 October 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on 31 December 2025?

Operational definitions:
- Presidential Returning Officer (PRO): The official in charge of ascertaining and declaring the result of the presidential election based on constituency reports, as described in official guidance. For the 2025 election, the PRO publishes results at https://www.presidentialelection.ie/election-results/index.html.
- First count: The initial tally of first-preference votes (the ‘1’ rankings) for each candidate, aggregated nationally after local counts and reported to the PRO; this is the first published count on the PRO site.
- First-preference vote: A vote marked with the numeral ‘1’ beside a candidate’s name under Ireland’s preferential PR–STV system.
- Valid votes / Valid Poll: Ballots judged valid and included in the “Valid Poll” figure displayed on the PRO’s results page; invalid ballot papers are excluded.
- Quota (for this election): The number of votes necessary for election in a single-winner contest, defined as fifty percent of valid votes plus one and calculated by the PRO; the PRO will display the official “Quota” on the results page.

Resolution rule:
- Resolve Yes if, according to the final official national first-count results published by the PRO, at least one candidate’s first-preference total is equal to or greater than the official Quota on the first count (i.e., the candidate is declared elected on the first count). Otherwise resolve No.

Source of truth and where to look:
- Primary source: The PRO’s official results page for the 2025 election at https://www.presidentialelection.ie/election-results/index.html and any associated official notices/declarations on the same site. Use the final figures as they stand after any recounts concluded before resolution (see below).

Timing and contingencies:
- Event window: Only outcomes determined and published between 00:00 UTC on 2025-10-15 and 23:59:59 UTC on 2025-12-31 are eligible for resolution.
- Recounts: If there is a recount or re-examination that alters the first-count totals or quota before the declaration, use the final official figures at the time the PRO declares the result; recount procedures exist under Irish election rules. If a recount is ordered and not concluded by 2025-12-31, postpone resolution until completion or resolve N/A if no definitive first-count figures are available by that date.
- Publication delay/backup: If the PRO website is unavailable for more than 72 hours after the declaration, resolve based on consistent, credible reporting from mainstream outlets (e.g., RTÉ, BBC, Reuters, AP) explicitly stating whether a candidate was elected on the first count, and corroborate when the PRO site becomes available again.

Notes for resolvers:
- The candidates on the 2025 ballot (per the official Notice of Poll) are Catherine Connolly, Jim Gavin, and Heather Humphreys. The official results page indicates it will publish the first count, the Valid Poll, and the Quota, which are the only figures needed to apply this criterion.

question: Spain: Will the Congress of Deputies approve the 2026 fiscal path and the Government’s 2026 non‑financial spending limit by December 31, 2025?
background:
Overview and status quo as of 2025‑10‑01:
• Spain’s 2026 General State Budget (PGE 2026) requires two key preliminary steps before a budget bill can be advanced: (1) the Government must set the objectives of budgetary stability and public debt for the next three fiscal years (commonly referred to as the “fiscal/stability path”), and (2) include the State’s non‑financial spending limit (also called the “techo de gasto” or “límite de gasto no financiero”) in the Government agreement. Under Spain’s Organic Law 2/2012 (LOEPSF), the Council of Ministers sets these and sends the stability and debt objectives to the Cortes Generales for debate and votes, including a Plenary vote in the Congress of Deputies.
• As of September 29–30, 2025, the Council of Ministers had not approved the 2026 spending ceiling (“techo de gasto”) or the fiscal path, and the Government stated it would present them “soon” for subsequent debate and votes in Congress. On October 1, 2025, reporting indicated the Council of Ministers met without these approvals, confirming continued delay.
• In July 2024, the Congress voted down the Government’s proposed stability and debt objectives linked to the 2025 budget process, illustrating the political difficulty of securing approval; recorded vote counts were 171 in favor and 178 against. In contrast, in February 2024, the Plenary recorded approval of the package for 2024—including the item that bundled stability/debt objectives and the State’s non‑financial spending limit—with 176 votes in favor and 171 against.

Key definitions and process:
• Congress of Deputies: the lower house of Spain’s Cortes Generales (see background: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_Deputies_(Spain)).
• Fiscal/stability path: the Government’s “objetivos de estabilidad presupuestaria y de deuda pública” set for the following three fiscal years, expressed as percentages of nominal GDP, and debated/voted in the Cortes Generales. LOEPSF Article 15 sets the framework, timing, and the requirement that Congress (and the Senate) pronounce on approval or rejection, with Congress able to ratify by simple majority if the Senate rejects.
• Non‑financial spending limit (“techo de gasto” or “límite de gasto no financiero”): the maximum non‑financial expenditure limit for the State Budget, coherent with the stability objective and the expenditure rule. LOEPSF Articles 15 and 30 specify that the Council of Ministers’ agreement includes the State’s non‑financial spending limit.
• Government agreement item and Congress vote: In practice, the Government submits a combined item to the Plenary that includes both the stability/debt objectives and, for information, the State’s non‑financial spending limit for the Budget year. Congress’s Plenary debates and votes on the objectives; official records (Diario de Sesiones and Open Data vote files) identify the item and result (approved/rejected).

Why this is non‑trivial: As of 2025‑10‑01, the Government has not advanced these steps and faces political hurdles to securing a majority, making the timing and outcome uncertain.

Suggested sources for verification:
• Congress of Deputies Open Data vote records (machine‑readable vote files by session/date).
• Diario de Sesiones (Plenary) for the debate and the presiding officer’s pronouncement (“quedan aprobados…”/“quedan rechazados…”).
• Minister of Finance/La Moncloa communications or BOE for Council of Ministers’ approval of the State’s non‑financial spending limit.
resolution_criteria:
Start and end of the observation window:
• Eligible events must occur between 00:00 UTC on October 1, 2025 and 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025.

What must happen to resolve YES:
• By 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, both of the following conditions are met:
  1) The Congress of Deputies Plenary approves the Government’s “objetivos de estabilidad presupuestaria y de deuda pública” for 2026–2028 (the fiscal/stability path) in accordance with LOEPSF Article 15. Approval is evidenced by either:
     – The Diario de Sesiones (Plenary) recording the presiding officer’s pronouncement that the objectives are approved (“quedan aprobados…”), or
     – The Congress Open Data vote record for the relevant Plenary session showing a result indicating approval (majority in favor) of the item corresponding to the stability/debt objectives (e.g., the vote file’s metadata and counts).
     Note: If the Senate rejects the objectives, the Congress may ratify by simple majority; approval is satisfied if the Congress has approved or ratified the objectives within the window.
  2) The Council of Ministers has approved and published the State’s non‑financial spending limit (“límite de gasto no financiero”) for the 2026 Budget. Evidence includes a Government/La Moncloa release or BOE publication identifying the Council of Ministers’ agreement that includes the 2026 State non‑financial spending limit, consistent with LOEPSF Articles 15 and 30.

Resolve NO if either condition (1) or (2) is not met within the observation window.

Clarifications to avoid ambiguity:
• “Congress approval” refers specifically to the Congress of Deputies Plenary vote on the Government agreement item for the stability/debt objectives (the fiscal path), not to committee votes. Use the Congress’s official Diario de Sesiones or Open Data vote records to confirm the approval status and date.
• “Non‑financial spending limit” refers to the State Budget’s limit set in the Council of Ministers’ agreement (the “techo de gasto”), as defined in LOEPSF Articles 15 and 30. The relevant approval event is a Council of Ministers decision published by the Government (e.g., La Moncloa) or the BOE.
• Time zone handling: If the official source provides only a date (without time), use the date in Madrid local time to assess whether it falls within the window; any such date on or before December 31, 2025 local time counts as within the window. If a timestamp is available, convert to UTC and apply the window.
• Pars pro toto indicator: The existence of the official Congress Plenary vote record and the Diario de Sesiones pronouncement is the proxy for “approval” of the fiscal/stability path; the existence of the Council of Ministers’ published agreement is the proxy for “approval” of the State’s non‑financial spending limit.

question: Between October 15 and December 31, 2025 (UTC), will Warner Bros. Discovery, Inc. and Paramount, a Skydance Corporation, publicly disclose that they have entered into a binding definitive agreement to merge or for one to acquire the other?
background:
Status quo as of October 1, 2025:
- Paramount Global and Skydance Media completed their merger on August 7, 2025, creating the combined parent company "Paramount, a Skydance Corporation" (also referenced in SEC filings as "Paramount Skydance Corporation"). The company’s press releases and investor relations materials confirm the new name and that Class B shares trade on Nasdaq under the ticker PSKY. The SEC Form 8-K filed on August 7, 2025 details the closing mechanics and uses the registrant name Paramount Skydance Corporation.
- Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) announced on June 9, 2025 plans to separate into two publicly traded companies by mid-2026—“Streaming & Studios” and “Global Networks”—including component lists and leadership roles, via its investor relations press release. WBD maintains a Financial News section on its IR website where such press releases are published.
- Media reporting in September 2025 indicates that Paramount, a Skydance Corporation, is exploring or preparing a majority-cash bid to acquire WBD; these reports describe an exploratory stage, not a signed agreement, and note that neither company commented at that time. The New York Times coverage provides additional market context, including WBD’s approximate valuation (~$41B) and debt (~$35B) and notes the strategic implications of any potential deal.

Key definitions and data sources forecasters may rely on:
- Merger and acquisition: A merger is the legal consolidation of two business entities into one; an acquisition occurs when one entity takes ownership of another’s share capital, equity interests, or assets.
- Material Definitive Agreement disclosures: U.S. public companies disclose entry into certain material, binding agreements not made in the ordinary course of business via Form 8-K Item 1.01; this is the standard mechanism by which definitive M&A agreements are publicly disclosed.
- Official press releases: Paramount, a Skydance Corporation publishes press releases on its IR site (e.g., its August 7, 2025 merger completion release) , and WBD publishes press releases on its IR site.

Why this question has non-trivial uncertainty:
- Industry consolidation remains plausible following Paramount’s recent merger and WBD’s stated plan to separate businesses by mid-2026, creating potential transaction structures (e.g., agreements contingent on the separation).
- Reputable reporting in September 2025 suggests active exploration by Paramount, but no binding agreement had been announced as of those reports.

Time window:
- Eligible announcements must occur between October 15, 2025 00:00:00 UTC and December 31, 2025 23:59:59 UTC.
resolution_criteria:
Resolve YES if, between October 15, 2025 00:00:00 UTC and December 31, 2025 23:59:59 UTC, either of the following public disclosures occurs, clearly stating that Warner Bros. Discovery, Inc. (WBD) and Paramount, a Skydance Corporation (also referenced as Paramount Skydance Corporation in SEC filings) have entered into a binding definitive agreement to merge or for one to acquire the other:

- A joint press release, or separate press releases issued by both WBD and Paramount, published on their official corporate newsroom or investor relations websites, explicitly announcing that a definitive agreement has been signed (e.g., merger agreement, stock purchase agreement) under which either (a) the companies will legally merge into one parent entity, or (b) one company will acquire the other such that the acquirer will become the legal parent controlling the target.

OR

- A Form 8-K filed on EDGAR by either WBD or Paramount that discloses entry into a material definitive agreement under Item 1.01 establishing a merger or acquisition between the two companies as defined above. The 8-K must name the counterparty as Warner Bros. Discovery, Inc. or Paramount (Paramount Skydance Corporation) and describe a merger or acquisition, not merely exploratory talks or non-binding documents.

Definitions for resolution:
- "Definitive agreement": A legally binding contract that sets out agreed terms for a merger or acquisition. For U.S. public companies, such agreements are typically disclosed via Form 8-K Item 1.01, which requires reporting entry into material binding agreements not made in the ordinary course.
- "Merger": Legal consolidation of two business entities into one.
- "Acquisition": One entity takes ownership of another entity’s share capital, equity interests, or assets such that the acquirer becomes the controlling parent of the target.
- "Announce": Publish an official press release on the company’s newsroom or investor relations website, or file a Form 8-K that discloses entry into a material definitive agreement under Item 1.01.
- "Paramount, a Skydance Corporation" vs "Paramount Skydance Corporation": The combined company formed by the merger of Paramount Global and Skydance Media on August 7, 2025 is branded as "Paramount, a Skydance Corporation" in press materials; SEC filings reference the registrant as "Paramount Skydance Corporation". Both refer to the same parent entity for purposes of this question.

What does NOT count:
- Non-binding documents such as letters of intent, term sheets, MOUs, exclusivity agreements, or announcements of talks/interest without a signed definitive agreement.
- Agreements limited to asset purchases or licensing that do not result in one company becoming the legal parent controlling the other (i.e., no change of corporate control of the parent entity).
- Agreements with third parties where WBD and Paramount are not counterparties to a merger or acquisition between themselves.

Sources of truth to be checked at resolution:
- Warner Bros. Discovery investor relations Financial News page (for press releases): https://ir.wbd.com/news-and-events/financial-news/.
- Warner Bros. Discovery Newsroom: https://www.wbd.com/newsroom/ (for press releases; no claim cited here).
- Paramount investor relations press releases: https://ir.paramount.com/press-releases (e.g., merger completion press release confirming this is the official outlet).
- SEC EDGAR for Form 8-K filings (Item 1.01): https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search/#/category/form-8-k. For illustration, Paramount’s Aug 7, 2025 8-K documents the prior merger closing mechanics under the registrant name "Paramount Skydance Corporation".

Resolution timing:
- YES resolves at the timestamp of the first qualifying disclosure within the window.
- NO resolves at 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC if no qualifying disclosure occurred within the window.

question: Official wholesale USD/ARS reference (BCRA A 3500): Dec 31, 2025 ≥10% vs Oct 15, 2025
background:
Overview and definitions:
- USD denotes the United States dollar, the official currency of the United States. ARS denotes the Argentine peso, the currency of Argentina. An exchange rate is the rate at which one currency is exchanged for another, representing the value of one currency relative to another (here, USD/ARS).
- This question uses the Banco Central de la República Argentina (BCRA) “Tipo de Cambio Mayorista ($ por US$) Comunicación A 3500 - Referencia” series as the official wholesale reference USD/ARS rate. BCRA displays this series on its Principales Variables pages, including a link to the detailed data page for series 272 labeled exactly as above. BCRA’s Tipos de Cambio page also lists “Tipo de Cambio de Referencia Comunicación A 3500 (Mayorista)” and provides downloadable data, corroborating the series labeling and purpose as the reference wholesale rate.
- Status quo: As an example of recent levels, the Principales Variables page shows “Tipo de Cambio Mayorista ($ por USD) Comunicación A 3500 - Referencia | 29/09/2025 | 1.341,00”.
- Recent context: In late September 2025, authorities announced a 90-day cross-restriction limiting arbitrage (“rulo”) between the official dollar and financial dollar markets (MEP/CCL), with the stated intent of curbing such arbitrage and strengthening reserves. Reporting noted widened gaps between official and financial exchange rates around the announcement and increases in reported reserves. This policy backdrop contributes to uncertainty about the official wholesale rate’s path into year-end.

Why this is non-trivial: The threshold is set to 10% over the roughly 2.5-month interval, balancing plausible policy-driven stability against market pressures and policy changes, such that informed forecasters could reasonably forecast either outcome.

Date/time conventions: Dates cited are calendar dates as labeled on BCRA’s site. Resolution will be determined after 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC; however, the values used are those labeled “2025-10-15” and “2025-12-31” on the BCRA series pages.
resolution_criteria:
- What is being compared: Let V_oct15 be the value labeled “2025-10-15” and V_dec31 be the value labeled “2025-12-31” in the BCRA series “Tipo de Cambio Mayorista ($ por US$) Comunicación A 3500 - Referencia” (series 272).
- Computation: Compute the percentage change as (V_dec31 / V_oct15) − 1. Resolve Yes if (V_dec31 / V_oct15) ≥ 1.10; otherwise resolve No. No rounding or smoothing will be applied beyond using the exact published series values.
- Primary source of truth: BCRA Principales Variables pages for the series labeled “Tipo de Cambio Mayorista ($ por US$) Comunicación A 3500 - Referencia” and its detailed data page (series 272). Secondary corroboration (if needed): BCRA Tipos de Cambio page listing “Tipo de Cambio de Referencia Comunicación A 3500 (Mayorista)” and its downloadable data.
- Handling edge cases: If, unexpectedly, either date does not have a value displayed on the Principales Variables series page, use the value for that labeled date from the Tipos de Cambio downloadable file (if available). If the labeled date is absent from both locations (e.g., due to a site outage), resolve based on the first-accessible BCRA source that lists the series value for that calendar date; if neither source provides a value for the labeled date, the question will be put on hold until BCRA publishes the value for that date, after which it resolves under the same computation.
- Units and formatting: Values are pesos per U.S. dollar ($/USD) as published by BCRA for the reference wholesale rate under Comunicación A 3500.

question: By December 31, 2025 (UTC), will the FOMC’s federal funds rate target range midpoint be at least 50 basis points lower than on September 22, 2025 (UTC)?
background:
Context: Interest rates materially affect insurers’ portfolio yields and investment income. The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) sets a target range for the federal funds rate, influencing broader interest rates. A basis point (bp) is one hundredth of a percentage point (0.01%).
Status quo (as of 2025-09-22): The FOMC lowered the federal funds target range to 4.00%–4.25%, effective 2025-09-18. FRED’s upper-limit series (DFEDTARU) shows 4.25% on 2025-09-18 onward, down from 4.50% on 2025-09-17. Therefore, the baseline midpoint on 2025-09-22 is (4.25% + 4.00%) / 2 = 4.125%.
Relevance: Additional cuts (e.g., cumulative ≥50 bps vs. baseline) would further lower fixed-income yields’ discount rates yet may reprice portfolios and new money yields, affecting insurers’ investment income and profitability. Forecasters can track DFEDTARU and DFEDTARL on FRED for ongoing policy changes.
resolution_criteria:
Definitions:
- Federal funds rate target range: The range for the overnight federal funds rate set by the FOMC. We use the lower and upper limits as reported by FRED series DFEDTARL (lower limit) and DFEDTARU (upper limit). The midpoint is defined as (upper limit + lower limit) / 2.
- Basis point (bp): 0.01 percentage point.
Timeframe and baseline:
- Start date/time: 2025-09-22 00:00:00 UTC.
- Baseline midpoint: Computed from DFEDTARU and DFEDTARL values for 2025-09-22 (which reflect the effective 4.00%–4.25% range established 2025-09-18), yielding 4.125%.
Primary resolution:
- On 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, resolve using the FRED daily values labeled 2025-12-31 for DFEDTARU and DFEDTARL. Compute the midpoint.
- YES if the midpoint on 2025-12-31 is at least 0.50 percentage points (≥50 bps) lower than the baseline midpoint (≤3.625%). NO otherwise.
Data sources:
- Primary: FRED DFEDTARU (upper limit) and DFEDTARL (lower limit) daily series.
- Backup (if FRED is unavailable on resolution): Official Federal Reserve releases indicating the target range in effect on 2025-12-31; for method and precedent, see the Implementation Note language confirming target ranges and effective dates.
Edge cases:
- If DFEDTARU/DFEDTARL show no entry for 2025-12-31, use the latest available daily values on or before 2025-12-31.
- “At least 50 bps” includes exactly 50 bps (i.e., a 0.500 percentage point reduction).

question: Will the EU formally adopt and publish a rule change enabling qualified majority voting (QMV) to open at least one accession negotiating cluster for Ukraine by 23:59 UTC on 31 December 2025?
background:
Status quo as of 1 October 2025
- Accession process launched/formalized: The Council of the EU approved the Negotiating Framework for Ukraine on 21 June 2024, and the EU held the first Intergovernmental Conference (IGC) with Ukraine on 25 June 2024 to open accession negotiations.
- What “negotiating clusters” are: Under the revised enlargement methodology, chapters of the EU acquis are grouped into six thematic clusters: (1) Fundamentals; (2) Internal market; (3) Competitiveness and inclusive growth; (4) Green agenda and sustainable connectivity; (5) Resources, agriculture and cohesion; (6) External relations. Clusters are opened by Council decision once opening benchmarks are met, and closing benchmarks are set at chapter level.
- Current decision rule in force: The Negotiating Framework states that, inter alia, laying down opening benchmarks and deciding to open clusters are Council decisions taken by unanimity (e.g., points 35, 42, 47–49). The Framework also includes “reverse QMV” only for certain corrective measures (e.g., suspending/resuming talks, withholding recommendations, or reversing prior openings).
- The proposed change being discussed: In late September 2025, European Council President António Costa floated a plan to allow opening negotiating clusters for Ukraine (and Moldova) by qualified majority, rather than unanimity; the European Commission publicly welcomed exploring QMV for certain interim steps in the enlargement process. Euronews reports the key obstacle is that amending the negotiating framework to permit QMV would itself require unanimous consent by the member states, and notes that Hungary has blocked the opening of the first “fundamentals” cluster for over a year.
- What QMV means in the Council: Under the Council’s “double majority” rule, a decision is adopted if at least 55% of member states (at least 15 of 27) representing at least 65% of the EU population vote in favour when acting on a Commission/High Representative proposal; when not acting on such a proposal, a reinforced threshold of 72% of member states (at least 20 of 27), plus 65% of the population, applies. A blocking minority must include at least four Council members.

Why this is forecastable now
- There is active political debate about a concrete procedural change (moving specific enlargement steps from unanimity to QMV) that would directly affect Ukraine’s accession negotiations.
- The change faces a clear legal/procedural hurdle (current unanimity rule embedded in the Negotiating Framework) , creating real uncertainty over whether a formal, adopted text enabling QMV will be in place by year-end 2025.

Key definitions (with sources)
- Council of the EU: The institution where national ministers from each EU country meet to adopt laws and coordinate policies; it is the forum that adopts and amends Negotiating Frameworks and takes related enlargement decisions.
- Negotiating Framework: The Council-approved document setting principles, guidelines, and modalities for accession talks with a candidate; for Ukraine it organizes chapters into six thematic clusters and prescribes decision-making rules, including unanimity for opening clusters.
- Negotiating cluster: A thematic grouping of chapters of the acquis (as listed above) used to structure accession talks under the revised methodology.
- Qualified Majority Voting (QMV): The Council’s decision rule defined by the “double majority” thresholds (55% of member states representing 65% of the EU population, or 72%/65% when not acting on a Commission/HR proposal) and blocking minority conditions.
resolution_criteria:
Time window
- Eligible adoptions must occur and be published between 00:00 UTC on 15 October 2025 and 23:59 UTC on 31 December 2025.

What resolves “Yes”
Resolve Yes if, within the time window, there is an adopted and publicly available Council act that explicitly enables the Council to decide by qualified majority to open at least one thematic negotiating cluster in the EU accession negotiations with Ukraine. Any one of the following qualifies:
1) An amendment to the Negotiating Framework for Ukraine (or a horizontal procedural decision explicitly applicable to Ukraine) that replaces or supersedes the unanimity rule with qualified majority for deciding to open at least one negotiating cluster (e.g., by stating that “the Council, acting by qualified majority, will decide on the opening of [cluster(s)]”). The existing Framework currently requires unanimity for opening clusters.
2) A Council decision that, without separately amending the Framework text, explicitly authorizes the Council to decide by qualified majority to open at least one specified cluster for Ukraine and states that the Council is acting by qualified majority within the meaning described by the Council’s voting system.
3) A Council decision that actually opens a specific negotiating cluster for Ukraine and explicitly states that the Council is acting by qualified majority in taking that opening decision (thereby demonstrating an adopted rule change in practice).

What does not count
- Non-binding political statements or European Council conclusions without legal effect; press reports; draft, leaked, or initialled but not adopted texts; Commission communications, proposals, or Q&A; European Parliament resolutions; member-state declarations; or statements by EU officials that do not embody a formally adopted Council decision/Framework amendment.

Definitions applied at resolution
- “Qualified majority” is interpreted per the Council’s official definition in force at the time of the act (double-majority thresholds; reinforced threshold when applicable; blocking minority rules).
- “Negotiating cluster” refers to any of the six thematic clusters listed in the Negotiating Framework for Ukraine (Fundamentals; Internal market; Competitiveness and inclusive growth; Green agenda and sustainable connectivity; Resources, agriculture and cohesion; External relations).
- “Formally adopt and publish” means the act appears on an official EU channel (e.g., consilium.europa.eu document register/press release or the Official Journal via EUR-Lex) within the time window. The Negotiating Framework and IGC milestones have been communicated through such channels in past practice.

Scope clarifications
- The change may apply to Ukraine alone or to Ukraine and Moldova (or more candidates), as long as it explicitly applies to opening at least one cluster in Ukraine’s negotiations.
- It is not necessary that a cluster is actually opened; a clearly worded, adopted rule change enabling the Council to use QMV for opening at least one cluster suffices. Conversely, an opening by QMV that is explicitly recorded as such in the adopted text also suffices even without a separate framework amendment.

Resolution source and procedure
- Primary sources: The Council of the EU’s official website/document register or press releases (consilium.europa.eu) and/or the Official Journal (EUR-Lex) where adopted acts are published. If multiple official sources exist, precedence is given to the adopted legal text itself as published on consilium.europa.eu or in the Official Journal.
- If no qualifying adopted text is published by the deadline, resolve No.

question: Will Palencia’s city council (Pleno) adopt the definitive approval of the 2026 General Budget by December 31, 2025?
background:
Summary of what’s being forecast: This question asks whether the Ayuntamiento de Palencia’s Pleno (the full municipal council) will adopt the agreement of “aprobación definitiva del Presupuesto General del ejercicio 2026” (definitive approval of the 2026 General Budget) on or before 2025-12-31 (local time, Europe/Madrid).

Status quo as of 2025-09-30:
- The City’s Presupuesto General page provides official budget documentation for recent years (2019–2025) and routinely includes links to approval steps and Official Provincial Gazette (BOP) announcements; there is no 2026 budget posted yet.
- For the 2025 budget, the official PDF notes: Dictamen (committee report) on 2025-04-25, initial approval by the Pleno on 2025-04-29, BOP announcement of the initial approval on 2025-05-02, and BOP announcement of definitive approval on 2025-05-28. These dates illustrate how the City records and publishes approval milestones.
- Local reporting on 2025-09-10 stated the first draft of the 2026 budget was expected by mid-October 2025, with negotiations from roughly 2025-10-20 to 2025-11-15, and emphasized the goal of having the budget approved by 2025-12-31; the finance councillor said, “Tenemos que tener presupuesto aprobado para el 31 de diciembre, o no tendremos”.
- Actas (minutes) of the Pleno are published online by the Ayuntamiento (available from 2009 onward), and are suitable for verifying plenary decisions. The transparency portal also points to pages for Pleno activities and recordings/retransmissions.

Why this may be uncertain (and interesting to forecast):
- The municipality’s stated intent is to have the 2026 budget approved by year-end, but negotiations among groups can delay proceedings; in 2025 the Pleno’s initial approval occurred in late April and the definitive approval was formalized at the end of May. Whether all steps for definitive approval can be completed by 2025-12-31 (rather than slipping into January) depends on the speed of negotiations, handling of any allegations during public exhibition, and scheduling of plenary sessions.

Key term links for clarity:
- Ayuntamiento (municipal government): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayuntamiento
- Municipal budget (Spain): https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presupuesto_municipal
- Pleno (municipal council): https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayuntamiento#Pleno
- Boletín Oficial de la Provincia (provincial official gazette): https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolet%C3%ADn_Oficial_de_la_Provincia

Primary sources relevant for resolution and verification:
- Ayuntamiento de Palencia Presupuesto General landing page (for official budget files and BOP announcements).
- Official 2025 budget PDF showing how approval milestones are documented (as precedent for what to look for).
- Actas del Pleno (minutes), published online since 2009 (for the authoritative record of plenary votes).
- Transparency portal pointers to Pleno materials and retransmissions.
- If needed for corroboration of the event date, mainstream local press coverage (e.g., El Norte de Castilla).
resolution_criteria:
Time window and time zone:
- Eligible events must occur between 2025-09-01 00:00:00 and 2025-12-31 23:59:59, Europe/Madrid local time.

What counts as a “Yes”:
- Resolve Yes if, on or before 2025-12-31 (Europe/Madrid), the Pleno of the Ayuntamiento de Palencia adopts the agreement of “aprobación definitiva del Presupuesto General del ejercicio 2026.”
- The authoritative evidence is any ONE of the following, listed in order of preference:
  1) The Acta (minutes) or a Certificado del Pleno stating that the Pleno approved definitively the Presupuesto General 2026 on a specific session date on/before 2025-12-31.
  2) An official document on the Presupuesto General page or linked budget PDFs that records the Pleno’s definitive approval (e.g., a section like the 2025 PDF listing approval milestones) on/before 2025-12-31.
  3) An Anuncio in the Boletín Oficial de la Provincia (BOP) that explicitly states the Pleno adopted the definitive approval on a date on/before 2025-12-31. Note: the BOP publication may appear after 2025-12-31; what matters is that it states a Pleno approval date within the window.
  4) If (1)–(3) are unavailable, a credible municipal press note or mainstream local press report that explicitly states the Pleno adopted the definitive approval and specifies the session date on/before 2025-12-31 (e.g., El Norte de Castilla).

What does NOT count:
- Initial approval (aprobación inicial) without subsequent definitive approval by the Pleno within the time window does NOT count as Yes.
- A budget draft, committee report, or mayoral/Junta de Gobierno action without the Pleno’s definitive approval does NOT count as Yes.

Handling conflicts and edge cases:
- If sources conflict on the date, the Acta/Certificado del Pleno (1) prevails over other sources. If the BOP (3) and the acta (1) disagree, the acta date prevails for this resolution.
- If the Pleno adopts definitive approval by 2025-12-31 but the BOP publication occurs later, this still resolves Yes provided the acta or the BOP states a Pleno adoption date within the window.
- If the Pleno vote ties and is approved via the mayor’s casting vote, that still counts as adoption if recorded in the acta.
- Subsequent legal challenges, suspensions, or annulments after a valid adoption within the window do not change a Yes outcome.

Resolution procedure:
- The resolver will look first for the acta/certificate on the municipal website (Actas del Pleno). If not available, the resolver will consult the Presupuesto General page and linked budget files for recorded approval milestones , and/or the relevant BOP announcement stating the Pleno adoption date. If necessary, credible local press will be used to corroborate the session date.

question: Canada Q3 2025 real GDP (expenditure-based, seasonally adjusted): Will the quarter-over-quarter change be negative?
background:
Status quo and context as of 2025-10-01:
- Statistics Canada’s release schedule and recent GDP reporting indicate that "Data on GDP by income and expenditure for the third quarter of 2025 will be released on November 28" via The Daily [d2ad23; b57946]. The Daily publishes each working day at 8:30 a.m. Eastern (13:30 UTC on November 28, 2025).
- In the latest quarterly report, real gross domestic product (GDP) declined 0.4% in Q2 2025, following a 0.5% gain in Q1 2025. This recent contraction increases uncertainty about the Q3 direction. Monthly GDP by industry rose 0.2% m/m in July 2025, breaking a string of monthly declines, offering mixed signals for Q3.
- The expenditure-based quarterly GDP series is published by Statistics Canada and available in chained (2017) dollars and current dollars (Table 36-10-0104-01). Statistics Canada defines GDP and seasonal adjustment within its methodology and glossary materials; seasonally adjusted series are altered to remove predictable seasonal regularities, and real GDP refers to GDP adjusted for price changes (volume/chained-dollar measures).

Key term definitions and references:
- Real gross domestic product (real GDP): GDP adjusted for price changes (a volume measure). See Statistics Canada’s definitions and methodological notes. For general orientation, see Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_domestic_product.
- Expenditure-based GDP: The national accounts measure of GDP compiled from the expenditure side; the quarterly series for Canada is published by Statistics Canada, including chained (2017) dollars (volume) and current dollars (value).
- Seasonally adjusted: A series altered to remove predictable seasonal patterns, as defined by Statistics Canada.
- Quarter-over-quarter (QoQ) change: Unless otherwise stated, growth rates in The Daily GDP release represent the percentage change in the series from one quarter to the next (e.g., from Q2 2025 to Q3 2025).
- The Daily: Statistics Canada’s official daily release platform for data publications; releases occur at 8:30 a.m. Eastern each working day.

Why this question has genuine uncertainty:
- Q2 2025 showed contraction (-0.4%), while Q1 2025 grew (+0.5%). July’s m/m uptick for GDP by industry (+0.2%) may or may not translate into a positive Q3 QoQ for expenditure-based real GDP. Together, these mixed signals suggest a forecast plausibly between 30% and 70%, rather than near-certainty.

Data and timing:
- Primary resolution will use The Daily: "Gross domestic product, income and expenditure, third quarter 2025" expected November 28, 2025 at 8:30 a.m. Eastern (13:30 UTC) [d2ad23; b57946; 00c0bb].
- If the primary article is delayed, the underlying quarterly series in Table 36-10-0104-01 will be used to compute QoQ change in chained (2017) dollars, seasonally adjusted (annualized level), comparing Q3 2025 to Q2 2025.
resolution_criteria:
Start and end window:
- Eligible publication window for resolution: 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC through 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

What is being forecast:
- Whether Canada’s real GDP (expenditure-based, seasonally adjusted) quarter-over-quarter change for Q3 2025 is negative (<0%). Q3 2025 refers to 2025-07-01 00:00:00 UTC through 2025-09-30 23:59:59 UTC.

Primary resolution source and method:
- Resolve based on Statistics Canada’s The Daily article titled "Gross domestic product, income and expenditure, third quarter 2025". If the article explicitly states that real GDP declined (or contracted) quarter-over-quarter in Q3 2025, resolve Yes; if it states that real GDP increased or was unchanged (0.0%), resolve No. Use the growth rate convention as stated by Statistics Canada: unless otherwise noted, growth rates represent the percentage change from one quarter to the next. The release is expected on November 28, 2025 at 8:30 a.m. Eastern (13:30 UTC) [b57946; 00c0bb; d2ad23].

Definitions used in resolution:
- Real GDP: GDP adjusted for price changes (volume measure), as defined by Statistics Canada.
- Expenditure-based quarterly GDP: The series published by Statistics Canada, including chained (2017) dollars, seasonally adjusted (annualized level), Canada-wide (Table 36-10-0104-01).
- Seasonally adjusted: Series altered to remove predictable seasonal patterns, per Statistics Canada methodology.
- Negative: Strictly less than 0.0% QoQ.

Fallback resolution (if primary source is unavailable by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC):
- Use Statistics Canada’s Table 36-10-0104-01 (Gross domestic product, expenditure-based, Canada, quarterly). Identify the level of real GDP in chained (2017) dollars, seasonally adjusted (at annual rates) for Q2 2025 and Q3 2025. Compute the QoQ percentage change as (Q3 2025 level / Q2 2025 level − 1). If the computed QoQ change is <0.0%, resolve Yes; otherwise resolve No.

Handling revisions:
- Resolution is based on the first publication of the Q3 2025 GDP by income and expenditure in The Daily. Subsequent revisions published after the initial article do not alter the resolution.

Timezone:
- All resolution checks are performed in UTC. The Daily’s publication time of 8:30 a.m. Eastern corresponds to 13:30 UTC on November 28, 2025.

question: Italy: Will the 2026 Budget Law freeze the statutory old-age pension age at 67 for 2027?
background:
Context and status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- Statutory old-age pension (pensione di vecchiaia) in Italy: INPS defines this as a benefit payable to workers who meet the legal age and contribution requirements. For the biennia 2023–2024 and 2025–2026, the age requirement is 67 years, with at least 20 years of contributions; starting 1 January 2027, requirements are adjusted to increases in life expectancy.
- Automatic life-expectancy-linked adjustment: The mechanism that updates pension eligibility requirements to life expectancy was established in the 2010–2011 reforms (including DL 78/2010 and DL 201/2011, the “Fornero” reform). Adjustments occur biennially and, per subsequent modifications, each adjustment cannot exceed three months, with any excess carried forward. From 2019, the legal old-age threshold has been 67; adjustments in 2021 and 2023 were nil per the applicable decrees.
- Scheduled 2027 adjustment: Reporting indicates the 2027–2028 biennial update would raise requirements by three months (old-age from 67.0 to 67.25 years), and that an implementing decree should be issued by end-2025 to formalize the update. Analyses by the Osservatorio Conti Pubblici Italiani (OCPI) estimate that freezing this +3 months adjustment would increase pension expenditure by €3.3bn in 2027 and €4.7bn in 2028 (with lower net deficit impact after taxes).
- Political signals: On 2025-09-24, PM Giorgia Meloni said the government had not discussed freezing the retirement age at 67, suggesting internal hesitation despite advocacy by some actors to suspend the increase. Separate reporting has described ministers and undersecretaries (e.g., Giorgetti, Durigon) as open to freezing the adjustment in the autumn budget (“manovra”).

Key definitions and sources for forecasters:
- “Statutory retirement age” refers here to the general INPS old-age pension (pensione di vecchiaia) age requirement for workers in the compulsory general insurance scheme (AGO/INPS), not special categories. See INPS overview and service pages.
- “Automatic life-expectancy-linked adjustment” refers to the biennial updating of pension eligibility requirements to life expectancy pursuant to the Fornero framework (e.g., Art. 24 DL 201/2011 and Art. 12 DL 78/2010), as summarized by the Chamber of Deputies dossier.
- Primary resolution source will be the official text of the Legge di Bilancio 2026 published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale (Official Journal). Background context and cost estimates can be cross-checked via OCPI and major media cited above.
resolution_criteria:
Time window and timezone:
- Eligible actions must occur between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. Resolution will be determined after 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Question and outcome:
- YES if, by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, the Legge di Bilancio 2026 (Budget Law for 2026), as published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale, contains an enacted provision that explicitly suspends or overrides the automatic life-expectancy-linked increase of the statutory old-age pension (pensione di vecchiaia) age scheduled to take effect on 2027-01-01, such that the general old-age pension age remains 67.0 years for the 2027–2028 biennium.
- NO otherwise (including if the Budget Law has not been published by 2025-12-31, or if it contains only statements of intent or delegations without an enacted clause that effectuates the suspension for old-age pension age).

What counts as “freeze”:
- The Budget Law must include normative language that suspends application of the life-expectancy adjustment to the old-age pension age for the 2027–2028 biennium (e.g., a clause stating that no increase shall apply and that the old-age requirement remains 67 years), thereby blocking the scheduled +3 months increase from 67.0 to 67.25 years referenced in reporting and analyses. Delegation to a future decree without the freeze taking legal effect in the Budget Law text does not count as YES.

Scope clarifications:
- “Statutory retirement age” in this question refers only to the general INPS old-age pension (pensione di vecchiaia) requirement for the compulsory general insurance scheme (AGO/INPS); special regimes and exclusions (e.g., “lavori gravosi”, disability, or early retirement channels) are out of scope for resolution.

Resolution source and verification:
- Primary source: the text of the Legge di Bilancio 2026 as published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale (Official Journal of the Italian Republic). Verify by locating the law’s publication and searching the enacted articles for a clause that suspends the 2027–2028 life-expectancy-linked increase for the old-age pension age.
- Secondary confirmation (if needed for clarity) may come from official MEF or INPS communications summarizing enacted measures, but the law text in the Gazzetta Ufficiale is authoritative. Background facts on current statutory age and the adjustment mechanism can be cross-checked with INPS pages and the Chamber dossier , while the scheduled magnitude (+3 months) and political/media context are documented in reporting and OCPI analyses.

question: Between January 1, 2024 and December 31, 2025 (UTC), will the United States and the Kyrgyz Republic sign a bilateral, government-to-government Memorandum of Understanding (or equivalent formal agreement) to strengthen cooperation on critical minerals?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01:
- What “critical minerals” means under U.S. policy: The Energy Act of 2020 defines “critical minerals” as non-fuel minerals or mineral materials that are essential to U.S. economic or national security and have supply chains vulnerable to disruption. USGS materials elaborate these criteria and their application in practice. The Department of the Interior/USGS published the 2022 Final List of Critical Minerals (50 commodities, e.g., tungsten, antimony, tin, graphite, rare earth elements, lithium, etc.), which remains a widely used reference point for policy and agreements through 2025.
- Regional framework and recent U.S. activity: The C5+1 Critical Minerals Dialogue (CMD) involving the United States and the five Central Asian states held its inaugural meeting on February 8, 2024, hosted by the U.S. Department of State. Objectives highlighted include increasing the region’s involvement in global critical minerals supply chains, strengthening economic cooperation, advancing the clean energy transition, protecting ecosystems, and catalyzing investment that meets high environmental and social standards, with continued dialogue and engagement around venues such as PDAC noted. As a bilateral precedent in Central Asia, the United States and Uzbekistan signed a Memorandum of Understanding on September 16, 2024 (Tashkent) to strengthen cooperation on critical minerals, aiming to diversify global mineral supply chains, catalyze investment, and support the clean energy transition; the announcement identifies signatories and the MoU’s aims.
- U.S.–Kyrgyz bilateral signals: In an April 22, 2024 co-issued joint statement following the United States–Kyrgyz Republic Annual Bilateral Consultations (ABCs), the two governments underscored their commitment to advance partnership on critical minerals and the green economy, alongside broader economic and connectivity goals, indicating political intent but not a signed bilateral instrument specifically on critical minerals. In the business domain, the B5+1 Forum—described as the business counterpart to C5+1—held its first forum in March 2024 in Almaty to strengthen regional economic ties, which may facilitate private-sector engagement complementing intergovernmental efforts.
- Kyrgyz Republic mining sector prospects and constraints: The World Bank’s Mining Sector Diagnostic (March 2023) notes geology favorable for gold and base metals and also tin, tungsten, antimony, rare earth metals, copper, and others. However, it highlights significant hurdles for near-term deals: regulatory instability, licensing system issues, increased state control/ownership requirements (e.g., equity stakes), environmental and social management gaps, infrastructure limitations as a landlocked, mountainous country, high accident rates, and a challenging investment climate. These factors create headwinds for rapid bilateral agreements and commercial follow-through.
- Why this question is uncertain: There are clear signals of U.S. interest and regional frameworks (CMD, B5+1) and a directly relevant U.S.–Uzbekistan MoU, while Kyrgyzstan’s sectoral and governance constraints make a signed U.S.–Kyrgyz bilateral instrument on critical minerals within the timeframe plausible but far from guaranteed.

Key definitions for this market:
- Critical minerals: As defined by U.S. law and USGS practice—non-fuel minerals/materials essential to U.S. economy/national security with vulnerable supply chains. For concreteness, the 2022 USGS Final List of Critical Minerals (50 items) provides the reference list for whether specific minerals named in an instrument qualify (e.g., tungsten, antimony, tin, rare earth elements, etc.).
- Memorandum of Understanding (MoU): An agreement expressing a convergence of will and an intended common line of action; often nonbinding unless specified or interpreted otherwise, and widely used in international relations as a formal instrument short of a treaty.
- Formal bilateral instrument on critical minerals cooperation (what “counts”): A written, co-signed, government-to-government instrument explicitly titled as a Memorandum of Understanding, Memorandum of Cooperation, (Framework) Agreement, Exchange of Notes, or similarly formal agreement that: (a) is signed by authorized representatives of both governments; and (b) explicitly establishes cooperation concerning “critical minerals” as defined above, or explicitly concerns one or more minerals on the USGS 2022 Critical Minerals list and states cooperation on exploration, mining, processing, trade, investment, or supply chains for those minerals. For precedent on how such instruments are framed and announced in the region, see the September 16, 2024 U.S.–Uzbekistan MoU.

Status quo: As of this writing, there is no cited, publicly posted U.S.–Kyrgyz signed MoU or equivalent bilateral agreement focused on critical minerals cooperation, though both sides have publicly referenced intent to advance cooperation in this area.
resolution_criteria:
Binary outcome, resolved as of 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Question: Between 2024-01-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC (inclusive), do the Government of the United States and the Government of the Kyrgyz Republic sign a bilateral, government-to-government Memorandum of Understanding (or equivalent formal agreement) to strengthen cooperation on critical minerals?

Definitions and inclusion rules:
1) Qualifying instrument (any one of the following, provided all conditions are met):
   - A document explicitly titled Memorandum of Understanding, Memorandum of Cooperation, Agreement, Framework Agreement, or Exchange of Notes; AND
   - It is a bilateral, government-to-government instrument (i.e., between the national governments and/or their ministries/agencies—not between a government and a private company, nor subnational entities); AND
   - It explicitly establishes cooperation on “critical minerals” or explicitly names at least one mineral on the USGS 2022 Final List of Critical Minerals and states cooperation relating to exploration, mining, processing, trade, investment, or supply chains for those minerals.

2) What does not count:
   - Multilateral statements/agreements (e.g., C5+1 communiqués) unless accompanied by a distinct, signed bilateral instrument that itself meets the criteria above.
   - Joint statements that merely express intent to cooperate but do not confirm that a qualifying, signed bilateral instrument has been executed.
   - Agreements limited to non-critical sectors or to minerals not on the USGS 2022 critical list, unless the instrument also explicitly references “critical minerals.”
   - Agreements between government and private-sector entities or between two private-sector entities.

3) “Signed” means the instrument bears signatures (or named signatories) of authorized officials of both governments, or both governments publish official announcements that such an instrument has been signed (the full text need not be public). The U.S.–Uzbekistan September 16, 2024 MoU announcement illustrates the standard of public confirmation expected.

Event window and timekeeping:
- Eligible instruments must be signed within 2024-01-01 00:00:00 UTC to 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. If both a signing date and a publication date are available and differ, the signing date governs eligibility. If only an official announcement is available and it states “signed today” or provides a specific signing date, that stated signing date governs.

Resolution sources and procedure:
- Primary sources: Official U.S. and Kyrgyz government publications, including but not limited to state.gov, kg.usembassy.gov, mfa.gov.kg, president.kg, gov.kg.
- Secondary confirmation: If primary posting is unavailable or down, reporting by major reputable outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, AFP) that explicitly quotes or cites an official government announcement is acceptable.
- Adjudication hierarchy: In case of discrepancies, an official text or announcement posted by either government takes precedence over secondary media reporting. Translations (English, Kyrgyz, Russian) are acceptable; if dates differ due to time zones, UTC conversion applies.

Outcome determination:
- YES: At least one qualifying instrument as defined above is signed within the window and is publicly announced or posted as per the sources listed.
- NO: No qualifying instrument is signed within the window, or any public statements reference only intent without confirmation of a signed instrument.

Definitions references: “Critical minerals” as per Energy Act of 2020/USGS criteria and the 2022 USGS Final List. MoU definition (general characteristics and use in international relations).

Background sources (for forecasters): Inaugural C5+1 Critical Minerals Dialogue (Feb 8, 2024) and objectives ; U.S.–Uzbekistan MoU on critical minerals (Sep 16, 2024) ; U.S.–Kyrgyz ABCs joint statement noting intent to advance cooperation on critical minerals and green economy (Apr 22, 2024) ; B5+1 Forum context (business counterpart to C5+1; first forum March 2024, Almaty) ; Kyrgyz mining sector opportunities and constraints (World Bank, March 2023).

question: DMA enforcement: Will the European Commission publish at least one additional non-compliance decision against a gatekeeper between Oct 15 and Dec 31, 2025?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01:
- The EU Digital Markets Act (DMA) is Regulation (EU) 2022/1925; official text and overview are on EUR-Lex (see: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/1925/oj/eng). Gatekeepers designated under the DMA currently include Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, ByteDance, Meta, Microsoft, and Booking (European Commission’s official gatekeepers page).
- On 25 March 2024, the European Commission opened five non-compliance investigations under the DMA concerning Alphabet (steering in Google Play, self-preferencing in Search), Apple (steering in the App Store, web browser choice screen design), and Meta (“pay or consent” model). The Commission stated it intended to conclude these proceedings within 12 months.
- On 23 April 2025, the Commission adopted non-compliance decisions finding Apple and Meta in breach of the DMA. Apple was found to have breached its anti-steering obligation; Meta’s “consent or pay” model was found non-compliant. The Commission imposed fines of €500 million (Apple) and €200 million (Meta).
- The Commission regularly publishes DMA enforcement news via its “Press Corner” and the dedicated DMA “Latest news” page (example entries include the 23 April 2025 non-compliance decisions).

Why this question:
- Additional non-compliance decisions in late 2025 are plausible but not guaranteed, given ongoing proceedings and the 12-month conclusion intention originally stated for the March 2024 cases. The timeframe from 2025-10-15 to 2025-12-31 captures a period when further decisions could realistically appear, producing meaningful uncertainty for forecasters.
resolution_criteria:
Yes/No resolution with strict definitions and sources.

Question:
Resolve “Yes” if, between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, the European Commission publishes at least one additional formal non-compliance decision under the DMA against any gatekeeper; resolve “No” otherwise.

Definitions (with links and examples):
- Digital Markets Act (DMA): EU Regulation (EU) 2022/1925 on contestable and fair digital markets. See EUR-Lex: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/1925/oj/eng (link provided for reference).
- Gatekeeper: A company designated by the European Commission under the DMA; the Commission’s consolidated list currently includes Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, ByteDance, Meta, Microsoft, and Booking. See the official EU page “DMA designated Gatekeepers”. For the purpose of resolution, “gatekeeper” refers to any company that is designated at the time of the decision’s publication.
- Non-compliance decision (for this question): An official decision by the European Commission that explicitly finds a gatekeeper to be in breach of the DMA (also termed “non-compliance decision” or described by the Commission as “finds [Company] in breach of the DMA”). For example, the Commission’s 23 April 2025 actions against Apple and Meta are described as non-compliance decisions and state those gatekeepers “breached”/“are not compliant with” DMA obligations.
- Publish/published: The decision is made public on an official European Commission web property, either: (a) the Commission’s Press Corner press release/news page for the decision; or (b) the official Digital Markets Act website’s “Latest news” page (digital-markets-act.ec.europa.eu/latest-news_en). The Commission uses these venues to announce DMA non-compliance decisions (e.g., Apple/Meta on 23 April 2025). The publication time is the timestamp shown on the relevant Commission page.
- Additional: Excludes non-compliance decisions published prior to the start of the resolution window. Specifically, it excludes the two non-compliance decisions concerning Apple and Meta published on 23 April 2025. Any qualifying decision published within the resolution window counts, even if concerning the same companies again.

Inclusions:
- Any Commission decision that the Commission itself describes as a non-compliance decision under the DMA, or that the Commission’s official announcement states “found [gatekeeper] in breach of the Digital Markets Act,” where the announcement is published on the Commission’s Press Corner or the DMA Latest news page.

Exclusions:
- Openings of investigations, statements of objections, preliminary findings, specification proceedings, commitments decisions, or workshop/consultation notices do not count unless the Commission explicitly states the adoption of a “non-compliance decision” finding a breach of the DMA.
- Decisions or actions published after 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, even if adopted earlier, do not count. Publication date/time controls.
- Publications outside official Commission web properties do not count for resolution.

Resolution process:
1) On or after 2026-01-01 00:00:01 UTC, check:
   - European Commission Press Corner for any press releases or news pages dated within the resolution window and explicitly announcing a non-compliance decision under the DMA against a gatekeeper.
   - The official DMA “Latest news” page (digital-markets-act.ec.europa.eu/latest-news_en) for entries in the window with the same explicit content.
2) If at least one qualifying announcement is found, resolve “Yes”; otherwise resolve “No”.
3) If both sources exist for the same decision, use the earliest Commission publication timestamp within the window.

Notes:
- The March 25, 2024 investigations and 12-month intention , and the April 23, 2025 Apple/Meta decisions and fines , are provided as context only and do not themselves determine resolution.
- Appeals, subsequent modifications, or later annulments do not affect resolution, which is based solely on the Commission’s publication within the specified window.

question: Will Israel publish an official renewal of the Israeli–Palestinian banking waiver during November 2025 (UTC)?
background:
Overview and status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- What the waiver is: Since 2016, Israel’s finance ministry has granted an annually renewed indemnity/waiver to certain Israeli banks (notably Israel Discount Bank and Bank Hapoalim) enabling them to maintain correspondent relationships with Palestinian banks. The waiver shields Israeli banks from anti–money-laundering/counter-terrorist-financing liability when processing payments linked to Palestinian counterparties, and allows shekel clearing, transfer of Palestinian Authority tax revenues collected by Israel, and currency conversion via the Bank of Israel.
- Current timing and uncertainty: UN experts stated in September 2025 that “Israel has threatened not to renew the annual waiver … in November 2025,” warning this would cut Palestinians off from the global financial system. Earlier reporting indicates the waiver was extended in late 2024 under pressure to run through November 2025. On June 10, 2025, Israel’s finance minister ordered cancellation of the waiver; the Palestinian Monetary Authority warned that ending the cooperation risks halting supplies of essential goods such as food and fuel and broadly threatens the Palestinian banking system and economy.
- Why it matters for forecasting: Renewal (or non-renewal) is a discrete, consequential policy step with clear documentary signals (official notices). The decision has direct operational and humanitarian implications and has been the subject of sustained international pressure and credible reporting.

Key definitions and links:
- Annual banking waiver/indemnity: The annually renewed Israeli governmental indemnification/waiver that enables Israeli banks to maintain correspondent relationships with Palestinian banks, shielding them from AML/CFT liability for such transactions.
- Israeli banks: Banks licensed to operate in Israel under Israeli banking law (see Bank of Israel for the central bank and supervisory authority: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Israel).
- Palestinian banks: Banks licensed by the Palestinian Monetary Authority (PMA). Directory: PMA “Banks” page (Directory of Licensed Banks): https://www.pma.ps/en/Control-of-financial-sector/Banks.
- Correspondent banking: A relationship between banks that allows one bank to provide services on behalf of another in a different jurisdiction; see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Correspondent_banking.
- Official notice/publish: For this question, an “official notice” is a press release, decision, order, resolution, or formal announcement published on an official Israeli government or central bank website (e.g., Ministry of Finance, Prime Minister’s Office/Security Cabinet, Bank of Israel), or in Israel’s official gazette (Reshumot). “Publish” means the notice appears on the relevant official website or gazette page accessible to the public.

Primary resolution sources (where such notices are typically posted):
- Bank of Israel Press Releases hub: https://www.boi.org.il/en/NewsAndPublications/PressReleases/Pages/default.aspx
- Ministry of Finance (gov.il ministry page; press releases/news are typically posted under the ministry’s site): https://www.gov.il/en/departments/ministries/ministry_of_finance
- Prime Minister’s Office / Security Cabinet announcements (gov.il): https://www.gov.il/en/departments/prime_ministers_office

Additional credible secondary sources (only if explicitly citing an official notice): Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Associated Press (https://apnews.com), Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com). Prior coverage of the waiver’s extension and cancellation has appeared on Reuters.

Context notes:
- UN experts emphasized that non-renewal in November 2025 has been threatened and would sever Palestinian access to the global financial system.
- Past reporting described how the waiver functions and that it was extended to run through November 2025 , while cancellation orders and the implied impacts were reported in June 2025.
resolution_criteria:
Event window and timezone:
- Eligible events must occur (be published) between 2025-11-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-11-30 23:59:59 UTC. The forecasting question’s start date for contradictory events (e.g., cancellation notices) is 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC. Resolution must be determined no later than 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Definitions of what counts:
- Renewal: A formal, official Israeli notice (press release, decision, order, resolution, or gazette entry) explicitly stating that the annual indemnity/waiver enabling Israeli banks to maintain correspondent relationships with PMA-licensed Palestinian banks is renewed/extended (or otherwise continues in force) beyond its prior expiry, effective immediately or on a specified date. The content must clearly indicate continuation of Israeli banks’ authorized cooperation/processing with Palestinian banks under the indemnity/waiver framework described in background.
- Official sources: Notices posted on official Israeli government/central bank websites (e.g., Bank of Israel press releases hub; Ministry of Finance website; Prime Minister’s Office/Security Cabinet site) or Israel’s official gazette (Reshumot). Secondary reports (Reuters/AP/Bloomberg) are acceptable only if they explicitly cite and link to, or unambiguously quote, such official notices.

Resolution rules:
- Resolve Yes if, during November 2025 (UTC), an eligible official notice is published confirming renewal/extension/continuation of the waiver/indemnity as defined above.
- Resolve No if any of the following holds:
  1) An official Israeli notice of non-renewal/cancellation is published between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, and there is no subsequent eligible official renewal notice published during November 2025 (UTC).
  2) No eligible official renewal notice is published during November 2025 (UTC) by the end of 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Exclusions and clarifications:
- Statements by officials to media without an accompanying official publication, anonymous leaks, or social media posts lacking a link to an official publication do not count.
- Bank-specific indemnifications/waivers count as renewal if they clearly pertain to enabling Israeli banks to maintain correspondent relationships with PMA-licensed Palestinian banks, regardless of whether the notice names particular banks (e.g., Israel Discount Bank or Bank Hapoalim).
- If multiple notices are published, the latest applicable notice within November 2025 (UTC) governs the outcome. If the only applicable notice is outside November, this forecast resolves No.

How to verify in ~10 minutes:
1) Check the Bank of Israel press releases hub and the Ministry of Finance and Prime Minister’s Office/ Security Cabinet sites for November 2025 publications.
2) If needed, search Reuters/AP/Bloomberg for articles explicitly citing and quoting an official Israeli notice of renewal/non-renewal and follow the links to the official publication.

question: IAEA–Iran: Will the IAEA publish a verified, quantified figure for Iran’s stockpile of uranium enriched to up to 60% U‑235 in Q4 2025?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01:
- Latest verified baseline before Q4 2025: In a Board of Governors report (GOV/2025/50) circulated on 2025-09-03, the IAEA stated that as of 2025-06-13 Iran’s stockpile included 440.9 kg of uranium enriched up to 60% U‑235, and noted that 432.9 kg of this was verified in the form of UF6 enriched up to 60% U‑235. The report details that since 2025-06-13 the Agency lost access to safeguarded facilities (except BNPP), withdrew inspectors for safety by end-June, and Iran enacted a law on 2025-07-02 suspending cooperation; consequently, the Agency lost continuity of knowledge and could not quantify the stockpile with previous confidence until resumption of in‑field verification.
- Director General statements: On 2025-09-08, the IAEA Director General reiterated loss of access since 2025-06-13, inspector withdrawal by end‑June, Iran’s 2025-07-02 law suspending cooperation, and the need to conclude modalities to resume full inspections; he noted verification of high‑enriched uranium was overdue without access.
- Prospects of resuming inspections: Credible reporting indicates that on 2025-09-09, the IAEA and Iran announced agreement “on practical modalities to resume inspection activities,” with both sides describing it as a step toward full resumption following June attacks; no firm operational timeline was disclosed at that press event.
- Where such stockpile figures appear: The IAEA typically publishes quantified enriched‑uranium stockpile figures in Director General reports to the Board of Governors (GOV/ documents) and occasionally references them in DG statements posted on iaea.org. The IAEA maintains an official page aggregating Iran‑related Board reports with links and dates (e.g., GOV/2025/25, GOV/2025/24, GOV/2025/10), updated through 2025.

Key definitions and terms:
- Uranium‑235 (U‑235): A fissile isotope of uranium; enrichment percentage denotes the fraction of U‑235 in uranium. Weapons‑grade uranium is commonly defined as ≥85% U‑235; HEU is ≥20% U‑235.
- Uranium hexafluoride (UF6): Volatile compound used in uranium enrichment processes. IAEA reporting of “kgU in UF6” refers to the mass of uranium contained in the UF6, not the total compound mass; IAEA reports explicitly specify figures as “kg of uranium in the form of UF6”.
- “Uranium enriched to up to 60% U‑235”: For this question, this refers to the IAEA’s stockpile category in GOV reports that explicitly labels uranium enriched “up to 60% U‑235” (near‑bomb‑grade) and provides mass in kilograms of uranium (kgU) in UF6 form.
- “Publish”: Release on official IAEA channels (iaea.org), including Director General reports to the Board of Governors (GOV/ series) or formal DG statements/news releases.
- “Verified, quantified figure”: A single number (not a range) in kilograms of uranium (kgU) for the “up to 60% U‑235” stockpile that the IAEA explicitly characterizes as based on its verification activities (e.g., uses terms like “verified,” “based on verification activities,” or indicates that in‑field verification enabling that figure has occurred).

Why this has uncertainty: Access and cooperation were suspended in mid‑2025, creating verification gaps; while a September 2025 announcement suggested modalities to resume inspections, implementation details remain unclear, making it uncertain whether the IAEA will regain sufficient access and publish a newly verified figure within Q4 2025.
resolution_criteria:
Event window and time zone:
- Eligible publications must occur between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Resolution:
- This resolves YES if, within the event window, the IAEA publishes on iaea.org either:
  1) a Director General report to the Board of Governors (GOV/ document), or
  2) a formal Director General statement or IAEA news release,
  that contains a newly verified, quantified figure for Iran’s stockpile of uranium enriched to up to 60% U‑235, expressed in kilograms of uranium (kgU), and the publication explicitly attributes the figure to the Agency’s verification activities. The figure must pertain to a reference date on or after 2025-10-15 or be explicitly described as newly verified during the event window.

- This resolves NO if no such publication appears within the event window, or if any number published during the window lacks explicit attribution to IAEA verification (e.g., is presented solely as an unverified estimate based on declarations without in‑field verification, or repeats the pre‑Q4 figure without new verification).

Scope clarifications:
- Acceptable phrasing indicating verification includes: “verified,” “based on verification activities,” “following resumption of in‑field verification,” or equivalent language establishing that the Agency’s verification activities underpin the figure.
- The figure must correspond specifically to the IAEA’s “enriched up to 60% U‑235” category reported in kgU in UF6 form; figures for different enrichment bands or without clear categorization do not count. If presented for total HEU without the 60% band delineated, it does not count.
- Ranges or qualitative descriptions (e.g., “around X kg” without a single quantitative value) do not count. Multiple figures for different dates are acceptable as long as at least one meets the criteria above.

Primary resolution sources:
- IAEA “IAEA and Iran – IAEA Board Reports” aggregation page (for GOV/ documents and dates): https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/focus/iran/iaea-and-iran-iaea-board-reports.
- Relevant GOV/ reports (e.g., GOV/2025/50 as an example of format and categorization) and DG statements on iaea.org.

Definitions references:
- Uranium‑235 and enrichment thresholds: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uranium-235.
- Uranium hexafluoride (UF6): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uranium_hexafluoride.

Adjudication notes:
- If needed to confirm publication timing or content, use the IAEA page above to access the specific GOV/ document or DG statement; resolution should be achievable within ~10 minutes by checking Q4 2025 entries.
- If IAEA and Iran implement modalities announced on 2025-09-09 and inspections resume, verification language may appear in Q4 documents; however, adjudication relies only on IAEA official publications, not third‑party reporting.

question: Will the U.S. Supreme Court grant certiorari in Trump v. Washington (No. 25-364) by 23:59 ET on December 31, 2025?
background:
Overview and status quo as of October 1, 2025:
- Underlying dispute: On January 20, 2025, President Trump issued Executive Order No. 14,160 concerning birthright citizenship. Related litigation has already reached the Supreme Court on emergency applications, and the Court granted partial stays on June 27, 2025 in consolidated matters connected to the order.
- Petitions filed: The Solicitor General filed two petitions on September 26, 2025: Trump v. Washington (No. 25-364) and Trump v. Barbara (No. 25-365). The article notes the filings were “nearly identical” and that the government asked for resolution in the October 2025 Term but did not request expedited consideration for the petitions or the merits if granted.
- Docket and filing details: The Supreme Court docket for No. 25-364 (Trump v. Washington) shows the petition filed on September 26, 2025, and as of October 1, 2025, no grant of certiorari is recorded.
- Vehicle differences: The Washington petition seeks standard certiorari under 28 U.S.C. § 1254(1), while Barbara seeks certiorari before judgment (Rule 11). The petition materials indicate Washington involves state plaintiffs whose Article III standing was contested in the lower courts, while Barbara involves individual plaintiffs, which the government suggests presents a cleaner path to merits review within the Term.

Key definitions (for clarity in resolution):
- “Certiorari” (grant of certiorari): A writ by which the Supreme Court orders a lower court to deliver the record for review; in Supreme Court practice, review via certiorari is discretionary and typically based on considerations such as conflicts among courts or important questions of federal law.
- “Certiorari before judgment” (Rule 11): A rarely used procedure allowing the Supreme Court to grant certiorari to review a case pending in a court of appeals before that court issues judgment, reserved for cases of imperative public importance.
- “Eastern Time (ET)”: The time zone used for Supreme Court orders in Washington, D.C.; ET is UTC−05:00 during standard time (EST) and UTC−04:00 during daylight saving time (EDT). Daylight saving time ends the first Sunday in November, after which ET is EST (UTC−05:00) through December 31, 2025.

Primary sources a resolver will check:
- Supreme Court docket page for No. 25-364: https://www.supremecourt.gov/docket/docketfiles/html/public/25-364.html (proceedings and orders section will show any certiorari grant).
- Supreme Court orders lists (weekly): https://www.supremecourt.gov/orders/ordersofthecourt (order lists will explicitly state if No. 25-364’s petition for a writ of certiorari is GRANTED).
- Acceptable corroboration, if needed: SCOTUSblog case page for Trump v. Washington  and reporting summarizing petition filings and timing expectations.
resolution_criteria:
Start and end of observation window:
- Eligible events must occur between 00:00 ET on October 1, 2025 and 23:59 ET on December 31, 2025.

What counts as “Yes”:
- Yes if, by 23:59 ET on December 31, 2025, an official Supreme Court source records that the petition for a writ of certiorari in Trump v. Washington (No. 25-364) is GRANTED. Qualifying records include:
  - The Supreme Court docket for No. 25-364 explicitly indicating “Petition for a writ of certiorari GRANTED,” or “certiorari before judgment GRANTED,” or an order granting certiorari in this docket number.
  - A Supreme Court orders list that explicitly states that No. 25-364’s petition for a writ of certiorari is GRANTED (including grants accompanied by dispositions such as grant-vacate-remand (GVR)).

What counts as “No”:
- No if, by 23:59 ET on December 31, 2025, neither the docket nor the orders list shows a certiorari grant for No. 25-364.
- Orders that do not constitute a grant of certiorari for No. 25-364 (e.g., denial of certiorari; dismissal; or transfer without an express grant applicable to No. 25-364) resolve to No.

Scope and consolidation clarifications:
