The announcement must clearly link the investigation to those firings (e.g., references to agents fired in late September 2025, or to agents fired who were photographed kneeling during 2020 protests, or similar phrasing grounded in the events described in the background ).
2) A recorded committee vote or officially posted committee business record (minutes, markup documents, or committee-approved memorandum) authorizing or initiating an investigation into the late-September 2025 firings, posted on Congress.gov or on the committee’s official website.
3) An official memorandum or letter on committee letterhead, posted on the committee’s official website, signed by the committee Chair (House: Chair of the Committee on the Judiciary; Senate: Chair of the Committee on the Judiciary) stating that the committee is opening or conducting an investigation into the late-September 2025 firings.

Exclusions (do not count as formal initiation):
- Statements or letters posted only on an individual member’s personal website or social media, or on non-committee domains.
- Minority-only announcements not authorized by the committee Chair or a committee vote (i.e., lacking formal committee authority).
- General FBI oversight or hearings not specifically opening an investigation into the late-September 2025 firings.

Primary resolution sources to be checked by the resolver:
- House Judiciary Committee site: https://judiciary.house.gov/ (press releases, documents).
- Senate Judiciary Committee site: https://www.judiciary.senate.gov/ (press releases, documents).
- Congress.gov for committee meeting records and votes: https://www.congress.gov/.

Resolve No if no qualifying announcement occurs within the time window.

Notes for resolver:
- Use exact language in official postings to verify that a formal “investigation/inquiry/probe” is being initiated and that it clearly pertains to the late-September 2025 FBI agent firings as defined in the background.
- If multiple announcements occur, the first qualifying announcement within the time window is sufficient for a Yes resolution.
- If ambiguity arises, prefer primary sources from the committees’ official domains and Congress.gov over media coverage; media reporting alone is insufficient for resolution.

question: Will Canada Post and CUPW both publish that ratified collective agreements for the Urban and RSMC bargaining units are in place by December 31, 2025?
background:
Overview and key terms
- Canada Post Corporation is Canada’s national postal operator and a Crown corporation. The Canadian Union of Postal Workers (CUPW) is the public‑sector trade union representing tens of thousands of postal workers at Canada Post, including the Urban Postal Operations (UPO) and Rural and Suburban Mail Carriers (RSMC) bargaining units. A collective agreement (also called a collective bargaining agreement) is a written contract between a union and an employer that governs employment terms; “ratification” commonly refers to approval by the union membership of the negotiated agreement.

Status quo as of 2025-10-01 (UTC)
- On 2025-09-25, CUPW launched a national strike. Canada Post stated that during the national strike, the postal system would shut down: mail and parcels would not be accepted, processed, or delivered, with service guarantees suspended; some post offices would be closed.
- Both parties maintain official, frequently updated web pages for negotiations and labour updates. Canada Post’s “Labour discussion updates” page is a chronological hub for negotiations-related announcements (offers, votes, strike actions, etc.) and links to detailed posts. CUPW communicates negotiations developments through its News & Events section and a dedicated “Urban and RSMC Negotiations 2023–2025” hub.

Why this question is informative
- After a national strike and prolonged bargaining, it is plausible—but uncertain—that agreements will be concluded and ratified by year‑end 2025. Forecasters can track official updates and signals from both sides (e.g., mediator involvement, tentative agreements, vote schedules, and government actions) via the linked hubs.

Relevant links (for forecasters)
- Canada Post Labour discussion updates (negotiations hub): https://www.canadapost-postescanada.ca/cpc/en/our-company/news-and-media/corporate-news/negotiations-list.page 
- Canada Post 2025-09-25 strike announcement: https://www.canadapost-postescanada.ca/cpc/en/our-company/news-and-media/corporate-news/news-release/2025-09-25-cupw-has-launched-a-national-strike-that-will-cause-postal-delays-for-canadians 
- CUPW News & Events: https://www.cupw.ca/en/news---events 
- CUPW Urban and RSMC Negotiations 2023–2025 hub: https://www.cupw.ca/en/collective-agreements/urban-and-rsmc-negotiations-2023-2025 
- Definitions: Canada Post ; CUPW ; collective agreement.
resolution_criteria:
Time window and timezone
- Eligible publications must occur between 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. All timestamps are interpreted in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

What counts as “Yes”
- Resolve Yes if, by the end of the time window, there is clear, public, on‑website confirmation from both parties that collective agreements covering BOTH CUPW bargaining units—(1) Urban Postal Operations (UPO) and (2) Rural and Suburban Mail Carriers (RSMC)—have been ratified. “Ratified” is satisfied by unambiguous language such as “ratified,” “members have ratified,” “ratification vote passed,” or equivalent phrasing indicating that the agreement has completed membership ratification and is accepted by the employer.
- Acceptable sources:
  1) Canada Post’s official negotiations/labour updates pages (the “Labour discussion updates” list page or any article linked from it).
  2) CUPW’s official website (either the News & Events section or the “Urban and RSMC Negotiations 2023–2025” hub or any directly linked bulletin).
- Non-contradiction fallback: If one party posts unambiguous ratification confirmation for BOTH UPO and RSMC and the other party does not post a contradiction (i.e., an explicit statement that ratification has not occurred) within 48 hours, resolve Yes. To use this fallback, the initial publication must be made no later than 2025-12-29 23:59:59 UTC to allow the 48‑hour window to elapse before resolution.

What does NOT count
- Announcements of tentative agreements, scheduling of ratification votes, endorsements by negotiating committees, mediator/arbitrator recommendations, or partial settlements that do not cover both UPO and RSMC do not satisfy the criterion. Press conferences or social media posts alone do not count unless mirrored on the official websites defined above.

What counts as “No”
- Resolve No if the above “Yes” conditions are not met by the deadline.

Definitions and entities (for clarity)
- Canada Post Corporation: Canada’s national postal operator and a Crown corporation.
- Canadian Union of Postal Workers (CUPW): the public‑sector trade union representing postal workers at Canada Post, including the Urban Postal Operations and RSMC units.
- Collective agreement (collective bargaining agreement): a written contract negotiated between a union and an employer governing employment terms; “ratification” refers to membership approval of the agreement.

Primary resolution sources
- Canada Post “Labour discussion updates” hub (and linked articles): https://www.canadapost-postescanada.ca/cpc/en/our-company/news-and-media/corporate-news/negotiations-list.page 
- CUPW official website (News & Events; Urban & RSMC Negotiations hub): https://www.cupw.ca/en/news---events; https://www.cupw.ca/en/collective-agreements/urban-and-rsmc-negotiations-2023-2025 

Context on current disruption (non-operative for resolution but informative)
- Canada Post’s 2025-09-25 strike notice indicates a national strike with a shutdown of acceptance, processing, and delivery for its duration. This provides context for why ratification by year‑end is consequential for operations and workers.

Method for resolvers
- On or after the deadline, check the specified Canada Post and CUPW pages (or directly linked articles) for unambiguous ratification statements affecting BOTH UPO and RSMC. If only one source has such a statement, apply the 48‑hour non‑contradiction rule if applicable. If sites are temporarily inaccessible, archived versions (e.g., via the Internet Archive) may be used to verify content. If both sites are inaccessible for an extended period, corroborating reports from at least two reputable outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, CBC) quoting official confirmation may be used as a last resort (not required if the primary sources are available). References: definitions and organizational roles as above ; official update hubs ; current strike context.

question: Will U.S. CPI‑U (All Items, U.S. city average) 12‑month percent change for November 2025 be at least 3.3%?
background:
Overview and status quo as of 2025‑10‑01
- What is being measured: The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI‑U) measures the average change over time in prices paid by urban consumers for a market basket of goods and services and covers over 90% of the U.S. population; the broad “All items” CPI‑U (U.S. city average, 1982‑84=100) is the most comprehensive headline index. The “12‑month percent change” (a.k.a. year‑over‑year, YoY) compares the index level to its level 12 months earlier; in BLS CPI news releases, the headline 12‑month percent change for All items is reported on a not seasonally adjusted basis (often phrased as “over the last 12 months … before seasonal adjustment”).
- Latest readings: As of October 1, 2025, the most recent published headline All items CPI‑U 12‑month change is for August 2025 at 2.9% (not seasonally adjusted), as stated in the BLS CPI Summary and on the CPI home page (“rose 2.9 percent over the last 12 months, not seasonally adjusted”). The CPI for September 2025 is scheduled to be released on Wednesday, October 15, 2025, at 8:30 a.m. ET.
- Relevant upcoming release: The BLS “Schedule of Selected Releases” lists “Consumer Price Index for November 2025” on Wednesday, December 10, 2025, at 08:30 AM (Eastern Time). Note on that page clarifies all times are Eastern Time; 08:30 ET corresponds to 13:30 UTC on 2025‑12‑10.

What forecasters should know
- Index and scope: This question uses the U.S. headline CPI‑U All items, U.S. city average, 1982‑84=100, not seasonally adjusted—i.e., the standard “headline inflation” figure cited in the first paragraph of BLS CPI news releases.
- Data source and publication: The canonical source will be the BLS CPI Summary news release page for the relevant month (HTML) and/or its accompanying PDF, which explicitly states the All items 12‑month percent change in the lead paragraph and tables.
- Timing: The November 2025 CPI report is scheduled for 2025‑12‑10 at 08:30 ET (13:30 UTC) per the BLS 2025 release calendar.

Definitions (for unambiguous resolution)
- CPI‑U: Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers, covering the urban population (over 90% of U.S. population).
- All items index: The broad headline CPI‑U for the U.S. city average, 1982‑84=100.
- 12‑month percent change (YoY): The percentage change in the not seasonally adjusted index level relative to the same month one year earlier; in BLS releases, the headline statement is “over the last 12 months … before seasonal adjustment”.
- “At least 3.3%”: Greater than or equal to 3.3%. All dates/times are in UTC unless explicitly labeled otherwise.
- Observation window: This question concerns the November 2025 reference month CPI‑U All items 12‑month percent change as first published by BLS on 2025‑12‑10; the observation period for this question runs from 2025‑10‑01 00:00 UTC through 2025‑12‑31 23:59 UTC, but only the 2025‑12‑10 publication is material to resolution.
resolution_criteria:
Resolve YES if, in the initial Bureau of Labor Statistics CPI Summary news release for November 2025 (published on 2025‑12‑10 at 08:30 ET / 13:30 UTC per the BLS calendar ), the headline All items CPI‑U (U.S. city average) 12‑month percent change (not seasonally adjusted) is greater than or equal to 3.3%, as stated in the narrative lead paragraph (e.g., “over the last 12 months … before seasonal adjustment”) or in the corresponding headline table showing the All items 12‑month percent change. Resolve NO otherwise.

Primary resolution source
- BLS CPI Summary (HTML): https://www.bls.gov/news.release/cpi.nr0.htm — use the value explicitly stated for the All items CPI‑U 12‑month percent change for November 2025 in the narrative paragraph. If there is any ambiguity in the narrative, use the All items (U.S. city average) 12‑month percent change reported in the main table on the same page or in the accompanying PDF for the same release.

Tie‑breakers and contingencies
- If the HTML and PDF differ, prefer the HTML CPI Summary page value as of the time of initial publication on 2025‑12‑10 (13:30 UTC). If BLS issues a same‑day correction on 2025‑12‑10, use the corrected value posted on the CPI Summary page that day. Later revisions after 2025‑12‑10 do not affect resolution.
- The scheduled date/time for the November 2025 CPI release is per the BLS Schedule of Selected Releases; if BLS reschedules within 2025, resolution will occur upon publication of the November 2025 CPI Summary within the question’s observation window.

Notes for context (non‑binding but informative)
- Latest status: As of 2025‑10‑01, the most recent headline All items CPI‑U 12‑month change is 2.9% for August 2025 (not seasonally adjusted).
- Definitions and scope for CPI‑U and “All items” come from BLS CPI FAQs.

question: Will the December 2025 WASDE project U.S. 2025/26 corn ending stocks at ≤ 2.05 billion bushels?
background:
Overview of the data and source: The World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates (WASDE) is a monthly report published by the USDA’s Office of the Chief Economist that provides forecasts of supply and use for U.S. and global commodities. The USDA lists 2025 WASDE release dates and confirms monthly publication; the December 2025 report is scheduled for December 9, 2025 (12:00 p.m. ET). Starting October 1, 2025, the WASDE archive is available via USDA’s National Agricultural Library ESMIS platform; the USDA WASDE overview page remains the primary access point.

What the specific metric is: In WASDE, U.S. corn projections appear in the table titled “U.S. Feed Grain and Corn Supply and Use (Corn)” and include a line item “Ending Stocks.” The projection is expressed in million bushels. For reference, the August 2025 WASDE projected 2025/26 U.S. corn ending stocks at 2,117 million bushels , and the September 2025 WASDE projected 2,110 million bushels. These values establish the current status quo near the proposed threshold.

Marketing year definition: USDA’s corn marketing year runs from September 1 to August 31; thus “2025/26” denotes September 1, 2025 through August 31, 2026. ERS materials and WASDE tables use million bushels for U.S. corn quantities.

Why the threshold is non-trivial: The threshold of 2.05 billion bushels (i.e., 2,050 million bushels) sits close to the most recent published projections (2,110 million bushels in September), making movements in yield, domestic use, exports, and stocks adjustments materially relevant to the outcome by December.

Definitions and links for clarity:
- WASDE: USDA’s monthly World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates overview page: https://www.usda.gov/about-usda/general-information/staff-offices/office-chief-economist/commodity-markets/wasde-report 
- Corn (maize): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maize
- Bushel (unit): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bushel
- “Ending Stocks” (operational definition for this question): The figure labeled “Ending Stocks” for “Corn” in the “U.S. Feed Grain and Corn Supply and Use” table for marketing year “2025/26” in the December 2025 WASDE PDF as posted by USDA.

Status quo as of Oct 1, 2025: Latest published WASDE projections for U.S. 2025/26 corn ending stocks are 2,117 (August) and 2,110 (September) million bushels. The December report is scheduled for release on Dec 9, 2025.
resolution_criteria:
Timeframe and start date: This question concerns the value published in the December 2025 WASDE report and will resolve based on that publication between October 15, 2025 00:00 UTC and December 31, 2025 23:59 UTC.

Primary resolution source: The December 2025 WASDE published by USDA’s Office of the Chief Economist. Use the publicly posted PDF accessible via USDA’s WASDE overview page: https://www.usda.gov/about-usda/general-information/staff-offices/office-chief-economist/commodity-markets/wasde-report. The USDA lists the December 2025 release date as December 9, 2025 at 12:00 p.m. ET (17:00 UTC).

What to check exactly: In the December 2025 WASDE, navigate to the table titled “U.S. Feed Grain and Corn Supply and Use” and locate the “Corn” portion. Read the “Ending Stocks” line for marketing year “2025/26.” Numbers are reported in million bushels.

Resolution rule:
- Resolve “Yes” if the “Ending Stocks” entry for U.S. corn in 2025/26 is less than or equal to 2,050 million bushels (i.e., ≤ 2.05 billion bushels).
- Resolve “No” if it is greater than 2,050 million bushels.

Rounding and presentation:
- Use the numeric value printed in the WASDE table. If the number is shown without decimals, treat it as an integer million-bushel figure. If decimals are present, compare the decimal figure numerically to 2,050. Do not convert units; use the million-bushel figure as printed.

Versioning and corrections:
- Use the December 2025 WASDE PDF as posted by USDA OCE. If USDA issues an official erratum or replaces the PDF before December 31, 2025, use the latest corrected version available by December 31, 2025 via the USDA WASDE page or the USDA ESMIS archive.

Exclusions:
- Do not use third-party summaries or non-USDA publications for resolution.
- Do not use preliminary press releases, social media posts, or non-official datasets.

Notes:
- “U.S.” refers to the United States as reported in the USDA WASDE. “Corn” refers to maize (Zea mays). “Ending Stocks” is operationally defined here as the specific line item in the designated WASDE table. All references to “billion” here follow the short scale (1 billion = 1,000 million), but resolution is solely based on the million-bushel figure printed in WASDE.

Evidence at question creation:
- August 2025 WASDE “Ending Stocks” (U.S. corn, 2025/26): 2,117 million bushels.
- September 2025 WASDE “Ending Stocks” (U.S. corn, 2025/26): 2,110 million bushels.
- WASDE is monthly; December 2025 release scheduled for Dec 9, 2025 (12:00 p.m. ET) with archive access via USDA ESMIS/NAL.

question: By 31 December 2025 (23:59:59 UTC), will at least two of three September 2025 donor pledges to the Palestinian Authority (Saudi Arabia USD 90m; Spain USD 50m; Germany EUR 30m) be officially confirmed as received in full?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01:
- On 25 September 2025 in New York, a donor meeting chaired by Norway announced new budget-support pledges to the Palestinian Authority (PA). Official PA communications and state media reported pledges of USD 90 million from Saudi Arabia, USD 50 million from Spain, and EUR 30 million from Germany, with further contributions expected. 
- Saudi Arabia simultaneously announced an emergency international coalition to fund the PA and said it would provide USD 90 million in direct support. Reuters also referenced the Saudi USD 90m pledge as part of efforts to stabilize PA finances. 
- Germany’s EUR 30 million one-time payment intended to support PA salaries faced scrutiny in the Bundestag’s budget committee as of 19 September 2025, delaying announcement and disbursement; the government indicated intent to proceed once concerns were addressed.
- The PA describes severe fiscal stress amid Israel’s withholding of tax revenues and called for an emergency budget support package; the September meeting communiqué and PMO statements emphasize urgency in disbursement.

Key entities and official sources for verification:
- Palestinian Authority (also known as the Palestinian National Authority), its structure, and relevant ministries are described here for definition/clarity. The PA Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) posts official statements at pmo.pna.ps. The State of Palestine Ministry of Finance and Planning (PMOF) posts official notices at pmof.ps.

Why this question: The three named, recent budget-support pledges are large, politically salient, and face operational/legislative constraints, creating substantial uncertainty over whether at least two will be fully disbursed—and officially confirmed as received—by year-end 2025. The verification pathway relies on routine official statements or widely covered wire reporting and should be checkable quickly on 31 December 2025.
resolution_criteria:
Outcome: Resolve Yes if, by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, at least two of the following three pledges have official confirmation that their full pledged amounts have been received by the Palestinian Authority (PA): 
- Saudi Arabia: USD 90,000,000 
- Spain: USD 50,000,000 
- Germany: EUR 30,000,000 
Resolve No otherwise.

Eligible confirmation window and time standard:
- Only confirmations dated between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC (inclusive) and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC (inclusive) count toward resolution. Time zone for all date/time references is Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

Definitions and what counts as confirmation of “received in full”:
- Palestinian Authority (PA): The governmental body exercising limited self-governance in parts of the West Bank (also referred to as the Palestinian National Authority); includes the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) and the Ministry of Finance and Planning (PMOF).
- “Received in full” means official confirmation that cumulative disbursements under the specified pledge (for that donor and amount) equal or exceed the announced figure in the pledge’s currency by the end time. Tranche payments may be aggregated if official sources explicitly indicate the cumulative total reaches the pledged amount.
- Acceptable confirmation sources:
  a) An official PA PMO statement (e.g., on pmo.pna.ps) or PA Ministry of Finance and Planning statement (e.g., on pmof.ps) explicitly confirming receipt by the PA of the full pledged amount from the donor.
  b) An official statement/press release by the donating government explicitly confirming that the full pledged amount has been disbursed to the PA (e.g., to the PA Treasury/Single Treasury Account or equivalent).
  c) A report by a major international newswire (Reuters or AP) that explicitly states—with attribution to an official PA or donating government statement—that the PA has received the full pledged amount from the donor by the time limit.
- Currency handling:
  • For Germany, measure in euros; for Saudi Arabia and Spain, in U.S. dollars. If a donor disburses in another currency, the confirmation must either (i) specify the equivalent in the pledge currency at disbursement, or (ii) provide an official exchange conversion used on the confirmation date. If neither is provided, the resolver will convert the disbursed amount to the pledge currency using the European Central Bank daily reference rate applicable on the confirmation date (16:00 CET). 

What does NOT count:
- Mere pledges, MoUs, appropriations, or allocations without explicit confirmation of executed disbursement to the PA do not count.
- Payments to third parties (e.g., UN agencies, NGOs) or in-kind assistance that are not disbursed to the PA (Treasury/Ministry of Finance) do not count, unless the PA itself officially confirms that such funds were received into PA-controlled accounts.
- Partial receipts that do not reach the full pledged amount by the end time do not count for that donor.

Event set and start date clarity:
- Only confirmations occurring within 2025-10-15 through 2025-12-31 UTC are eligible to be counted. Confirmations before 2025-10-15 UTC are excluded from consideration, even if they meet other criteria.

Primary verification sources (examples/handles):
- PA PMO official site: pmo.pna.ps (example statement about the meeting and pledges).
- WAFA report summarizing the same meeting and amounts (for background; final confirmation must still meet the criteria above).
- PA Ministry of Finance & Planning official site: pmof.ps.
- Major wires for confirmatory reporting: Reuters, AP (background examples referencing the pledges and context).

Edge cases and tie-breaking:
- If the PA is renamed or restructured during the question period, confirmations by its direct institutional successor responsible for the West Bank government’s finances count, provided continuity is clear from official sources.
- If conflicting reports exist, precedence is given in this order: (1) explicit PA PMOF confirmation; (2) explicit donor government confirmation; (3) Reuters/AP reports with clear attribution to official confirmations. If still irreconcilable, resolve conservatively as No.

Provenance of the pledges and context for forecasters:
- Pledges (KSA USD 90m; Spain USD 50m; Germany EUR 30m) and meeting details were publicly described by the PA PMO and WAFA following the 25 September 2025 New York meeting, chaired by Norway. Saudi Arabia announced the USD 90m contribution as part of an emergency coalition. Germany’s planned EUR 30m payment faced budget-committee scrutiny as of 2025-09-19. Reuters also highlighted the Saudi USD 90m pledge as part of broader efforts to stabilize PA finances.

question: Will MITECO’s cumulative “nº de solicitudes” for CAE issuance be at least 5,200 as of November 30, 2025?
background:
Context and definitions
- Spain’s Sistema de Certificados de Ahorro Energético (CAE) is an official mechanism under which Energy Saving Certificates (CAE) are issued to recognize verified final-energy savings. A CAE is an electronic document and an alternative instrument for obligated parties (“Sujetos Obligados”) to meet annual saving obligations; issuance requests (“solicitudes de emisión de CAE”) are submitted by obligated or accredited delegated parties once savings are verified.
- “Solicitud de emisión de CAE” refers to the formal application to obtain CAEs for verified energy savings, filed by a Sujeto Obligado or Sujeto Delegado with the required documentation (including a favorable verifier report). CAEs are recorded in the Registro Nacional de CAE after regional validation and national definitive registration.

What MITECO publishes
- The Ministry (MITECO) publishes monthly “Informe CAE” PDFs that include the indicator “nº de solicitudes” (number of issuance requests), shown both as a cumulative progression (“Progresión acumulada de solicitudes de emisión de CAE”) and as monthly counts (“Solicitudes de emisión de CAE en cada mes”), with a clear cutoff label such as “datos actualizados a DD/MM/YY”.
- These reports also include a status breakdown (“Estado de las solicitudes de emisión de CAE (resueltas y en trámite)”), evidencing that requests span multiple statuses (e.g., en trámite, favorables, desfavorables, desistidas). The overall “nº de solicitudes” used in the cumulative/monthly charts refers to issuance requests regardless of status category (the status chart provides the split).
- In September 2025, MITECO announced a new “Seguimiento del Sistema de CAE” interactive monitoring tool (Power BI) that is updated monthly and intended to make follow-up data more accessible; it tracks deployment of the CAE system and allows filtering by date and other dimensions.

Status quo (latest available figures as of today)
- Cumulative “nº de solicitudes” reported in the monthly Informe CAE:
  - As of June 30, 2025 (“datos actualizados a 30/06/25”): 3,441 cumulative requests.
  - As of July 31, 2025 (“datos actualizados a 31/07/25”): 4,003 cumulative requests.
  - As of August 31, 2025 (“datos actualizados a 31/08/25”): 4,379 cumulative requests.
- The monthly reports present the exact indicator labels we will reference for resolution (“Progresión acumulada de solicitudes de emisión de CAE” and “Solicitudes de emisión de CAE en cada mes”) and the cutoff phrasing (“datos actualizados a DD/MM/YY”), ensuring a clear, auditable source.

Why this threshold
- From June to August 2025, cumulative requests rose from 3,441 to 4,379 (+938), with recent monthly increments appearing in the low-to-mid hundreds, though historical month-to-month changes vary. Setting a threshold of 5,200 aims for a plausible, non-trivial outcome by November 30, 2025, balancing the likelihood that cumulative requests continue to increase against uncertainty in submission and processing cadence.
resolution_criteria:
Forecasting subject
- This question forecasts whether the cumulative “nº de solicitudes” (number of CAE issuance requests) reported by MITECO will be at least 5,200 as of November 30, 2025.

Definitions (authoritative)
- Certificado de Ahorro Energético (CAE): An electronic certificate recognizing verified final-energy savings, part of Spain’s CAE system, used by obligated parties to meet annual savings obligations.
- Solicitud de emisión de CAE: A formal application submitted by a Sujeto Obligado or Sujeto Delegado to obtain CAEs for verified savings, following a favorable verifier report and regional validation; CAEs are definitively registered by the Coordinador Nacional in the Registro Nacional de CAE.
- “nº de solicitudes” for this question: The count displayed by MITECO in the monthly Informe CAE under the chart titled “Progresión acumulada de solicitudes de emisión de CAE” (i.e., cumulative number of issuance requests). Where needed, the monthly chart “Solicitudes de emisión de CAE en cada mes” and the status chart “Estado de las solicitudes de emisión de CAE (resueltas y en trámite)” provide context, but resolution relies on the cumulative chart value.

Observation window and cutoff
- Target date: November 30, 2025.
- Time zone: The report’s “datos actualizados a 30/11/25” refers to Spain local time. For avoidance of doubt, interpret the cutoff as the value MITECO reports for “datos actualizados a 30/11/25,” which corresponds to end-of-day on 2025-11-30 in Spain (CET/UTC+1). The forecast resolves between October 15 and December 31, 2025.

Primary resolution source (preferred)
- Use the November 2025 monthly “Informe CAE” PDF published by MITECO. Read the cumulative value in the chart titled “Progresión acumulada de solicitudes de emisión de CAE,” ensuring the report’s cutoff label reads “datos actualizados a 30/11/25.” The monthly Informe CAE PDFs consistently include these chart titles and cutoff phrasing (see June, July, August 2025 examples).

Fallback resolution source (if the November PDF is not published by 2025-12-31 23:59 UTC)
- Use MITECO’s “Seguimiento del Sistema de CAE” interactive monitoring tool (Power BI) value for the cumulative “nº de solicitudes” with data as of 30/11/2025. MITECO announced this dashboard and its monthly update cadence in September 2025; it tracks the CAE system deployment and allows filtering by date. Document the exact on-screen label, date filter, and value used.

Decision rule
- YES if the cumulative “nº de solicitudes” reported by MITECO (as defined above) is ≥ 5,200 as of 30/11/2025. NO otherwise.

Auditability
- Cite the specific November 2025 “Informe CAE” PDF and page/section where the cumulative chart appears (typically titled “Progresión acumulada de solicitudes de emisión de CAE,” with cutoff “datos actualizados a 30/11/25”), or, if needed, the dashboard screen capture with filters showing the as-of date. Precedent reports (June, July, August 2025) demonstrate the standard structure and labeling , and MITECO’s September 2025 announcement establishes the dashboard as an official monthly source.

question: As of 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, will Mexico’s maximum MFN ad valorem IGI rate for passenger motor vehicles (HS heading 87.03) be 50%?
background:
Context and status quo as of 2025-09-30:
- Policy trajectory: On 2025-09-10, Mexico announced a plan to raise tariffs on automobiles from countries without a free trade agreement (notably including China) to 50% as part of a broad overhaul of import levies; the plan still required approval by Congress as of 2025-09-11. A follow-up report noted the proposed 50% levy would target autos from non-FTA countries and likewise stated that congressional approval was still needed. These reports underscore that, as of mid-September 2025, the measure had been announced but not yet enacted into law.
- Existing rates are heterogeneous across subheadings: Reporting indicates that, over the prior year, Mexico raised tariffs on Chinese-manufactured electric vehicles from 0% to 15%. Other reporting characterizes existing levies on Chinese cars as 20% prior to the proposed increase to 50%. This suggests that within heading 87.03, individual tariff fractions may have different IGI rates at present.
- Earlier legal changes: On 2024-04-22, the Ministry of Economy published in the Diario Oficial de la Federación (DOF) a decree modifying the Tarifa de la Ley de los Impuestos Generales de Importación y de Exportación (TIGIE), imposing temporary tariffs ranging from 5% to 50% on 544 tariff lines effective 2024-04-23 through 2026-04-23; these increases apply to goods from countries without a free trade agreement, and the decree also included PROSEC measures to mitigate impacts in some sectors. Those materials explicitly mention coverage of multiple sectors including transport material, indicating the government has used across-the-board temporary tariff adjustments in 2024–2026.
- Definitions and legal sources: The TIGIE is Mexico’s legally binding tariff schedule (import/export tax rates) as published and modified via decrees in the DOF; it specifies IGI (Impuesto General de Importación) and IGE rates and is modified through legally effective DOF publications. HS heading 87.03 covers “Motor cars and other motor vehicles principally designed for the transport of persons (other than those of heading 87.02), including station wagons and racing cars,” while 8703.10 covers special vehicles like snow and golf carts. The MFN principle in WTO terms requires a country to extend any trade advantage (e.g., a tariff rate) granted to one WTO member to all WTO members, absent applicable exceptions such as free trade agreements; in practice, for countries without an FTA with Mexico (e.g., China), the MFN (general) IGI rate applies. An ad valorem import duty is levied as a percentage of the customs value of the goods.

Why this question is forecastable and non-trivial:
- As of 2025-09-30, a 50% rate for passenger vehicles has been proposed but not yet legally enacted; enactment before year-end is plausible but uncertain, depending on congressional approval, legal drafting, sectoral carve-outs, and timing of DOF publication. The outcome could reasonably resolve Yes or No.

Key terms (with definitions):
- MFN (Most-Favoured-Nation) treatment: Non-discriminatory tariff treatment extended to all WTO members, unless overridden by a preferential trade agreement; for countries without an FTA with Mexico, the MFN (general) IGI rate applies.
- Ad valorem: A duty calculated as a percentage of the customs value of the goods.
- TIGIE: Tarifa de la Ley de los Impuestos Generales de Importación y de Exportación, the legally binding Mexican tariff schedule as published and modified via decrees in the DOF.
- Passenger motor vehicles: Goods classified under HS heading 87.03 per the heading text (excluding heading 87.02 for buses and 8703.10 special vehicles for snow/golf).
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves based on the legally effective Mexican tariff schedule (TIGIE) and related decrees as published in the Diario Oficial de la Federación (DOF).

Resolution date and time:
- The state to be evaluated is the rate “as of” 2025-12-31 at 23:59:59 UTC. Only legal provisions in force at that moment count. Any measures published after this time or with an effective date after this time do not affect resolution. Retroactive provisions (if any) count only if they legally make the rate in force at that moment.

What is being measured:
- Let Rmax be the maximum MFN ad valorem IGI rate applicable to any tariff fraction (fracción arancelaria) under HS heading 87.03 in the TIGIE that is applicable to imports from countries without a free trade agreement with Mexico (i.e., the general MFN rate). We include both internal combustion and electric passenger vehicles (e.g., subheadings within 8703, including 8703.80 for electric vehicles where applicable) but exclude 8703.10 (special vehicles for snow/golf) from the calculation. The rate is the percentage figure listed in the IGI column for the relevant fraction(s).

Resolution rule:
- Resolve Yes if Rmax = 50%.
- Resolve No if Rmax ≠ 50% (i.e., less or greater than 50%).

Primary resolution source:
- The Diario Oficial de la Federación (https://www.dof.gob.mx/), specifically the most recent legally effective TIGIE text and/or the decree(s) modifying the TIGIE in force on 2025-12-31, will be consulted to verify the IGI (MFN) ad valorem rate(s) for HS heading 87.03. If a consolidated TIGIE page is unavailable, the specific DOF decree(s) that establish the rate(s) will be used.

Supporting references used for context (not required for resolution but informative):
- Reports on the 2025-09 announcement to raise auto tariffs to 50% and its then-pending congressional approval.
- The 2024-04-22 DOF decree establishing temporary tariffs of 5%–50% for non-FTA origins effective 2024-04-23 to 2026-04-23, which demonstrates the legal mechanism and timing windows relevant to potential changes before year-end 2025.

question: Between 00:00 UTC on 15 Oct 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on 31 Dec 2025, will India’s Ministry of Defence sign a contract with Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) to procure the Anant Shastra (formerly QRSAM) air-defence system?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-09-30:
- The Indian Army issued a tender/RFP to Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) for five to six regiments of the Anant Shastra air-defence system (formerly known as QRSAM), with the project estimated around ₹30,000 crore. Reporting attributes the issuance to late September 2025 and states the Indian Army as the issuer. Wikipedia’s Anant Shastra page likewise records a tender issued to BEL on 27 September 2025 for approximately ₹30,000 crore.
- BEL management guidance has suggested the company is confident a major portion of the QRSAM/Anant Shastra order could be booked in FY26 Q3–Q4 (Oct 2025–Mar 2026), with optimism about Q4 FY26 specifically, following Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) approval.
- The Defence Acquisition Council accorded Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) in July 2025 for multiple capital acquisitions under the Buy (Indian–IDDM) category, including surface-to-air missiles; AoN is an approval to initiate procurement, not a contract award. A later DAC round of approvals on 5 Aug 2025 covered other systems and sustainment items and did not reference QRSAM/Anant Shastra.

Key definitions and links forecasters may need:
- Anant Shastra (formerly Quick Reaction Surface-to-Air Missile, QRSAM): An Indian short-range air-defence system developed for the Indian Army. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anant_Shastra.
- Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL): Government-owned defence electronics company. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharat_Electronics (background link provided for convenience; not required for resolution).
- Ministry of Defence (India): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Defence_(India) (background link for convenience).
- Indian Army: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Army (background link for convenience).
- Request for Proposal (RFP): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Request_for_proposal (background link for convenience).

Why this is a non-trivial, plausibly 30–70% question:
- A tender reportedly issued in late September 2025, coupled with prior DAC AoN, creates a plausible—but not guaranteed—window for contract signature within Oct–Dec 2025. BEL has publicly expressed confidence in order booking within FY26 Q3–Q4, covering the forecast window, but slippage into early 2026 remains possible.

Primary sources to monitor:
- PIB (Press Information Bureau) – Ministry of Defence press releases (official government source for contract signings): https://pib.gov.in/ (see typical MoD press release format and reliability ).
- BEL stock-exchange filings (corporate announcements) on BSE/NSE for contract-signing disclosures (e.g., Regulation 30 material events).
resolution_criteria:
Question: Resolve Yes if, during the interval 00:00:00 UTC on 15 Oct 2025 through 23:59:59 UTC on 31 Dec 2025, there is a binding contract signed between India’s Ministry of Defence (MoD) or the Indian Army and Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) to procure the Anant Shastra air-defence system (also referred to as Anant Shastra/QRSAM). Resolve No otherwise.

Definitions and what counts:
- Binding contract signed/award: A capital procurement contract under India’s defence procurement process that is executed (signed) by the Government of India (MoD/Indian Army) and BEL, evidenced by an official announcement that explicitly uses contract-signing/award language (e.g., “Ministry of Defence signs contract with Bharat Electronics Limited for procurement of…”) and names the system as Anant Shastra and/or QRSAM. The event date is the signing date stated by the official source; if no signing date is stated, use the publication timestamp of the first qualifying announcement in UTC.
- System identity: References to “Anant Shastra,” “QRSAM,” or “Quick Reaction Surface-to-Air Missile” for Army induction count as the same system. If the official announcement uses the legacy name (QRSAM) or the new name (Anant Shastra) or both, it qualifies.
- Eligible counterparties: The Government of India’s Ministry of Defence (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Defence_(India)) or the Indian Army (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Army). BEL must be a signatory to the contract.
- Scope: Contracts must be for the procurement of the Anant Shastra/QRSAM weapon system (e.g., regiment(s)/batteries/launchers/radars/missiles as part of the system) consistent with the tendered program; sub-system or maintenance-only contracts that do not explicitly state procurement of the Anant Shastra/QRSAM system do not count.
- Partial awards and joint contracts: If the procurement is split across multiple contracts and at least one contract that meets the above criteria is signed with BEL in the time window, resolve Yes. If the contract is a multi-party joint agreement and BEL is a contracting party for Anant Shastra/QRSAM system supply, it counts.

What does NOT count:
- Acceptance of Necessity (AoN), Requests for Proposal (RFPs), tenders, commercial negotiation committee outcomes, Letters of Intent, Letters of Acceptance without a signed procurement contract, Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs), offsets-only agreements, trial/evaluation MoUs, or mere press reports without an official announcement.
- Contracts for unrelated systems or for QRSAM-related sustainment/AMC alone.

Resolution sources (must be publicly accessible and dated):
- Primary: Press Information Bureau (PIB) press release issued by the Ministry of Defence announcing a signed contract with BEL for Anant Shastra/QRSAM (example of official MoD press release format and reliability ).
- Alternative primary: BEL’s stock-exchange filing (BSE/NSE corporate announcement) stating that BEL has signed a contract with MoD/Indian Army to supply Anant Shastra/QRSAM.

Adjudication notes:
- If both a PIB MoD press release and a BEL stock-exchange filing exist and conflict on dates, prefer the signing date stated in the PIB release. If one source provides a signing date and the other provides only a publication date, use the explicit signing date.
- The event must occur within the specified UTC window. Announcements made after the window that refer to a signing that occurred within the window will be considered if the signing date is clearly stated by the official source.

Context for forecasters (non-binding for resolution):
- Media reports indicate the Army issued an RFP/tender to BEL around 27–29 Sep 2025 for 5–6 regiments of Anant Shastra/QRSAM, estimated at ~₹30,000 crore.
- BEL has guided to potential order booking in FY26 Q3–Q4, with optimism for Q4 FY26, following DAC AoN in July 2025.
- A separate DAC approval round on 5 Aug 2025 did not reference QRSAM/Anant Shastra, avoiding confusion with other approvals.

question: Will the Bank of Ghana’s MPC announce a Monetary Policy Rate below 21.5% at its November 17–19, 2025 meeting?
background:
Summary of the status quo (as of 2025-09-30):
- At its meeting concluding on 17 September 2025, the Bank of Ghana (BoG) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) announced a 350-basis-point reduction in the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR), bringing it to 21.5 percent. In the same press release, the BoG stated that the next MPC meeting is scheduled for 17–19 November 2025, with the announcement of the policy decision on 19 November 2025.
- The BoG’s amended 2025 MPC calendar likewise lists the November 2025 MPC meeting for November 17–19, with the press release on Wednesday the 19th.
- Inflation context: Ghana’s year‑on‑year CPI inflation for August 2025 was 11.5 percent, per the Ghana Statistical Service (GSS) CPI bulletin.

Definitions and key terms:
- Bank of Ghana (BoG) Monetary Policy Rate (MPR): Per BoG, the MPR is the main policy tool that “signals the monetary policy stance and it is the rate at which short‑term monetary policy operations are conducted with counterparties – mainly, the commercial banks, on a day‑to‑day basis.” It anchors short‑term market interest rates to achieve the primary objective of price stability (see BoG’s “Our Monetary Policy Framework”). Link: https://www.bog.gov.gh/monetary-policy/our-monetary-policy-framework/
- Basis point (bp): One hundredth of one percentage point (i.e., 0.01 percentage points = 0.01%). Link: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basis_point
- Time zone: Ghana observes Greenwich Mean Time (GMT), which is UTC+00:00. All dates/times in this question are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). Link: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_in_Ghana

Why this is a forecast with meaningful uncertainty:
- After a large September cut, the November decision will balance disinflation progress against risks. The current policy rate level (21.5%) and the timetable for the November decision are clearly documented by the BoG , while headline inflation suggests room for debate on the size and timing of further easing.
resolution_criteria:
Question: Will the Bank of Ghana’s MPC announcement concluding its meeting scheduled for November 17–19, 2025 state a Monetary Policy Rate strictly below 21.5 percent?

Start and end of observation window:
- Eligible announcements are those published between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC (inclusive). Times are UTC; Ghana is UTC+00:00.

How to resolve:
- Primary source of truth: the official MPC press release announcing the outcome of the November 2025 MPC meeting on the BoG website (e.g., the same location/format as the 17 September 2025 MPC press release). The BoG’s amended 2025 MPC calendar indicates the November 17–19 meeting with a press release on Wednesday the 19th, which establishes the expected publication timing.
- Resolve Yes if the press release that announces the conclusion of the November 17–19, 2025 MPC meeting states an MPR (a.k.a. “Monetary Policy Rate”) that is strictly less than 21.5 percent.
- Resolve No if the announced MPR is 21.5 percent or higher.

Tie‑breakers and edge cases:
- If the November 2025 MPC meeting dates are amended by the BoG, use the BoG’s November 2025 MPC press release that explicitly states it is the conclusion of the November 2025 MPC meeting, provided it is published within the observation window.
- If multiple BoG pages differ, prefer the signed PDF press release for the November 2025 MPC decision posted by the BoG (as in prior MPC press releases).
- The baseline rate of 21.5 percent is provided for the threshold only; this question resolves solely based on the level of the MPR stated in the November 2025 MPC announcement, not on the direction of change relative to any prior rate.

Links for verification:
- September 2025 MPC press release (example of format and source; establishes current MPR as of that date and notes the November meeting): https://www.bog.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/MPC-Press-Release-September-2025-.pdf 
- BoG 2025 MPC calendar (amended): https://www.bog.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/MPC-Meeting-Dates-2025-Amended.pdf 
- BoG monetary policy framework (definition of MPR): https://www.bog.gov.gh/monetary-policy/our-monetary-policy-framework/ 
- Ghana CPI inflation bulletin (context): https://statsghana.gov.gh/gssmain/fileUpload/Price%20Indices/August%202025CPI-Bulletin.pdf 

Resolution deadline:
- This question will be resolved as soon as the relevant November 2025 MPC press release is published and verified, and in any case no later than 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

question: Will Romania sign at least one subsequent contract under its SHORAD/VSHORAD framework agreement with Rafael between October 15 and December 31, 2025?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-09-30:
- On July 18, 2025, Romania’s Ministry of National Defence (MApN) — via CN Romtehnica SA — and Israel’s Rafael Advanced Defense Systems Ltd signed a framework agreement to procure SHORAD-VSHORAD air defense systems. The agreement is valued at 10.33 billion lei (approx. €2.038 billion excluding VAT), covers six integrated SHORAD-VSHORAD air defense systems (six SHORAD and six VSHORAD systems), and explicitly envisages three subsequent contracts over a seven-year period. It includes training, a simulation system for VSHORAD operators, ammunition, and logistical support.
- Reuters reported that this framework agreement provides for signing three further contracts through which six integrated anti-aircraft systems will be acquired, with deliveries beginning within three years of signing the first of those contracts, and attributed the information to the Romanian defense ministry.
- Multiple defense outlets reported that Romania selected Rafael’s SPYDER air defense system for the V/SHORAD program, with total program value cited around €1.9–2.3 billion and the award to be finalized via a framework agreement and subsequent contracts.

Definitions and context a forecaster may need:
- SHORAD (Short-Range Air Defense): Anti-aircraft weapons and tactics designed to defend against low-altitude air threats such as helicopters, low-flying aircraft, UCAVs, and loitering munitions.
- VSHORAD (Very Short-Range Air Defense): Commonly refers to very short-range systems, typically including MANPADS (man-portable air-defense systems), which are shoulder-launched guided surface-to-air missiles used against low-flying aircraft and cruise missiles.
- SPYDER: An Israeli short- and medium-range mobile air defense system (Surface-to-air PYthon and DERby) that employs Python-5 and Derby missiles; a typical battery includes a command-and-control unit and multiple missile launchers.
- Iron Dome: An Israeli mobile, all-weather air defense system designed primarily for C-RAM and short-range air defense, using the Tamir interceptor, an EL/M-2084 radar, and a battle management & weapon control system.
- Framework agreement (in this specific case): The MApN press release explicitly defines the procurement structure for Romania’s SHORAD-VSHORAD program as a framework agreement that will be followed by three subsequent contracts over seven years.
- Time zone: Eastern European Time (EET) is UTC+02:00; during summer, Eastern European Summer Time (EEST) is UTC+03:00.

Why this question is uncertain and interesting:
- The framework agreement has been signed, but execution of any of the subsequent contracts — the concrete procurement steps — depends on administrative, budgetary, and political timing. Reporting indicates the selection and planned structure, but not exact signing dates for the subsequent contracts, making the outcome by year-end 2025 uncertain.
resolution_criteria:
Event window and time zone:
- Eligible events must occur between 00:00 EET (UTC+02:00) on October 15, 2025 and 23:59 EET (UTC+02:00) on December 31, 2025.

What resolves Yes:
- Resolve Yes if, by 23:59 EET on December 31, 2025, there is public, authoritative evidence that at least one of the three “subsequent contracts” envisaged in the SHORAD-VSHORAD framework agreement signed on July 18, 2025 has been signed (i.e., executed by authorized representatives) between CN Romtehnica SA/the Romanian Ministry of National Defence and Rafael Advanced Defense Systems Ltd.

Acceptable resolution evidence sources (any one suffices):
- An official press release or announcement on the Romanian Ministry of National Defence (MApN) website or press release archive confirming the signing of a subsequent contract under the SHORAD-VSHORAD framework agreement.
- An official announcement from CN Romtehnica SA or Rafael Advanced Defense Systems Ltd confirming the signing of a subsequent contract under the SHORAD-VSHORAD framework.
- Publication in Romania’s Official Gazette (Monitorul Oficial) indicating execution/signing of a subsequent contract under this framework agreement.
- A report by a major international wire service (e.g., Reuters) that explicitly states a subsequent contract under the referenced framework agreement has been signed, attributing the information to official government or company statements.

Clarifications and exclusions:
- “Subsequent contract” refers specifically to the contracts envisaged by the framework agreement described in the MApN press release (three contracts over seven years for six integrated SHORAD-VSHORAD systems).
- Contracts must be signed/executed; award decisions, notices of intent, memorandum of understanding (MOU), letters of intent (LOI), or framework agreement amendments without executed subsequent contracts do not count.
- The contract’s branding (e.g., SPYDER, Iron Dome, or other Rafael offerings) is irrelevant for resolution; what matters is that it is a subsequent contract executed under the SHORAD-VSHORAD framework agreement referenced above.

What resolves No:
- Resolve No if no such subsequent contract signing under the specified framework agreement is evidenced by the acceptable sources within the event window.

Notes for resolvers:
- For baseline context on the framework agreement and expected subsequent contracts, see the MApN press release  and Reuters coverage. For system selection context (SPYDER) and program reporting, see.

question: Will 2025 world oil demand growth be below 1.0 mb/d according to the latest IEA Oil Market Report published by 31 Dec 2025 (UTC)?
background:
Context for forecasters: This question is about whether the International Energy Agency (IEA) will assess that 2025 world oil demand grew by less than 1.0 million barrels per day (mb/d) versus 2024 when measured on an annual-average basis, as reported in its Oil Market Report (OMR). The IEA publishes monthly OMRs that include “world/total oil demand” annual levels and often an explicit y/y growth figure for the calendar year. Forecasters should consult the most recent 2025 OMR issues to see the current full‑year estimate and the IEA’s discussion of drivers (e.g., transport fuel demand, petrochemicals, electric vehicles, macroeconomic conditions, policy impacts). Key references:
- IEA Oil Market Report (monthly landing page): https://www.iea.org/reports/oil-market-report
- IEA OMR Glossary (scope/method notes for “oil demand” and units): https://www.iea.org/articles/oil-market-report-glossary
- IEA Glossary (definitions for kb/d and mb/d): https://www.iea.org/glossary
Definitions to know:
- World/total oil demand (IEA OMR usage): The OMR tracks “total oil” demand (sometimes termed total liquids), expressed as average million barrels per day over a calendar year. See OMR Glossary for scope and methodology.
- Barrels per day (b/d), thousand barrels per day (kb/d), and million barrels per day (mb/d): Unit conventions used by the IEA. See the IEA Glossary.
As of today (2025‑09‑22), the outcome is uncertain and depends on year‑end assessments; the IEA’s monthly OMR updates can change during the year. Forecasters should use the latest public IEA OMR, plus other reputable sources (e.g., OPEC MOMR, EIA STEO, macro indicators), to form a view. This question will resolve strictly on the IEA OMR as specified below.
resolution_criteria:
What is measured:
- Growth equals the IEA’s 2025 annual-average world (total) oil demand minus the IEA’s 2024 annual-average world (total) oil demand, both as presented in the same IEA Oil Market Report (OMR) used for resolution.

Primary source and timing:
- Use the latest IEA OMR published on or before 2025‑12‑31 23:59:59 UTC. The IEA OMR landing page is: https://www.iea.org/reports/oil-market-report. Within that report, use the world/total oil demand annual figures for 2025 and 2024.

How to extract the value:
- If the OMR provides an explicit 2025 y/y growth number for world/total oil demand, use that value.
- If only annual levels are presented, compute growth as (2025 annual average) − (2024 annual average) using the figures from the same OMR issue.

Scope, units, and comparisons:
- “World/total oil demand” follows the IEA OMR’s scope (total liquids) and methodology as described in the OMR Glossary: https://www.iea.org/articles/oil-market-report-glossary.
- Units: Use mb/d (million barrels per day). If values are shown in kb/d, convert at 1,000 kb/d = 1.0 mb/d. Unit definitions: https://www.iea.org/glossary.
- Precision: Compare using the highest-precision figure published in that OMR (e.g., two decimal places in mb/d) without additional rounding by the resolver.

Outcome rule:
- YES if growth < 1.00 mb/d.
- NO if growth ≥ 1.00 mb/d.

Discrepancies and precedence:
- If numerical values in OMR narrative text and OMR tables differ, tables take precedence. If multiple tables exist, prefer the summary “world/total oil demand” table that lists annual levels (or growth) by year.
- If more than one OMR is published on or before 2025‑12‑31, use the latest one.

Fallback if the OMR page is temporarily inaccessible:
- Accept the figure as quoted by a major international wire service (e.g., Reuters, Associated Press, or AFP) that explicitly attributes the exact 2025 world oil demand growth figure to the IEA OMR published on or before 2025‑12‑31, with a working link or clear date reference. If multiple such reports conflict, prefer the one that directly cites the OMR table figure.

Finality and revisions:
- The resolution uses the specified OMR available by 2025‑12‑31 UTC. Any later revisions or subsequent OMRs in 2026 or beyond do not affect the outcome.

question: By 23:59 IST on December 31, 2025, will India’s cumulative KMS 2025–26 paddy procurement (in terms of rice) be at least 350.0 LMT (i.e., 35.0 million tonnes)?
background:
Context as of October 1, 2025: India’s Department of Food & Public Distribution (DFPD) convened a national meeting on September 1, 2025, and fixed the Kharif Marketing Season (KMS) 2025–26 paddy procurement estimate at 463.50 lakh metric tonnes (LMT) “in terms of rice.” The meeting was chaired by the DFPD Secretary and involved state food secretaries and the Food Corporation of India (FCI). The Kharif Marketing Season is defined in DFPD’s Annual Report as starting on October 1 and lasting until the following September 30. For calibration, DFPD reported that in the previous season (KMS 2024–25), cumulative procurement “of paddy in terms of rice” for the central pool as of December 31, 2024, was 313.13 LMT; DFPD also shows state- and India-level “as on” reporting formats for procurement totals. DFPD’s recurring monthly Foodgrain Bulletins publish “as on” or “upto” date cumulative procurement figures, specifically using the phrasing “Procurement of paddy (in terms of rice),” confirming the metric and that authoritative monthly reports exist and are routinely updated (e.g., November 2024: 189.14 LMT “upto 30.11.2024”; January 2024 bulletin: “upto 31.01.2024” shows cumulative procurement for KMS 2023–24).

Definitions and units:
- Kharif Marketing Season (KMS): The DFPD defines procurement operations as seasonal, with KMS starting on October 1 and lasting up to the next September 30. For this question, “KMS 2025–26” means October 1, 2025 to September 30, 2026.
- Procurement and “paddy (in terms of rice)”: DFPD and FCI report national procurement under the central pool at the Minimum Support Price (MSP), often expressed as “Procurement of paddy (in terms of rice).” DFPD converts paddy quantities into rice equivalents using an “out-turn ratio,” commonly 67% (i.e., 0.67), as evidenced in official financial calculations and footnotes indicating CMR derivation using a 67% conversion factor.
- Lakh: In the Indian numbering system, one lakh equals 100,000.
- Tonne: A metric tonne equals 1,000 kilograms; 35.0 million tonnes equals 35,000,000 tonnes. 350.0 LMT equals 35.0 million tonnes (since 350.0 × 100,000 = 35,000,000 tonnes).
- Indian Standard Time (IST): UTC+05:30; India does not observe daylight saving time.
- Kharif crop/season context: Kharif crops are cultivated during the monsoon and typically harvested around September–October, aligning with KMS beginning in October for procurement operations.

Why the threshold and uncertainty: The official national estimate for KMS 2025–26 is 463.50 LMT “in terms of rice”. As a benchmark, cumulative procurement “in terms of rice” as of December 31, 2024, was 313.13 LMT. Setting the threshold at 350.0 LMT (35.0 million tonnes) by December 31, 2025, is close enough above last year’s as-of date to be non-trivial and plausibly uncertain, while remaining well below the full-season estimate, encouraging informed forecasting based on monsoon harvest timing, state-level procurement execution, milling/CMR logistics, and storage/operational constraints, all of which are reflected in DFPD’s periodic “as on” reporting.
resolution_criteria:
Resolution timeframe and metric:
- Observation time: 23:59 IST (UTC+05:30) on December 31, 2025.
- Metric to check: India’s national cumulative “Procurement of paddy (in terms of rice)” for KMS 2025–26, expressed in LMT (lakh metric tonnes) or tonnes, for the central pool as reported by DFPD/FCI.
- Threshold: 350.0 LMT (i.e., 35,000,000 tonnes).

Primary resolution source:
- Use the DFPD’s official monthly Foodgrain Bulletin covering December 2025 (or the first subsequent bulletin/report that explicitly states the figure “upto 31.12.2025” or “as on 31.12.2025”) and the national total for “Procurement of paddy (in terms of rice)” in KMS 2025–26. DFPD’s bulletins consistently report cumulative procurement as of specific dates and use the exact phrasing “paddy (in terms of rice)” (e.g., November 2024 bulletin, January 2024 bulletin).

Secondary/fallback sources and tie-breakers:
- If the December 2025 Foodgrain Bulletin is not yet available by the time of resolution, use any official DFPD procurement publication that provides the national cumulative “as on 31.12.2025” figure for KMS 2025–26 (e.g., year-end DFPD Annual Report section or dashboard/press note on DFPD’s website). DFPD precedent shows it reports “as on 31.12” national procurement figures and defines KMS timing (e.g., “as on 31.12.2024, 313.13 LMT of paddy in terms of rice”). Prefer DFPD over FCI if figures conflict; if two DFPD publications conflict, use the one with the later publication timestamp.

Decision rule:
- Resolve Yes if the national cumulative “Procurement of paddy (in terms of rice)” for KMS 2025–26 is reported as ≥ 350.0 LMT by 23:59 IST on December 31, 2025. Resolve No otherwise.

Term clarifications:
- “KMS 2025–26” refers to the Kharif Marketing Season running from October 1, 2025 to September 30, 2026, per DFPD.
- “Procurement of paddy (in terms of rice)” uses DFPD’s rice-equivalent reporting, which applies an out-turn ratio (commonly 67%) to convert paddy to rice equivalents; rely on the figures as reported by DFPD without recalculation.
- Units: 1 lakh = 100,000; 1 tonne = 1,000 kg; 350.0 LMT equals 35,000,000 tonnes.

Source links for reference (dynamic, not for citation):
- DFPD website home (for Bulletins/Reports): https://dfpd.gov.in/en
- PIB press release confirming the 463.50 LMT estimate: https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2162849

All claims above that derive from documents are cited by Document ID: DFPD Annual Report (KMS definition, “as on 31.12.2024” procurement, out-turn footnote) ; monthly Foodgrain Bulletins (phrasing and “as on/upto” reporting) ; out-turn ratio usage ; tonne and lakh definitions ; IST offset ; PIB press release (national 463.50 LMT estimate, agencies present).

question: Will Ulta Beauty report GAAP diluted EPS of at least $5.60 for Q3 FY2025?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30:
- Company and fiscal calendar: Ulta Beauty’s fiscal year ends on the Saturday closest to January 31, based on a 52/53-week year, with four 13‑week quarters and an extra week added to the fourth quarter every five or six years.
- Upcoming event timing: Ulta’s investor relations calendar lists the “Q3 2025 Ulta Beauty Earnings Conference Call” on December 4, 2025, indicating the Q3 FY2025 results release is scheduled for that date. Ulta posts earnings press releases to its News & Events press release archive at https://www.ulta.com/investor/news-events/press-releases.
- Recent performance and guidance:
  • Q1 FY2025 diluted EPS (GAAP): $6.70, including a $0.01 benefit due to income tax accounting for stock-based compensation; Q1 net sales increased 4.5% to $2.8B; comparable sales increased 2.9%.
  • Q2 FY2025 diluted EPS (GAAP): $5.78, including a $0.03 benefit due to income tax accounting for stock-based compensation.
  • On August 28, 2025, Ulta updated FY2025 guidance, including diluted EPS of $23.85–$24.30, net sales of $12.0–$12.1B, comparable sales of 2.5%–3.5%, and operating margin of 11.9%–12.0%.
  • Prior-year benchmark: Q3 FY2024 diluted EPS (GAAP) was $5.14, per Ulta’s Dec 5, 2024 8-K with the attached press release (Exhibit 99.1).
- Definition: Diluted earnings per share (diluted EPS) is a company’s earnings per share calculated using fully diluted shares outstanding, i.e., including the impact of stock option grants and convertible bonds.
Rationale for threshold: Given Q3 FY2024 EPS of $5.14 , Q1 FY2025 EPS of $6.70 , Q2 FY2025 EPS of $5.78 , and raised full-year guidance , a $5.60 threshold targets a middle ground where outcomes appear uncertain and research into category mix, promotions, margin trends, inventory, and competitive dynamics could materially affect forecasts.
resolution_criteria:
Resolution window: This question resolves based on Ulta Beauty’s official reporting of GAAP diluted EPS for the third quarter of fiscal year 2025, published between October 15, 2025 00:00 UTC and December 31, 2025 23:59 UTC.
Primary source of truth: Ulta Beauty’s Q3 FY2025 earnings press release posted on the company’s investor relations News & Events press release archive (https://www.ulta.com/investor/news-events/press-releases), expected on December 4, 2025 per the IR calendar.
Backup source: If the press release is not available by December 31, 2025 23:59 UTC, resolve using the GAAP diluted EPS reported in Ulta’s SEC filing for the quarter (Form 10‑Q or, if applicable, an 8‑K attaching the earnings release), consistent with how Q3 FY2024 was reported via an 8‑K with the press release as Exhibit 99.1.
Definitions and comparison rules:
- “Ulta Beauty” means Ulta Beauty, Inc. (NASDAQ: ULTA).
- “Q3 FY2025” refers to Ulta’s third fiscal quarter of fiscal year 2025, as designated in Ulta’s official reporting; Ulta’s fiscal year structure is per company FAQ.
- “GAAP diluted EPS” means the diluted earnings per share figure Ulta reports under U.S. GAAP in its official materials; diluted EPS includes the impact of potential dilutive securities (options, warrants, convertibles) as defined by standard references.
- Use the exact GAAP diluted EPS figure as stated by Ulta in the Q3 FY2025 press release (or backup SEC filing). Do not adjust for any noted tax benefits or other commentary; compare the reported GAAP diluted EPS as printed.
- Rounding/comparison: Compare the threshold to the figure exactly as reported by Ulta. If Ulta reports to two decimal places, use that printed value. The question resolves “Yes” if the reported GAAP diluted EPS for Q3 FY2025 is greater than or equal to $5.60; “No” if it is less than $5.60.
Adjudication examples:
- If the press release states “Diluted earnings per share: $5.62,” resolve Yes.
- If the press release states “Diluted earnings per share: $5.59,” resolve No.
- If Ulta only reports adjusted/non‑GAAP EPS and does not provide GAAP diluted EPS in the press release, use the GAAP diluted EPS from the SEC filing (10‑Q or 8‑K).
Time zone: All timestamps for the resolution window are in UTC.

question: After its December 10, 2025 announcement, will the Bank of Canada’s policy interest rate be at or below 2.25%?
background:
Context as of October 1, 2025: The Bank of Canada (BoC) reduced its target for the overnight rate (the BoC’s “policy interest rate”) to 2.5% on September 17, 2025, with the Bank Rate at 2.75% and the deposit rate at 2.45%. The next interest rate announcements are scheduled for October 29 and December 10, 2025, with releases posted at 09:45 Eastern Time (ET). The BoC defines its policy interest rate as the target for the overnight rate—this is the single, authoritative rate to use for this question.

Recent macro context (potentially relevant to forecasters): As of the September 17 decision, the BoC cited a weaker economy and reduced upside risks to inflation. Canada’s CPI inflation was 1.9% in August, preferred core measures were around 3% with dissipating monthly momentum, the unemployment rate was 7.1% in August, and Q2 GDP declined by about 1.5%—with notable softness in exports and business investment. The October 29, 2025 announcement is scheduled to coincide with the Monetary Policy Report, which could further inform the December decision.

Scheduling and publication: In 2025 the BoC has eight fixed-date announcements, including October 29 and December 10, with all interest rate announcements at 09:45 ET. The Bank’s Upcoming Events page lists these announcements and indicates how and when they are published.
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves based on the Bank of Canada’s official press release for the December 10, 2025 interest rate announcement.

Definitions and scope:
- “Policy interest rate” means the Bank of Canada’s “target for the overnight rate,” as defined by the BoC; this is the sole rate used for resolution.
- “At or below 2.25%” means the stated target for the overnight rate in the press release is less than or equal to 2.25%. If the BoC uses fractional notation (e.g., “2½%” or “2¼%”), interpret “½” as 0.5 and “¼” as 0.25.
- Only the target for the overnight rate is relevant; the Bank Rate and deposit rate are not used for resolution.

Operational resolution steps:
1) Locate the BoC’s December 10, 2025 interest rate announcement press release, published at approximately 09:45 ET on bankofcanada.ca (see schedule confirmation and Upcoming Events listings).
2) Read the value of the “target for the overnight rate” stated in that press release.
3) Resolve “Yes” if the stated target for the overnight rate is ≤ 2.25%; otherwise resolve “No.”

Edge cases and clarifications:
- If multiple BoC communications are issued on December 10, use the official press release that announces the setting of the target for the overnight rate for that fixed-date decision (not subsequent summaries, speeches, or technical notes).
- If the press release is posted later the same day due to operational delays, resolve using that same press release once published.
- If an extraordinary, unscheduled rate change occurs on or before December 10, this question still resolves solely on the target for the overnight rate as stated in the fixed-date December 10 press release.

question: Will OFAC issue a Venezuela-related General License between October 15 and December 31, 2025 that explicitly authorizes either expansion of Chevron’s joint ventures into new fields in Venezuela or export of Chevron JV petroleum/petroleum products to non-U.S. jurisdictions?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- OFAC’s Venezuela General Licenses (GLs) 41A (issued March 4, 2025) and 41B (issued March 24, 2025) authorized only wind-down transactions for Chevron’s joint ventures in Venezuela and explicitly did not permit expansion into new fields; both also prohibited export of Chevron JV petroleum/petroleum products to jurisdictions other than the United States. GL 41B Note 2 states: “Nothing in this general license authorizes any expansion of the Chevron JVs into new fields in Venezuela”. Both GLs barred “the sale of petroleum or petroleum products produced by or through the Chevron JVs for the exportation to any jurisdiction other than the United States”.
- The Federal Register published these web general licenses (GLs 41A, 5R, and 41B) on July 23, 2025, confirming issuance dates and summarizing their scopes and restrictions, including the wind-down authorization and prohibitions noted above. OFAC’s Venezuela-related sanctions page lists selected general licenses and references these publications, providing authoritative context on the program and the GLs.

Definitions to eliminate ambiguity:
- Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) licenses: A license is an authorization from OFAC to engage in a transaction that otherwise would be prohibited; a general license authorizes a particular type of transaction for a class of persons without requiring an individual application, while a specific license is issued to a particular person/entity for a specific transaction.
- Venezuela-related General License: A general license issued pursuant to the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations (31 CFR part 591), typically titled “Venezuela General License X” and published by OFAC (and later in the Federal Register as a web general license).
- Chevron JVs: “Chevron’s joint ventures in Venezuela,” as referenced in GL 41A/41B (the “Chevron JVs”), involving Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. (PdVSA) or any entity in which PdVSA owns, directly or indirectly, a 50% or greater interest.
- Field (oil field): An area containing accumulations of liquid petroleum in subsurface reservoirs of economic interest; used here to define “new fields” as oil fields not already part of the Chevron JVs’ authorized operations under prior GLs.
- Export: A good produced in one country that is sold into another country; here, “export to non-U.S. jurisdictions” means sale for export to destinations outside the United States.

Why this question is high-entropy yet resolvable:
- The current GLs are restrictive, but policy could plausibly shift to explicitly permit either JV expansion or third-country exports, and such changes are documented by OFAC and the Federal Register, enabling a clear binary resolution.
resolution_criteria:
Resolve Yes if ALL of the following conditions are met; otherwise resolve No.

1) Time window and scope:
- Between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, OFAC issues a Venezuela-related General License under the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations (31 CFR part 591) that meets Condition 2. For “issues,” use the issuance date printed on the GL document signed by the OFAC Director (the date appearing on the GL PDF posted by OFAC).

2) Explicit authorization in the GL text (either A or B suffices):
A) Expansion into new fields: The GL’s text contains an explicit affirmative authorization stating that expansion of Chevron’s joint ventures in Venezuela into new oil fields is authorized. “Chevron’s joint ventures” and “new fields” are defined as in GL 41A/41B (“Chevron JVs”) and oil fields as defined above; omission of prohibitions alone does not qualify—there must be explicit permitting language. GL 41B’s Note 2 currently disallows such expansion; this criterion requires a GL that affirmatively permits it.
OR
B) Export to non-U.S. jurisdictions: The GL’s text contains an explicit affirmative authorization stating that the sale for export to any destination outside the United States of petroleum or petroleum products produced by or through the Chevron JVs is authorized. Again, omission of prohibitions alone does not qualify—there must be explicit permitting language. GL 41A/41B currently prohibit such exports; this criterion requires a GL that affirmatively permits them.

3) Applicability to Chevron JVs:
- The GL must apply to “Chevron’s joint ventures in Venezuela,” either by naming Chevron/its JVs explicitly or by clearly defining scope equivalent to the Chevron JVs under prior GLs (e.g., GL 41A/41B).

4) Source of truth and verification:
- Primary source: The GL PDF posted on ofac.treasury.gov (OFAC’s official website) showing (i) the issuance date within the time window, and (ii) the explicit authorization language satisfying 2A or 2B.
- Secondary corroboration (if available by the resolution date): The Federal Register “Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses” notice associated with the GL, which typically confirms issuance and summarizes scope. Presence of the Federal Register notice is helpful but not required to resolve; the OFAC-posted GL PDF alone suffices.

Operational notes:
- If multiple Venezuela-related GLs are issued in the window, the question resolves Yes if any one GL satisfies Condition 2.
- If a GL is issued in the window but later amended/superseded, resolution is based on the text of the GL as issued in the window. Amendments outside the window do not alter the resolution unless they retroactively change the issued GL’s text within the window (which OFAC does not typically do for already-issued documents).
- If the GL text authorizes only pilot programs, temporary trials, or limited exceptions, it still qualifies if the authorization explicitly permits either 2A or 2B for the Chevron JVs as defined above.
- If the GL authorizes exports to “jurisdictions other than the United States” or uses synonymous phrasing that unambiguously includes third-country destinations, it meets 2B.

Exclusions:
- Specific licenses, FAQ guidance, interpretive guidance, press releases, or enforcement actions do not count; only a General License under 31 CFR part 591 qualifies.

question: Between 2025-06-01 and 2025-12-31 (UTC), will the IAEA publicly confirm, or will Iranian state bodies officially announce, that the Isfahan Fuel Enrichment Plant (IFEP) has begun enrichment operations?
background:
Summary of status quo as of 2025-09-30:
- On 2025-06-12, Iran informed the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) that it intended to establish a new enrichment facility named the Isfahan Fuel Enrichment Plant (IFEP) at the Nuclear Reactors Fuel Company (NRFC) site in Esfahan; Iran indicated the related Design Information Questionnaire (DIQ) was available for examination at the facility. The IAEA planned to conduct a design information examination/verification (DIE/DIV) on 2025-06-13, but these activities were cancelled due to the commencement of military attacks that day.
