- “Act of 2 April 2009 on Polish citizenship” refers to the statute governing acquisition and confirmation of Polish citizenship; recognition (uznanie za obywatela polskiego) is the administrative pathway defined in Article 30.
- “Minimum continuous residence” refers to the residency duration parameter stated in the statute’s recognition provision, which currently reads “nieprzerwanie … co najmniej od 3 lat” in Art. 30(1)(1). For resolution, no interpretation of “continuous” beyond the statute’s phrasing is required.
- “Published in Dziennik Ustaw” (promulgated) means the amending act appears in the official Journal of Laws website as an electronic publication; Dziennik Ustaw is the only official source of law for promulgation of Polish statutes.

How this resolves:
- Resolve Yes if, by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, an amending act to the 2009 Polish Citizenship Act has been published in Dziennik Ustaw and the published amendment’s text unambiguously sets the minimum continuous residence for recognition (uznanie za obywatela polskiego) at 10 years (10 lat), replacing the current 3-year threshold, in Article 30(1)(1) or its successor/renumbered equivalent.
- Resolve No if no such amending act has been published in Dziennik Ustaw by the cutoff, or if any enacted changes do not set the recognition minimum at 10 years.

Clarifications:
- Exceptions or alternative pathways (e.g., special rules for certain categories) do not affect resolution provided the general recognition provision’s minimum continuous residence is set at 10 years.
- Passage by the Sejm/Senate without promulgation by the cutoff does not count; only publication in Dziennik Ustaw determines resolution.
- Verification procedure: The resolver will locate the amending act on the Dziennik Ustaw website (https://www.dziennikustaw.gov.pl/) and read the amendment text to confirm that the recognition provision’s minimum period is 10 years. If numbering has changed, the resolver will match the recognition pathway provision by content (the provision governing uznanie za obywatela polskiego) and confirm the 10-year minimum.

question: EU DMA — Will the European Commission adopt at least one additional DMA non‑compliance decision (Article 29(1)) or impose an Article 30 fine against Apple between 2025‑04‑24 and 2025‑12‑31 (UTC)?
background:
Context as of 2025‑10‑01:
- On 23 April 2025, the European Commission adopted its first DMA non‑compliance decisions. It found Apple in breach of the DMA’s anti‑steering obligation and imposed a €500 million fine. Apple was ordered to comply within 60 days, otherwise risking periodic penalty payments. Official Commission press release (IP/25/1085): https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/api/files/document/print/en/ip_25_1085/IP_25_1085_EN.pdf; Commission news page: https://digital-markets-act.ec.europa.eu/commission-finds-apple-and-meta-breach-digital-markets-act-2025-04-23_en.
- Apple is a designated DMA gatekeeper (designation in 2023; iPadOS designated on 29 April 2024), meaning the DMA obligations apply to relevant Apple core platform services. Official gatekeeper overview: https://digital-markets-act.ec.europa.eu/gatekeepers_en.
- The DMA’s enforcement framework relevant to this question:
  • Non‑compliance decision: Where the Commission finds a gatekeeper does not comply with Articles 5, 6, or 7, it may adopt a decision “finding non‑compliance and requiring the gatekeeper to take the necessary measures to ensure compliance,” and may specify measures and set a compliance deadline (DMA Article 29). Full text: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32022R1925.
  • Fines: In a non‑compliance decision, the Commission may impose fines up to 10% of worldwide turnover (or up to 20% for repeated infringements) (DMA Article 30).
  • Periodic penalty payments: The Commission may impose periodic penalty payments up to 5% of average daily worldwide turnover per day to compel compliance with certain decisions (DMA Article 31).
- Additional context in 2025: The Commission has continued DMA compliance engagement, including technical workshops and updates involving Apple and other gatekeepers. Latest news page: https://digital-markets-act.ec.europa.eu/latest-news_en.

Key definitions and scope for this question:
- Digital Markets Act (DMA): Regulation (EU) 2022/1925 on contestable and fair markets in the digital sector; Articles 29–31 govern non‑compliance decisions, fines, and periodic penalty payments.
- Apple: Any Apple group entity that is the addressee of a Commission decision under the DMA. Apple’s gatekeeper status is established by the Commission.
- Non‑compliance decision: A formal Commission decision pursuant to DMA Article 29(1) finding Apple non‑compliant with Articles 5, 6, or 7 and requiring measures to ensure compliance. Decisions that only specify measures without a finding of non‑compliance (e.g., Article 29(2) specification decisions) do NOT count.
- Fine: A pecuniary sanction imposed under DMA Article 30 in a non‑compliance decision (e.g., up to 10% of worldwide turnover). For this question, “fine” excludes periodic penalty payments under Article 31.
- Adopted: The event date is the formal adoption date of the Commission decision (as stated by the Commission in Press Corner or in Official Journal/EUR‑Lex summaries). The 23 April 2025 Apple non‑compliance decision and fine serve as the baseline and are excluded from counting as “additional”.

Why this is high‑entropy and non‑trivial: The Commission has already taken one major enforcement action against Apple in 2025 , and continues active engagement. Whether another formal non‑compliance decision or fine is adopted by year‑end depends on Apple’s subsequent behavior, Commission assessments, and procedural timelines under Articles 29–31. Forecasters can analyze Apple’s compliance changes, Commission signals, and enforcement precedents to inform probabilities.
resolution_criteria:
Timeframe and counting window:
- Eligible events must be adopted between 2025‑04‑24 00:00:00 UTC and 2025‑12‑31 23:59:59 UTC.

Question resolution:
- YES if, within the window above, the European Commission formally adopts at least one of the following against Apple:
  1) A DMA non‑compliance decision pursuant to Article 29(1) finding Apple non‑compliant with Articles 5, 6, or 7; and/or
  2) A fine imposed pursuant to DMA Article 30.
- NO otherwise.

Inclusions and exclusions:
- Inclusion: A single Commission decision can satisfy both criteria (e.g., a non‑compliance decision that also imposes an Article 30 fine). Multiple qualifying decisions or fines count as a single YES outcome.
- Exclusion: Periodic penalty payments under DMA Article 31 alone do NOT count as a “fine.” Decisions that only specify measures or provide guidance without a formal non‑compliance finding (e.g., Article 29(2) specification decisions) do NOT count. Actions not adopted by the Commission (e.g., third‑party reports, media speculation) do NOT count.
- Baseline: The 23 April 2025 Apple decision and associated fine are excluded from counting as “additional”.

Primary resolution sources to check on 2025‑12‑31 (UTC):
- European Commission Press Corner for DMA decisions concerning Apple (search/filter by “Digital Markets Act” and “Apple”). Example baseline source: IP/25/1085 (23 April 2025). Press Corner homepage: https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/home/en.
- European Commission DMA website “Latest news” and case pages (Apple) for official announcements. Latest news: https://digital-markets-act.ec.europa.eu/latest-news_en.
- Official Journal/EUR‑Lex summaries of Commission decisions (C series), which provide adoption dates and legal bases (e.g., the 23 April 2025 decisions). EUR‑Lex: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/.

Adjudication procedure:
- A human resolver will search the sources above. If any qualifying Commission adoption is found with an adoption date in the window, resolve YES; if none is found, resolve NO. If sources disagree, prefer official Commission publications; use EUR‑Lex (OJ) to confirm adoption dates and legal bases.

Resolution date:
- The question will be resolved on or after 2025‑10‑15 and no later than 2025‑12‑31 (UTC), with the final check performed at 2025‑12‑31 23:59:59 UTC.

Notes for edge cases:
- If a qualifying decision is adopted within the window but published later, resolve according to the adoption date stated in Commission or OJ documents.
- If a decision is adopted that includes both specification of measures and a finding of non‑compliance, it counts (because of the non‑compliance finding).
- If the Commission announces intent or preliminary findings without a formal adoption, it does not count.

question: At the Reserve Bank of New Zealand’s November 2025 Monetary Policy Statement, will the Official Cash Rate (OCR) be changed from its prevailing level immediately prior to the announcement?
background:
Context and definitions
- Official Cash Rate (OCR): The OCR is the policy interest rate set by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) to implement monetary policy and maintain price stability. It influences banks’ funding costs and lending/deposit rates. The OCR is set by the RBNZ’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), which reviews it seven times per year. See: https://www.rbnz.govt.nz/monetary-policy/about-monetary-policy/the-official-cash-rate
- Monetary Policy Statement (MPS): The RBNZ publishes an MPS quarterly; the MPS release includes any changes to the OCR and communicates the MPC’s decision at 2pm local time. See: https://www.rbnz.govt.nz/news-and-events/events/2025/november/november-monetary-policy-statement
- Time zone: New Zealand observes New Zealand Daylight Time (NZDT, UTC+13:00) during November. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_Time

Status quo as of 2025-10-01
- Current OCR: On 20 August 2025, the MPC decreased the OCR by 25 basis points to 3.00%. See: https://www.rbnz.govt.nz/hub/news/2025/08/ocr-lowered-to-3-percent
- Next scheduled decisions: The RBNZ indicates that the November 2025 Monetary Policy Statement (and OCR decision) is scheduled for publication at 2pm local time. RBNZ communications specify the November 2025 MPS publication timing at 2pm (local) and indicate that the MPS includes any OCR changes. The RBNZ has also published calendar guidance indicating the November 2025 MPS will occur on Wednesday, 26 November 2025 at 2pm local time. See: https://www.rbnz.govt.nz/news-and-events/events/2025/november/november-monetary-policy-statement and https://www.rbnz.govt.nz/hub/news/2024/06/monetary-policy-announcement-and-financial-stability-report-dates-for-late-2025-and-2026
- Where to verify OCR decisions: The RBNZ maintains a “Past monetary policy decisions” page that lists each decision, the OCR level, and links to the media release and statement (when applicable). This page provides an authoritative record to verify whether the OCR changed at a given meeting. See: https://www.rbnz.govt.nz/monetary-policy/monetary-policy-decisions

Why this question is high-entropy and decision-relevant
- By late 2025, inflation, growth, labour market, and financial stability considerations could plausibly support either holding or adjusting the OCR. The question is binary, tied to a specific, well-publicized event, and is resolvable using official RBNZ publications.
resolution_criteria:
What is being forecast
- Whether, at the RBNZ’s Monetary Policy Statement release that the Bank schedules for Wednesday, 26 November 2025 at 2:00 pm New Zealand Daylight Time (NZDT, UTC+13), the Monetary Policy Committee announces a change (increase or decrease) to the Official Cash Rate (OCR) relative to its prevailing level immediately prior to that announcement.

Definitions
- Official Cash Rate (OCR): The policy rate set by the RBNZ’s Monetary Policy Committee to implement monetary policy and maintain price stability.
- Monetary Policy Statement (MPS): The RBNZ’s quarterly publication that includes the OCR decision and is announced at 2pm local time.
- Prevailing level immediately prior: The OCR in effect as of 1:59:59 pm NZDT on 26 November 2025, as determined by the most recent prior OCR decision published by the RBNZ (typically visible on the “Past monetary policy decisions” page and/or the latest OCR media release).
- Changed: The MPS media release and/or statement explicitly states that the OCR is increased or decreased to a new numerical level (in percent). Any change in the numerical OCR level relative to the prevailing level counts as a change; updates to projections, forward guidance, or other policy tools (e.g., LSAP/FLP) do not count unless they are accompanied by a change to the OCR itself.

Resolution rules
- Resolve YES if the RBNZ’s official publications for the November 2025 MPS (media release and/or the MPS document) state that the OCR is increased or decreased relative to the prevailing level immediately prior to the announcement.
- Resolve NO if those publications state that the OCR remains unchanged.

Primary sources of truth (any one is sufficient; if there is a discrepancy, use the media release first, then the MPS document, then the decisions timeline)
1) The RBNZ media release for the November 2025 MPS (linked from the RBNZ website’s MPS page or the decisions timeline).
2) The November 2025 MPS document on the RBNZ website.
3) The RBNZ “Past monetary policy decisions” page showing the OCR level for the 26 November 2025 decision.

Timing and timezone
- The relevant announcement is the MPS publication scheduled for 2:00 pm NZDT (UTC+13) on Wednesday, 26 November 2025, as per RBNZ communications and calendar guidance. Only the OCR decision associated with this MPS release counts toward resolution.

Edge cases
- If the RBNZ re-schedules the November 2025 MPS but still publishes the quarterly MPS intended for late November 2025 no later than 31 December 2025 (local New Zealand time), resolve based on that publication’s OCR decision at its time of publication.
- If the RBNZ does not publish the Q4 2025 MPS or an equivalent quarterly MPS intended for late November 2025 by 31 December 2025 (local New Zealand time), the market resolves NO (i.e., no OCR change at that event) because no such decision was announced within the resolution window.

Notes for forecasters
- As of 20 August 2025, the OCR stands at 3.00% following a 25 bp cut by the MPC.
- The RBNZ indicates that the MPS is the vehicle for communicating OCR changes and is released at 2pm local time. The decisions timeline provides a quick way to verify whether the OCR level changed at the November 2025 MPS.

question: Will the BEA’s advance estimate show real U.S. GDP growth for Q3 2025 at or above 3.4% (SAAR)?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01 (UTC):
- Recent GDP prints: According to the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), real GDP grew at an annual rate of 3.8% in Q2 2025 in the third estimate. BEA’s third estimate for Q1 2025 showed a 0.5% annualized decline.
- Nowcast for Q3 2025: The Atlanta Fed’s GDPNow model estimated Q3 2025 real GDP growth at 3.9% (seasonally adjusted annual rate, SAAR) as of 2025-09-26; GDPNow is a model-based estimate, not an official forecast.
- Release timing: BEA indicates the Q3 2025 Gross Domestic Product (Advance Estimate) news release is scheduled for October 30, 2025 at 8:30 a.m. EDT.

Definitions and what to look at:
- Real GDP: Inflation-adjusted gross domestic product as published by BEA in its National Income and Product Accounts (see BEA’s overview of GDP: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product). This question will use the value BEA reports for the percent change in real GDP from the preceding quarter, annualized, in the Q3 2025 “Advance Estimate” news release.
- Annual rate / SAAR: BEA reports quarterly percent changes at annual rates unless otherwise specified (i.e., the quarter-over-quarter change expressed at an annualized rate). BEA explicitly notes this practice in its GDP news releases. For general background on SAAR, see also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seasonally_adjusted_annual_rate.
- Advance estimate: The BEA’s first official estimate for a given quarter, released ahead of the “second” and “third” estimates. The Q3 2025 “Advance Estimate” news release is titled along the lines of “Gross Domestic Product, 3rd Quarter 2025 (Advance Estimate)”.

Why the 3.4% threshold? With Q2 2025 at 3.8% (third estimate) and GDPNow at 3.9% for Q3 as of late September, a 3.4% cutoff creates meaningful uncertainty around whether growth will come in above or below the threshold.

Primary source(s) to monitor:
- BEA’s Q3 2025 advance GDP news release (scheduled 2025-10-30 08:30 EDT): look for the sentence in the opening paragraph stating “Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of x.x percent…” and/or the corresponding figure in Table 1 of the release.
resolution_criteria:
Time window and scope:
- Eligible event window: 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC through 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. The question pertains specifically to the BEA’s “Gross Domestic Product, 3rd Quarter 2025 (Advance Estimate)” news release.

Exactly what is measured:
- Use the percent change in real GDP from the preceding quarter at an annual rate (SAAR) as reported by BEA in the Q3 2025 “Advance Estimate” news release. Prefer the value stated in the opening paragraph (e.g., “Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of x.x percent…”). If needed for clarity, the same value in Table 1 (percent change from the preceding quarter, chained dollars, SAAR) in the same news release can be used. BEA reports these quarterly percent changes at annual rates unless otherwise specified.

Resolution rule:
- Resolve Yes if the reported annualized quarter-over-quarter growth rate for real GDP in the Q3 2025 advance estimate is greater than or equal to 3.4%. Resolve No if it is less than 3.4%.

Tie-breaking and revisions:
- Rounding: Use the percentage as published by BEA in the news release (typically to one decimal place). Do not attempt to infer additional precision beyond what BEA reports.
- Revisions: Ignore subsequent “second” or “third” estimates and later comprehensive revisions. If BEA issues an official correction (erratum) to the Q3 2025 advance news release by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, resolve based on the corrected figure.

Primary source of truth:
- BEA’s Q3 2025 advance GDP news release on bea.gov (scheduled for 2025-10-30 08:30 EDT). If, for any reason, BEA does not publish an “Advance Estimate” but does publish another official estimate for Q3 2025 real GDP by 2025-12-31 (e.g., a “Second Estimate”), resolve using the first such official estimate published in 2025 on bea.gov.

question: Will Shein’s IPO result in its shares beginning to trade on a public stock exchange by December 31, 2025 (UTC)?
background:
Context and status quo as of early Q4 2025:
- What is Shein? Shein (SHEIN Group) is a global fast-fashion e-commerce company headquartered in Singapore, operating the SHEIN marketplace/brand and related apparel/accessories businesses.
- Definitions you’ll need: An initial public offering (IPO) is the first sale of a company’s shares to the public, typically underwritten by investment banks and accompanied by a listing on a stock exchange (i.e., the first time the shares are offered to public investors). A stock exchange is an organized marketplace where securities such as shares are bought and sold.
- 2025 listing timeline and regulatory posture:
  - April 2025: Shein secured approval from the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) for a planned London IPO, but still needed approval from China’s securities regulator (CSRC) for an offshore listing under Beijing’s rules; as of that date, the IPO had not occurred.
  - May 2025: Reporting indicated the London IPO attempt stalled due to the lack of CSRC approval; Shein began working toward a Hong Kong listing within 2025.
  - July 2025: Shein confidentially filed a draft prospectus with the Hong Kong exchange and sought a CSRC nod, while keeping London as a preference if an FCA-accepted, CSRC-approved prospectus were possible.
  - August 2025: Shein considered relocating its headquarters back to mainland China to improve prospects of obtaining Beijing’s approval for a Hong Kong IPO; discussions were preliminary.
  - Late September 2025: Reuters’ coverage still described Shein as working toward a Hong Kong listing after the proposed London IPO failed to secure CSRC approval.
- Additional headwinds cited in coverage: Allegations and political scrutiny tied to supply chains; U.S. tariff changes affecting Shein’s de minimis import treatment; and broader geopolitical tensions, all potential influences on timing and valuation.

Taken together, public reporting through late September 2025 describes Shein as actively pursuing an IPO with Hong Kong as the most likely venue, while London remained a possibility contingent on CSRC approval; none of these reports indicate that an IPO had already been completed at those times.

Why this question is forecastable now: Multiple regulatory dependencies (CSRC approval, exchange admission), venue uncertainty (HKEX vs. LSE), and political/trade headwinds create genuine uncertainty about whether Shein can complete an IPO and commence trading by year-end 2025.
resolution_criteria:
Time window and timezone:
- Eligible events must occur between 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, inclusive. All times are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

What counts as “Yes”:
- Resolve Yes if all of the following occur within the time window:
  1) Shein conducts an initial public offering (IPO), defined as the company’s first sale of shares to public investors in connection with admission to trading on a stock exchange.
  2) The issuer’s equity securities (ordinary shares or depositary receipts representing such shares) are admitted to trading on a stock exchange (i.e., an organized marketplace where securities are bought and sold).
  3) Trading in those securities “begins” (i.e., the exchange’s official communication indicates admission/commencement of dealings, such as “admission to trading” or “dealing in the shares commences,” and the first trading session opens) within the time window. 

What does not count:
- The following do NOT satisfy this market:
  - A direct listing without a primary share sale (no IPO).
  - A merger with or acquisition by a SPAC (de-SPAC), reverse takeover, or any transaction where the resulting listing is not the result of Shein’s own IPO.
  - A priced IPO where the first day of trading is scheduled outside the time window (e.g., priced on Dec 31 UTC but trading starts Jan 1 UTC).

Who “Shein” refers to:
- “Shein” means SHEIN Group (the corporate parent of the SHEIN fast-fashion business) or any successor holding company identified in the IPO prospectus as the top-level parent that directly or indirectly consolidates substantially all of Shein’s operating business (e.g., the SHEIN e-commerce marketplace and related apparel/accessory operations).

Primary resolution sources (examples):
- Official exchange notices confirming admission and first day of dealings/trading, such as:
  - HKEX New Listing Information (Main Board): https://www2.hkexnews.hk/New-Listings/New-Listing-Information/Main-Board?sc_lang=en
  - HKEX Application Proof/PHIP index (for corroboration of issuer identity and listing documents): https://www1.hkexnews.hk/app/appindex.html
  - London Stock Exchange Regulatory News Service (RNS) admission notices: https://www.londonstockexchange.com/news
- Issuer press releases on SHEIN Group’s newsroom: https://www.sheingroup.com/newsroom/corporate-news/press-releases/
- Corroboration from major wire services (e.g., Reuters), which have extensively covered Shein’s listing process.

How the resolver will decide on Dec 31, 2025:
- The resolver will check whether any official exchange notice (HKEX, LSE, or another recognized stock exchange) shows that trading in Shein’s equity securities commenced within the specified UTC time window, and confirm issuer identity matches the “Who Shein refers to” definition. If such a notice exists, and at least one of the above corroborating sources reports the debut, the market resolves Yes. Otherwise, the market resolves No.

Edge cases and clarifications:
- If trading begins and is subsequently suspended or halted, it still counts as Yes provided trading commenced within the time window per the exchange’s official notice.
- Dual listings: If Shein lists on multiple exchanges, the first date and time trading begins on any one exchange within the window controls.
- Depositary receipts: If the IPO is executed via depositary receipts representing Shein’s equity and those receipts are listed/trading as part of the IPO, it counts.
- If the issuer reorganizes (e.g., inserts a new holding company) solely to facilitate the IPO, it still counts as Yes so long as the post-reorg parent matches the “Who Shein refers to” definition and the transaction otherwise meets the IPO and trading criteria.

question: Will the EU formally endorse and commit to implementing a “Reparations Loan” to Ukraine using immobilised Russian sovereign asset cash balances (via an EU- or G7-backed SPV) between 2025-10-01 and 2025-12-31 (UTC)?
background:
Summary of the concept and current status as of 2025-10-01:
- The European Commission has outlined a plan often termed a “Reparations Loan” to fund Ukraine in 2026–2027 by leveraging cash balances accrued from immobilised Russian central bank securities held in Europe, particularly at Euroclear in Belgium. Under the plan, cash balances would be transferred to an EU- or G7-owned special purpose vehicle (SPV), while Euroclear would receive EU-backed zero-coupon bonds or a tailored debt instrument to cover legal risk; Ukraine would only repay the loan if Russia pays war reparations in a future settlement.
- Reuters’ detailed explainer reports roughly €210bn of frozen Russian sovereign assets held in Europe, with about €185bn at Euroclear and around €175bn of those having become cash as securities matured; after first covering the existing G7 ERA loan (~€45bn), officials discuss an additional loan capacity of ~€130–€140bn for the new Reparations Loan, subject to an IMF needs assessment for 2026–27. Euronews similarly describes a cash pot of ~€176bn at Euroclear (with ~€10bn expected), a total loan framework up to €185bn (of which ~€140bn would be available after backing the €45bn G7 credit), and the Commission’s concept of a zero-interest loan to Ukraine with repayment contingent on reparations.
- Euroclear’s H1 2025 press release states that as of end-June 2025, €194bn of sanctioned Russian assets were on Euroclear Bank’s balance sheet, and interest on those cash balances was ~€2.7bn in H1 2025. This contextualises the scale of immobilised assets and proceeds.
- As of Oct 1, 2025, major EU leaders have signaled support in principle but highlighted legal and risk-sharing concerns. Reuters reports leaders planned to discuss legal aspects at the European Council meeting on Oct 23–24, with Belgium, France, and Luxembourg insisting on strong guarantees given asset location and litigation risk; Denmark, Sweden, the Netherlands, and Germany expressed varying degrees of support, while the EU’s top diplomat noted not all member states were fully on board; G7 participation in guarantees was to be discussed as well. AP similarly notes a proposed loan size around €140bn, positions from leaders (including caution on international law and guarantees), and that the plan aims to use cash balances without outright confiscation of sovereign assets.
- Politically and legally, multiple reports emphasise the design seeks to avoid confiscation (a red line for many governments and the ECB) while still mobilising cash balances for Ukraine via an SPV, with risks to be collectively guaranteed by EU (and potentially non-EU G7) governments.

Key definitions and helpful references for forecasters:
- European Council: the body of EU heads of state or government. See official overview: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/european-council-and-council-of-the-eu/
- European Council conclusions: the formal document adopted at the end of each European Council meeting stating the Council’s political positions and decisions. See: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/european-council/conclusions/
- European Commission Communication (COM document): an official Commission document published on EUR-Lex and/or the Commission’s “Press corner”, often outlining adopted policy/legislative initiatives. See EUR-Lex document types: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/content/tools/TableOfSectors/types_of_documents_in_eurlex.html
- Special purpose vehicle (SPV): a legally distinct entity used to isolate financial risk. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special-purpose_entity
- Euroclear: a Brussels-based central securities depository. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euroclear
- “Frozen”/“immobilised” Russian sovereign assets: Russian central bank securities and related balances restricted under sanctions; figures and mechanics described in Reuters and Euronews reports above.

Why this is forecastable with non-trivial uncertainty:
- There is momentum and high-level political support to discuss the Reparations Loan in late October 2025, yet significant legal, institutional, and guarantee-sharing hurdles remain, and unanimity issues around sanction renewals could complicate timelines. A formal endorsement (by European Council conclusions) or a Commission commitment via an adopted Communication/Decision is plausible but far from assured by year-end, creating high entropy.
resolution_criteria:
Time window and timezone:
- Eligible actions must occur between 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Outcome definition:
- Resolve “Yes” if, within the time window, either of the following is satisfied:
  1) European Council conclusions explicitly endorse proceeding with the EU “Reparations Loan” concept or an equivalent SPV structure that uses cash balances from immobilised/frozen Russian sovereign assets to fund a loan to Ukraine, with Ukraine’s repayment contingent on future war reparations. “Explicitly endorse proceeding” means the conclusions unambiguously support the EU implementing the plan (e.g., by stating that the European Council endorses/supports/mandates/decides to proceed with such a loan/SPV or invites/mandates the Commission to prepare/establish it for financing Ukraine in 2026–27). Mere calls to “explore”, “study”, or “consider” options without endorsing proceeding do NOT count.
  2) The European Commission publishes an adopted Communication (COM document) or an adopted Commission Decision (a formal College adoption), which explicitly commits the Commission to implement the scheme (e.g., establishing the SPV and/or initiating the transfer of cash balances from Euroclear or equivalent custodians, backed by EU guarantees), beyond exploratory or consultation papers. A press release in the Commission “Press corner” stating that “the Commission has adopted” such a Communication/Decision also suffices if it clearly describes the mechanics (loan to Ukraine backed by cash balances from immobilised Russian sovereign assets and repayment contingent on reparations).

What qualifies as “equivalent SPV structure”:
- Any EU- or EU+G7-owned SPV arrangement that: (a) sources funding from cash balances accrued from immobilised/frozen Russian sovereign assets (not outright confiscating the assets); (b) extends an interest-free or zero-interest loan to Ukraine; and (c) specifies that Ukraine’s repayment obligation is contingent upon Russia paying war reparations. This captures the variants reported by Reuters and Euronews.

What does NOT count:
- Council of the EU (ministerial) conclusions, informal statements by individual leaders, speeches, interviews, op-eds, media leaks, non-adopted drafts, feasibility studies, or generic language about “supporting Ukraine” that lacks explicit endorsement to proceed with the Reparations Loan/SPV mechanics described above.

Sources of truth for resolution:
- For European Council conclusions: the official conclusions published on consilium.europa.eu for European Council meetings held in the window (e.g., Oct 23–24 or any subsequent meeting in 2025). See: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/european-council/conclusions/
- For Commission actions: the European Commission “Press corner” and EUR-Lex entries of adopted Commission Communications/Decisions (COM documents and Commission Decisions) in the window. See: https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner and https://eur-lex.europa.eu/ (document type overview: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/content/tools/TableOfSectors/types_of_documents_in_eurlex.html)

Context citations supporting the defined mechanics and current status:
- Detailed plan mechanics, asset amounts, cash-balance transfer to an SPV, zero-coupon bonds to Euroclear, loan repayment contingent on reparations: Reuters explainer ; corroborating mechanics and amounts: Euronews.
- Asset scale at Euroclear and interest proceeds: Euroclear H1 2025 press release.
- Leaders’ positions, legal concerns, and planned European Council discussion dates: Reuters Oct 1 status ; summary of positions and legal cautions: AP.

Resolution notes:
- The resolver should locate the relevant European Council conclusions or Commission documents/press releases in the specified window and check for explicit endorsement/commitment that matches the mechanics defined above. If neither criterion is met by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, resolve “No”.

Rationale for this framing:
- The event is significant, plausibly time-bound to late-2025 discussions, and depends on legal/institutional hurdles and cross-national guarantees, making outcomes genuinely uncertain and researchable.

question: UK consumer confidence: Will the NIQ/GfK Overall Index Score for December 2025 be at least -18?
background:
Scope and definitions
- What this question measures: The “Overall Index Score” (also called the headline score) reported in the monthly UK NIQ/GfK Consumer Confidence Barometer press release for December 2025. NIQ/GfK’s press materials consistently refer to the composite headline as the Overall Index Score and publish it as an integer (e.g., -17, -18) alongside the component measures.
- What consumer confidence is: Consumer confidence is an economic indicator reflecting consumers’ optimism about the economy and their personal financial situation; higher confidence is associated with greater spending, lower confidence with more saving (overview: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consumer_confidence).
- What the NIQ/GfK UK Consumer Confidence Barometer is: A long-running monthly survey of UK adults tracking sentiment on personal finances, the general economic situation, and major purchases. It has provided monthly snapshots since 1974 and is currently published by NIQ/GfK, powered by NIM. Recent NIQ/GfK releases describe the survey sample as approximately 2,002 UK adults aged 16+ with quotas to be nationally representative and note the Overall Index Score is calculated from underlying data to two decimal places but reported as an integer.
- Components: The Overall Index Score is derived from five measures NIQ/GfK publish monthly: Personal Financial Situation (last 12 months), Personal Financial Situation (next 12 months), General Economic Situation (last 12 months), General Economic Situation (next 12 months), and the Major Purchase Index. The Savings Index is discussed in releases but is not part of the Overall Index Score.

Status quo as of 2025-09-30
- Recent headline readings in 2025:
  • June: -18 
  • July: -19 
  • August: -17 
  • September: -19 
- Publication schedule: NIQ/GfK list press release dates for late 2025 as September 19, October 24, November 21, and December 19, indicating the December figure will be available before year-end.

Why this threshold and timeframe
- The headline score has been range-bound in 2025 around -20 to -15; setting an inclusive threshold at -18 targets an area of genuine uncertainty given the recent glide path and volatility.
- The December 2025 press release is scheduled for December 19, 2025, ensuring timely resolution before December 31, 2025.

Links and sources forecasters may consult
- NIQ/GfK UK Consumer Confidence press releases (NIQ News Center): These pages publish the monthly headline (Overall Index Score) and components, with clear timestamps and methodology notes. Examples for 2025 months cited above: June (-18), July (-19), August (-17), September (-19).
- Product overview: GfK’s Consumer Confidence Barometer product page describes the UK survey, monthly cadence, and component measures.
- General concept: Wikipedia entry for consumer confidence provides a definition and context (link above).
resolution_criteria:
How this resolves
- Event window: Publications between October 15, 2025 00:00 UTC and December 31, 2025 23:59 UTC.
- Primary source of truth: The official NIQ/GfK UK Consumer Confidence Barometer press release for December 2025 on NIQ’s News Center, scheduled for December 19, 2025. Resolve Yes if, in that press release, the “Overall Index Score” (headline score) for December 2025 is greater than or equal to -18; resolve No otherwise.
- Figure to use: Use the integer Overall Index Score exactly as published in the December 2025 press release (do not re-compute or re-round from underlying decimals). NIQ/GfK note the headline is calculated from data to two decimal places but presented as an integer; rely on the presented integer.
- Fallbacks if the December press release is inaccessible by the resolution deadline:
  1) Use the NIQ/GfK UK Consumer Confidence press page or News Center item that lists the December 2025 Overall Index Score (e.g., the monthly series page for 2025 releases). If multiple official NIQ/GfK pages exist, prefer the one explicitly titled for December 2025.
  2) If no official NIQ/GfK publication is accessible by the deadline, adjudicate using credible mainstream wire-service reporting (e.g., Reuters, AP) that clearly states the December 2025 UK NIQ/GfK Overall Index Score, with preference given to reports that cite NIQ/GfK directly. If credible sources conflict, prefer NIQ/GfK’s figures.
- Geographic scope: United Kingdom (UK) survey only as defined by NIQ/GfK’s Consumer Confidence Barometer.
- Ambiguity handling: If an official correction to the December 2025 Overall Index Score is posted on NIQ/GfK before December 31, 2025 23:59 UTC, use the corrected figure; corrections after the deadline are ignored.
- Out-of-scope: Any sub-index (e.g., Savings Index) or non-UK consumer confidence measures are excluded from resolution.

question: Will the U.S. seasonally adjusted U-3 unemployment rate for November 2025 be at least 4.6%?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01: The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported the seasonally adjusted national unemployment rate at 4.3% for August 2025. The BLS “Employment Situation” (monthly jobs report) for November 2025 is scheduled to be released on December 5, 2025 (date only; time not needed for resolution).

Key definitions and scope:
- Unemployment rate (U-3): The official unemployment rate used by BLS, defined as the number of unemployed people as a percentage of the labor force; calculated as (Unemployed ÷ Labor Force) × 100. BLS definitions for “unemployed,” “labor force,” and the unemployment rate are provided in the Current Population Survey (CPS) glossary page: https://www.bls.gov/cps/definitions.htm.
- Civilian labor force: All people age 16 and older who are classified as either employed or unemployed (per CPS definitions on the same page).
- Seasonally adjusted: The question concerns the seasonally adjusted national unemployment rate as labeled in BLS’s Employment Situation release tables. The rate is taken from the “Seasonally adjusted” column in Table A-1 of the Employment Situation news release (“Household data”) page: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.t01.htm.
- National series reference: The BLS data series LNS14000000 corresponds to the seasonally adjusted national unemployment rate for persons 16 years and over: https://data.bls.gov/timeseries/LNS14000000. This is provided as a reference to the underlying series; the authoritative resolution source is the Employment Situation news release Table A-1.

Status quo and why this is interesting:
- The latest available headline rate cited above is 4.3% for August 2025, indicating modest labor market slack relative to earlier periods. Whether the rate ticks up to at least 4.6% in November 2025 is uncertain, making the threshold nontrivial.
- The Employment Situation follows a regular cadence, with the November 2025 report scheduled for December 5, 2025, enabling resolution well before December 31, 2025.
resolution_criteria:
Resolution window and time zone:
- Eligible data period: This question pertains specifically to the CPS reference month November 2025.
- Resolution determination will be made based on the figure published by BLS no later than 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025.

Exactly what is being measured:
- “U.S. seasonally adjusted U-3 unemployment rate for November 2025” means the seasonally adjusted unemployment rate for “Total, 16 years and over” (national scope) as published in the BLS Employment Situation news release, Table A-1 (“Household data”) for November 2025. Source page: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.t01.htm. Definitions for “unemployment rate,” “unemployed,” “labor force,” and U-3 are per BLS CPS: https://www.bls.gov/cps/definitions.htm.

Question and threshold:
- Resolve Yes if the BLS Employment Situation news release for November 2025 reports a seasonally adjusted national unemployment rate (U-3) of greater than or equal to 4.6% in Table A-1 for “Total, 16 years and over.” Resolve No otherwise.

Source of record and handling of revisions:
- Primary source of record: The November 2025 Employment Situation Summary/Table A-1 on bls.gov. The release is scheduled for December 5, 2025 (date only; time not required for resolution).
- Use the value in the initial November 2025 Employment Situation news release as posted on bls.gov. If BLS issues an official correction to that November 2025 Table A-1 value before 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, the corrected value supersedes the initial value.

Notes for resolvers:
- For context, the August 2025 unemployment rate was 4.3% per BLS’s Employment Situation news release narrative. This does not directly affect resolution but provides recent baseline conditions.

All claims above sourced from BLS materials as cited: August 2025 rate ; CPS definitions ; Table A-1 structure/scope ; national series reference ; November 2025 release schedule/date.

question: Between 2025-09-25 and 2025-12-31 (UTC), will a U.S.-based TikTok joint venture close such that ByteDance and its affiliates own <20% of the U.S. entity that operates TikTok’s U.S. application?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- On 2025-09-25, the White House issued a presidential action describing a framework under which TikTok’s U.S. application would be operated by a new U.S.-based joint venture (the “U.S. TikTok JV”), majority-owned and controlled by U.S. persons, with ByteDance Ltd. and its affiliates holding less than 20% of the JV upon completion. The action also directed the Attorney General not to enforce the relevant Act for 120 days to permit the contemplated divestiture to be completed. A contemporaneous White House fact sheet likewise states ByteDance will hold less than 20% of the new U.S. joint venture and outlines JV governance and security controls (e.g., Oracle-hosted U.S. data environment).
- Separately, on 2025-09-16, a presidential action further extended the enforcement delay for the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (the “Act”) until 2025-12-16, directing DOJ to take no action to enforce the Act or impose penalties during the specified delay periods.

What forecasters should know:
- The 2025-09-25 presidential action describes a “qualified divestiture” framework, under which implementation agreements are to be executed and the transaction closed so that U.S. persons control the U.S. TikTok JV and ByteDance’s residual stake is <20%.
- A determination or public confirmation by U.S. authorities (e.g., White House/DOJ/CFIUS) that TikTok has undergone a “qualified divestiture” per the 2025-09-25 order would be strong evidence that the JV has closed consistent with the <20% ByteDance ownership condition specified in the presidential materials.

Key definitions and references (for clarity):
- “U.S. TikTok JV”: the new joint-venture company based in the United States that will operate TikTok’s U.S. application as described by the White House on 2025-09-25. See also general joint venture background: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_venture.
- “ByteDance and its affiliates”: ByteDance Ltd. and any “affiliate” of ByteDance (affiliate has the meaning in 17 CFR 240.12b-2: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-240.12b-2).
- “Owns” / “ownership percentage”: assessed on a beneficial ownership basis consistent with 17 CFR 240.13d-3 (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-240.13d-3), including any securities exercisable or convertible within 60 days. For this market question, the practical test is what the authoritative closing source (defined below) states regarding ByteDance’s percentage. If both a precise percentage and a clear statement that the stake is below 20% are provided, either suffices.
- “Close,” “closed,” or “completed”: the transaction has been consummated (i.e., all closing conditions satisfied and effectiveness occurred), as evidenced by an official closing announcement or filing by one of the defined authoritative sources below.
- Time zone: All dates/times in this question are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
- Eligible window for events: 2025-09-25 00:00:00 UTC through 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Context on resolution sources:
- Presidential actions and fact sheets are posted on whitehouse.gov at durable URLs (e.g., the 2025-09-25 presidential action and fact sheet) and will be accepted for determining whether an official “qualified divestiture” determination has been made and/or the transaction has closed consistent with the specified ownership.
- The 2025-09-16 enforcement-delay action remains relevant background regarding DOJ non-enforcement timing through 2025-12-16.
resolution_criteria:
This resolves based on publicly available information posted no later than 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Question: Between 2025-09-25 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, will there be a confirmed closing of the transaction to form and/or transfer operations to a U.S.-based TikTok joint venture such that ByteDance Ltd. and its affiliates own less than 20.00% of the U.S. entity that operates TikTok’s U.S. application?

Resolution rules:
- Resolve “Yes” if, within the eligible window, at least one of the following authoritative sources confirms that the transaction has closed (using language such as “closed,” “completed,” or “consummated”) and that ByteDance’s ownership in the U.S. TikTok JV is strictly less than 20% (i.e., <20.00%):
  1) An official press release or transaction closing announcement posted on the websites of TikTok, ByteDance, or the U.S. TikTok JV (if named/created), or an SEC filing by a public company party to the transaction that discloses closing and ownership percentages (e.g., Form 8-K, 6-K, or similar).
  2) A U.S. Government announcement (e.g., White House presidential action/fact sheet, DOJ or CFIUS public statement) explicitly stating that the transaction has closed consistent with the 2025-09-25 “qualified divestiture” framework under which ByteDance’s ownership is <20%.
  3) Major wire-service reporting (Reuters, AP) or top-tier outlets (e.g., WSJ, Bloomberg, FT) that explicitly cite one of the sources in 1) or 2) above, and relay both the occurrence of closing and the ByteDance <20% ownership.

- Resolve “No” if by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC there is no such confirmation, or if available authoritative sources confirm closing but indicate ByteDance’s ownership is greater than or equal to 20.00% at closing.

Clarifications:
- If the White House/DOJ/CFIUS publicly determines that TikTok has undergone a “qualified divestiture” per the 2025-09-25 presidential action, that will suffice for “Yes,” because the presidential materials specify ByteDance will hold <20% of the U.S. JV under the qualified divestiture framework.
- “Ownership” refers to beneficial ownership and any direct/indirect equity interest, including via instruments exercisable/convertible within 60 days, consistent with 17 CFR 240.13d-3. However, for resolution, the percentage explicitly stated by the authoritative closing source governs.
- The U.S. entity (“U.S. TikTok JV”) is the new U.S.-based joint venture that will operate TikTok’s U.S. application as described by the White House on 2025-09-25.
- Non-binding agreements, letters of intent, partial step completions (e.g., only regulatory approval without closing), or speculative media reports without a qualifying source do not count.

Primary resolution sources (non-exhaustive):
- White House Presidential Actions and Fact Sheets (e.g., “Saving TikTok While Protecting National Security” on 2025-09-25; related fact sheet).
- DOJ or CFIUS public statements or notices.
- Corporate press releases posted on official websites of TikTok, ByteDance, or the U.S. TikTok JV; relevant SEC filings by parties to the transaction.

Edge cases:
- If multiple sources conflict, prefer primary official sources (White House/DOJ/CFIUS; company filings/press releases). If still conflicting, the market administrator will wait up to seven calendar days for clarifying official statements before resolving.
- If the closing occurs within the window but is posted publicly after the deadline, it does not count. Conversely, filings/announcements posted within the window that clearly state closing has occurred within the window do count.

Time zone: All times UTC.

Citations for background claims: presidential action describing the JV structure, <20% ByteDance ownership, and 120-day DOJ non-enforcement (2025-09-25) ; White House fact sheet reiterating <20% ownership and JV governance and security controls ; enforcement delay extension to 2025-12-16 (2025-09-16).

question: Will Russia’s nationwide ban on exports of automotive gasoline be in force at 23:59 Moscow Time (UTC+3) on December 31, 2025?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-09-30: Russia has extended a temporary ban on exports of automotive gasoline through December 31, 2025, as part of measures to stabilize its domestic fuel market amid shortages linked to Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian refineries. Multiple reports state that the extension applies to all exporters, including producers, and was implemented via government decree on September 30, 2025. In parallel, Russia announced partial restrictions on diesel exports that target resellers but exempt direct producers, highlighting the government’s willingness to fine-tune measures by product and exporter type. Reuters and other outlets report gasoline shortages and rationing in several regions, including Crimea, which provide the context for these export limits. 

Policy timeline relevant to gasoline exports in 2024–2025:
- 2025-02-20: Russia extended a gasoline export ban covering March 1–August 31, 2025, with exemptions for producers and certain intergovernmental deliveries; the measure was aimed at stabilizing domestic prices and supply.
- 2025-08-27: Government Decree No. 1294 introduced a temporary export ban for automotive gasoline from September 1 to October 31, 2025; it applied to all exporters including producers for September, with restrictions to be lifted for producers in October.
- 2025-09-30: The government extended the gasoline export ban until December 31, 2025, and clarified that it applies to all exporters, including direct producers; this was conveyed via government communications and covered by major outlets. 

Where government decrees are published: Government decrees (Postanovleniya) are published on the official legal portal (publication.pravo.gov.ru) and summarized on government.ru. For example, Government Decree No. 229 (26 Feb 2025) “On the introduction of a temporary ban on the export of commodity gasoline from the Russian Federation” appears on the official legal portal, illustrating the publication channel resolvers should check. 

Definitions and clarifications used for this question:
- Automotive gasoline: A refined petroleum product used as motor fuel for spark-ignition engines. See Gasoline (general): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gasoline. In Russian government communications, the term "автомобильный бензин" (automotive gasoline) is used; for the purposes of resolution, we rely on the product descriptions in the relevant government decree(s) in force at resolution time rather than any colloquial usage.
- Export: The shipment of goods from the Russian Federation to another country. See Export: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Export.
- Government decree/order: A normative legal act of the Government of the Russian Federation (e.g., Postanovlenie) that is legally binding and officially published on publication.pravo.gov.ru and/or government.ru.
- In force: Legally effective—i.e., the validity period stated in the decree includes the resolution time.
- Nationwide gasoline export ban (as used in this question): A government decree or equivalent normative act that prohibits exports of automotive gasoline from the entire territory of the Russian Federation to foreign destinations and applies to all exporters, including producers. Exemptions explicitly enumerated in the decree (e.g., intergovernmental deliveries) may exist; their presence does not negate that the decree is a “nationwide … export ban.” Measures that prohibit exports only for resellers/traders while exempting producers do not count as a nationwide export ban for this question.
- Timezone: Moscow Time (MSK) is UTC+3. See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_in_Russia.

Why this is forecastable and non-trivial: As of 2025-09-30, the government states the ban runs through end-2025, but Russian authorities have repeatedly adjusted scope, length, and exemptions in response to evolving domestic supply conditions and refinery outage dynamics. It is plausible they could either maintain the blanket ban through year-end or lift/modify it before then.
resolution_criteria:
Resolution date/time: 2025-12-31 at 23:59 Moscow Time (MSK; UTC+3).

Question start date: upon question posting; only the state of policy at the resolution timestamp matters.

Resolve Yes if, at the resolution time, there is a valid, in-force Government of the Russian Federation decree (Postanovlenie) or equivalent normative act that: (a) explicitly prohibits exports of automotive gasoline from Russia, (b) applies nationwide, and (c) applies to all exporters, including producers. The decree may include enumerated exemptions (e.g., intergovernmental deliveries); their presence does not negate “ban” status.

Resolve No if, at the resolution time, no such in-force decree exists (e.g., it expired or was revoked), or if the only restrictions in force do not constitute a nationwide ban applying to all exporters (for example, restrictions limited to resellers/traders while exempting producers).

Primary resolution sources to check at resolution time:
1) The official legal portal publication.pravo.gov.ru for the relevant decree(s) being in force on 2025-12-31 (example of decree publication channel: Government Decree No. 229 dated 26 Feb 2025 appears on this portal ).
2) Government.ru for official summaries and document pages indicating the validity of the September 30, 2025 extension through December 31, 2025 (e.g., Government communications on 2025-09-30 stating the extension applies to all exporters ).

Secondary confirmation (if primary sources are inaccessible at resolution time): Reputable wire services (e.g., Reuters energy desk) reporting on the status of Russia’s gasoline export policy at year-end.

Resolver instructions:
- Step 1: Search publication.pravo.gov.ru and government.ru/docs for decrees adopted on/after 2025-09-30 that govern export of automotive gasoline. Confirm whether a decree extending the ban through 2025 remains in force at 23:59 MSK on 2025-12-31.
- Step 2: Verify whether the decree’s scope applies to all exporters, including producers. If the in-force measure at resolution time exempts producers (i.e., it is limited to resellers), resolve No.
- Step 3: If official portals are down or inaccessible, use Reuters coverage to confirm whether the ban remains in force for all exporters at year-end.

Notes:
- Illustrative context for this policy (not itself determinative of resolution): The September 2025 extension and concurrent diesel restrictions were justified by shortages and refinery outages caused by Ukrainian drone attacks, and gasoline rationing was observed in Crimea.
- If multiple overlapping decrees exist, resolve based on whether any in-force decree meeting the criteria (nationwide, applies to all exporters, explicitly bans export of automotive gasoline) is active at the resolution time. If all such decrees expire/are revoked or only narrower measures remain, resolve No.

question: Will cumulative global insured losses from natural catastrophes reach at least USD 150 billion by 2025-11-30?
background: Context as of 2025-09-22: The insurance industry has seen persistently high natural-catastrophe insured losses in recent years. According to the provided artifact, global insured losses reached about USD 100 billion in H1 2025 and Swiss Re projects full-year insured losses on trend to ~USD 145 billion, with the possibility of much higher losses in peak years. This question targets whether cumulative year-to-date (YTD) insured losses will hit or exceed USD 150 billion by November 30, 2025, a threshold chosen to create genuine uncertainty (above trend but below extreme scenarios). "Insured losses" means losses covered by insurance and reinsurance policies (claims paid and reserves) attributable to natural-catastrophe events; excludes total economic losses/protection gap. Forecasters should monitor monthly/quarterly catastrophe recap publications that report YTD insured losses and major events (e.g., Aon Global Catastrophe Recap, Munich Re NatCatSERVICE releases, Swiss Re Institute sigma/insights). question: By 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, will Smartmatic obtain a court-entered monetary damages judgment or a filed settlement agreement requiring payment from Mike Lindell and/or My Pillow, Inc. in D. Minn. case 0:22-cv-00098?
background:
Case context and status quo (as of 2025-10-01):
- Litigation: Smartmatic USA Corp., Smartmatic International Holding B.V., and SGO Corporation Limited v. Michael J. Lindell and My Pillow, Inc., U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota, No. 0:22-cv-00098. In late September 2025, the court granted Smartmatic partial summary judgment and ruled that Mike Lindell defamed Smartmatic, while leaving the questions of actual malice and damages for further proceedings [afb482; 3fbe9f; 92ca60; 8561e8].
- Recent orders: On September 26, 2025, the court granted Smartmatic’s motion for partial summary judgment, denied defendants’ summary judgment motion, ruled on several expert motions, and directed Smartmatic to file a proposed order for permanent injunctive relief by December 1, 2025, with defendants’ objections due by December 31, 2025. On July 25, 2025, the court granted Smartmatic’s supplemental fee petition related to a contempt motion; this was a fee award rather than a damages award.
- What remains: As of October 1, 2025, no damages have been awarded; actual malice and the amount of any damages remain to be determined (e.g., by a jury). Reporting indicates Smartmatic is seeking nine-figure damages, and that damages had not yet been awarded at the time of the late-September rulings [3fbe9f; 92ca60; 8561e8]. The docket does not reflect any monetary damages judgment or a filed settlement agreement to date.

Key terms and definitions to avoid ambiguity:
- Monetary damages judgment: A judgment entered under Federal Rules of Civil Procedure 54 and 58 that awards monetary damages (compensatory and/or punitive) to any Smartmatic plaintiff against Michael J. Lindell and/or My Pillow, Inc. See FRCP 54 (Judgment; Costs) and FRCP 58 (Entering Judgment) on the U.S. Courts website; for general background on civil judgment, see the Wikipedia entry for “Judgment (law).”
- Filed settlement agreement requiring payment: A written settlement agreement filed on the docket of case No. 0:22-cv-00098 in the District of Minnesota that obligates Michael J. Lindell and/or My Pillow, Inc. to pay money to any Smartmatic plaintiff. A mere stipulation of dismissal without an attached agreement or without explicit payment terms does not qualify. For background on settlement agreements and Rule 41 dismissals, see FRCP 41(a)(1)(A)(ii).
- Exclusions: The following do not count as “monetary damages judgment or filed settlement agreement requiring payment” for this question: attorney’s fee awards, cost awards, sanctions, or contempt-related fee awards (even if monetary); injunctive or declaratory relief; proposed orders; jury verdicts not reduced to a judgment under FRCP 58; and confidential settlements not filed on the docket. These exclusions are included to ensure clear, documentable resolution on the public docket.
- Parties: “Smartmatic” refers to any of the three plaintiffs in this case (Smartmatic USA Corp.; Smartmatic International Holding B.V.; SGO Corporation Limited). “Mike Lindell” refers to Michael J. Lindell. “MyPillow” refers to My Pillow, Inc..

Why this is forecast-relevant now: The court has established defamation but left actual malice and damages to later proceedings, creating genuine uncertainty about whether a damages judgment or filed settlement will appear on the docket by year-end 2025. The court has also set briefing around injunctive relief into December, which may affect timing for any damages proceedings or settlement dynamics [afb482; 3fbe9f; 92ca60; 8561e8].

question: Will the UK HPI show an annual price change of at least 3.0% for August 2025?
background:
Overview and status quo as of 2025-09-30
- What is being measured: The UK House Price Index (UK HPI) is a National Statistic that measures changes in the prices of residential properties across the United Kingdom. It is jointly produced by HM Land Registry, the Office for National Statistics (ONS), Registers of Scotland, and Land & Property Services Northern Ireland. The index uses a hedonic regression methodology and is published monthly on GOV.UK at 09:30. Estimates for the most recent months are provisional and subject to revision. The ‘annual’ percentage change compares prices with the same month 12 months earlier.
- Where the key figure appears: The monthly “UK House Price Index summary: [month year]” page on GOV.UK reports the UK-level “annual price change” (also described as “average UK house price annual inflation”), which is the 12‑month (year-over-year) percentage change for that month.
- Release timing for this question: The August 2025 UK HPI is scheduled to be published at 09:30 (UTC) on Wednesday 22 October 2025 within the UK HPI reports collection on GOV.UK.
- Current market context: In the most recent available summary, “UK House Price Index summary: July 2025,” the UK-level annual house price inflation is reported as 2.8% (provisional estimate) in the 12 months to July 2025, down from a revised 3.6% in the 12 months to June 2025. This page confirms both the phrasing and placement of the UK-level annual figure.

Why this threshold: Setting the threshold at 3.0% centers the question near recently observed values (2.8% in July 2025, provisional), aiming for non-trivial uncertainty around whether August 2025 will meet or exceed that level.

Primary sources and where to check
- UK House Price Index: reports collection (GOV.UK): https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/uk-house-price-index-reports — includes the monthly summary page for August 2025 and notes that August 2025 is scheduled for 09:30 on 22 October 2025.
- About the UK House Price Index (GOV.UK): https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/about-the-uk-house-price-index/about-the-uk-house-price-index — defines the UK HPI, publishers, methodology, revision policy, and that the ‘annual’ change is the 12‑month percentage change.
- Example of the monthly summary format and phrasing: “UK House Price Index summary: July 2025” (published 17 September 2025), which shows how the UK-level annual figure is presented.
resolution_criteria:
Question
- Resolve “Yes” if the UK-level annual price change (year-over-year percentage change) for August 2025 reported on the GOV.UK page “UK House Price Index summary: August 2025” is greater than or equal to 3.0%.
- Resolve “No” otherwise.

Definitions and scope
- UK House Price Index (UK HPI): The official National Statistic measuring residential property price changes across the UK, jointly produced by HM Land Registry, the ONS, Registers of Scotland, and Land & Property Services Northern Ireland; calculated using a hedonic regression method; published monthly at 09:30 on GOV.UK. See “About the UK House Price Index”.
- UK-level: The United Kingdom aggregate reported by the UK HPI (i.e., not any single nation or region).
- Annual price change / annual inflation (YoY): The percentage change in the average UK house price compared with the same month 12 months earlier (the 12‑month change). This is the figure labeled on the monthly summary page as “annual price change” or “average UK house price annual inflation.” We will use the figure as displayed on the August 2025 summary page.
- Reference month: “August 2025” refers to the UK HPI statistics for the calendar month of August 2025, as defined and published by the UK HPI on GOV.UK.
- Time zone: All times are UTC.

Source of truth and how to read it
- Primary source: The GOV.UK page “UK House Price Index summary: August 2025,” within the “UK House Price Index: reports” collection. The collection states this release is scheduled for 09:30 on Wednesday 22 October 2025. The monthly summary format presents the UK-level annual figure explicitly (e.g., “Average UK house price annual inflation was X.X% in the 12 months to [Month] [Year]”).
- Decision rule (what number to use): Use the UK-level annual percentage change for August 2025 as displayed on the summary page (to the precision shown on GOV.UK; rounding is whatever the page displays). If the page uses wording like “Average UK house price annual inflation was X.X% in the 12 months to August 2025,” that X.X% is the operative figure.
- Revisions: If GOV.UK revises the August 2025 UK-level annual figure after first publication, this market resolves based on the latest figure displayed on the summary page as of 23:59 UTC on 31 December 2025 (the UK HPI is a monthly National Statistic with a formal revisions policy; recent months are flagged as provisional).
- Publication delay contingency: If the August 2025 UK HPI summary is not published on GOV.UK by 23:59 UTC on 31 December 2025, resolve “N/A” due to no official figure available within the resolution window. This is unlikely given the schedule published in the GOV.UK collection.

Operational notes
- Where to find it on the day: Start at the collection page (https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/uk-house-price-index-reports) and click through to “UK House Price Index summary: August 2025” once it appears. The collection lists the release date/time and links to the summary and data files.
- Examples of correct field/phrasing: See the July 2025 summary for the exact placement and phrasing of the UK-level annual figure.

question: OPEC+8: Will the eight-country group announce a net increase in required production for January 2026 by December 31, 2025?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01 (UTC):
- What is OPEC and OPEC+? The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) is an intergovernmental organization of oil-producing nations; “OPEC+” refers to OPEC members plus allied non-OPEC producers that cooperate under the Declaration of Cooperation framework.

- The 2025 eight-country arrangement (“OPEC+8”): In 2025, eight OPEC+ producers — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman — have been issuing monthly decisions on production adjustments, coordinated via OPEC press releases. On September 7, 2025, an OPEC press release stated an adjustment of +137 thousand barrels per day (kbd) to be implemented in October 2025 and identified these eight countries as the participants. A July 5, 2025 OPEC press release described the ongoing monthly-meeting structure and noted that an August 2025 adjustment of +548 kbd (equivalent to four monthly increments) would be implemented from the July 2025 required production level, with flexibility to pause or reverse based on market conditions. Earlier, on April 3, 2025, OPEC announced an increase of +411 kbd for May 2025, described as “equivalent to three monthly increments”.

- Current forward-looking signals: On September 30, 2025, Reuters reported that OPEC+ was considering a larger November increase (indicative ranges included roughly +274–411 kbd, with one source mentioning up to +500 kbd, which OPEC publicly disputed), and that eight OPEC+ members would hold an online meeting on October 5 to decide November output. Separately, the 62nd OPEC Joint Ministerial Monitoring Committee (JMMC) meeting on October 1, 2025 reaffirmed monitoring adherence to the production adjustments decided at the 38th OPEC and non-OPEC Ministerial Meeting (ONOMM), with the next JMMC set for November 30, 2025.

- Where official decisions are published: OPEC and OPEC+ communiqués and press releases are published on the OPEC press releases index page (opec.org).

Key terms used by OPEC in 2025 communications:
- “Required production”: In 2025 OPEC materials, “required production levels” are referenced in the context of the 38th ONOMM baseline and subsequent voluntary adjustments (e.g., UAE’s required production phased increase per the 38th ONOMM). We will rely on the terminology and figures as presented in OPEC’s official releases when calculating any month-to-month changes.

Why this is a live question: The OPEC+8 have been incrementally unwinding prior cuts with month-by-month adjustments through 2025. Reuters coverage indicates that further increases were under active consideration for late 2025 meetings, but it is not yet determined whether an explicit production increase for January 2026 relative to December 2025 will be officially announced by year-end.
resolution_criteria:
Time window for eligible announcements: 00:00 UTC on 2025-10-15 through 23:59 UTC on 2025-12-31.

Operational group definition ("OPEC+8"): For this question, “group-wide” refers specifically to the eight OPEC+ producers that have been issuing monthly adjustments via OPEC press releases in 2025: Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman. This narrower definition is used to ensure unambiguous sourcing and calculation from the ongoing 2025 communication format.

Primary source of truth: Official OPEC/OPEC+ press releases or communiqués published on the OPEC press releases index (https://www.opec.org/press-releases.html). Reputable wire services (e.g., Reuters) may be used only to locate/point to the official OPEC release, not as a standalone resolution source.

Definitions and measurement rules:
- “Required production” and “production adjustment” will be interpreted as they are used in OPEC’s official communications tied to the 38th ONOMM baseline and subsequent voluntary adjustments. When OPEC provides per-country “required production” figures and/or an aggregate “production adjustment” (e.g., “+411 kbd for May”), we will use those officially stated numbers for calculation.
- “Aggregate required production of the OPEC+8” in a given month is defined as the sum of the eight countries’ required production levels for that month, if per-country figures are provided in the OPEC release. If OPEC instead provides a single explicit net “production adjustment” for the OPEC+8 for a given month relative to the prior month (e.g., “the eight countries will implement an adjustment of +N kbd in January 2026 from December 2025 required production level”), that explicit aggregate adjustment will be used as the authoritative month-on-month change.

Resolution rule (YES/NO):
- Resolve YES if, by 23:59 UTC on 2025-12-31, there exists an official OPEC release (on the press releases index) that clearly indicates a net increase in the OPEC+8’s output for January 2026 relative to December 2025, as evidenced by either:
  (A) An explicit positive “production adjustment” for January 2026 (vs December 2025) announced for the OPEC+8; or
  (B) Per-country required production values for both December 2025 and January 2026 for the OPEC+8, such that the sum for January exceeds the sum for December.
- Resolve NO if no such qualifying official release exists by the deadline, or if the official release(s) indicate no change or a net decrease for January 2026 vs December 2025.

Additional tie-breakers and edge cases:
- If multiple official releases are published within the window that address January 2026, the most recent OPEC release before the deadline prevails.
- If OPEC publishes both per-country tables and an explicit aggregate adjustment for January, but they conflict due to an obvious erratum, prefer the later corrected/updated version, if any; otherwise, prefer the explicit aggregate adjustment stated in the text of the same release.
- If OPEC uses synonyms (e.g., “quota,” “target,” “required production”) for the month-by-month mandated levels, use the figures as presented to compute the aggregate month-to-month change.
- Announcements that do not pertain to January 2026 or do not specify a January vs December month-on-month change are ineligible for YES.
- Time zone for all cut-offs is UTC.
