question: Will Ofcom publish at least one confirmation decision imposing a monetary penalty under the UK Online Safety Act between 2025-10-15 and 2025-12-31 (UTC)?
background: Scope and regulator: The UK Online Safety Act 2023 (OSA) establishes duties for providers of regulated online services and empowers Ofcom, the UK communications regulator, to investigate and enforce compliance. Ofcom’s enforcement process under the OSA includes opening investigations, issuing provisional notices of contravention, and, where appropriate, issuing a final “confirmation decision” that may impose monetary penalties [862da1; 1aeb87]. Ofcom’s published enforcement guidance explains that confirmation decisions (and penalty notices) are made by a senior decision maker, that opening an investigation does not imply a breach finding, and that non‑confidential decisions are published on Ofcom’s website after investigations are closed. Maximum penalties: Ofcom may impose penalties up to £18 million or 10% of qualifying worldwide revenue (QWR), whichever is greater, in line with its penalty guidelines and the OSA framework. Current status as of 2025-10-01: Ofcom’s September 2025 Online Safety industry bulletin reports more than a dozen investigations opened under the Act, including probes into age assurance on pornography sites and investigations into file‑sharing services suspected of hosting child sexual abuse material (CSAM), as well as an investigation into 4chan’s illegal content risk assessment duties. Ofcom also describes live enforcement programmes focused on children’s safety (age assurance and risk assessments), illegal content risk assessments, and monitoring impacts on major platforms. Why this is forecastable: The legal framework and enforcement mechanisms are in place [1aeb87; 862da1], and Ofcom has multiple ongoing investigations and programmes , but whether at least one investigation will culminate in a confirmation decision imposing a monetary penalty during Q4 2025 remains uncertain.
resolution_criteria:
Outcome type: Binary (Yes/No). Time bounds: Eligible decisions must be published between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, and resolution occurs at 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Definitions (with sources and links):
- Online Safety Act 2023 (OSA): UK statute governing online safety and Ofcom’s enforcement powers. See the legislation website (e.g., Part 7, Chapter 6 on enforcement) and statutory cross‑headings on provisional notices and confirmation decisions. Link: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2023/50
- Ofcom: The UK communications regulator responsible for OSA enforcement. Link: https://www.ofcom.org.uk
- Provisional notice of contravention: A preliminary notice issued when Ofcom has reasonable grounds to believe a failure to comply with an enforceable requirement; it may propose a penalty and invites representations. Link (legislation overview): https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2023/50/part/7/chapter/6/crossheading/provisional-notices-and-confirmation-decisions
- Confirmation decision: The final decision following a provisional notice, issued if Ofcom is satisfied a failure to comply with a notified requirement has occurred; it may require steps and/or require payment of a monetary penalty. Link (legislation overview): https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2023/50/part/7/chapter/6/crossheading/provisional-notices-and-confirmation-decisions
- Monetary penalty (under OSA enforcement): A penalty required to be paid pursuant to a confirmation decision; it can be a single amount, a daily rate (if a failure continues after a compliance date), or both. Link (legislation overview): https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2023/50/part/7/chapter/6/crossheading/provisional-notices-and-confirmation-decisions
- Publication of decisions: Ofcom’s enforcement guidance states that after closing an investigation, Ofcom will publish a non‑confidential version of the confirmation decision (or penalty notice) on its website. Link: https://www.ofcom.org.uk/siteassets/resources/documents/online-safety/information-for-industry/illegal-harms/online-safety-enforcement-guidance.pdf
- Qualifying Worldwide Revenue (QWR) and maximum penalties: Ofcom’s guidance explains that maximum penalties under the OSA are up to £18 million or 10% of QWR, whichever is greater. Link: https://www.ofcom.org.uk/siteassets/resources/documents/online-safety/information-for-industry/illegal-harms/online-safety-enforcement-guidance.pdf

Resolution rule:
- YES if Ofcom publishes, on ofcom.org.uk, at least one non‑confidential confirmation decision under the OSA that requires a provider of a regulated service to pay a monetary penalty (single amount and/or daily rate) during the time bounds above [1aeb87; 862da1]. The decision must be accessible on Ofcom’s website by the resolution timestamp.
- NO otherwise.

What counts and does not count:
- Counts: A confirmation decision (as defined above) that imposes a monetary penalty under Section 137 (penalties) following a provisional notice process under Part 7, Chapter 6 of the OSA. Either a single penalty or a daily rate penalty qualifies.
- Does not count: Provisional notices of contravention (since they are preliminary and do not by themselves impose a payable penalty) ; press releases or media reports without an accompanying published decision on ofcom.org.uk by the resolution timestamp ; enforcement outcomes under other Ofcom regimes (e.g., broadcast code) that are not OSA confirmation decisions.

Evidence sources at resolution:
- Primary source: Ofcom’s website publication of the non‑confidential confirmation decision (decision document or page). Ofcom’s enforcement guidance commits to publishing these decisions.
- Secondary corroboration (if needed): Ofcom press releases linking to the decision on ofcom.org.uk, provided the decision itself is published on the site by the resolution timestamp.

question: Will Saudi Information Technology Company (SITE) obtain CMA approval for an IPO or have its shares begin trading on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul) between 2025-10-01 and 2025-12-31 (UTC)?
background:
Saudi Information Technology Company (SITE) is a Saudi technology firm established in 2017 and part of the Public Investment Fund (PIF) portfolio; it specializes in cybersecurity services, digital and cloud solutions, systems integration, and data science. On May 29, 2025, Bloomberg reported that Saudi Arabia’s PIF was exploring an initial public offering (IPO) of SITE, with banks invited to pitch for roles; deliberations were said to be at an early stage and without official confirmation at that time. Argaam independently summarized the same core points (wholly owned by PIF, exploring an IPO, banks invited, early-stage discussions) based on Bloomberg’s reporting.

Key institutions and terms relevant to resolution:
- Capital Market Authority (CMA): Saudi Arabia’s financial markets regulator that oversees the Saudi Exchange and securities issuance. CMA publishes approval announcements for IPOs; such approvals are explicitly stated to be valid for six months from the Board resolution date and are canceled if offering/listing is not completed within that window.
- Saudi Exchange (Tadawul): The sole authorized securities exchange in Saudi Arabia. The exchange publishes issuer and financial advisor announcements and listing communications on its official site (saudiexchange.sa).
- Initial Public Offering (IPO): A public offering where shares of a company are sold to investors, transforming a private company into a public one.
- Prospectus: A disclosure document for securities offerings (including IPOs) that provides material information to investors. The CMA site hosts IPO prospectuses; for example, Rasan Information Technology Company’s IPO prospectus was published with a date of 26/05/2024G, with the Arabic version on the CMA website being the legally binding version.

Why this question is timely and uncertain: SITE’s potential IPO was in exploration stage as of late May 2025 with no official confirmation then. Saudi listings continue to occur under CMA oversight and are publicly documented through CMA approvals/prospectuses and Saudi Exchange announcements, providing clear, verifiable resolution sources. The window from October through December 2025 captures potential end-of-year transaction timing while keeping both Yes and No outcomes plausible.

Links for definitions and context (non-exhaustive):
- IPO: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial_public_offering 
- CMA: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_Market_Authority_(Saudi_Arabia) 
- Saudi Exchange (Tadawul): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Stock_Exchange

CMA’s processes and public disclosures (approvals, prospectuses) and Saudi Exchange announcements provide the mechanisms by which an IPO or listing would be publicly verified.
resolution_criteria:
Time window and timezone:
- Start: 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC
- End: 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC

Entity definition:
- “Saudi Information Technology Company (SITE)” refers to the Saudi technology company established in 2017, part of PIF’s portfolio, and active in cybersecurity, cloud, systems integration, and data science. This is the entity commonly abbreviated as “SITE.”

Definitions and what counts:
- “Initial Public Offering (IPO)” means a public offering of company shares to investors as defined in standard equity market usage.
- “Prospectus” means the formal securities offering document published for an IPO, containing material information for investors. For Saudi IPOs, prospectuses are published on the CMA website, with the Arabic prospectus as the legally binding version.
- “CMA approval announcement” means an official posting on the CMA’s site (cma.gov.sa) stating that the CMA Board has issued its resolution approving a company’s registration and IPO, typically including language about the approval validity period (six months).
- “Begin trading” means that the Saudi Exchange (saudiexchange.sa) publishes an announcement indicating that SITE’s shares are listed and trading on the Main Market or on Nomu (Parallel Market). Authoritative announcements and issuer communications are published on saudiexchange.sa, including issuer and financial advisor announcements.

Resolution rule:
- Resolve Yes if, between the start and end timestamps (UTC), any one of the following occurs and is verifiably published on the official domains:
  1) The CMA publishes an approval announcement for SITE’s registration and IPO (on cma.gov.sa).
  2) The CMA publishes an IPO prospectus for SITE (on cma.gov.sa), demonstrating an approved offering.
  3) The Saudi Exchange publishes an announcement that SITE’s shares are listed and have begun trading on the Main Market or Nomu (on saudiexchange.sa).
- Resolve No if none of the above conditions are met within the specified window.

Primary sources of truth (URLs):
- CMA announcements: https://cma.gov.sa/en/Market/NEWS/Pages/default.aspx 
- CMA prospectuses section: https://cma.gov.sa/en/Market/Prospectuses/Pages/default.aspx (example precedent: Rasan prospectus) 
- Saudi Exchange issuer/financial advisor announcements: https://www.saudiexchange.sa/wps/portal/saudiexchange/newsandreports/issuer-news/issuer-announcements 

Verification notes:
- A forecaster/resolver should search for “Saudi Information Technology Company” or “SITE” on the CMA announcements page and the CMA prospectuses page, and on the Saudi Exchange announcements pages. The presence of an official CMA approval announcement or prospectus for SITE (on cma.gov.sa), or an official Saudi Exchange listing/trading announcement for SITE (on saudiexchange.sa), within the defined time window (UTC), will determine a Yes outcome.

question: Between October 15 and December 31, 2025 (UTC), will the IMF Executive Board complete the second review of Pakistan’s Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and approve a disbursement under the EFF?
background:
Summary and status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- Pakistan is under an International Monetary Fund (IMF) Extended Fund Facility (EFF) arrangement. On May 9, 2025, the IMF Executive Board completed the first review of Pakistan’s EFF arrangement and stated this decision allowed for an immediate disbursement of about US$1 billion (SDR 760 million). In the same press release, the Board also approved an arrangement under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF) for Pakistan.
- On May 23, 2025, an IMF press release stated that “The next mission associated with the next EFF and RSF reviews is expected in the second half of 2025,” indicating timing for subsequent reviews.

Key definitions and references (for forecasters):
- IMF Executive Board: The IMF’s resident decision‑making body that conducts regular Board meetings and takes decisions on member country arrangements. See IMF overview of the Executive Board: https://www.imf.org/en/About/Our-Structure/Executive-Board and Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#Governance.
- Extended Fund Facility (EFF): An IMF lending arrangement to provide assistance to countries experiencing serious balance of payments problems because of structural weaknesses, with longer‑term engagement than stand‑by arrangements. See IMF factsheet: https://www.imf.org/en/About/Factsheets/Sheets/2016/08/01/20/56/Extended-Fund-Facility and Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_Fund_Facility.
- Review (in the context of IMF arrangements): Periodic assessments of a program where IMF staff and authorities evaluate performance against quantitative criteria and structural benchmarks; the IMF Executive Board then considers completion of the numbered review. Completion of a review is announced via an IMF press release that typically uses language such as “Executive Board completes the [Nth] review under the Extended Fund Facility arrangement with [country]” and states whether a disbursement (also called a “purchase” under the EFF) was approved/made available. For example, the May 9, 2025 press release explicitly states that completing the first review enabled an immediate disbursement.
- Disbursement under the EFF: The amount (in Special Drawing Rights, SDR, and often translated into US$) that the press release states is approved/made available for the member to draw (“purchase”) under the EFF upon completion of the review. See IMF glossary entry on purchases/disbursements: https://www.imf.org/en/About/Factsheets/IMF-Lending.
- IMF press release: A news item published on imf.org under the News > Press Releases section and bearing a Press Release number (e.g., PR 25/137). Example for Pakistan (May 9, 2025): https://www.imf.org/en/News/Articles/2025/05/09/pr-25137-pakistan-imf-completes-1st-rev-of-eff-arrang-and-approves-req-for-arrang-under-rsf. The IMF country page for Pakistan also aggregates relevant releases and documents: https://www.imf.org/en/Countries/PAK.

Why this is a non‑trivial forecast:
- Whether the second review can be completed by year‑end depends on Pakistan meeting program conditions, macroeconomic developments, and IMF‑Pakistan negotiations. The May statements set expectations for a second‑half‑2025 mission, but the exact timing and outcome of the Executive Board’s consideration are uncertain. Forecasters should monitor IMF press briefings, staff‑level announcements, and Pakistan’s fiscal/monetary policy news for signals of progress toward Board consideration.

What data/source will be used for resolution:
- The IMF’s official press releases (imf.org News > Press Releases) and, secondarily, the IMF’s Pakistan country page (which links to the same releases). The May 2025 press releases establish the format and language used to indicate completion of a review and approval of a disbursement.
resolution_criteria:
Event window and time zone:
- Eligible events are those announced in IMF press releases dated between 00:00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, inclusive. The “date” used is the date displayed on the IMF press release page.

Question restated precisely:
- Resolve Yes if, during the event window, there exists an IMF press release that explicitly states all of the following for Pakistan:
  1) The IMF Executive Board completed the second review under the Extended Fund Facility (EFF) arrangement with Pakistan (wording such as “completed the Second Review under the EFF” or “completes second review under the EFF arrangement with Pakistan” is acceptable, including “Second” or “2nd”).
  2) A disbursement/purchase under the EFF strictly greater than zero was approved/made available upon completion of that second review (the press release typically specifies an amount in SDR and often in US$ as well). If the press release combines EFF and RSF items, only the EFF disbursement counts for this criterion.
- Resolve No if no such press release satisfying both (1) and (2) is dated within the event window.

Authoritative sources for resolution:
- Primary: IMF News > Press Releases (https://www.imf.org/en/News/Articles) and the IMF Pakistan country page (https://www.imf.org/en/Countries/PAK) linking to the relevant press release(s).

Inclusions and exclusions:
- Included: An IMF press release bearing a Press Release number (e.g., “PR 25/xxx”) that explicitly states Board completion of the second EFF review for Pakistan and an approved/made‑available disbursement under the EFF greater than zero.
- Excluded: Staff‑level agreements, end‑of‑mission statements, staff concluding statements, press briefings, blogs, or social media posts; press releases that do not mention Board completion of the second EFF review; press releases that mention Board completion but do not approve/make available any disbursement under the EFF (i.e., zero EFF disbursement); press releases dated outside the event window.

Edge cases and tie‑breaking:
- If more than one relevant press release is published within the window, any one that satisfies both (1) and (2) is sufficient for a Yes.
- If a press release announces Board completion of the second review after the window (dated in 2026) referring to a Board decision taken in late 2025, this does not count (the press release date governs eligibility).
- If the press release announces completion of a combined review (e.g., EFF second review and RSF review) and only the RSF disbursement is approved while EFF disbursement is zero, resolve No.
- If the ordinary meaning of “second review” is not used but equivalent numbering is unambiguously indicated (e.g., “completion of Review 2 under the EFF”), treat it as the second review.

Verification time budget:
- A resolver should be able to verify the outcome within 10 minutes by searching imf.org press releases for Pakistan and scanning the relevant press release text.

Citations supporting status quo and precedent wording:
- IMF Executive Board completed Pakistan’s first EFF review on May 9, 2025 and allowed an immediate disbursement of about US$1 billion (SDR 760 million).
- IMF stated on May 23, 2025 that the next mission associated with the next EFF and RSF reviews was expected in the second half of 2025.

question: Will Chile’s national unemployment rate for the Sep–Nov 2025 moving quarter be at least 8.6%?
background:
Context and data source
- Chile’s official labor market statistics are produced by the Instituto Nacional de Estadísticas (INE) via the Encuesta Nacional de Empleo (ENE). ENE publishes estimates for moving quarters (trimestres móviles) of key indicators, with the unemployment rate (tasa de desocupación) being the primary headline indicator. INE states that these estimates are officially published on the last business day of each month.
- The unemployment rate can be expressed as the number of unemployed people divided by the labor force, times 100; the labor force comprises employed plus unemployed individuals (ILO-aligned standard). ENE classifies the population aged 15 years and over by labor force status (employed, unemployed, or outside the labor force), and provides indicators at the national level.
- Publication timing for this specific period: INE’s Agenda Estadística lists “Empleo Nacional y Empleo Región Metropolitana, período septiembre – noviembre 2025” scheduled for December 30 at 09:00 (local publication time as listed on the INE Agenda).

Recent readings (national unemployment rate, ENE, moving quarters)
- Apr–Jun 2025: 8.9%.
- May–Jul 2025: 8.7%.
- Jun–Aug 2025: 8.6%.
These figures show a recent drift from 8.9% toward 8.6% into late Q3 2025, suggesting that a 8.6% cutoff for Sep–Nov 2025 is a high-uncertainty threshold.

What exactly will be measured
- The question targets the national unemployment rate (tasa de desocupación, total país, personas de 15 años y más) for the moving quarter September–November 2025 (i.e., the three-month period including September, October, and November 2025) as reported by INE in the ENE/“Empleo Nacional” release. INE also disseminates seasonally adjusted series, but their press materials and bulletins show both adjusted and unadjusted rates; we will rely on the headline non-seasonally adjusted unemployment rate for the national total.

Why this question is timely and resolvable by year-end
- INE’s Agenda Estadística places the relevant publication on Dec 30, 2025, allowing resolution prior to Dec 31, 2025. INE describes ENE outputs and their official monthly publication cadence, providing a clear and authoritative single source of truth for the figure needed to resolve this question.
resolution_criteria:
Binary outcome (Yes/No) and threshold
- Resolve Yes if INE’s national unemployment rate (tasa de desocupación, non-seasonally adjusted) for the moving quarter September–November 2025 is greater than or equal to 8.6%. Resolve No if it is below 8.6%.

Definitions and scope (authoritative sources)
- “National unemployment rate” refers to INE’s ENE headline tasa de desocupación for the national total (total país), persons aged 15+ (personas de 15 años y más), as published in INE’s official release materials (press release and/or ENE national bulletin). The unemployment rate conceptually equals unemployed divided by labor force times 100 (ILO-aligned standard).
- “Moving quarter September–November 2025” is the three-month period covering September, October, and November 2025 (a trimestre móvil, as used by ENE).
- “At least” means greater than or equal to (≥).

What exact number will be used
- Use the non-seasonally adjusted national unemployment rate for the period September–November 2025 as published by INE in its ENE/Empleo Nacional release scheduled on Dec 30, 2025. If both seasonally adjusted and non-seasonally adjusted figures are shown, the non-seasonally adjusted “tasa de desocupación” is the number of record (INE press materials commonly show both, but the headline rate is the unadjusted one).

Eligible sources and tie-breakers
- Primary source: INE’s official publication on ine.gob.cl for the ENE national employment release corresponding to September–November 2025, specifically the press release page and/or the ENE national bulletin (Boletín Estadístico: Empleo Trimestral). The general ENE/“Ocupación y desocupación” portal confirms the outputs and their publication cadence, and links to the relevant release/bulletin on the last business day. The Agenda Estadística lists the specific Dec 30, 2025 publication for this period.
- If INE’s press release and the national bulletin display different unadjusted national rates prior to the resolution deadline, use the value in the ENE national bulletin (Boletín Estadístico: Empleo Trimestral) posted on ine.gob.cl before 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. If INE issues an official correction before the deadline, use the corrected value.

Timing and cutoff
- The figure must be published by INE no later than 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. Publications appearing after this cutoff, or revisions issued after this cutoff, will not be considered.

Examples for context (do not determine resolution)
- Recent national unemployment rates for prior moving quarters were 8.9% (Apr–Jun 2025), 8.7% (May–Jul 2025), and 8.6% (Jun–Aug 2025). These examples are only for background and do not determine the outcome for Sep–Nov 2025.

question: Will the Bank of England change Bank Rate at either the 6 November or 18 December 2025 MPC announcements?
background:
Summary of what forecasters need to know as of 2025-09-30 (UTC):
- What is “Bank Rate”? The Bank of England (BoE) sets Bank Rate, the interest rate it pays on reserves held with it and charges on certain loans to eligible institutions. Bank Rate influences other UK interest rates.
- When are the relevant meetings? The BoE’s 2025 MPC schedule includes meetings/announcement dates on Thursday 6 November 2025 and Thursday 18 December 2025. The Monetary Policy Summary and minutes are published eight times a year, typically at 12 noon on a Thursday. The BoE explainer page also states: “We will announce our next decision on Thursday 6 November 2025”.
- Current status quo: At its meeting ending on 6 August 2025, the MPC voted 5–4 to reduce Bank Rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4.00%. At its meeting ending on 17 September 2025, the MPC voted 7–2 to maintain Bank Rate at 4.00%. The BoE’s explainer page shows “Current Bank Rate 4%” and references the August 2025 reduction.
- Market expectations (context only): In the September 2025 Market Participants Survey, respondents’ median expected Bank Rate was 4.00% for 6 November 2025 and 3.75% for 18 December 2025; for 6 November, the mean probability mass was concentrated at 4.00% (57.8%) and 3.75% (38.7%).
- Primary sources to watch on the day: The BoE publishes a “Monetary Policy Summary and minutes” page for each meeting (e.g., November 2025 and December 2025 pages are scheduled “to be published at 12pm”). The BoE also maintains an official Bank Rate database with the current and historical Official Bank Rate.

Key definitions and links:
- Bank Rate (a.k.a. Official Bank Rate): The BoE’s policy rate; see BoE explainer.
- MPC announcement: The BoE’s Monetary Policy Summary and minutes publication for the relevant meeting date (links available on the BoE site and “Monetary policy summary and minutes” index page).
- The two relevant dates are fixed by the BoE’s 2025 schedule: 6 November 2025 and 18 December 2025.

Why this is forecastable now: As of late September 2025, Bank Rate is 4.00% following an August cut, and the MPC kept it unchanged in September. There is meaningful uncertainty about whether the MPC will change Bank Rate at one or both late‑2025 meetings, with survey expectations split across 3.75% and 4.00% for November and a 3.75% median for December.
resolution_criteria:
Question and date range:
- Resolve whether the Bank of England changes Bank Rate at either of the MPC announcements on Thursday 6 November 2025 or Thursday 18 December 2025. Eligible events must occur between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. All times are UTC.

Definitions:
- “Bank Rate” means the Bank of England’s Official Bank Rate, as defined by the BoE (its policy interest rate that influences other UK interest rates).
- “MPC announcement” means the Bank of England’s published “Monetary Policy Summary and minutes” for the relevant meeting date, which the BoE publishes eight times per year, typically at 12 noon on a Thursday. For November and December 2025, the BoE’s schedule specifies announcements on 6 November 2025 and 18 December 2025. The BoE also flags that the next decision announcement is on 6 November 2025.
- “Change (in Bank Rate) at a meeting” is satisfied if the relevant Monetary Policy Summary explicitly states that the MPC voted to set Bank Rate to a level different from the level in effect immediately prior to that announcement (e.g., “voted to reduce Bank Rate by 0.25 percentage points, to 4%” counts as a change; “voted to maintain Bank Rate at 4%” does not). This determination will be based on the wording in the BoE’s Monetary Policy Summary for that meeting.

Resolution rule:
- Resolve Yes if the BoE’s Monetary Policy Summary and minutes for either 6 November 2025 or 18 December 2025 states that the MPC changed Bank Rate (as defined above). Resolve No if both the 6 November 2025 and 18 December 2025 Monetary Policy Summaries and minutes state that Bank Rate was maintained (i.e., no change at either meeting).

Primary resolution sources (any one is sufficient; the Monetary Policy Summary text governs):
- The BoE’s “Monetary Policy Summary and minutes” index, which links to each meeting’s announcement and is published at 12 noon on Thursdays eight times a year.
- The November 2025 Monetary Policy Summary and minutes page (marked “to be published at 12pm”) and the December 2025 page (marked “to be published at 12pm”).

Secondary corroborating source (if needed):
- The BoE Official Bank Rate database, which lists the current and historical Official Bank Rate values and can confirm the rate before and after the relevant announcements.

Edge cases and contingencies:
- Only decisions announced in the Monetary Policy Summary and minutes for the specified 6 November 2025 and 18 December 2025 meetings count. Inter‑meeting changes (if any) do not affect resolution unless the change is explicitly decided at one of these two meetings and stated in the corresponding Monetary Policy Summary.
- If either meeting is rescheduled but the corresponding Monetary Policy Summary for that meeting is still published within 2025, that publication will count for this question; otherwise, if a meeting is cancelled or its Monetary Policy Summary is not published by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, treat that meeting as “no change” for the purpose of this question and resolve based on the remaining meeting.
- The question resolves as soon as the first of the two specified Monetary Policy Summaries indicating a change is published (Yes), or after the 18 December 2025 publication if neither indicates a change (No).

question: Between 2025-10-15 and 2025-12-31 (UTC), will the European Commission adopt at least one Digital Services Act (DSA) fining decision against a designated Very Large Online Platform (VLOP) or Very Large Online Search Engine (VLOSE) for a breach explicitly concerning the protection of minors?
background:
Overview and why this matters
- The EU’s Digital Services Act (DSA) is an EU regulation setting obligations for online intermediaries and platforms, with the most stringent rules applying to Very Large Online Platforms (VLOPs) and Very Large Online Search Engines (VLOSEs) that serve over 45 million average monthly users in the EU. The European Commission supervises VLOPs/VLOSEs and maintains a public list of designated services.
- Under the DSA enforcement framework, the Commission can impose administrative fines of up to 6% of a provider’s worldwide annual turnover for breaches of DSA obligations. It can also impose periodic penalty payments (up to 5% of average daily worldwide turnover) for non-compliance with remedies/interim measures/commitments, and fines up to 1% for incorrect, misleading, or incomplete responses to requests for information, or refusal to submit to inspection.

Protection of minors under the DSA
- The DSA requires online platforms accessible to minors to ensure a high level of privacy, safety and security for them (Article 28(1)). The European Commission published guidelines on 2025-07-14 that provide a non-exhaustive set of appropriate and proportionate measures platforms can take (e.g., age-appropriate design and content controls; disabling addictive design features by default; strengthening moderation/reporting; robust age assurance), and stated it will use these guidelines to assess compliance with Article 28(1).
- The DSA also prohibits targeting minors with advertising based on profiling and requires VLOPs/VLOSEs to identify and address systemic risks affecting society, including those related to the protection and well-being of minors.

Current enforcement context relevant to minors
- The European Board for Digital Services launched a coordinated action on 2025-05-27 to reinforce protection of minors regarding pornographic platforms, with the Commission opening formal proceedings against Pornhub, Stripchat, XNXX, and XVideos for suspected DSA breaches related to safeguarding minors. Earlier, on 2024-06-13, the Commission sent requests for information to Pornhub, Stripchat, and XVideos about their minors-protection and related risk mitigation measures, noting that fines can be imposed for incorrect, incomplete, or misleading responses under Article 74(2) DSA.

Key definitions and sources for forecasters
- VLOP/VLOSE: Platforms or search engines with more than 45 million average monthly users in the EU; the Commission designates and supervises these services and maintains a public list.
- DSA fines and penalties: The Commission’s enforcement tools include fines up to 6% of worldwide turnover for breaches of obligations, periodic penalty payments for non-compliance, and separate fines for incorrect/misleading information—distinct categories that matter for resolution.
- Protection of minors: Includes Article 28(1) duties and other minors-related obligations under the DSA (e.g., ban on profiling-based targeted ads to minors; VLOP/VLOSE systemic risk duties).

These developments, including the July 2025 minors guidelines and the coordinated actions/formal proceedings involving adult-content platforms, indicate active 2025 enforcement attention on minors’ protection under the DSA, while leaving uncertainty about whether a fine decision explicitly tied to minors-related breaches will be adopted during the final quarter of 2025.
resolution_criteria:
Eligible time window
- Only events occurring between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC (inclusive) count toward resolution.

Question restated for precision
- Resolve Yes if, within the eligible window, the European Commission adopts a formal decision imposing an administrative fine under the DSA on an entity that, at the time of that decision, is designated as a VLOP or VLOSE, and the decision text or accompanying Commission press release explicitly states that the infringement concerns obligations related to the protection of minors. Resolve No otherwise.

Operational definitions (with sources)
- Very Large Online Platform (VLOP) / Very Large Online Search Engine (VLOSE): A platform or search engine designated by the European Commission under the DSA for having more than 45 million average monthly users in the EU; the Commission supervises these services and maintains a public list of designations. For the purpose of this market, the provider must be designated as a VLOP/VLOSE at the time of the fining decision.
- Fine under the DSA (what counts): An administrative pecuniary penalty imposed by a European Commission decision under the DSA for a breach of DSA obligations, which can be up to 6% of worldwide annual turnover.
- What does NOT count: (a) Periodic penalty payments imposed to compel compliance (up to 5% of average daily worldwide turnover) ; (b) fines solely for procedural non-compliance (e.g., incorrect/misleading/incomplete responses to requests for information; refusal to submit to inspection) ; (c) interim measures; (d) commitments/settlements without a fining decision; (e) fines under other legal frameworks such as the Digital Markets Act (DMA) or EU competition law.
- Protection of minors (what must be explicitly cited in the decision): Obligations pertaining to minors under the DSA, including but not limited to Article 28(1) (high level of privacy, safety and security for minors) and VLOP/VLOSE systemic risk identification/mitigation duties as they affect minors; as context, the Commission’s 2025 guidelines detail recommended measures and state they will be used to assess Article 28(1) compliance.
- Minor: A person under the age of 18, consistent with the general legal definition of a minor.

How to adjudicate
- Primary resolution sources (any one suffices):
  1) European Commission Press Corner press release announcing the DSA fining decision; OR
  2) The Commission’s fining decision text as published in the Official Journal of the European Union.
- If both a press release and an Official Journal decision are available and the dates differ, use the date of adoption stated in the decision. If the adoption date is not readily available, use the date on the Commission press release.
- Verification steps for the resolver:
  1) Confirm the provider is designated as a VLOP or VLOSE on the Commission’s public list at the time of the decision.
  2) Read the decision text and/or press release to verify that the fine is imposed for a DSA breach explicitly concerning minors-related obligations (as described above).
  3) Confirm that the decision imposes an administrative fine (not a periodic penalty payment; not a procedural fine) under the DSA.
- Edge cases:
  - If the Commission adopts a decision imposing both a substantive fine and a periodic penalty payment, the market resolves Yes if and only if the decision explicitly includes a substantive fine (as defined above) for a minors-related breach within the eligible window.
  - If the Commission adopts a substantive DSA fining decision within the window but publication occurs later, resolution uses the adoption date as stated in the decision (or the press release date if the adoption date is not available).

question: Between 00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, will the Ksi Lisims LNG project announce a positive Final Investment Decision (FID)?
background:
Overview and current status as of October 1, 2025:
- Project identity: The “Ksi Lisims LNG – Natural Gas Liquefaction and Marine Terminal Project” is a proposed floating LNG export facility on Nisga’a Nation land near the community of Gingolx on Canada’s northwest Pacific coast. The project proponents are Nisga’a Nation, Rockies LNG Limited Partnership, and Western LNG LLC.
- Regulatory status: On September 15, 2025, the federal Minister of Environment and Climate Change issued an Impact Assessment Decision Statement, effectively green-lighting the project at the federal level under the Impact Assessment Act and setting legally binding conditions for the proponents. On September 16, 2025, the Government of British Columbia announced that the project received its provincial Environmental Assessment Certificate; the announcement noted that the partners had not yet made a final investment decision at that time.
- Capacity and design: Public reporting and proponent materials describe the project as a 12 million tonnes per annum (mtpa) LNG facility.
- Official information sources likely to host an FID announcement: The official Ksi Lisims LNG website has a News page (https://www.ksilisimslng.com/news) that hosts press releases. Western LNG also maintains a News page (https://www.westernlng.com/news). The IAAC project page provides authoritative project documentation and updates , and the Government of British Columbia posts related provincial announcements.

Key definitions and scope for this question:
- Time window and timezone: Only announcements published between 00:00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025 are eligible.
- Project covered: “Ksi Lisims LNG – Natural Gas Liquefaction and Marine Terminal Project,” as identified by Canada’s Impact Assessment Agency project page.
- Proponents: Nisga’a Nation; Rockies LNG Limited Partnership; Western LNG LLC.
- “Final Investment Decision” (FID) for the purpose of resolution: An explicit announcement by one or more proponents that a “final investment decision” (or “FID”) has been made and is positive/affirmative, committing the project to proceed. For resolvability, the announcement must include the phrase “final investment decision” or “FID.” 

Notes for forecasters:
- As of mid-September 2025, the project cleared major federal and provincial assessment milestones, but an FID had not yet been taken.
- Market, financing, offtake, and EPC readiness typically influence LNG FID timing; however, this question resolves solely on the presence of an explicit FID announcement within the defined window.
resolution_criteria:
How this question will resolve:
- Resolve YES if, between 00:00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, there is an official announcement explicitly stating that a positive “final investment decision” (or “FID”) has been made for the Ksi Lisims LNG project, where:
  - Eligible announcements include: 
    - A press release or website update posted on any official proponent website (e.g., Ksi Lisims LNG News page: https://www.ksilisimslng.com/news ; Western LNG News page: https://www.westernlng.com/news ; Rockies LNG News page: https://www.rockieslng.com/news ).
    - An announcement on an official government page confirming the FID (e.g., Impact Assessment Agency of Canada or Government of British Columbia news/updates).
    - Coverage by a major, reputable outlet (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg) directly quoting or citing an official proponent or government statement that a positive FID has been made.
  - The announcement must include the exact phrase “final investment decision” or “FID” and indicate that the decision is positive/affirmative. Announcements of intent to reach FID, “pre-FID” steps, conditional or deferred FIDs, or generic terms like “sanction” or “approval” without explicit reference to a “final investment decision” or “FID” do not count.
  - If multiple announcements exist, the earliest publication timestamp within the window (standardized to UTC) will be used to confirm eligibility.
- Resolve NO if no eligible announcement meeting the above criteria is published within the time window.

Verification steps (for resolvers):
1) Check the Ksi Lisims LNG News page and the proponents’/government pages listed above for any press releases explicitly stating a positive “final investment decision” or “FID”.
2) If necessary, verify via major wire services (e.g., Reuters) that directly quote a proponent/government confirming a positive FID.
3) Record the publication date/time and confirm it falls within the defined UTC window.

Edge cases:
- If an announcement uses synonyms (e.g., “project sanctioned”) but does not explicitly include “final investment decision” or “FID,” it will not count unless accompanied by a direct statement that a positive FID has been made.
- If an announcement is published on December 31, 2025 in a local timezone after 23:59:59 UTC, it will not count. The resolver must convert timestamps to UTC when needed.
- If an announcement is later retracted within the window, the question resolves based on the status at 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025; a retraction before that cutoff negates eligibility.

Primary sources for resolution:
- IAAC Canada news/updates and project page 
- Government of British Columbia news releases 
- Proponent websites: Ksi Lisims LNG News page ; Western LNG News page ; Rockies LNG News page 
- Major wire services directly quoting officials, if needed

question: Will Boeing complete its acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems between 00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025?
background:
Summary of the transaction and current status (as of 2025-10-01):
- Transaction: The Boeing Company (NYSE: BA) seeks to acquire Spirit AeroSystems Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: SPR). As part of the broader package around the deal, Airbus is set to take on certain Spirit Europe-focused activities (including Spirit’s Prestwick, Scotland and Subang, Malaysia operations that support Airbus programs), while Spirit’s Belfast operations not supporting Airbus programs would be sold, according to reporting on Boeing’s submitted remedies to the European Commission (EC).
- EU antitrust review: Boeing has offered remedies/commitments to the European Commission in order to secure approval. Following submission of these commitments, the EC extended its decision deadline for the deal to October 14, 2025, and is expected to gather market feedback before deciding whether to accept the remedies or open an in-depth (up to four-month) investigation.
- UK competition review: The UK Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) cleared the anticipated acquisition on August 8, 2025.
- Shareholder approval: Spirit AeroSystems shareholders approved the acquisition at a special meeting held on January 31, 2025.

Why this is forecastable now: The EC’s provisional decision deadline of October 14, 2025 means the key remaining obstacle could be cleared (or extended to in-depth review) just before the start of the resolution window (October 15). Depending on that outcome, the transaction could close in Q4 2025 or be delayed, making both Yes and No plausible by year-end.

Key references and where to track updates:
- EU review: European Commission merger case page for Boeing/Spirit (case M.11578). Reuters coverage confirms remedies submission and the Oct 14, 2025 deadline extension.
- UK review: CMA case page records the Phase 1 clearance on August 8, 2025.
- Company approvals: Spirit’s January 31, 2025 shareholder approval is documented on the company’s investor relations site.
- Closing confirmations (once/if the deal completes): Company press releases on their investor relations pages and SEC EDGAR Form 8-K filings (Form 8-K is the current report used by U.S. public companies to announce material events).

Definitions and useful links (for clarity):
- Acquisition/closing: For this question, “complete its acquisition” means the transaction has closed (i.e., become effective/consummated) such that Boeing becomes the owner of Spirit AeroSystems via completion of the merger under the governing merger agreement, as evidenced by official company disclosures (see Resolution Criteria). Closing is typically reported in a Form 8-K “current report” filing and/or a press release.
- Time standard: UTC refers to Coordinated Universal Time (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time). Date and time windows in this question are measured in UTC.
- Official company communications: Press release is a public announcement posted on an official corporate press/IR site (e.g., Boeing investor relations: https://investors.boeing.com; Spirit investor relations: https://investor.spiritaero.com). SEC EDGAR database: https://www.sec.gov/edgar/searchedgar/companysearch.

Status quo snapshot:
- EC review ongoing; decision deadline extended to Oct 14, 2025 after Boeing offered remedies, with market testing expected and a possible four-month in-depth investigation if concerns remain.
- CMA has cleared the deal (Phase 1) as of Aug 8, 2025.
- Spirit shareholders approved the acquisition on Jan 31, 2025.
- Form 8-K is the standard SEC mechanism for companies to announce material events such as deal closings.
resolution_criteria:
Binary resolution (Yes/No).

Time window for eligible events:
- Start: 00:00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025
- End: 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025

Question restated precisely: Resolve “Yes” if Boeing’s acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems is completed (i.e., the transaction closes/merger becomes effective) at any time during the window above, as evidenced by the acceptable sources below. Resolve “No” otherwise.

Acceptable resolution evidence (primary sources preferred):
Any one of the following is sufficient for a Yes resolution, so long as it unambiguously states that the acquisition has closed (or the merger has been consummated/become effective) and the closing date falls within the window above (interpreting date-only statements as UTC dates):
1) A Form 8-K filed on the SEC’s EDGAR system by either The Boeing Company or Spirit AeroSystems that explicitly states the closing/completion of the acquisition/merger (e.g., Item 2.01 Completion of Acquisition or a filing that clearly states the merger closed on [date]). Form 8-K is the SEC “current report” used by public companies to announce material events.
2) A joint or concurrent press release posted on the official investor relations/press pages of both companies that explicitly states that the transaction has closed (e.g., “Boeing completes acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems”).

Secondary corroboration (if needed for clarity, but not required if a primary source is clear): Reports by major, reputable outlets (e.g., Reuters, Associated Press, Bloomberg) that the deal has closed on [date]. Note: If there is any discrepancy between press reports and the companies’ official disclosures, the companies’ Form 8-K filings and official press releases take precedence.

Interpretation rules and edge cases:
- Date-only statements: If a source states only a calendar date for closing (without a time), interpret it as occurring on that UTC date. If multiple sources give different dates, prefer the date stated in a Form 8-K, if available.
- After-hours filings: If an SEC filing is timestamped outside the window but explicitly states that closing occurred on a date within the window, it counts as Yes.
- Partial asset transfers/divestitures: The question concerns completion of Boeing’s acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems. Related divestitures (e.g., transfers to Airbus) do not need to have closed for this question to resolve Yes, provided the Boeing–Spirit transaction itself is completed as per the companies’ official disclosures.
- Termination: If the transaction is terminated or remains unclosed through 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, resolve No.

Pre-identified sources to check at resolution time:
- SEC EDGAR company pages for Boeing and Spirit (for Form 8-K filings).
- Boeing and Spirit investor relations news pages (for press releases). 

Context for forecasters:
- As of Oct 1, 2025, the EC has extended its decision deadline to Oct 14, 2025 following Boeing’s submission of remedies and is expected to conduct market testing; it may accept the remedies or open a four-month investigation. The UK CMA cleared the deal on Aug 8, 2025. Spirit shareholders approved the acquisition on Jan 31, 2025. These milestones frame the regulatory path remaining before potential closing within the window.

question: By December 31, 2025 (23:59:59 UTC), will the United States publish an official instrument that explicitly caps tariffs on EU- or Japan‑origin pharmaceutical products at 15% ad valorem?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-09-30:
- EU framework implementation: A Federal Register notice amending the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS) to implement elements of the August 21, 2025 U.S.–EU framework states that, for automobiles and parts, the combined tariff rate (MFN plus reduced Section 232 rate) is capped at 15% ad valorem for EU‑origin products and that certain goods (including generic pharmaceuticals and their ingredients and chemical precursors) are treated separately. CBP subsequently issued guidance explaining HTSUS implementation details, including an exemption from reciprocal tariffs for EU generic pharmaceuticals (using heading 9903.02.77), effective September 1, 2025.
- Japan agreement implementation: A Federal Register notice implementing tariff‑related elements of the U.S.–Japan agreement establishes a baseline 15% ad valorem tariff structure for nearly all Japanese imports, with sector‑specific treatment for automobiles, aerospace, generic pharmaceuticals, and certain natural resources; it includes effective‑date and in‑transit exceptions. A White House presidential action page similarly describes the baseline 15% structure and authorizes zero reciprocal tariffs for generic pharmaceuticals and related inputs.
- Public statements on pharmaceuticals: Reuters reported EU and Japan officials’ confidence that U.S. tariffs on pharmaceuticals would not exceed 15% under joint statements with Washington, referencing a 15% ceiling for EU exports including pharmaceuticals. CNN reported President Trump’s announcement of a 100% tariff on branded/patented pharmaceutical products effective October 1, 2025, while noting that the White House confirmed it would honor a 15% tariff cap agreed in trade deals with the EU and Japan, implying capped rates for EU/Japan‑origin pharmaceuticals.

Interpretation and current uncertainty:
- As of today, specific codified HTSUS or agency‑level text that explicitly caps EU‑ or Japan‑origin pharmaceutical products at 15% ad valorem (covering all HTSUS Chapter 30 pharmaceuticals, not only generics) has not been clearly identified in the cited notices; autos and certain sectoral carve‑outs are explicitly treated, and generic pharmaceuticals are addressed separately (exemptions/zero reciprocal tariffs), but an explicit 15% cap covering pharmaceutical products broadly would require a further instrument or explicit language.

Key definitions and scope for forecasters:
- Pharmaceutical products: For this question, “pharmaceutical products” means goods classified under HTSUS Chapter 30 (“Pharmaceutical Products”). See HTSUS Chapter 30 (U.S. International Trade Commission) at https://hts.usitc.gov/reststop/file?release=currentRelease&filename=Chapter%2030.
- Country of origin: Determined under U.S. non‑preferential rules of origin and CBP practice (see 19 CFR Part 102, Rules of Origin) at https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-19/chapter-I/part-102.
- Tariff (ad valorem): A customs duty stated as a percentage of the customs value (see “Tariff” overview: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tariff; “Ad valorem tax”: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ad_valorem_tax).
- EU and Japan: The European Union (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union) and Japan (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan).

Why this is forecastable with meaningful entropy:
- Public statements indicate intent to cap EU/Japan pharmaceutical tariffs at 15%, but codification specific to pharmaceuticals—especially patented/brand‑name drugs—may require additional instruments (e.g., HTSUS modifications or agency guidance) that could be issued or not by year‑end. The interplay between the baseline 15% Japanese tariff structure and sector‑specific carve‑outs, and the EU framework’s sectoral exemptions, leaves open whether an explicit cross‑sector cap for pharmaceuticals will be published in official text.
resolution_criteria:
Event window and resolution time:
- Window: From 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC through 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.
- Resolve at 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Question resolves “Yes” if, within the window, a U.S. official instrument is publicly posted that explicitly establishes a 15% ad valorem maximum (cap/ceiling) applicable to pharmaceutical products of EU or Japan origin, as defined below. Otherwise “No.”

Qualifying official instrument (any one suffices):
- A Federal Register notice (Commerce/USTR/CBP) that amends the HTSUS or sets tariff application rules, or a Presidential Executive Order/Proclamation posted on whitehouse.gov/federalregister.gov, or a CBP CSMS bulletin/guidance, or an official USTR or Commerce directive/notice that is publicly accessible on an official.gov domain.

What “explicitly caps at 15%” means:
- The instrument must, in its operative language, state either: (a) “pharmaceutical” or “pharmaceutical products” or otherwise clearly reference HTSUS Chapter 30 goods and an applied tariff ceiling of 15% ad valorem for EU‑ or Japan‑origin entries; or (b) provide HTSUS modifications or headings that unambiguously result in a combined applied duty rate (base Column 1 duty plus any additional duties under Sections 232/301/IEEPA/reciprocal tariffs, etc.) not exceeding 15% ad valorem for EU‑ or Japan‑origin Chapter 30 entries.
- The cap must apply to pharmaceutical products broadly (HTSUS Chapter 30) and not be limited solely to “generic” pharmaceuticals; instruments that only exempt generics (non‑patented pharmaceutical applications) without capping branded/patented products do not qualify.

Scope definitions for resolution:
- “Pharmaceutical products”: All goods classifiable under HTSUS Chapter 30. Link: https://hts.usitc.gov/reststop/file?release=currentRelease&filename=Chapter%2030.
- “EU‑ or Japan‑origin”: Country of origin determined under U.S. non‑preferential rules of origin. Link: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-19/chapter-I/part-102.
- “Tariff” and “ad valorem”: A duty assessed as a percentage of customs value. Links: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tariff and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ad_valorem_tax.
- “Official instrument” and “published”: Content posted on official U.S. government sites (e.g., federalregister.gov, whitehouse.gov, cbp.gov, ustr.gov, commerce.gov) that is public by the resolution time.

Verification guidance for resolvers:
- Check Federal Register notices implementing EU or Japan frameworks and any subsequent amendments for explicit pharmaceutical 15% cap language or HTSUS headings that produce a 15% ceiling.
- Review White House presidential actions and Executive Orders that might modify reciprocal tariffs or sectoral treatment.
- Review CBP CSMS bulletins/guidance for tariff application instructions to Chapter 30 entries from EU or Japan (note: existing CSMS already exempts generics but does not constitute a broad cap).
- Cross‑check credible reporting only as confirmation of official issuance (e.g., Reuters/CNN), but the resolution requires the instrument itself to meet the explicit cap standard; statements of intent alone do not qualify.

Edge cases:
- If multiple instruments exist and one meets the explicit cap standard, resolve “Yes,” even if others are silent or conflicting.
- If an instrument establishes a 15% ceiling for only EU or only Japan pharmaceutical products, resolve “Yes.”
- If an instrument caps only a subset of Chapter 30 (e.g., specific headings) and leaves others above 15%, resolve “No.”
- If an instrument provides exemptions or zero reciprocal tariffs for generic pharmaceuticals only, with no cap on branded/patented products, resolve “No”.

question: At the 40th OPEC and non-OPEC Ministerial Meeting on 30 November 2025, will OPEC+ announce an increase in group oil production for December 2025 versus November 2025?
background:
Definitions and scope
- OPEC+: For this question, “OPEC+” refers to the grouping of OPEC members together with cooperating non-OPEC oil-producing countries that coordinate policy under the Declaration of Cooperation (DoC). See OPEC’s description of the OPEC and non-OPEC Participating Countries in the DoC and the ONOMM context, and a concise overview of OPEC/OPEC+ on Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OPEC).
- OPEC and non-OPEC Ministerial Meeting (ONOMM): The ONOMM is the ministerial-level meeting of the OPEC and non-OPEC Participating Countries in the DoC at which collective production policy decisions are announced via official OPEC press releases ("Press Releases" page: https://www.opec.org/press-releases.html). The 40th ONOMM is scheduled to be held on 30 November 2025, as stated in the 39th ONOMM press release.
- Group oil production increase (for resolution): An “increase … for December 2025 versus November 2025” means the official ONOMM outcome states that OPEC+ will set or adjust the group’s oil production/quotas upward for December 2025 relative to November 2025. This can be expressed in the press release with phrases such as “increase,” “raise,” or “adjust upward” of quotas/production for December as compared with November, whether decided group-wide or via recognized country-level adjustments announced in the ONOMM context.

Status quo as of today (to inform forecasting)
- Meeting timing: The 39th ONOMM (May 28, 2025) confirmed that the 40th ONOMM will be held on November 30, 2025. OPEC posts ONOMM outcomes on its Press Releases page, which serves as the authoritative public record of such decisions.
- Current production policy context: Reporting in late September 2025 indicates OPEC+ reversed its strategy of output cuts beginning in April 2025 and has already raised quotas by more than 2.5 million barrels per day (roughly 2.4% of world demand). Eight producers have been unwinding specific layers of cuts, including a 137,000 bpd increase for October and consideration of at least another 137,000 bpd increase for November, with discussion of potentially larger November hikes in the 274,000–411,000 bpd range. Some reports mention even larger figures being floated but characterized as inaccurate by OPEC+ sources.
- Monitoring and implementation: The Joint Ministerial Monitoring Committee (JMMC) reviews adherence to ONOMM decisions and additional voluntary adjustments and has continued to request compensation plans from underperforming participants; its 62nd meeting was scheduled for 1 October 2025. JMMC communiqués reference the decisions of the Dec 5, 2024 ONOMM and subsequent voluntary adjustments by some members, framing the implementation context for 2025 policy.

Why this could be uncertain
- As of late September 2025, the alliance has been increasing output, but whether it will explicitly announce a further month-on-month increase for December 2025 at the November 30 ONOMM remains uncertain and depends on demand, inventory, compliance, and macro/geopolitical conditions. Pre-meeting reporting highlighted potential further changes for November, but December guidance was not fixed as of the reporting cited above, leaving room for either a December increase or a hold/decline.
resolution_criteria:
Question: At the 40th OPEC and non-OPEC Ministerial Meeting (ONOMM) held on 30 November 2025, will OPEC+ announce an increase in group oil production for December 2025 versus November 2025?

Eligible time window
- Events and sources must occur between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. The meeting itself is scheduled for 30 November 2025 as per OPEC’s 39th ONOMM press release.

Primary resolution source
- The official OPEC press release communicating the outcome of the 40th ONOMM, published on OPEC’s Press Releases page (https://www.opec.org/press-releases.html). This page is where ONOMM outcomes are posted and serves as the authoritative record. If OPEC publishes multiple items on that date, use the item explicitly titled for the 40th OPEC and non-OPEC Ministerial Meeting (ONOMM).

What counts as “announce an increase … for December 2025 versus November 2025”
- Resolve Yes if the 40th ONOMM press release explicitly states that the group will increase oil production/quotas for December 2025 relative to November 2025. Accept phrasing such as “increase,” “raise,” or “adjust upward” for December compared with November, whether as a group-wide decision or via recognized adjustments announced in the ONOMM context that are applicable to December (e.g., language that monthly step-ups extend into December).
- Resolve No if the press release states that December 2025 production/quotas are unchanged versus November 2025, reduced, deferred to a later date without specifying a December increase, or if it does not mention any December 2025 increase relative to November 2025.

Fallback resolution (only if the OPEC press release is not sufficiently specific about December vs November)
- If the 40th ONOMM press release does not clearly specify December 2025 versus November 2025, resolve based on consistent reporting by at least two of the following credible outlets: Reuters, Associated Press (AP), and Bloomberg. The outcome must state that the ONOMM decided to raise December 2025 production/quotas relative to November 2025. If no such consistent reporting exists by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, resolve No. Reuters is cited here as an example of the kind of reporting this refers to.

Edge cases and clarifications
- If the ONOMM is postponed or canceled and no official OPEC press release or credible media reporting by the outlets listed above indicates that a December 2025 increase versus November 2025 was decided by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, resolve No.
- “OPEC+” and “ONOMM” are used as defined above; the ONOMM consists of the OPEC and non-OPEC Participating Countries in the DoC. The 39th ONOMM press release provides the formal context and scheduling reference for the 40th ONOMM.
- This question does not require calculating aggregate barrels per day. Resolution depends on the presence or absence of an explicit announcement (as defined) in the specified sources. If both increases and decreases for different members are announced but the sources do not state that the group’s December level is higher than November’s, resolve No.
- All dates/times are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

question: Between 2025-01-01 and 2025-12-31 (UTC), will the European Union designate “State Atomic Energy Corporation Rosatom” under Council Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 (Annex I asset-freeze list)?
background:
Context and definitions a forecaster needs to know as of 2025-09-30:

- What is Rosatom? “State Atomic Energy Corporation Rosatom” is Russia’s state corporation for nuclear energy (Russian: Государственная корпорация по атомной энергии «Росатом»). Common English aliases include Rosatom, Rosatom State Nuclear Energy Corporation, and Rosatom State Corporation. See Wikipedia for a reference overview: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosatom.

- EU legal mechanism in scope: Council Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 establishes asset freezes and prohibitions on making funds and economic resources available to listed natural and legal persons in connection with Russia’s actions in Ukraine. Designated persons and entities appear in Annex I, and listings are enacted by Council Implementing Regulations/Decisions published in the Official Journal (OJ). Key features of the measures and the role of Annex I are summarized in the consolidated text as of 2025-05-15: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02014R0269-20250515.

- Status quo for this question: As of 2025-05-15, Rosatom was not listed in Annex I of Regulation 269/2014 in the EU consolidated text, i.e., it was not under EU asset freeze measures pursuant to that regulation. In a May 20, 2025 OJ act listing additional individuals, Rosatom was mentioned in the narrative for a listed person but Rosatom itself was not designated in that act. Members of the European Parliament formally asked the Commission in mid-2025 about sanctioning Rosatom and its subsidiary Atomflot, indicating ongoing political debate and that Rosatom remained unsanctioned at EU level under asset-freeze listings at that time: https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/E-10-2025-002927_EN.html.

- Relevant background on EU reliance and constraints: The EU has historically depended on Russian nuclear fuel cycle services. Parliamentary and policy analyses quantify this dependence and ongoing diversification:
  • In 2024, Russia met about 23% of the EU’s total demand for uranium conversion services and 24% for enrichment services; in 2023, 23.5% of uranium consumed in the EU came from Russia and 30.1% of the EU fleet’s uranium was enriched by Russia. An EP report also notes 18 reactors of Russian/Soviet design in five EU countries and reiterates political calls to avoid new engagements with Rosatom: https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/A-10-2025-0121_EN.html.
  • A Bruegel analysis (2025) frames 2023 reliance at roughly 27% of EU conversion and 38% of enrichment services and details capacity-expansion plans by Western suppliers (Orano, Urenco, Cameco/Westinghouse) and contract/legal constraints that affect sanction design, emphasizing that independence from Russian enrichment will take years: https://www.bruegel.org/analysis/ending-european-union-imports-russian-uranium.
  • NGO reporting indicates EU and US purchases of Russian enriched uranium and nuclear fuel fell markedly in 2024 (e.g., EU low-enriched uranium imports <100 t for the first 10 months), reflecting stockpiling in 2023 and accelerated diversification; France remained a key buyer but also reduced volumes: https://bellona.org/news/nuclear-issues/2025-01-eu-and-us-reduce-russian-uranium-and-nuclear-fuel-purchases-in-2024.

- Why this is forecast-relevant: Whether the EU designates Rosatom under 269/2014 before year-end 2025 depends on evolving political alignment within the Council, security/foreign policy developments, legal feasibility (e.g., long-term contracts, force majeure considerations), and the pace of diversification away from Russian services—all of which remain uncertain as of today.

Notes on scope: This question is intentionally limited to designation under Regulation 269/2014’s Annex I (asset freeze). Other EU restrictive measures in Regulation 833/2014 (sectoral/transactional restrictions) or any national measures are out of scope for resolution. The subject is the parent legal person “State Atomic Energy Corporation Rosatom” only; listings of subsidiaries or individuals do not, by themselves, satisfy this question unless the parent entity itself is designated in Annex I of 269/2014.
resolution_criteria:
What must happen to resolve “Yes”:
- Between 2025-01-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC (inclusive), the EU publishes in the Official Journal a Council Implementing Regulation and/or Council Decision that adds the legal person “State Atomic Energy Corporation Rosatom” (including aliases: “Rosatom,” “Rosatom State Nuclear Energy Corporation,” “Rosatom State Corporation,” and the Russian name Государственная корпорация по атомной энергии «Росатом») to Annex I of Council Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 (asset-freeze list). Verification source: EUR-Lex entry for Regulation 269/2014 and/or the specific OJ act that amends Annex I. See the consolidated text describing the Annex I listing mechanism and measures. See the most recent consolidated Annex I as of mid-2025 (which did not yet include Rosatom) for baseline comparison.

What does NOT count:
- Any EU or Member State announcement, press release, draft, proposal, or leaked list without publication in the Official Journal does not count.
- Designation of any Rosatom subsidiaries or affiliates alone, or port/sectoral restrictions under other legal bases (e.g., Regulation 833/2014), does not count unless the parent legal person “State Atomic Energy Corporation Rosatom” itself appears in Annex I to Regulation 269/2014.

How to resolve:
- Primary check: On or after 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC, and no later than 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, search EUR-Lex for the latest consolidated version of Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 and Annex I, or identify any Implementing Regulation/Decision in 2025 that amends Annex I. If “State Atomic Energy Corporation Rosatom” (or an accepted alias above) is included as a designated legal person, resolve “Yes”; otherwise resolve “No”.

- If there is any ambiguity in naming, accept official aliases consistent with authoritative references (e.g., English and Russian names listed on Rosatom’s Wikipedia entry) when matched to the EU listing text: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosatom.

Timing and timezone:
- Event window: 2025-01-01 00:00:00 UTC to 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC (inclusive).
- Resolution window: The question will be resolved no earlier than 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and no later than 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Resolution sources (non-exhaustive but preferred):
- EUR-Lex landing page for Regulation 269/2014 and its consolidated texts/implementing acts: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2014/269/oj/eng.
- Any specific 2025 Council Implementing Regulation/Decision in the OJ that amends Annex I (e.g., searchable via EUR-Lex by date). For baseline confirmation that Rosatom was not listed in Annex I as of 2025-05-15, see the consolidated text.

Edge cases:
- If Rosatom is listed and then delisted within the event window, the question resolves “Yes” (listing occurred). If listed before 2025-01-01 UTC, it would not count unless a new, distinct listing adding the parent entity occurs again within the 2025 window.
- Subsidiary-only listings do not count unless the parent entity is explicitly designated in Annex I.

question: By November 30, 2025, will either Canada Post or CUPW publish an official announcement of a tentative agreement for the Urban Postal Operations or the Rural and Suburban Mail Carriers (RSMC) bargaining unit?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30:
- On September 25, 2025, the Canadian Union of Postal Workers (CUPW) launched a nationwide strike. Canada Post stated that operations would shut down during the strike, that mail and parcels would not be processed or delivered, that some post offices would close, and that scheduled pickups were cancelled, with service guarantees suspended.
- On the same day, the Government of Canada instructed Canada Post to begin a transformation, citing an “existential crisis” driven by sustained losses and declining mail volumes. The government stated that since 2018 the corporation has accumulated more than $5 billion in losses, that it lost over $1 billion in 2024, and that it was on track to lose close to $1.5 billion in 2025; it also noted a $1‑billion federal cash injection earlier in 2025 and about $10 million in daily losses, with Q2 2025 being the worst quarterly result at a $407‑million loss.
- Canada Post reported a loss before tax of $407 million for Q2 2025, with substantial declines in Parcels and other revenues; cumulatively from 2018 to Q2 2025, it reported more than $4.2 billion in losses before taxes and over $5 billion in cumulative losses from operations.
- For 2024, Canada Post recorded a loss before tax of $841 million (its seventh consecutive annual loss). The 32‑day national strike in late 2024 contributed an estimated net negative impact of $208 million, with lingering effects into 2025 as customers did not fully return.
- Canada Post maintains an actively updated negotiations hub for CUPW-related labour updates (canadapost.ca/negotiations). CUPW maintains a dedicated "Negotiations Update Bulletins" page for Urban and RSMC negotiations (2023–2025).
- Bargaining units covered by this question:
  • Urban Postal Operations (UPO): CUPW’s Urban unit includes letter carriers, mail service couriers, postal clerks, mail handlers, dispatchers, technicians, mechanics, electricians and electronic technicians working in Canada Post facilities.
  • Rural and Suburban Mail Carriers (RSMC): RSMCs deliver mail in rural and suburban areas and constitute a CUPW-represented bargaining unit at Canada Post.

Why this is forecastable and meaningful: A tentative agreement announcement for either the Urban or RSMC unit would be a major step toward resolving the 2025 labour dispute and restoring service. Given the ongoing strike, financial pressures, and government-directed transformation, such an announcement is plausible but uncertain within the specified timeframe.
resolution_criteria:
Question: Will either Canada Post or CUPW publish an official announcement of a tentative agreement for either (a) the Urban Postal Operations (UPO) bargaining unit or (b) the Rural and Suburban Mail Carriers (RSMC) bargaining unit between 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-11-30 23:59:59 UTC?

Definitions and scope:
- Canada Post: The Crown corporation that provides postal service in Canada (announcement must appear on its official domain, canadapost-postescanada.ca). Primary resolution sources include the Canada Post negotiations hub and linked updates (https://www.canadapost-postescanada.ca/cpc/en/our-company/news-and-media/corporate-news/negotiations-list.page). Corporate news releases on the same domain are also acceptable if they explicitly announce a tentative agreement.
- CUPW: The Canadian Union of Postal Workers (announcement must appear on cupw.ca). Primary resolution source includes CUPW’s Negotiations Update Bulletins for Urban and RSMC (https://www.cupw.ca/en/collective-agreements/urban-and-rsmc-negotiations-2023-2025/negotiations-update-bulletins).
- Urban Postal Operations (UPO) bargaining unit: CUPW-represented Canada Post employees in roles such as letter carriers, mail service couriers, postal clerks, mail handlers, dispatchers, technicians, mechanics, electricians, and electronic technicians.
- Rural and Suburban Mail Carriers (RSMC) bargaining unit: CUPW-represented carriers delivering in rural and suburban areas.
- Tentative agreement: For this question, an official announcement explicitly using one of the following terms referring to a new collective agreement for the UPO or RSMC unit: “tentative agreement,” “memorandum of agreement,” “memorandum of settlement,” “MOA,” or “MOS.” French equivalents such as “entente de principe,” “protocole d’entente,” or “protocole de règlement” also qualify if clearly referring to a new collective agreement for the specified unit(s). Ratification is not required for a Yes resolution.
- Official announcement: A public-facing post on one of the official sources above. Social media posts, media leaks, interviews, or third-party reporting do not count unless mirrored in an eligible post on the specified official domains.

Inclusions:
- An eligible announcement may pertain to either UPO or RSMC; an announcement for either unit is sufficient for a Yes resolution. If both units are covered in one announcement, it also counts.
- The announcement may be jointly or separately posted by Canada Post and/or CUPW. Only one posting by either party is required.

Exclusions (do NOT count):
- Announcements limited to return-to-work protocols, back-to-work legislation, mediator/fact-finder appointments or reports, “best and final offers,” “agreement to continue bargaining,” “framework for discussions,” or other process updates without an explicit tentative agreement/MOA/MOS for the UPO or RSMC collective agreement.
- Agreements for other CUPW units or non-CUPW bargaining units.

Timing and time zone:
- Eligible window: 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC through 2025-11-30 23:59:59 UTC. Publication time is determined by the timestamp on the eligible webpage in its local time converted to UTC, or if ambiguous/undated, by confirmation that the page was publicly accessible on the eligible domain within the window, as evidenced by standard site timestamps or a public web archive snapshot within the window.

Resolution:
- Resolve Yes if at least one eligible official announcement meeting the above criteria is published within the window.
- Resolve No otherwise (i.e., if no such announcement is published by 2025-11-30 23:59:59 UTC). The question may be resolved as No on 2025-12-01 00:00:00 UTC after verifying the absence of an eligible announcement.

Primary resolution sources (examples):
- Canada Post negotiations hub and linked posts: https://www.canadapost-postescanada.ca/cpc/en/our-company/news-and-media/corporate-news/negotiations-list.page.
- CUPW Negotiations Update Bulletins (Urban & RSMC 2023–2025): https://www.cupw.ca/en/collective-agreements/urban-and-rsmc-negotiations-2023-2025/negotiations-update-bulletins.

Status quo context sources (for forecasters):
- Canada Post strike operations update, Sept 25, 2025.
- Government direction to transform Canada Post and loss figures.
- Canada Post Q2 2025 financial results.
- Canada Post 2024 loss and impact of 2024 strike.
- Unit definitions: UPO ; RSMC.

question: Between 2025-10-15 and 2025-12-31 (UTC), will Stem, Inc. file or disclose a registered public offering of equity or equity-linked securities?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-09-30: Stem, Inc. (NYSE: STEM; SEC CIK 0001758766) reported cash and cash equivalents of $40.8 million as of June 30, 2025. The company implemented a 1-for-20 reverse stock split effective at 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on June 23, 2025, citing a goal to regain NYSE minimum average closing price compliance; the common stock began trading on a split-adjusted basis the same day, and authorized shares were reduced from 500,000,000 to 250,000,000.
