On June 30, 2025, Stem completed privately negotiated exchanges of its 0.50% Convertible Senior Notes due 2028 and 4.25% Convertible Senior Notes due 2030 into new Senior Secured PIK Toggle Notes due 2030 and warrants, along with $10 million in cash consideration; the transactions reduced outstanding debt and modified its capital structure. These actions suggest active capital markets management and make a further registered equity or equity-linked financing in Q4 2025 plausible.

Definitions and context for terms used in resolution:
- Public offering: Offering securities of a company to the public; generally intended to be publicly listed.
- Rule 424 prospectus supplement: Under 17 CFR § 230.424, post-effective prospectuses and supplements (e.g., 424B5, 424B3) must be filed with the SEC when used in offerings after a registration statement is effective; these filings disclose offering details such as pricing or substantive changes.
- Form 8-K: The SEC’s current report filed by public companies within four business days of significant events; it is commonly used to disclose entry into material definitive agreements, offering announcements, Regulation FD disclosures, and other material events.
- At-the-market (ATM) offering: A follow-on offering in which a public company sells newly issued shares into the market through a sales agent at prevailing prices over time.
- Equity-linked securities: Securities that can convert into, or provide rights to acquire, common equity. Examples include convertible bonds or preferred stock (which offer the holder the option to convert into common shares) , and warrants (rights to buy the issuer’s stock at a fixed exercise price).

Why this question has non-trivial uncertainty: Stem’s low cash balance as of Q2 2025 , recent reverse split to maintain listing , and debt exchanges  make additional capital raising plausible, but timing and market conditions create uncertainty about whether a registered public offering will be filed or disclosed in the specified window.
resolution_criteria:
Forecasting window: Events must occur between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC (inclusive).

Resolve Yes if any of the following is filed on SEC EDGAR by Stem, Inc. (CIK 0001758766) during the window:
- A prospectus supplement filed pursuant to Rule 424(b) (e.g., forms 424B5 or 424B3) for a registered primary offering in which the securities offered are any of the following: common stock; warrants (including pre-funded warrants); preferred stock convertible into common stock; or convertible notes/bonds. Rule 424 governs filing of post-effective prospectuses and supplements used in offerings [1b6d73; 9ab4fb; c57159].
- A Form 8-K that discloses the launch, pricing, or entry into a material definitive agreement (e.g., an underwriting agreement or sales agreement) for a registered public offering of any of the securities listed above, or discloses commencement of a registered at-the-market (ATM) equity program via a filed sales agreement and related prospectus supplement. Form 8-K is the SEC’s current report for material events, including offering-related agreements and disclosures [2ba2e5; 63a943; 1b6d73; 1209ca].

Clarifications:
- “Filed” means the acceptance timestamp on EDGAR for the relevant filing falls within the window.
- “Registered public offering” refers to offerings made to the public under an effective Securities Act registration statement and documented via Rule 424(b) prospectus supplements; announcements in Form 8-K must explicitly refer to a public offering or to entry into agreements for such an offering and/or reference the related prospectus supplement [1b6d73; 2ba2e5; 1209ca].
- The following do NOT satisfy the criterion: private placements of securities (e.g., unregistered sales disclosed under Item 3.02 of Form 8-K), equity grants to employees/directors, or filings that do not pertain to a registered offering (e.g., S-3/Shelf registrations without a corresponding Rule 424(b) takedown during the window).

Primary resolution sources:
- SEC EDGAR company filings for Stem, Inc. (CIK 0001758766): review Forms 424B*, 8-K filed between the start and end timestamps [2ba2e5; 1b6d73].
- As context for the type of offerings that qualify: definitions of public offering , Rule 424 prospectus supplements , Form 8-K , ATM offerings , convertible securities , and warrants.

question: Will the European Commission adopt an implementing act suspending monthly (EAGF) or interim (EAFRD) CAP payments to Greece between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01:

- Common Agricultural Policy (CAP): The EU’s CAP is financed by two funds: the European Agricultural Guarantee Fund (EAGF) and the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development (EAFRD). For general overviews, see CAP, EAGF, and EAFRD (Wikipedia): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_Agricultural_Policy, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Agricultural_Guarantee_Fund, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Agricultural_Fund_for_Rural_Development.

- Payment mechanics and suspension powers: Under Regulation (EU) 2021/2116 on financing, management and monitoring of the CAP, the Commission makes monthly payments for EAGF expenditures (Articles 20–21) and interim payments for EAFRD (Article 32). The Regulation also empowers the Commission to reduce (Article 39) or suspend payments in relation to annual clearance (Article 40), multi-annual performance monitoring (Article 41), and deficiencies in governance systems (Article 42). Key provisions include Article 21(3) for Commission implementing acts determining monthly payments; Article 32(1)–(2), (8)–(10) for interim payments; and Articles 40–42 expressly authorizing “implementing acts suspending” monthly or interim payments to a Member State.

- Greece’s recent situation: On 2025-06-17, the EU imposed a €392.2 million financial correction on Greece over mismanagement of agricultural subsidies for 2016–2022; Greece announced plans to overhaul its paying agency (OPEKEPE), including merging functions into the national tax authority (AADE), and the Commission decided to cut future subsidies by 5%. In mid-September 2025, the Commission warned Greece to submit a revised farm subsidy plan by October 2, 2025 or risk suspension of payments. As of late September, Greece’s paying agency OPEKEPE had informally halted disbursements for about three months, with €598 million owed to farmers for 2024 subsidies; the Commission’s deadline for the revised action plan was extended, and Greece must submit by November 4, 2025.

- Key actors and institutions: The European Commission (EU executive; Press Corner: https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/home/en; Directorate‑General for Agriculture and Rural Development (DG AGRI) newsroom: https://agriculture.ec.europa.eu/news_en) issues implementing acts and communications. OPEKEPE is Greece’s Payment and Control Agency for Guidance and Guarantee Community Aid (national “paying agency”). AADE is the Independent Authority for Public Revenue (Greek tax authority).

Why this matters for forecasting: The Commission has clear legal avenues to suspend monthly (EAGF) or interim (EAFRD) CAP payments if performance or governance deficiencies persist. Greece faces ongoing scrutiny, a recent record correction, and explicit Commission warning deadlines, creating meaningful uncertainty about the likelihood of a suspension event within Q4 2025.
resolution_criteria:
Resolution window and timezone:
- The observation period runs from 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC through 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. Only Commission acts adopted (or official statements published) within this window are eligible. Events before 2025-10-15 do not count, even if their effects persist into the window.

Definitions (for this question):
- European Commission: The executive of the European Union (see Wikipedia link in Background).
- Common Agricultural Policy (CAP): EU policy financed by EAGF and EAFRD (see Wikipedia links in Background).
- Monthly payments (EAGF): Appropriations made available via Commission monthly payments based on expenditure by accredited paying agencies, per Regulation (EU) 2021/2116 Articles 20–21. Commission determines these via implementing acts under Article 21(3).
- Interim payments (EAFRD): Reimbursements made by the Commission for CAP Strategic Plans via interim payments per Regulation (EU) 2021/2116 Article 32.
- Suspension (counts): An explicit Commission implementing act adopted under Regulation (EU) 2021/2116 that states monthly payments referred to in Article 21(3 or related) or interim payments under Article 32 are “suspended” for Greece, pursuant to Articles 40, 41, or 42 (e.g., “The Commission may adopt implementing acts suspending the monthly payments…” and “…suspending the monthly payments… or the interim payments…”).
- Exclusions (do not count): Reductions of payments (Article 39), interruptions of the time limit for interim payments (Article 32(10)), inadmissible declarations, national or agency-level de facto halts (e.g., OPEKEPE pauses), or press reports without an official Commission act/statement. A general EU-wide suspension not specifically applying to Greece does not count.
- Greece: The Hellenic Republic.

What resolves “Yes”:
- Yes if, during the observation window, the European Commission either:
  1) adopts and publishes on an official EU channel (e.g., EUR‑Lex or Commission website) an implementing act that explicitly suspends monthly payments (EAGF) or interim payments (EAFRD) to Greece under Regulation (EU) 2021/2116 Articles 40, 41, or 42; or
  2) publishes an official Commission press release/statement (Press Corner or DG AGRI newsroom) that explicitly announces such a suspension for Greece under Regulation (EU) 2021/2116, even if the implementing act’s EUR‑Lex entry is not yet visible, provided the statement clearly identifies Greece and specifies suspension of monthly or interim payments.

- Scope: A suspension applicable to any portion of Greece’s CAP monthly or interim payments (including partial or total suspension) counts as Yes. The decisive factor is the existence of an official Commission suspension decision targeting Greece, not its magnitude.

What resolves “No”:
- No if no qualifying suspension (as defined above) is adopted or officially announced by the Commission within the observation window.

Source of truth and how to verify within ~10 minutes:
- Primary: EUR‑Lex for Commission implementing acts (search by Regulation (EU) 2021/2116 and by Greece/Hellenic Republic in titles or preambles): https://eur-lex.europa.eu/; Commission Press Corner: https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/home/en; DG AGRI newsroom: https://agriculture.ec.europa.eu/news_en. If sources conflict, the text of the implementing act on EUR‑Lex prevails.

Edge cases and clarifications:
- Adoption date governs: If an act is adopted before 2025-10-15 but published during the window, it does not count. If only a publication date is available, use that date unless the text clearly states an earlier adoption outside the window.
- Reversals: A suspension adopted within the window counts even if later lifted within the window.
- Multi‑state acts: If a single act suspends payments to multiple Member States and includes Greece, it counts.
- Terminology: Only “suspension” per Articles 40–42 counts; “reduction,” “deduction,” “interruption,” “adjustment,” or other non‑suspensive measures do not.

question: Italy: Will the Unioncamere–Excelsior December 2025 “planned hires” (entrate previste) be ≥ 360,000?
background:
Context and status quo (as of 2025-10-01):
- What is being measured: Unioncamere and Italy’s Ministry of Labour publish a monthly Excelsior Informa bulletin that reports the national total of “entrate previste” (also referred to as “assunzioni previste”) for a given month. In the December 2024 release, they stated “Sono circa 356mila le assunzioni previste dalle imprese nel mese di dicembre” (≈356,000 expected hires in December) and dated the release 12 December 2024. The press release footnotes clarify scope: “Assunzioni con un contratto a tempo determinato superiore a un mese o a tempo indeterminato.” (Hires with a fixed-term contract longer than one month or an open-ended contract).
- Publication cadence and availability: The Excelsior monthly survey is continuous and fielded on a regular schedule. For example, the survey covering needs for November 2025–January 2026 was scheduled to be fielded from 25 September to 6 October 2025, evidencing ongoing monthly data collection into late 2025. Historically, the December bulletin/press release has been published in mid-December (e.g., 12 Dec 2024) , which supports timely resolution before year-end.
- Why this threshold: December 2024’s national total was approximately 356,000, close to the proposed 360,000 threshold, making outcomes on either side plausible and non-trivial.

Useful references (for context and where results are typically published):
- Excelsior portal: https://excelsior.unioncamere.net/
- Ministry of Labour news section (often mirrors Excelsior bulletins): https://www.lavoro.gov.it/pn-giovani-donne-lavoro/comunicazione/notizie
- UTC time definition (for resolution timestamping): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time
resolution_criteria:
Objective: Determine whether the nationally reported total of planned hires (Italian: “entrate previste” / “assunzioni previste”) for the month of December 2025, as published by Unioncamere/Ministry of Labour via the Excelsior monthly release, is greater than or equal to 360,000.

What counts as the metric:
- Use the national total for “Entrate previste nel mese di dicembre 2025” expressed in absolute values (v.a., headcount) as reported in the December 2025 Excelsior Informa monthly bulletin (Bollettino mensile) produced by Unioncamere and the Ministry of Labour. This is the same concept used in prior releases, e.g., “sono circa 356mila le assunzioni previste … nel mese di dicembre” and defined in footnotes as hires with a fixed-term contract longer than one month or an open-ended contract. The Excelsior monthly survey is continuous into late 2025, with fielding documented for the Nov 2025–Jan 2026 wave.

Primary resolution source (preferred, in order):
1) The December 2025 “Excelsior Informa” monthly bulletin PDF on the Excelsior portal (excelsior.unioncamere.net), using the exact integer shown for the national total “Entrate previste nel mese di dicembre 2025 (v.a.).” If both a monthly (nel mese) and a quarterly/trimestral total are shown, use only the monthly figure.

Fallback sources if the bulletin PDF is not publicly accessible by the deadline:
2) The official Unioncamere press release or Excelsior news item specific to December 2025 (on excelsior.unioncamere.net) that states the national total “assunzioni/entrate previste” for the month (e.g., analogous to the 12 Dec 2024 press release).
3) The Italian Ministry of Labour’s official news post summarizing the December 2025 Excelsior bulletin (on lavoro.gov.it), if it explicitly states the national total monthly figure.

Disambiguation and tie-break rules:
- If multiple documents are available, prefer the Excelsior Informa bulletin PDF (1). If unavailable, use (2); if (2) is unavailable, use (3) by the deadline.
- If only a press release/news item (2 or 3) is available and it states the national total as a rounded phrase such as “circa X mila,” interpret that as exactly X,000 for the purpose of this resolution. If it states an exact figure (e.g., 355.750), use that exact value.
- Ignore any figures referring to the three-month period (e.g., “dicembre 2025–febbraio 2026”); only the “nel mese di dicembre 2025” national total counts.
- If multiple versions are published, use the first version accessible by the deadline; subsequent revisions are ignored.

Timeframe and deadline:
- Eligible sources for resolution must be first published between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC (inclusive). The question resolves Yes if the qualifying national total is ≥ 360,000, and No otherwise.

Definitions and links for clarity:
- “Entrate previste” / “assunzioni previste”: monthly expected hires by enterprises, defined in prior Excelsior releases as hires with a fixed-term contract longer than one month or an open-ended contract.
- Excelsior monthly survey continuity into late 2025: documented fielding schedule for Nov 2025–Jan 2026 (25 Sep–6 Oct 2025).

question: Will China’s 1-year Loan Prime Rate (LPR) published for December 2025 be strictly lower than the 1-year LPR published for October 2025?
background: Context as of 2025-09-30: China’s Loan Prime Rate (LPR) is a key market-based lending benchmark calculated and published by the National Interbank Funding Center (NIFC) under authorization of the People’s Bank of China (PBOC). It serves as the pricing reference for bank lending, with two published maturities: one year and over five years. The LPR is fixed monthly: quoting banks submit quotes in 0.05 percentage-point steps; NIFC excludes the highest and lowest quotes, averages the remainder, and rounds to the nearest 0.05% to set the official LPR. Publication occurs on the 20th day of each month at 9:00 a.m., postponed if the date falls on a holiday (and, in practice, if the 20th falls on a weekend). PBOC’s English website routinely publishes monthly “Announcement on Loan Prime Rate” notices with the official values; for example, on 2025-09-22 it announced the one-year LPR at 3.0% and the over-five-year LPR at 3.5%, effective until the next release. Definitions and access: - Loan Prime Rate (China): see NIFC/CFETS overview pages (e.g., shibor.org) and PBOC notices for official definitions and mechanics. - One-year LPR refers to the LPR with a one-year maturity. - Official monthly values and archives are available via PBOC’s English site in the “Announcement on Loan Prime Rate” section. Additional links for context (non-binding): PBOC LPR announcements index: http://www.pbc.gov.cn/en/3688229/3688335/3883798/index.html; NIFC/CFETS LPR page: https://www.shibor.org/english/bmklpr/. Current status: The latest published one-year LPR at the time of writing is 3.0% (announced 2025-09-22), unchanged from recent months. This sets a clear baseline for forecasters assessing potential late-2025 moves.
resolution_criteria: Scope and time window: - Eligible publications occur between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. - The question compares the official one-year LPR published for October 2025 to the official one-year LPR published for December 2025. Terms and definitions (authoritative): - One-year LPR: The Loan Prime Rate with one-year maturity, calculated and published by NIFC/CFETS pursuant to PBOC authorization, based on panel bank quotes and rounded to the nearest 0.05%. - Publication schedule and timing: LPR is published on the 20th day of each month at 9:00 a.m. Beijing Time (UTC+8), postponed if the date falls on a holiday (and, if the 20th is a non-business day such as a weekend, to the next business day). When postponed, the next business day’s publication is the official monthly fixing. - “Strictly lower” means the December 2025 one-year LPR numeric value is less than the October 2025 one-year LPR numeric value (e.g., 2.95% < 3.00%). Both values are compared as published by the official sources; precision reflects the LPR’s 0.05% increment. Identification of the two fixings: - “October 2025 one-year LPR” is the value in the official LPR announcement published on or immediately after 2025-10-20 (Beijing Time), consistent with the monthly schedule. - “December 2025 one-year LPR” is the value in the official LPR announcement published on or immediately after 2025-12-20 (Beijing Time), consistent with the monthly schedule. Primary source of truth: - PBOC English website’s monthly “Announcement on Loan Prime Rate” pages (e.g., as exemplified by the 2025-09-22 announcement stating the one-year LPR at 3.0% and over-five-year at 3.5%). - If the PBOC English site is temporarily inaccessible, use the NIFC/CFETS LPR page(s) that define and publish the LPR and describe its monthly schedule. Fallback source (only if both primary sources are unavailable by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC): - Credible wire-service reporting on the monthly LPR announcement (e.g., Reuters, AP) citing the official one-year LPR values and dates for October and December 2025; use the earliest such report that clearly states the official values. Resolution: - Resolve “Yes” if the officially published one-year LPR for December 2025 is strictly lower than the officially published one-year LPR for October 2025. - Otherwise resolve “No.” - If either the October or December 2025 one-year LPR value is not published by the official sources and no credible fallback reports exist by the deadline, resolve “No” (non-publication prevents confirming a strictly lower outcome). Notes: - Timezone for publication references is Beijing Time (UTC+8). - If PBOC/NIFC modifies the LPR methodology or panel, resolution relies on the officially published one-year LPR values for those months regardless of methodology changes.

question: Will the U.S. property/casualty industry’s net combined ratio for the first nine months of 2025 be below 98.5%?
background:
Overview: This question asks whether the U.S. property/casualty (P/C) insurance industry’s statutory net combined ratio for the first nine months (year-to-date through September 30) of 2025 will be strictly less than 98.5%.

Key definitions and scope:
- U.S. property/casualty insurance industry: The aggregation of U.S. insurers writing property and casualty lines (i.e., non-life), as compiled in industrywide statutory reporting and used by standard industry reports. See “Casualty insurance” (scope of non-life) for context: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casualty_insurance. This question uses the scope exactly as defined by the selected resolution source (see Resolution Criteria); life/health-only entities are excluded.
- Combined ratio: A calendar-year underwriting profitability metric defined as (incurred losses + loss adjustment expenses + underwriting/operating expenses) divided by premiums earned, expressed as a percentage. A combined ratio below 100% indicates underwriting profit; above 100% indicates underwriting loss. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combined_ratio and the Insurance Information Institute glossary entry: https://www.iii.org/taxonomy/term/95/combined-ratio.
- Net combined ratio: Combined ratio computed on a net basis (i.e., after reinsurance), as reported by the source used for resolution. If the resolution source presents both direct and net figures, the net combined ratio governs.
- Timeframe measured: January 1, 2025 00:00:00 UTC through September 30, 2025 23:59:59 UTC (the “first nine months of 2025”).

Why this matters: The combined ratio is a central indicator of underwriting performance in P/C insurance. Shifts in inflation, catastrophe losses, prior-year reserve development, pricing adequacy, and expense trends can all materially influence the nine-month combined ratio. Forecasters should consider catastrophe activity through Q3, premium growth, and reported reserve development when forming a view.

Status quo and data cadence: Industry organizations routinely publish year-to-date (nine-month) results in late Q4. This question targets that commonly available nine-month statistic to ensure resolution before year-end 2025 without waiting for full-year final results, which are typically reported after year-end.
resolution_criteria:
Outcome: Resolve YES if the U.S. P/C industry’s net combined ratio for the first nine months of 2025 is reported as strictly less than 98.5%. Resolve NO if it is reported as greater than or equal to 98.5%, or if no qualifying figure is available by the deadline.

Primary source (preferred): An A.M. Best press release on news.ambest.com explicitly reporting the industrywide “net combined ratio” (or “combined ratio” where that term unambiguously refers to the industry’s net combined ratio) for the first nine months (nine-month, year-to-date through September 30) of 2025. The title typically references “First Look: Nine-Month 2025 U.S. Property/Casualty Financial Results,” but any A.M. Best press release that clearly presents the nine-month 2025 industry net combined ratio suffices.

Fallback sources (only if the primary source is unavailable by the deadline): A press release or report page from one of the following that explicitly states the U.S. P/C industry’s net combined ratio for the first nine months of 2025: (a) Verisk + American Property Casualty Insurance Association (APCIA) newsroom pages; or (b) S&P Global Market Intelligence research pages. If multiple fallback sources disagree, use a majority among them; if no majority, prefer Verisk+APCIA over S&P Global Market Intelligence. Links must point to publicly accessible web pages (not PDFs behind paywalls) published on or before the deadline.

Figure selection rules:
- Use the net combined ratio for the overall U.S. P/C industry (all lines combined). Do not use line-of-business subsets or accident-year-only adjustments unless they are clearly labeled as the industry’s net combined ratio headline figure for nine months 2025 by the selected source.
- If both direct and net are presented, use net. If multiple net figures are shown (e.g., excluding cats), use the headline overall net combined ratio that includes all items (i.e., not excluding catastrophe losses), unless the source clearly defines “combined ratio” to exclude them in the headline figure. Do not substitute accident-year ex-PYD metrics unless that is explicitly the headline “combined ratio.”
- Rounding: Compare the unrounded figure as stated by the source. If the source reports only to one decimal place, treat that as exact for comparison (e.g., 98.5% equals 98.5%). “Below 98.5%” means strictly less than 98.5 percentage points.

Timing and deadline:
- Eligible publications must be available on or before 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.
- If the primary source publishes multiple versions or revisions before the deadline, use the most recent version available at the deadline.

Edge cases:
- If sources report only a nine-month 2025 figure that is clearly an estimate subject to revision, use that figure as published by the deadline.
- If the selected source reports a range, use the midpoint for threshold comparison.
- If no qualifying source publishes the nine-month 2025 net combined ratio by the deadline, resolve NO.
- If the source’s scope definition differs slightly (e.g., inclusion of U.S.-domiciled P/C reinsurers), use the figure that the source labels as the overall U.S. property/casualty industry nine-month net combined ratio; do not attempt to adjust it.

question: Will the U.S. CPI‑U All Items 12‑month percent change for November 2025 be at least 3.2%?
background:
Definitions and context as of 2025‑09‑30:

- Consumer Price Index (CPI): A measure of the average change over time in the prices paid by urban consumers for a market basket of goods and services.
- CPI‑U (Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers): The broadest CPI measure, based on expenditure patterns of urban consumers covering over 90% of the U.S. population; it excludes certain populations such as rural non‑metropolitan areas, farm households, military bases, and institutions.
- Headline CPI in this question is defined precisely as the CPI‑U “All items” U.S. city average 12‑month percent change, not seasonally adjusted (NSA), as reported in the BLS CPI news release and Table 1. The BLS CPI news releases report the 12‑month percent change on a not seasonally adjusted basis [c88b58; see also Table 1 footnote indicating NSA ].

Status quo: In the latest published CPI Summary (August 2025 data), the CPI‑U “All items” index increased 2.9% over the last 12 months (NSA). Component details noted in that release include food +3.2% YoY, energy +0.2% YoY, and core (all items less food and energy) +3.1% YoY; with shelter +3.6%, used cars and trucks +6.0%, motor vehicle insurance +4.7%, medical care +3.4%, and household furnishings +3.9% YoY. The BLS also indicates a methodological change taking effect with October 2025 data (released November 13, 2025): removal of long‑term care (LTC) insurance from the health insurance index due to market changes making LTC out of scope for CPI pricing.

Release timing: The CPI for the November 2025 reference month is scheduled for release on December 10, 2025 at 08:30 AM Eastern Time (13:30 UTC). This comes from the BLS calendar of selected releases for December 2025, which lists the Consumer Price Index on that date/time, with times denoted in Eastern Time.
resolution_criteria:
Resolve Yes if, upon publication of the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) Consumer Price Index news release for November 2025, the CPI‑U All items U.S. city average 12‑month percent change (not seasonally adjusted) is reported as 3.2% or higher; otherwise resolve No.

- Measurement to use: the “12‑month percent change” for “All items” CPI‑U (U.S. city average), not seasonally adjusted, as displayed in the November 2025 CPI news release (the Summary text and Table 1). Table 1 in the CPI news release provides the 12‑month percent change for CPI‑U All Items and denotes that 12‑month percent changes are not seasonally adjusted. The BLS CPI site describes that the 12‑month change referenced in news releases is not seasonally adjusted. Definitions of CPI‑U and “All items” are per the BLS Handbook of Methods.
- Resolution timestamp: Use the value as published at the initial release time on December 10, 2025 at 08:30 AM Eastern Time (13:30 UTC). Subsequent revisions, if any, do not affect resolution.
- Primary source of truth: The BLS CPI news release for November 2025 on the BLS website (e.g., the CPI Summary page and accompanying tables accessible via https://www.bls.gov/news.release/cpi.htm). The release date/time for November 2025 CPI is scheduled for Dec. 10, 2025 at 08:30 AM ET.
- Term definitions applied in this question: “CPI” and “CPI‑U” per BLS definitions ; “All items” refers to the headline aggregate index covering all expenditure categories, as described in BLS methodology ; “12‑month percent change” is the year‑over‑year change in the index level, computed on not seasonally adjusted data as reported by BLS [c88b58; see Table 1 footnote: “Not seasonally adjusted.” ].
- Edge cases: If the November 2025 CPI news release is delayed beyond December 31, 2025 (unlikely for a principal federal economic indicator), resolve using the first BLS‑published November 2025 CPI‑U “All items” 12‑month percent change once available; if BLS fails to publish by December 31, 2025, adjudicators may reference credible wire services (e.g., AP, Reuters, Bloomberg) quoting the BLS figure when it is released. However, the intended and primary resolution source is the BLS CPI news release itself.

question: Between 2025-10-15 and 2025-12-31 (UTC), will the European Union publicly specify a target size of at least €120 billion for an EU “reparations loan” to Ukraine backed by immobilised Russian assets?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- Scale and composition of immobilised Russian assets in the EU: Of roughly $300 billion frozen globally, about €210 billion are held in Europe, with around €185 billion at Euroclear (Brussels-based central securities depository). Approximately €175 billion of these assets have matured into cash balances at Euroclear.
- Relationship to the G7 ERA loan: The G7 agreed an around €45 billion ($50 billion) loans initiative to Ukraine repaid by the extraordinary/windfall profits generated by immobilised Russian assets. The European Commission has begun disbursing its share (first €3 billion tranche) under this ERA framework, with repayment ensured via extraordinary revenues from immobilised Russian assets in the EU; EU envoys previously agreed on using these windfall profits (estimated €15–€20 billion by 2027, ~€3 billion in 2025) largely for Ukraine’s defense and recovery. European Council conclusions affirm assets remain immobilised until Russia ceases aggression and compensates Ukraine; they also note a 2025 EU financial commitment and ERA-related financing.
- The proposed EU “reparations loan”: The European Commission has floated a new, separate “reparations loan” to Ukraine, distinct from the ERA mechanism. Officials have indicated the loan could be “up to €130 billion,” contingent on IMF assessments of Ukraine’s 2026–2027 financing needs and agreement on guarantees and structure. Mechanically, the plan avoids outright confiscation: cash balances associated with immobilised Russian assets would be exchanged for EU-issued zero‑coupon bonds, likely via a special purpose vehicle (SPV), with guarantees provided by participating EU (and possibly G7) governments, and the risk carried collectively. Ukraine would only repay this loan after receiving reparations from Russia in a peace accord. The plan is also designed to bypass a potential veto by using an intergovernmental agreement among a coalition of willing EU members.
- Implication for sizing: After accounting for repayment of the ERA/G7 loans from the matured cash, officials estimate about €130 billion could remain as the basis for the EU “reparations loan.” Final sizing is expected to be decided only after IMF assessments and political agreement on guarantees and structure.

Definitions and scope:
- European Union (EU): The political and economic union of 27 member states; for resolution, “EU” refers to official communications by EU institutions (e.g., European Commission, European Council, European Parliament, EEAS) published on their official domains (e.g., europa.eu, ec.europa.eu, consilium.europa.eu, eeas.europa.eu).
- Official EU communication: A public, written communication issued by an EU institution and published on an official EU website, including but not limited to: press releases (e.g., Commission “Press corner”), European Council conclusions press releases, and published Commission proposal texts (e.g., on europa.eu or EUR-Lex). Media reports or leaks do not count.
- Reparations loan: For this question, the loan described by EU institutions whereby Ukraine receives financing backed by immobilised Russian central bank assets held in the EU, with repayment by Ukraine contingent on receiving reparations from Russia. The mechanism may involve transferring cash balances linked to immobilised assets to an SPV in exchange for EU-issued zero‑coupon bonds, with guarantees by participating governments; assets themselves are not confiscated.
- Immobilised (frozen) Russian assets: Central Bank of Russia assets immobilised under EU sanctions and held by EU financial market infrastructures (e.g., Euroclear), including securities that have matured to cash balances. Figures above reflect current estimates reported by reputable sources.
- Target size: Any explicit numeric euro figure published in an official EU communication that identifies the intended maximum envelope, ceiling, or nominal principal amount of the EU reparations loan (acceptable phrasings include “up to €X,” “envelope of €X,” “loan size €X,” “maximum €X”). If a range is stated (e.g., “€X–€Y”), the target size is interpreted as the upper bound (Y) for resolution purposes.
- Currency: Amounts must be stated in euros. If multiple currencies are provided, the euro figure governs.
- Timezone and window: Eligibility window begins 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and ends 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Why this is uncertain and interesting:
- As of 2025-10-01, the Commission and member states have not finalized guarantees, structure, or the IMF‑aligned sizing, with reported figures ranging up to €130 billion. Political dynamics (e.g., coalition of the willing vs. unanimity), legal risk management, and budgetary considerations could determine whether a specific target is publicly set within 2025. The threshold of €120 billion balances plausibility with uncertainty, given the indicative availability and the contingent nature of the plan.
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves based on official EU publications during the eligibility window.

- Start and end of eligibility window: From 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC through 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

- Resolution rule:
  • YES if, within the window, at least one eligible official EU communication (as defined) publicly specifies a target size for the EU reparations loan to Ukraine that is at least €120,000,000,000.
  • NO otherwise.

- Eligible sources include:
  • European Commission press releases published on the Commission’s Press corner (ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner) or other official europa.eu pages.
  • European Council conclusions press releases on consilium.europa.eu.
  • Official Commission proposal texts published on europa.eu or EUR‑Lex.
  • Official EEAS or Commission webpages hosting written speeches or communications, provided they include an explicit numeric euro figure and clearly relate to the reparations loan described above.

- What counts as “publicly specify a target size”: The communication must include an explicit numeric amount in euros that clearly denotes the intended maximum envelope, ceiling, or nominal principal amount for the reparations loan (e.g., “up to €130 billion,” “loan envelope of €130 billion”). If a range is given, the upper bound is used as the target size. Media articles (e.g., Reuters) are not used for resolution; they are background only.

- Ties/conflicts: If multiple eligible official EU communications within the window specify different figures, the most recent publication within the window governs. If no eligible official EU communication within the window specifies a numeric euro figure as defined, resolve NO.

- Verification guidance (examples of official sources used in background):
  • Prior reporting and official statements outline the loan concept, potential sizing up to ~€130 billion, and mechanism (SPV, zero‑coupon bonds).
  • Official EU materials confirm the distinct ERA windfall‑profit mechanism and initial disbursements, as well as Council positions on immobilisation and 2025 financing.

Notes:
- This question does not require that the loan be approved, disbursed, or legally enacted—only that an official EU communication within the window publicly states a target size meeting the threshold and refers to the reparations loan backed by immobilised Russian assets as defined.
- All times are UTC.

question: Will the IAEA Director General’s Iran report published between Oct 15 and Dec 31, 2025 (UTC) assess Iran’s stockpile of uranium enriched up to 60% at or above 450.0 kg (U mass)?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-10-01: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) Director General’s 3 September 2025 report (GOV/2025/50) estimated that, as of 13 June 2025, Iran’s total enriched uranium stockpile included 440.9 kg of uranium enriched up to 60% U‑235 (reported in kilograms of uranium mass, i.e., U mass). The report footnoted that 432.9 kg of this amount had been verified in the form of UF6. An independent analysis of the same IAEA reports notes this represented a 32.3 kg (U mass) increase in the 60% category since the prior reporting reference date (May 17). Reuters reporting on the confidential IAEA assessment the same day also cited the 440.9 kg figure for material enriched up to 60%.

Definitions and context: 
- Enriched uranium refers to uranium in which the fraction of the fissile isotope U‑235 has been increased via isotope separation; an enrichment level like “60%” denotes the percentage (assay) of U‑235 in the uranium.
- UF6 (uranium hexafluoride) is the chemical form used in enrichment; quantities in safeguards reports are commonly expressed as kilograms of uranium content (“kg (U mass)”), not the total mass of UF6. A known conversion exists between UF6 mass and U mass, underscoring that “U mass” refers to the elemental uranium contained in the compound.
- The IAEA’s Iran reports (e.g., GOV/2025/50) enumerate Iran’s enriched uranium stockpile by enrichment bands, including a line item for “uranium enriched up to 60% U‑235,” expressed in kg (U mass).

Why this should be high-entropy: With the last published estimate at 440.9 kg (U mass) for the “up to 60%” category and recent quarter-to-quarter changes on the order of tens of kilograms , plausible outcomes by year-end include increases (continued production), decreases (downblending, conversion, or removals), or stasis; external shocks (e.g., facility disruptions) also introduce uncertainty reported in contemporaneous coverage.
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves based on the figure for “uranium enriched up to 60% U‑235” in kilograms of uranium mass (“kg (U mass)”) as reported by the IAEA Director General in a report published on iaea.org between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. Primary target documents are the Director General’s Iran safeguards/verification reports (e.g., titled “Verification and monitoring in the Islamic Republic of Iran in light of United Nations Security Council resolution 2231 (2015)” and related Iran safeguards documents), as exemplified by GOV/2025/50. 

- Resolution: 
  - Resolve YES if the chosen IAEA report states a value greater than or equal to 450.0 kg for the stockpile line item “uranium enriched up to 60% U‑235” (kg (U mass)). Resolve NO if it states a value below 450.0 kg.

- Selection of source document within the window: If more than one qualifying IAEA Director General report on Iran is published within the window, use the one with the latest publication date/time (UTC) on iaea.org. If a report carries a publication date but appears on iaea.org later, use the IAEA document’s stated publication date. 

- Exactly what number to use: Use the numeric value in the report’s main stockpile breakdown for the line item labeled “uranium enriched up to 60% U‑235,” expressed in kg (U mass). If the report provides both (a) an estimated total for that line and (b) a smaller “verified” subset in a footnote, use the estimated total (the main-line figure), mirroring the presentation in GOV/2025/50 where the main text lists 440.9 kg and a footnote notes 432.9 kg verified. Do not convert units; rely on the figure as stated in kg (U mass).

- Category naming contingencies: If the exact label differs but the report provides a clearly corresponding category for material with assay up to and including 60% U‑235 (and distinct from any category above 60%), use that category’s kg (U mass) value. If the “up to 60%” category is absent but a specifically labeled “60%” category exists, use that figure. 

- If the IAEA has not publicly posted a qualifying Director General report by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, resolve using credible reporting that quotes the figure from the confidential IAEA report, with preference for Reuters, AP, or AFP; for example, Reuters contemporaneously reported the “440.9 kg” figure from the September 3, 2025 assessment. In such a case, use the figure quoted by the most authoritative of these outlets, prioritizing Reuters if multiple differ. 

Definitions for clarity: 
- “Enriched up to 60%” means an enrichment assay up to and including 60% U‑235 of the uranium content, consistent with IAEA stockpile banding and standard enrichment definitions.
- “kg (U mass)” means kilograms of the elemental uranium contained in the material (not the mass of uranium hexafluoride), consistent with safeguards reporting conventions and UF6-to-U conversion practice.

Source of truth (where to check on/after publication): The relevant IAEA Director General reports are published on iaea.org as GOV documents; for example, see GOV/2025/50 (dated 3 September 2025), which illustrates the exact stockpile line item and units used.

question: Will Telecinco’s monthly audience share (Ind. 4+, Total día) be ≥9.8% in November 2025?
background:
Context and definitions
- Telecinco is a Spanish free-to-air private television channel operated by Mediaset España (https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telecinco).
- Audience share (cuota de pantalla, “share”) is a measure estimating the percentage of households or viewers watching a program/channel out of the total with TV sets turned on during the broadcast (https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuota_de_pantalla). Barlovento’s glossary clarifies key terms used in their reports: “Cuota (Share)” is the percentage of viewers watching a program/channel out of total consumption, and “Total día” denotes the all-day time band defined as 02:30–26:30 (local).
- In Spain, Kantar Media is the official provider of TV audience measurement, using panels and audimeters to deliver person-based viewing data that the industry relies on. Barlovento Comunicación publishes monthly analyses of Spanish TV audiences based on Kantar data, with a long-running series (“Análisis Mensual del comportamiento de la audiencia televisiva”), typically released on the first day of each month on their publications page (https://barloventocomunicacion.es/publicaciones/). Their monthly PDFs include channel rankings and shares; for example, the December 2024 report lists channel shares (including Telecinco) and uses the “Ind. 4+” audience metric in sections like “Visión Global” and “RÁNKING CADENAS ABIERTO”.

Status quo (as of Oct 1, 2025)
- Telecinco recorded an 8.0% monthly share in August 2025, reported as a historical minimum for the channel.
- In September 2025, Telecinco’s monthly share was 9.2% (Ind. 4+, Total día), as reported across multiple sections of Barlovento’s September 2025 monthly report (“Titulares,” “Visión Global,” and “RÁNKING CADENAS ABIERTO”).

Why this threshold and month?
- November 2025’s monthly share will be published by Barlovento at the start of December 2025, enabling resolution before year-end while remaining close to current dynamics. Given Telecinco’s rebound from 8.0% (Aug) to 9.2% (Sep), a 9.8% threshold is plausible yet uncertain, creating a balanced forecasting target. Forecasters can incorporate expectations around programming changes, competition, and seasonal patterns while grounding estimates in the standard metric (Ind. 4+, Total día) and official reporting cadence.
resolution_criteria:
Binary Yes/No.

What exactly will be measured
- Metric: Telecinco’s monthly audience share (“cuota de pantalla”) for Spain, Individuals 4+ (“Ind. 4+”), Total día time band, as reported by Barlovento Comunicación based on Kantar Media data.
- Definition of terms:
  - “Cuota de pantalla (share)”: Percentage of households/viewers watching a channel out of those with TVs on during viewing (https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuota_de_pantalla) ; Barlovento glossary usage aligns with this and defines “Total día” as 02:30–26:30 (local).
  - “Telecinco”: Spanish free-to-air private TV channel operated by Mediaset España (https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telecinco).
  - Measurement/source: Kantar Media provides the official TV audience measurement in Spain; Barlovento publishes the monthly audience reports used for resolution.

Resolution rule
- The question resolves to Yes if Telecinco’s share for November 2025, listed for Individuals 4+ in the Total día scope within Barlovento’s monthly report (“Análisis Audiencia TV Tradicional | Noviembre 2025”), is greater than or equal to 9.8%; otherwise, No.
- Source document: Barlovento’s monthly report posted on their publications page (https://barloventocomunicacion.es/publicaciones/). Use the value shown for “Telecinco” (which may appear as “T5”/“Telecinco”) in the “RÁNKING CADENAS ABIERTO” (or equivalent channel ranking) table and/or “Visión Global” sections for November 2025. If multiple consistent listings exist within the same report, any of them may be used; if they differ, prioritize the value in the “RÁNKING CADENAS ABIERTO.”
- Precision/rounding: Compare the exact percentage as printed in the report (to the precision shown). “≥9.8%” means that values printed as 9.8% or higher meet the criterion. No independent recalculation will be performed.

Timing and scope
- Temporal scope of the measured month: Calendar month November 2025 in Spain; the underlying metric is “Total día” (02:30–26:30 local) aggregated across the month.
- Resolution deadline: As soon as the November 2025 monthly report is available (expected around Dec 1, 2025) and no later than Dec 31, 2025 at 23:59 UTC.

Notes and contingencies
- If the November 2025 report is posted in multiple versions, use the latest version available by Dec 31, 2025 23:59 UTC.
- If Barlovento’s site is temporarily inaccessible but the standard November 2025 report has been publicly released, resolution may wait until the document is accessible again within the resolution deadline. If the report is not publicly released by Dec 31, 2025 (unlikely given historical cadence), the market will be resolved as N/A and clarified to participants.

Examples and precedent
- Barlovento’s monthly reports include channel rankings and shares and use the Ind. 4+ metric; see the December 2024 report as an example of format/sections where Telecinco’s share appears. Recent performance benchmarks include Telecinco’s 8.0% share in August 2025 (historical minimum)  and 9.2% in September 2025.

question: Will China and Bangladesh officially launch negotiations on a bilateral Free Trade Agreement between 00:00 UTC on 2025-10-15 and 23:59 UTC on 2025-12-31?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01:
- In July 2024, during Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s visit to Beijing, official statements highlighted moving toward a China–Bangladesh Free Trade Agreement (FTA). China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs published a joint statement noting both sides would "conclude the joint feasibility study on a China-Bangladesh free trade agreement, and launch formal negotiations as soon as possible". The Chinese Embassy in Bangladesh subsequently stated the two sides "have concluded the joint feasibility study... and will launch formal negotiations as soon as possible".
- On March 28, 2025, a China–Bangladesh Joint Press Release underscored the importance of initiating FTA negotiations "at an early date". Reuters coverage the same day reported the joint press release emphasized starting negotiations on a China–Bangladesh FTA soon.
- As of late September 2025, Reuters reported that Bangladesh (along with Hong Kong, Sri Lanka, and Chile) is seeking to join the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), indicating broader trade-integration ambitions.
- On China’s official "FTA Network" (MOFCOM), the China–Bangladesh FTA appears under items documenting a "Joint Feasibility Study" rather than an active negotiating track, consistent with public statements emphasizing intention rather than a formal launch as of the dates cited above.

Definitions and key terms:
- Free Trade Agreement (FTA): An international treaty aimed at reducing or eliminating tariffs, quotas, and other trade barriers between signatories. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_trade_agreement.
- Official notice/press release: A publicly accessible announcement posted on an official government website or press page of the competent authority (see below). Acceptable websites include: for China, the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM: https://www.mofcom.gov.cn/ and the MOFCOM FTA portal https://fta.mofcom.gov.cn/) and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (FMPRC: https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/); for Bangladesh, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA: https://mofa.gov.bd/) and the Ministry of Commerce (MOC: https://www.commerce.gov.bd/). Announcements in English, Chinese, or Bangla are acceptable.
- Competent authority: For China, MOFCOM or FMPRC; for Bangladesh, MOFA or MOC.
- Official launch of negotiations (this question’s operative event): Any of the following, provided it is publicly announced by a competent authority (or reported by a qualifying wire service, see "Resolution sources"), explicitly referring to the China–Bangladesh "Free Trade Agreement" negotiations:
  a) A statement that negotiations "have officially launched/commenced/started" or are "formally launched"; or
  b) An announcement that the "first round of [China–Bangladesh FTA] negotiations" has been held.

Clarifications:
- Statements that merely express intent to negotiate or to start negotiations at an "early date" or "as soon as possible" do not count.
- Announcements concerning negotiations to upgrade or optimize a separate "Investment Agreement" do not count unless they also explicitly state the launch/commencement of FTA negotiations.
- Joint communiqués/press releases issued by both governments count if posted on an official government site (see above) and explicitly indicate the launch/commencement of FTA negotiations, or that the first round has been held.
- Media reports based solely on unnamed sources do not count. Social media posts are excluded unless they are posted by the official account of a competent authority and replicate the content of an official press release.

Why this is non-trivial: Both sides have repeatedly signaled intent to start FTA talks and have completed a joint feasibility study, but they have not publicly documented a formal launch as of the dates cited. Bangladesh’s exploration of RCEP accession in late 2025 adds nuance to incentives and timing.
resolution_criteria:
YES if, between 00:00 UTC on 2025-10-15 and 23:59 UTC on 2025-12-31, there is a public announcement by a competent authority (China’s MOFCOM or FMPRC; Bangladesh’s MOFA or MOC) on an official government website stating that China–Bangladesh Free Trade Agreement negotiations have been launched/commenced/started (or are "formally launched"), or stating that the first round of China–Bangladesh FTA negotiations has been held. Alternatively, YES if a credible international wire service (e.g., Reuters, AP, Xinhua) reports such an announcement based on those official statements. NO otherwise.

Examples that count (illustrative):
- "China and Bangladesh have officially launched negotiations on a bilateral Free Trade Agreement" (posted on MOFCOM, FMPRC, Bangladesh MOFA, or Bangladesh MOC websites).
- "The first round of China–Bangladesh Free Trade Agreement negotiations was held on [date] in [city]."

Examples that do NOT count:
- "The two sides agreed to start negotiations at an early date".
- "The two sides will launch formal negotiations as soon as possible".
- Announcements only about upgrading/optimizing an investment agreement.

Primary resolution sources:
- Official government websites: MOFCOM (including the China FTA Network), FMPRC, Bangladesh MOFA, Bangladesh MOC.
- Credible wire services: Reuters, AP, Xinhua. For context on prior official language and status signaling, see: FMPRC joint statement and embassy remarks in July 2024 ; the March 28, 2025 China–Bangladesh Joint Press Release  and Reuters coverage ; and Reuters’ September 25, 2025 report on Bangladesh seeking RCEP entry ; MOFCOM’s FTA Network entry noting the joint feasibility study status.

If conflicting reports arise, precedence is given to official government publications. If an official announcement is posted and later removed, archived versions or contemporaneous reports by the specified wire services will be accepted for verification.

question: On TRAC’s December 21, 2025 snapshot, will ICE’s total detained population be at least 60,000?
background:
Overview and status quo as of today (2025-10-01)
- What is ICE and who runs immigration detention? U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is a federal law enforcement agency within the Department of Homeland Security; ICE’s Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) component manages civil immigration detention and removals. In the U.S., immigration detention is a civil (not criminal) form of custody used during immigration processing and removal; it is distinct from criminal incarceration and is complemented by Alternatives to Detention (ATD) programs that monitor some individuals in the community.

- How is the “total detained population” typically measured? Journalistic guidance summarizing ICE data practices notes that the total detained population is counted as beds occupied at midnight on a single day (a snapshot), rather than, for example, an average across days.

- Public, regularly updated source for timely snapshots: The Transactional Records Access Clearinghouse (TRAC) publishes an Immigration Detention Quick Facts page that displays a single total for people “held in ICE detention,” labeled with “data current as of [DATE]”. As of late September 2025, TRAC reported: “Immigration and Customs Enforcement held 59,762 in ICE detention according to data current as of September 21, 2025,” and also reported 181,210 individuals monitored by ICE ATD programs as of September 20, 2025. TRAC additionally noted that 71.5% of the 59,762 had no criminal conviction, all using date-stamped snapshots. These details underscore that TRAC’s “held in ICE detention” figure is separate from ATD counts.

- ICE’s own public statistics: ICE publishes Enforcement and Removal Operations statistics and detention data products, typically on a lag (“one quarter in arrears”), and provides definitions focused on book-ins and detainee categorizations. These official dashboards are not guaranteed to publish a day-specific “currently detained” total for a selected date in December 2025 by December 31, 2025, which is why TRAC’s dated snapshots are favored for timely resolution.

Why this question and why this threshold?
- Detention utilization has risen in 2025, but week-to-week levels respond to enforcement intensity, border flows, available capacity, and legal constraints. TRAC’s late-September snapshot (59,762) sits near the 60,000 mark, making “≥ 60,000” a salient and uncertain threshold for a late-December snapshot. Forecasters can incorporate policy developments, seasonal patterns, and facility capacity dynamics when forming a view.

Key term definitions used for this question
- ICE: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, a DHS agency. ERO, a component of ICE, manages civil immigration detention.
- Immigration detention (civil): Custody for immigration control purposes (distinct from criminal incarceration), administered by ICE/CBP and often carried out in contracted facilities; some individuals may instead be supervised via ATD.
- Total detained population (for resolution): The single number labeled by TRAC as “held in ICE detention … according to data current as of [DATE]” on its Immigration Detention Quick Facts page; this excludes individuals on ATD (which TRAC reports separately).
- Snapshot: A single-day point-in-time count, conceptually measured as “beds occupied at midnight,” consistent with how such snapshots are commonly compiled and communicated in ICE-related reporting.
resolution_criteria:
Outcome: YES if the TRAC total for individuals “held in ICE detention” on the designated snapshot date is ≥ 60,000; NO otherwise.

Snapshot date and timezone
- Designated snapshot date: Sunday, 2025-12-21 (UTC).
- TRAC’s Quick Facts page displays “data current as of [DATE]” without a time; for this market, the resolver will match the calendar date shown on TRAC to the designated date. If the exact date is not shown, see fallback rules below.

Primary resolution source
- TRAC Immigration Detention Quick Facts: https://tracreports.org/immigration/quickfacts/ 
- Use the total displayed in prose as: “Immigration and Customs Enforcement held [N] in ICE detention according to data current as of [DATE]” (or equivalent wording on that page). Record N and the displayed [DATE].

Decision rule and fallbacks (applied in order)
1) Exact-date rule: If TRAC shows “data current as of 2025-12-21,” compare its “held in ICE detention” total to 60,000 and resolve accordingly.
2) Nearest subsequent-date rule: If no 2025-12-21 snapshot is displayed on TRAC by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, use the earliest TRAC snapshot with “data current as of” a date after 2025-12-21 and on or before 2025-12-31, and resolve based on that total.
3) Latest prior-date rule: If no subsequent snapshot exists by 2025-12-31, use the latest TRAC snapshot with “data current as of” a date on or after 2025-12-14 and before 2025-12-22 (i.e., the nearest available prior snapshot within the week preceding the designated date).
4) TRAC page unavailable fallback: If the Quick Facts page is inaccessible or lacks the total on 2025-12-31, use TRAC’s “What’s New” posts (https://tracreports.org/whatsnew/) that explicitly report the total “held in ICE detention” with a “data current as of [DATE]” label; apply the same date-selection logic as above. An example of the phrasing used by TRAC in such posts is: “Immigration and Customs Enforcement held 59,762 in ICE detention according to data current as of September 21, 2025”.
5) Last-resort official source: Only if no TRAC source meeting the above criteria is accessible on 2025-12-31, the resolver may use an official ICE detention statistics file/dashboards published at https://www.ice.gov/statistics that provide a clearly date-stamped, day-specific snapshot of “currently detained” for a December 2025 date according to ICE’s own labeling; if present for 2025-12-21 (preferred) or a date between 2025-12-22 and 2025-12-31 (nearest subsequent), or between 2025-12-14 and 2025-12-20 (latest prior), apply the same date-selection logic. Note: ICE indicates some statistics are published one quarter in arrears and may not include a day-specific current total; therefore ICE is a last-resort fallback only.

What exactly counts
- The figure must be the TRAC Quick Facts total for those “held in ICE detention,” which is distinct from TRAC’s reported ATD enrollment; ATD participants do not count toward the detained total for this question.
- Conceptually, the snapshot represents “beds occupied at midnight” on the snapshot date, consistent with how such daily totals are commonly counted; however, the operative value is exactly the total displayed by TRAC for its “data current as of [DATE]” snapshot.

Timing and accessibility
- All resolution steps and source checks must be performed no later than 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. Publicly accessible pages or files (including reputable web archives of the specified pages as they appeared by that time) are acceptable.

Tiebreakers and discrepancies
- If multiple qualifying sources are available (e.g., TRAC Quick Facts and a TRAC “What’s New” post for the same date) and they disagree, prefer the TRAC Quick Facts page for the final number. Only use ICE official statistics if no TRAC source satisfying the rules above is accessible by the resolution deadline.

Examples and current baseline (non-binding)
- Example of acceptable wording on TRAC: “Immigration and Customs Enforcement held 59,762 in ICE detention according to data current as of September 21, 2025”. As of that late-September snapshot, the total was 59,762 and 71.5% had no criminal conviction, while ATD monitoring stood at 181,210 as of September 20, 2025; these are included here only as context and do not affect resolution.

question: Will TCMB cut the one-week repo auction rate at its December 11, 2025 MPC meeting?
background: Context as of 2025-10-01: The Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye (TCMB) communicates monetary policy decisions via a “Monetary Policy Committee Decision” press release for each Monetary Policy Committee (MPC; Turkish: Para Politikası Kurulu, PPK) meeting, followed within five working days by a “Summary of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting”. The TCMB’s public calendar lists a Monetary Policy Committee Decision scheduled for December 11, 2025 and the corresponding Summary scheduled for December 18, 2025. The TCMB’s policy rate is defined in its decisions as “the policy rate (the one-week repo auction rate),” and decisions typically state both the previous and the new level of this rate. Recent policy stance: On July 24, 2025, the MPC “decided to reduce the policy rate (the one-week repo auction rate) from 46% to 43%”. On September 11, 2025, the MPC again reduced the policy rate “from 43 percent to 40.5 percent,” with the press release noting that the meeting summary would be released within five working days. These documents also illustrate the standard phrasing and structure TCMB uses when announcing changes to the policy rate. The December 11, 2025 MPC decision and its summary provide a clear and timely source to determine whether the policy rate is cut at that meeting. Definitions: • “Policy rate” means TCMB’s one-week repo auction rate as explicitly referred to in TCMB’s MPC decision press releases and meeting summaries. • “Cut” means any reduction in the policy rate relative to its level immediately before the December 2025 MPC meeting, measured as the difference between the pre-meeting policy rate and the policy rate announced in the December 2025 MPC decision. • “December 2025 MPC meeting” refers to the meeting corresponding to the Monetary Policy Committee Decision listed on the TCMB calendar for December 11, 2025; if TCMB officially reschedules the December MPC decision within December 2025, it refers to the meeting the TCMB calendar associates with December (see Calendar). Status quo datapoints included above come from the cited TCMB documents and calendar.
resolution_criteria: Yes/No question. Resolve YES if the TCMB reduces the policy rate (the one-week repo auction rate) at its December 2025 MPC meeting; resolve NO if the policy rate is unchanged or increased. Primary source of truth: the TCMB’s “Monetary Policy Committee Decision” press release for the December 2025 MPC meeting as listed on the TCMB calendar (the item scheduled for December 11, 2025). Operationalization: 1) Determine the “pre-meeting policy rate” as the policy rate level stated in the most recent TCMB “Monetary Policy Committee Decision” press release issued before the December 2025 MPC decision (TCMB decisions explicitly identify the policy rate as “the one-week repo auction rate” and state old and new values). 2) Read the December 2025 MPC “Monetary Policy Committee Decision” press release (scheduled for December 11, 2025 per TCMB’s calendar) and identify the announced policy rate level. 3) If the announced policy rate is lower than the pre-meeting policy rate, resolve YES; otherwise resolve NO. Backups and edge cases: • If the December MPC decision is officially rescheduled within December 2025, use the first “Monetary Policy Committee Decision” press release in December 2025 that the TCMB Calendar associates with the December MPC meeting. • If TCMB publishes an “Interim Monetary Policy Committee Meeting Decision” in December and the TCMB Calendar associates it with the December MPC actions instead of a regular decision, use that decision in place of the regular item. • If the “Monetary Policy Committee Decision” press release for the December 2025 MPC meeting is not available but the official “Summary of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting” for that meeting is published and unambiguously states the decision on the policy rate, use the Summary as the source. • If no TCMB press release or summary corresponding to the December 2025 MPC meeting is published by 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, resolve NO. Time bounds and scope: This question concerns only the decision associated with the TCMB’s December 2025 MPC meeting (scheduled for December 11, 2025 on the TCMB Calendar) and will resolve upon publication of the relevant TCMB document(s), which typically occurs on or shortly after the meeting date; the market close time zone is immaterial, and the evaluation cutoff for late publications is 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025. Exclusions: Changes to other TCMB rates (e.g., overnight lending/borrowing) do not affect resolution; only the policy rate (one-week repo auction rate) matters.

question: By December 31, 2025, will the U.S. federal government have finalized and publicly announced taking an equity stake in Lithium Americas Corp. (or an eligible Thacker Pass holding entity)?
background:
Context as of September 30, 2025:
- Negotiations and status: As of September 26, 2025, the Associated Press reported that the White House was “moving forward with a deal” for the U.S. government to take a small equity stake in Lithium Americas Corp. (LAC) but emphasized the deal was “not yet completed,” with a White House official describing the contemplated stake as “very small — less than 10%”. On September 23–24, 2025, Reuters reported the administration was seeking an equity stake of up to 10% in LAC while renegotiating terms of a roughly $2.26 billion Department of Energy (DOE) loan for the Thacker Pass project; Reuters additionally reported that LAC had offered the government no‑cost warrants equating to 5–10% of common shares as part of those talks [917570; c67a6].
- Loan and counterparties: The reported potential stake is tied to renegotiation of a DOE Loan Programs Office (LPO) financing package of about $2.26–$2.3 billion for Thacker Pass in Nevada, a project in which General Motors is a key partner; both AP and Reuters noted discussions among LAC, DOE/LPO, and GM, and that the equity element was under consideration but not finalized at the time of reporting [86d4d6; 917570].
- Project significance and market reaction: Reuters described Thacker Pass as the largest planned lithium mine in the Western Hemisphere and noted LAC’s shares surged on the news that Washington was considering a stake; these articles did not report a completed transaction as of September 24–26, 2025 [c67a6; 86d4d6].

Key definitions and links a forecaster may need:
- U.S. federal government: The federal government of the United States (executive branch departments and agencies, e.g., DOE, DoD, Treasury, or a wholly owned federal entity). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_the_United_States
- Lithium Americas Corp. (LAC): The publicly traded company that owns the Thacker Pass lithium project in Nevada via subsidiaries. Corporate site: https://www.lithiumamericas.com/; Thacker Pass overview: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thacker_Pass_lithium_deposit
- Equity security/equity stake: An ownership interest represented by securities such as common or preferred shares. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equity_(finance) and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equity_security
- Warrant: A derivative that gives the holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy shares at a set price before expiration; unexercised warrants confer no present ownership. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warrant_(finance)
- Primary resolution sources (where an official announcement would appear):
  • SEC EDGAR filings by Lithium Americas (e.g., Forms 6‑K/8‑K/10‑Q or prospectus filings): https://www.sec.gov/edgar/searchedgar/companysearch
  • Lithium Americas’ investor relations press releases: https://www.lithiumamericas.com/investors/news/
  • DOE Loan Programs Office announcements/newsroom: https://www.energy.gov/lpo/news
  • White House statements/press releases: https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
  • Major wire services (AP, Reuters, Bloomberg) reporting that explicitly cites/links to one of the above.

Status quo summary for forecasters (as of late September 2025):
- AP: “moving forward with a deal,” “not yet completed,” stake described as “very small — less than 10%.” Discussions involve restructuring a roughly $2.3B DOE loan; GM declined detailed comment during ongoing negotiations.
- Reuters: administration “seeking an equity stake of as much as 10%” while renegotiating a ~$2.26B DOE loan; LAC “offered the government no‑cost warrants” equating to 5–10% of common shares; first loan draw was delayed while terms were being renegotiated.
- Reuters market/industry context: Thacker Pass is described as the largest planned lithium mine in the Western Hemisphere; LAC shares spiked on the consideration of a stake; no completed transaction was reported as of Sept. 24, 2025 [c67a6].
resolution_criteria:
Question: Between 00:00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, will there be an official public announcement that a transaction has closed such that the U.S. federal government has acquired an equity stake in Lithium Americas Corp. (or an eligible Thacker Pass holding entity), with an effective closing date on or before 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025?

How this resolves:
- Resolve Yes if, by 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, there is a public, official announcement confirming that closing has occurred and that the U.S. federal government (as defined below) has acquired an equity security (as defined below) in one of the eligible entities (as defined below). The announcement must be published within the question window (Oct 15–Dec 31, 2025 UTC), and the closing/effective date must be on or before the cutoff.
- Resolve No otherwise (including if there is only an agreement in principle, a term sheet, or unexercised warrants/options; or if an announcement occurs after the cutoff; or if closing occurs but is not publicly announced within the window).

Definitions:
- U.S. federal government: The federal government of the United States, including any executive department or agency (e.g., DOE, DoD, Treasury) or a wholly owned federal entity and its nominees, but excluding state/local governments and purely private entities. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_the_United_States
- Eligible entities: (a) Lithium Americas Corp. (LAC), or (b) a directly controlled subsidiary or special‑purpose entity that holds the Thacker Pass project (e.g., Lithium Nevada Corp., or its legal successor), or (c) a joint venture vehicle directly holding Thacker Pass in which LAC is a member, provided the equity security is in that vehicle. Lithium Americas overview: https://www.lithiumamericas.com/; Thacker Pass background: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thacker_Pass_lithium_deposit
- Equity security/equity stake: Ownership interest such as common or preferred shares, units, or equivalent that confer present ownership as of closing, consistent with the concept of equity securities under U.S. securities law and standard finance usage. Unexercised options/warrants, SAFE notes, revenue‑share agreements, royalties, or purely debt instruments do not count until and unless they are exercised/converted and result in issued equity by the cutoff. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equity_security; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equity_(finance); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warrant_(finance)
- Publicly announced/official announcement: One of the following published within the window: (i) a company filing on SEC EDGAR (e.g., Form 6‑K/8‑K/10‑Q/prospectus supplement) explicitly stating the U.S. government (or named agency) has closed an equity investment in an eligible entity; (ii) a press release posted on Lithium Americas’ investor relations site explicitly stating closing of such investment; (iii) a DOE Loan Programs Office or other federal agency webpage/news release explicitly stating that closing has occurred and that the U.S. government has received equity securities in an eligible entity; (iv) a White House press release/statement explicitly stating the same. If none of (i)–(iv) are available, two or more independent major wire services (e.g., AP, Reuters, Bloomberg) directly citing/quoting one of the foregoing official statements or filings will suffice.

Inclusions and exclusions:
- Included: Any transaction structure that results in the U.S. federal government holding issued equity securities at closing (e.g., direct share issuance, share purchase, conversion of an instrument into shares) in an eligible entity by the cutoff and publicly announced within the window.
- Excluded: Unexercised warrants or options; non‑binding MOUs/term sheets; agreements contingent on future approvals without closing; revenue‑share, royalty, or offtake deals without equity; state/local government stakes; stakes in unrelated LAC subsidiaries that do not hold Thacker Pass.
- Disposals: If the government closes on an equity stake and later disposes of it before the cutoff, it still resolves Yes (closing occurred).

Resolution sources and verification priority:
1) SEC EDGAR filings by Lithium Americas naming the U.S. government (or specific agency) as having acquired equity (preferred). 2) Lithium Americas IR press releases. 3) DOE/LPO or other U.S. federal agency official pages. 4) White House press releases. 5) If needed, two or more independent major wire services (AP, Reuters, Bloomberg) that explicitly cite one of the foregoing.

Notes for forecasters (status quo cues):
- AP (Sept 26, 2025): White House “moving forward” but “not yet completed,” with the stake characterized as “very small — less than 10%,” tied to changes in a roughly $2.3B DOE loan; GM and DOE/Company indicated ongoing discussions.
- Reuters (Sept 23, 2025): Administration was “seeking an equity stake of as much as 10%,” and LAC “offered the government no‑cost warrants” equating to 5–10% to facilitate closing of a ~$2.26B DOE loan restructure; first loan draw was delayed amid renegotiation.
- Reuters (Sept 24, 2025): Thacker Pass described as the largest planned lithium mine in the Western Hemisphere; the stake was still under consideration; no closing reported as of that date [c67a6].

question: Will the FOMC cut the federal funds rate target range by at least 75 basis points cumulatively in calendar year 2025?
background:
Interest rates materially affect insurers’ and reinsurers’ investment income by changing yields on cash and fixed-income portfolios. The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) sets a target range for the federal funds rate, and changes (“cuts”) to this target range propagate through short-term rates, influencing portfolio returns. In 2025, market participants have debated the pace and extent of easing; the year has already seen at least one reduction, with additional meetings remaining in 2025. This question is framed to capture whether, in total, the FOMC lowers the target range by 75 basis points (bps) or more during 2025.

Key context and definitions forecasters may want to consult:
- Federal funds rate target range: The FOMC announces a lower and upper bound for the overnight federal funds rate; policy changes are reflected as equal-sized adjustments to both bounds. See the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy press releases: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary.htm
- Basis point (bp): A unit equal to 0.01 percentage points (e.g., 25 bps = 0.25 percentage points). See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basis_point
- Historical and current target range changes can be cross-checked via authoritative series such as the “Federal Funds Target Range – Upper Limit” on FRED: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DFEDTARU

Status quo as of 2025-09-22: The FOMC has maintained a restrictive stance for much of 2025 and has already lowered the target range at least once; further cuts in late-2025 remain possible and debated. Forecasters should reference the official press releases linked above for exact dates and magnitudes.
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves based on official FOMC monetary policy press releases published on federalreserve.gov.

- Time window: From 2025-01-01 00:00:00 ET through 2025-12-31 23:59:59 ET (inclusive).
- Definitions:
  - “Cut” means an FOMC decision that lowers both the lower and upper bounds of the target range for the federal funds rate, as explicitly stated in the press release.
  - “Basis points (bps)” are units of 0.01 percentage points.
  - “Cumulative cuts” means the sum (in bps) of all downward changes to the target range announced within the time window; increases within the window are ignored for this sum.
