Question: Will either the Government of the Russian Federation or the Government of the People’s Republic of China issue a qualifying public statement explicitly declaring non‑implementation of the reimposed UN Security Council sanctions on Iran between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC?

Operational definitions:
- Time window: Events must occur between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC (inclusive). All dates/times are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
- Reimposed UN Security Council sanctions on Iran: The sanctions set that came back into force at 0000 GMT on 2025-09-28 via the snapback mechanism under UNSCR 2231 (2015), following the E3’s 2025-08-28 notification and the Security Council’s failure on 2025-09-26 to pass a resolution continuing relief. This term refers specifically to UN Security Council measures reactivated under the JCPOA/2231 framework, not to separate US, EU, or other national/regional sanctions regimes.
- Qualifying public statement: One of the following, attributable to the national government of Russia or China:
  1) An official publication on a government or ministry website (e.g., Russia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kremlin; China’s State Council, Ministry of Foreign Affairs), or an official government gazette; or
  2) An official transcript from an on‑the‑record government press briefing or press conference; or
  3) A decree, order, policy document, or formal diplomatic note released by the national government; or
  4) A direct, on‑the‑record quote by a named senior official to a major international news wire (e.g., Reuters, Associated Press, Agence France‑Presse) explicitly stating the policy, where the quote is clearly about the UN Security Council sanctions reimposed via snapback.

- Senior official (for criterion 4): For Russia, includes the President, Prime Minister, Minister or Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs, official MFA Spokesperson, or Permanent Representative to the UN. For China, includes the President, Premier, Foreign Minister (State Councilor), Vice Foreign Minister, official MFA Spokesperson, or Permanent Representative to the UN.
- Explicitly declaring non‑implementation: The statement must unambiguously communicate that the country “will not implement,” “will not apply,” “will not enforce,” or “will not comply with” the reimposed UN Security Council sanctions on Iran as a set. Statements that only (a) assert the sanctions are “illegal,” “null and void,” or “cannot be implemented” in the abstract; or (b) merely indicate intent to continue specific trade without referencing the UN sanctions or implementation policy, do not qualify.

Inclusions and exclusions:
- Included: A blanket declaration that the country will not implement the UN Security Council sanctions reimposed via snapback (e.g., “We will not implement the UN sanctions reimposed on Iran under Resolution 2231’s snapback”).
- Included: A government policy document stating that the country will not implement the reimposed UN Security Council sanctions on Iran.
- Excluded: Statements that lack explicit reference to the UN Security Council sanctions reimposed via snapback; statements only describing the sanctions as unlawful without stating a non‑implementation policy; statements by sub‑national officials; unattributed media reports; anonymous sources; editorials; think‑tank reports; or statements limited to EU/US/national sanctions rather than UN measures.
- Language/translation: Statements in any language are acceptable. If the qualifying statement is not available in English, an official English translation is acceptable. If none exists, reputable wire-service translations (e.g., Reuters, AP, AFP) are acceptable.

Resolution rules:
- Resolve Yes if at least one qualifying statement (as defined above) by either Russia or China is made within the time window.
- Resolve No if no such qualifying statement is made within the time window.
- If multiple statements conflict, resolution is based on whether any statement meeting the inclusion criteria occurred within the window (conflicting later or earlier statements do not negate a qualifying occurrence).

Primary verification sources (non-exhaustive examples):
- Russia: Kremlin (http://en.kremlin.ru/), Ministry of Foreign Affairs (https://mid.ru/), Russia’s Permanent Mission to the UN (https://russiaun.ru/), and/or wire reports carrying direct quotes (Reuters/AP/AFP).
- China: State Council/central government portal (https://www.gov.cn/), Ministry of Foreign Affairs (https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/), China’s Permanent Mission to the UN (https://www.china-un.org/eng/), and/or wire reports carrying direct quotes (Reuters/AP/AFP).

question: By December 31, 2025, will Turkish Airlines announce a firm purchase agreement for at least 100 additional Boeing 737 MAX aircraft between October 15 and December 31, 2025?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-09-30:
- On Sept 25–26, 2025, Boeing and Turkish Airlines announced a firm order for up to 75 Boeing 787 Dreamliners. In the same communication, Turkish Airlines "announced its intent to purchase up to 150 more 737 MAX airplanes," explicitly framed as intent and "when finalized," not a firm order.
- Reuters reported on Sept 26, 2025 that Turkish Airlines had completed negotiations to buy 150 737 MAX planes, consisting of 100 firm and 50 options, but that placing the orders was "subject to the successful conclusion of discussions with engine manufacturer CFM International," with negotiations ongoing regarding engines and maintenance services. This indicates uncertainty about when any firm MAX order would be signed and announced.
- The Boeing 737 MAX family comprises MAX 7/8/8-200/9/10 variants, the fourth generation of the 737, and serves as Boeing’s current single-aisle product line.
- In aircraft procurement, an "option" gives an airline the right—but not the obligation—to purchase additional aircraft later at agreed terms; options differ from "firm orders," which are binding purchase commitments.
- Turkish Airlines’ official disclosures may appear on the Public Disclosure Platform (KAP), Turkey’s official electronic system for capital markets disclosures operated by MKK, which is a credible resolution source for corporate announcements.
- AJet is a wholly owned low-cost subsidiary of Turkish Airlines and has its own AOC; this context is relevant to whether any orders attributed to AJet should count as part of the Turkish Airlines group for resolution purposes.

Why this question has genuine uncertainty:
- There is clear intent and reported negotiation structure (100 firm + 50 options) for 737 MAX aircraft, but finalization depends on engine agreements and contract execution. Given typical complexities around engine selection, financing, and governance approvals, both Yes and No outcomes by year-end are plausible.
resolution_criteria:
Time window and timezone:
- Eligible announcements must occur between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

What resolves Yes:
- Resolve Yes if, within the time window above, a firm purchase agreement ("firm order") is publicly announced naming Turkish Airlines (Türk Hava Yolları A.O.) or its wholly owned subsidiary AJet as the customer for Boeing 737 MAX aircraft, and the cumulative number of such newly announced firm orders for the Boeing 737 MAX family is at least 100.

Definitions and counting rules:
- "Boeing 737 MAX aircraft" are those in the MAX 7, MAX 8, MAX 8-200, MAX 9, and MAX 10 variants (collectively the 737 MAX family). Boeing Business Jet (BBJ) variants do not count.
- A "firm order" is a binding purchase commitment between the airline (or its wholly owned subsidiary) and Boeing and must be described in the announcement as a firm order, a firm purchase agreement, or otherwise clearly indicate that it is not an MoU/LoI, mere intent, or option. Announcements that reference only "intent," MoU, LoI, or that are expressly contingent (e.g., "subject to engine talks") do not count until a firm purchase agreement is announced.
- "Additional" means firm orders newly announced within the specified time window. Orders announced prior to 2025-10-15 UTC do not count toward the threshold. Exercising previously documented options counts only when the exercise is publicly announced within the time window and results in additional firm orders (i.e., increases the airline’s firm commitments compared to the status as of 2025-10-15 UTC).
- "Attributable to Turkish Airlines" includes orders naming Turkish Airlines (Türk Hava Yolları A.O.) or AJet (a wholly owned subsidiary) as the customer; orders placed by third-party lessors (operating leases) do not count because they are not firm purchase agreements between the airline group and Boeing. If an announcement explicitly states that an AJet order is part of the Turkish Airlines group fleet plan, it counts under this criterion.
- Counting is cumulative across multiple qualifying announcements within the time window.

Resolution sources:
- Primary: Official announcements from Boeing (e.g., Boeing Newsroom/Investor News) and Turkish Airlines (Press Room) describing the deal as a firm order, or electronically signed company notifications on Turkey’s Public Disclosure Platform (KAP).
- Acceptable URLs to check include: Boeing Newsroom (https://boeing.mediaroom.com/), Boeing Investor News (https://investors.boeing.com/investors/news/), Turkish Airlines Press Room/News (https://www.turkishairlines.com/en-us/news-press-release/), and KAP (https://www.kap.org.tr/en/).
- Secondary corroboration (if needed): Reputable wire services (e.g., Reuters, AP) that explicitly state a firm order was signed and announced, with sufficient detail to identify the customer, quantity, and aircraft family.

What resolves No:
- Resolve No if, by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, the cumulative number of newly announced firm orders for Boeing 737 MAX aircraft attributable to Turkish Airlines (as defined) within the time window is less than 100, or if only intent/MoU/LoI/options/contingent agreements are announced without a firm purchase agreement.

Examples to illustrate:
- A Boeing press release on Nov 10, 2025 stating "Turkish Airlines places firm order for 80 737 MAX 8 and 20 737 MAX 10" counts (Yes if cumulative ≥100).
- A Turkish Airlines news post on Dec 20, 2025 saying "we intend to purchase 150 737 MAX subject to engine talks" does not count.
- A KAP filing indicating an electronically signed notification of a firm purchase agreement for 105 737 MAX aircraft within the window counts.

question: By 11:59:59 pm ET on December 31, 2025, will Anthem and Northern Light Health publicly announce an agreement that explicitly grants retroactive in-network coverage for Anthem commercial members for services rendered at Northern Light Health on or after October 1, 2025?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-09-30: Northern Light Health (NLH), a Maine-based health system, and Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield in Maine (Anthem) are in a contract dispute with staged out-of-network (OON) transitions if no deal is reached. NLH states that, for Anthem commercial plans (excluding Medicare Advantage), NLH physicians and some ancillary services (e.g., dialysis, home care & hospice, skilled nursing facility, urgent care, ambulance [facility and Northern Light Medical Transport], rural health clinic) will be OON effective 2025-10-01, while hospital-based services remain in-network until becoming OON effective 2025-12-31. Local reporting corroborates that if no agreement is reached, primary care and specialists become OON on 2025-10-01 and hospital care remains in network through year-end for commercial members; emergency room services remain covered at in-network cost-sharing regardless of contract status. The parties entered formal mediation in late August; in late September they exchanged public statements disputing who had walked away, but both indicated willingness to continue talks. Tens of thousands of patients are affected; contemporaneous reporting references roughly 30,000 Mainers as being in limbo regarding coverage during the dispute.

Key definitions (with sources):
- In-network/Network provider: A provider who has a contract with a health insurer or plan to provide services to members, typically at lower member cost-sharing; also called preferred or participating provider. Out-of-network provider: a provider without such a contract, typically leading to higher member cost-sharing. These definitions come from the federal Uniform Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms published by CMS/CCIIO (see: https://www.cms.gov/cciio/resources/forms-reports-and-other-resources/downloads/ug-glossary-508-mm.pdf).
- Network: The facilities, providers, and suppliers the plan has contracted with (as per the same Uniform Glossary).
- Anthem commercial plans: For purposes of this question, “Anthem commercial plans” refers to Anthem employer-sponsored and individual/family (non-Medicare) plans in Maine, as used by NLH in its official Anthem Insurance Notice; Medicare Advantage is explicitly excluded from the commercial category in NLH’s description.
- Ancillary services: For purposes of this question and consistent with NLH’s public notice, examples include dialysis, home care & hospice, skilled nursing facility, urgent care, ambulance (facility and Northern Light Medical Transport), and rural health clinic services.
- Retroactive in-network coverage (operational definition for this market question): A public commitment by Anthem and/or NLH that claims for covered services rendered by NLH providers to Anthem commercial members on or after 2025-10-01 will be processed as in-network (i.e., “at in-network benefits/rates/cost-sharing” or “as if in-network”) despite the providers’ out-of-network status at the time of service. Wording that is acceptable includes clear equivalents like “claims since October 1 will be reprocessed and paid at in-network benefits” or “treated as in-network,” but not vague statements lacking an explicit in-network equivalence.

Why this is forecastable with non-trivial uncertainty: In payer–provider disputes, some settlements include retroactive in-network provisions to protect patients caught during OON gaps, but this is not guaranteed. Given the staged OON dates (Oct 1 for physicians/ancillary; Dec 31 for hospital-based services), active mediation, public acrimony, and significant affected membership, retroactivity is plausible yet uncertain. Forecasters must weigh incentives (member disruption, political pressure, reputational risk) against contract economics and negotiating dynamics.

Useful primary sources for monitoring: 
- NLH’s Anthem Insurance Notice page (expected to update with status and any agreement): https://northernlighthealth.org/anthem.
- NLH Newsroom postings on negotiations/mediation: https://northernlighthealth.org/News/2025/Northern-Light-Health-seeks-mediation-with-Anthem.
- Credible local reporting likely to cover any agreement: Bangor Daily News and Portland Press Herald ; TV outlets like NEWS CENTER Maine have closely tracked the timeline.
resolution_criteria:
Question scope and time window:
- Event window for qualifying announcements: Any time from 2025-09-01 00:00:00 UTC through the deadline (see below). The market will remain open for forecasting but will resolve at the deadline.
- Resolution deadline and time zone: Resolves based on information available by 2026-01-01 04:59:59 UTC, which is exactly 11:59:59 pm Eastern Time (ET) on 2025-12-31.

Resolution rule (Yes/No):
- YES if, by the deadline above, Anthem (Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield in Maine) and/or Northern Light Health publish an official public statement that explicitly states that covered services rendered by NLH providers to Anthem commercial plan members on or after 2025-10-01 will be treated as in-network (i.e., “at in-network benefits/rates/cost-sharing” or “as if in-network”), for at least some portion of the out-of-network period beginning 2025-10-01.
- NO otherwise (including cases where there is a new agreement but no explicit retroactive in-network language).

What counts as an official public statement:
- A press release, website update, or dedicated page posted on either organization’s official website (e.g., NLH’s Anthem page or News/Press pages; Anthem’s Maine site news/press sections), or a joint statement posted to either site. NLH’s Anthem page is https://northernlighthealth.org/anthem and has been used for official notices.
- If not posted on an official site, a YES can also be supported by corroborating reports in at least two credible news outlets that directly quote or clearly paraphrase the parties’ explicit retroactive in-network commitment. Examples of credible local outlets include Bangor Daily News, Portland Press Herald, and NEWS CENTER Maine. If used, at least one of the reports must quote or link to an official statement.

Term definitions applied in resolution:
- “In-network,” “network provider,” and “out-of-network” are interpreted per the federal Uniform Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms (CMS/CCIIO), which defines a network provider as one contracted with the plan, and an out-of-network provider as one without such a contract; network is the contracted set of facilities/providers (https://www.cms.gov/cciio/resources/forms-reports-and-other-resources/downloads/ug-glossary-508-mm.pdf).
- “Anthem commercial plans” excludes Medicare Advantage for the purposes of this question, following NLH’s own categorization.
- “Services rendered on or after October 1, 2025” refers to services with dates of service at or after 2025-10-01 00:00:00 Eastern Time (ET), which corresponds to 2025-10-01 04:00:00 UTC.

Inclusions and exclusions:
- Inclusion: Any explicit statement that claims for services since 2025-10-01 will be paid/reprocessed at in-network benefits, even if limited to particular service categories (e.g., physicians/ancillary) or dates within the Oct 1–Dec 31 window.
- Exclusions: Statements limited to waiving or reducing some patient cost-sharing without equating to “in-network” benefits; statements about continuity-of-care exceptions mandated by law without a general retroactive in-network policy; Medicare Advantage or Traditional Medicare arrangements (these are out of scope).

Adjudication notes:
- If statements are ambiguous, prefer explicit language such as “treated as in-network,” “paid at in-network benefits,” or “reprocessed at in-network rates.”
- If conflicting reports exist, prioritize official postings by the parties; otherwise require at least two credible outlets and, where possible, a quoted official statement.
- The question resolves NO if the only applicable statements emerge after the deadline or lack explicit retroactive in-network language.

Primary resolution sources to check at deadline:
- NLH Anthem Insurance Notice page: https://northernlighthealth.org/anthem.
- NLH Newsroom (e.g., mediation and contract updates): https://northernlighthealth.org/News.
- Credible press coverage such as Bangor Daily News, Portland Press Herald, NEWS CENTER Maine for corroboration if needed.

question: Colombia: Will the 2025 Financing Law set IVA (VAT) on hybrid vehicles at 19% or higher by December 31, 2025?
background: Context and status quo as of 2025-10-01: • On 2025-09-01, Colombia’s Executive Branch submitted a “Ley de Financiamiento” (Financing Law) bill to Congress. Among its principal proposals is: “Aumento del IVA del 5% al 19% para vehículos híbridos” (raising IVA from 5% to 19% for hybrid vehicles). Major tax advisories summarizing the bill likewise report that hybrid cars would move to the general 19% VAT rate (i.e., the preferential 5% rate would be removed). • Therefore, as of today, the applicable reduced IVA rate for hybrid vehicles is 5%, and the pending bill proposes increasing it to the general 19% rate. Key definitions for forecasters: • IVA/VAT: A value-added tax (VAT) is a consumption tax levied on the value added at each stage of production/distribution; consumers ultimately bear the tax, though businesses remit it to the government. • Hybrid electric vehicle (HEV): A vehicle that combines an internal combustion engine (ICE) with one or more electric motors in a combined propulsion system. • Plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV): A type of HEV with a rechargeable battery pack that can be charged by plugging into an external power source. • Diario Oficial (Colombia): The Government of Colombia’s official journal that publishes laws, decrees, acts, and official notices; enacted laws are published here. The Diario Oficial site operated by the Imprenta Nacional describes its role as publishing official norms and documents to guarantee legal certainty. Why this forecast is interesting: The proposal to end the 5% reduced IVA rate on hybrids and apply the 19% general rate is politically salient and may be amended during congressional debate. Clause-level outcomes are uncertain even when headline revenue targets are stable, creating forecasting entropy around this specific measure. What will be looked up at resolution time: • The final enacted text of the Ley de Financiamiento (2025) as published in the Diario Oficial to determine the IVA rate (or classification under the general IVA rate) applicable to “vehículos híbridos” (including “vehículos híbridos eléctricos” and “vehículos híbridos enchufables”). • If the enacted law explicitly sets 19% (or higher) for hybrids, or clearly removes hybrids from any reduced 5% list without assigning another reduced rate (thereby subjecting them to the 19% general rate as described in professional summaries of the bill’s intent) that will be used in resolution. Notes and scope: • This question concerns the national IVA rate applicable to hybrid vehicles in the enacted Financing Law text. It does not consider other taxes (e.g., excise/consumption taxes, import duties) or subnational taxes. • For the purpose of this question, “vehículo híbrido” includes HEVs and PHEVs as defined above , but resolution will follow the categorization and terminology actually used in the enacted law text in the Diario Oficial.
resolution_criteria: Yes resolution: • Time window: The question may resolve any time between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC based on official publications available by that time. If the relevant law is published before 2025-10-15, the question will resolve on or after 2025-10-15 using that already-published text. • Source of truth: The text of the enacted 2025 Ley de Financiamiento as published in Colombia’s Diario Oficial (official journal). • Criterion: Resolve Yes if, by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, the enacted Financing Law’s text, as published in the Diario Oficial, does any of the following with respect to hybrid vehicles (vehículos híbridos), including hybrid electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids: 1) Explicitly sets the IVA (VAT) rate for hybrid vehicles at 19% or higher; OR 2) Explicitly removes hybrid vehicles from any 5% reduced-rate listing and assigns them to the “tarifa general del IVA” of 19% (e.g., states that hybrids are subject to the general rate of 19%), or otherwise makes clear in the text that hybrids are taxed at the general 19% IVA rate. No resolution: • Resolve No if, by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC: a) The enacted law maintains a rate below 19% for any category of hybrid vehicles (e.g., 5%, 10%), OR b) No Ley de Financiamiento addressing IVA on hybrid vehicles is enacted and published in the Diario Oficial by the deadline, OR c) The enacted law is silent on hybrid vehicles and does not otherwise make them subject to a 19% IVA rate in its text. Additional guidance to avoid ambiguity: • Terminology matching: The law may reference “vehículos híbridos,” “vehículos híbridos eléctricos (HEV),” and/or “vehículos híbridos enchufables (PHEV).” Any of these terms are in scope, and the criterion applies to all such hybrid vehicle categories in the enacted law’s IVA provisions. • Out of scope: This question ignores other taxes or incentives (e.g., excise/consumption taxes, import tariffs) and focuses solely on the IVA rate set in the enacted Financing Law. • How to verify: Locate the Diario Oficial publication of the 2025 Ley de Financiamiento. Check the articles amending IVA rate provisions to see whether hybrid vehicles are listed among 5% items or are expressly assigned a 19% (or higher) rate, or are made subject to the 19% general rate. The Diario Oficial is the official repository for enacted laws. Background references on the bill’s submitted proposal to increase hybrids from 5% to 19%:.

question: Will Colombia’s Procuraduría General or Fiscalía General publicly announce opening an investigation related to President Petro’s call for volunteers to fight in Gaza between Oct 15 and Dec 31, 2025?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-09-30:
- On 2025-09-26/27 in New York during UNGA events, Colombia’s President Gustavo Petro said he would open “la lista de voluntarios” to go fight for the liberation of Palestine/Gaza. Reported quotes include: “hablaré en Colombia para abrir la lista de voluntarios colombianos y colombianas que quieran ir a luchar por la liberación de Palestina,” and his willingness to personally go to that combat. In a Times Square demonstration, he further said he would open registrations for volunteers “con experiencia militar” to support the Palestinian cause as soon as he returned to Colombia. The Swissinfo report also notes Colombia broke relations with Israel in 2024, contextualizing the political environment.
- Institutional roles relevant to potential oversight:
  • Procuraduría General de la Nación (PGN, Colombia): the head of the Public Ministry for disciplinary oversight of public officials and entities; investigates and can sanction irregularities by public servants and those exercising public functions, per the 1991 Constitution and disciplinary law (overview: https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Procuradur%C3%ADa_General_de_la_Naci%C3%B3n_(Colombia)).
  • Fiscalía General de la Nación (FGN, Colombia): independent prosecutorial body within the judicial branch; investigates and prosecutes alleged crimes, directs judicial police, applies precautionary measures, etc. (overview: https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiscal%C3%ADa_General_de_la_Naci%C3%B3n_(Colombia)).
- Time zone reference for resolution timing: Colombia Time (COT) = UTC−05:00 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_in_Colombia).
- Geography reference: “Gaza”/“Gaza Strip” refers to the Palestinian territory in the Southern Levant (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip).
- Likely resolution sources: official institutional websites/press sections, e.g., Fiscalía’s “Noticias” section (https://www.fiscalia.gov.co/colombia/category/noticias/).
Why this question has forecasting value: Petro’s public call and intent to open a volunteer registry could plausibly trigger disciplinary or criminal scrutiny, but whether PGN/FGN formally open and publicly announce an investigation is uncertain and depends on legal interpretations, internal criteria, and political dynamics.
resolution_criteria:
Question: Will either Colombia’s Procuraduría General de la Nación (PGN) or Fiscalía General de la Nación (FGN) publish, on their official website, an announcement that they have opened an investigation related to President Gustavo Petro’s late-September 2025 call to register volunteers to fight in Gaza, between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 and 2025-12-31 23:59:59, Colombia Time (COT, UTC−05:00) ?

Definitions (with links for clarity):
- Procuraduría General de la Nación (Colombia): the national disciplinary oversight body (https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Procuradur%C3%ADa_General_de_la_Naci%C3%B3n_(Colombia)).
- Fiscalía General de la Nación (Colombia): the national prosecutorial authority (https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiscal%C3%ADa_General_de_la_Naci%C3%B3n_(Colombia)).
- Gaza/Gaza Strip: the Palestinian territory commonly referenced as Gaza (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip).
- Time zone: Colombia Time (COT) = UTC−05:00 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_in_Colombia).
- “The presidential call to register volunteers to fight in Gaza”: public statements by President Gustavo Petro during the 2025 UNGA period in New York, including phrases such as “abrir la lista de voluntarios… que quieran ir a luchar por la liberación de Palestina” and references to opening registrations for volunteers with military experience to support the Palestinian cause. For this question, “related to the presidential call” requires that the announcement explicitly references this call or clearly identifies it as the subject matter (e.g., mentions of “lista/registro de voluntarios,” “llamamiento/convocatoria,” “combatir en Gaza/Palestina,” in connection with President Gustavo Petro’s statements at UNGA late September 2025).
- “Publish on their official website”: content hosted on procuraduria.gov.co (for PGN) or fiscalia.gov.co (for FGN). For the Fiscalía, examples of official announcements include items in its “Noticias” section (https://www.fiscalia.gov.co/colombia/category/noticias/). Social media posts alone do not count unless the same text is mirrored on the official website.
- “Opened an investigation”: the announcement must state that the institution has initiated a proceeding about the call, using language such as:
  • For PGN (disciplinary): “apertura de investigación disciplinaria,” “apertura de indagación preliminar,” or equivalent, indicating initiation of disciplinary proceedings or a preliminary disciplinary inquiry.
  • For FGN (criminal): “apertura de investigación,” “apertura de indagación preliminar,” “apertura de noticia criminal,” or equivalent, indicating initiation of a criminal investigation or preliminary inquiry.
  Mere monitoring, information requests, petitions, general statements of concern, or third-party complaints without a stated opening of an investigation do NOT count.

Eligible time window for qualifying announcements: 2025-10-15 00:00:00 through 2025-12-31 23:59:59 (COT, UTC−05:00). Announcements before 2025-10-15 do not count; announcements after 2025-12-31 23:59:59 COT do not count.

Resolution sources and procedure:
- Primary sources are official website announcements on procuraduria.gov.co or fiscalia.gov.co. The resolver will search:
  1) procuraduria.gov.co for press/news pages referencing the event; and
  2) fiscalia.gov.co, including the “Noticias” section (https://www.fiscalia.gov.co/colombia/category/noticias/).
- YES resolves if at least one qualifying announcement is found within the eligible window, by either PGN or FGN, that explicitly states the opening of an investigation as defined above and explicitly links it to President Petro’s late-September 2025 call to register volunteers to fight in Gaza.
- NO resolves if no such qualifying announcement is found within the eligible window.

Edge cases and clarifications:
- If the announcement is later removed, an archived copy (e.g., Internet Archive) of the official page published within the eligible window is acceptable.
- Announcements by other bodies (e.g., Defensoría del Pueblo, Personerías, courts, ministries) do not count unless the PGN or FGN themselves publish the qualifying announcement on their official sites.
- Media reports quoting unnamed sources or leaks do not count without an official-website announcement.
- If both PGN and FGN make qualifying announcements within the window, the outcome remains YES (only one needed).

Rationale for clarity: The terms and sources are precisely defined; the event must be publicly and officially announced by the competent national bodies; the time window is fixed in COT per UTC−05:00; and the subject matter is tied specifically to the President’s late-September 2025 call to open a volunteer registry for combat in Gaza.

question: Will the U.S. Sahm Rule recession indicator (FRED series SAHMREALTIME) trigger by December 31, 2025?
background:
Overview and status quo context as of 2025-09-22 (UTC):
- What this asks: Whether the Real-time Sahm Rule Recession Indicator reaches its trigger threshold (≥ 0.50 percentage points) for any reference month in late 2025, using the official FRED series “SAHMREALTIME” as the resolution source. This is a real-time proxy for the onset of recession that updates monthly, allowing resolution before year-end.
- Why not use NBER directly: The National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) Business Cycle Dating Committee is the authoritative arbiter of U.S. recessions, but its announcements typically occur with a lag and may not be available by year‑end. See NBER overview and FAQ for definitions and process: https://www.nber.org/research/business-cycle-dating; https://www.nber.org/research/business-cycle-dating/business-cycle-dating-procedure-frequently-asked-questions.
- What is the Sahm Rule: It signals that the economy is in the early months of a recession when the three‑month moving average of the national unemployment rate (U‑3, seasonally adjusted) rises by 0.50 percentage point or more above its low over the previous 12 months. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahm_rule and the FRED series description: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/SAHMREALTIME.
- Data source and cadence: The Sahm indicator is computed from the U.S. unemployment rate (U‑3, seasonally adjusted) as reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) via the Current Population Survey (CPS) and summarized in the monthly Employment Situation release. See: BLS Employment Situation News Release hub https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.htm and CPS overview https://www.bls.gov/cps/.
- Practical implication for timing: BLS typically releases the prior month’s unemployment data on the first Friday of each month. Therefore, by 2025‑12‑31, the Sahm indicator values for reference months through November 2025 should be publicly available on FRED. The December 2025 value would be published in January 2026 and is excluded from this question to ensure timely resolution.

Key definitions (with links):
- NBER recession: A significant decline in economic activity spread across the economy, lasting more than a few months, dated monthly by the NBER’s Business Cycle Dating Committee (see NBER links above).
- Sahm Rule trigger: Three‑month moving average of U‑3 minus its 12‑month low ≥ 0.50 percentage point (see Wikipedia and FRED links above).
- Unemployment rate (U‑3): Seasonally adjusted national unemployment rate from BLS CPS (see BLS links above).
- SAHMREALTIME: The FRED series “Real‑time Sahm Rule Recession Indicator” used for resolution (see FRED link above).
- UTC: All timestamps are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
resolution_criteria:
Start and end of observation window:
- Start: 2025-09-22 00:00:00 UTC
- End: 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC

What counts as a “trigger” for this question:
- The Real-time Sahm Rule Recession Indicator (FRED series SAHMREALTIME) has a monthly reference period. For this market, eligible reference months are September 2025, October 2025, and November 2025. The question resolves YES if the value of SAHMREALTIME is greater than or equal to 0.50 percentage points (i.e., ≥ 0.50) for any one of these eligible reference months, as displayed on the FRED SAHMREALTIME page (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/SAHMREALTIME) at or before 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. Otherwise it resolves NO.

Primary resolution source:
- The value(s) as displayed on the FRED series page for SAHMREALTIME: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/SAHMREALTIME.

If the primary source is unavailable or displays an error at the resolution time:
- Fallback computation uses the BLS seasonally adjusted unemployment rate series (UNRATE) from FRED (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/UNRATE) or directly from BLS, and applies the standard Sahm Rule formula as follows:
  1) For each eligible reference month m ∈ {September 2025, October 2025, November 2025}, compute the three‑month moving average MA(m) of UNRATE for months m and the two immediately preceding months.
  2) For each eligible month m, identify L(m), the minimum (lowest) monthly UNRATE over the 12 months ending with month m (inclusive).
  3) Compute S(m) = MA(m) − L(m). If S(m) ≥ 0.50 percentage point for any eligible month, resolve YES; else NO.

Additional rules to avoid ambiguity:
- Use the values as published (seasonally adjusted) and as displayed by FRED at or before the cutoff timestamp; any revisions posted after the cutoff do not affect resolution.
- Units and rounding: Evaluate SAHMREALTIME (or S(m) if using the fallback) to two decimal places as displayed. Values of 0.50 or higher count; 0.49 or lower do not.
- Time zone: All timing/availability checks use UTC.
- Scope limitation: Only the three eligible reference months (Sep–Nov 2025) are considered to ensure the market resolves by 2025‑12‑31. Values for December 2025 (released January 2026) are explicitly excluded.

Examples:
- If SAHMREALTIME shows 0.53 for October 2025 on FRED by 2025‑12‑31 23:59:59 UTC, resolve YES.
- If SAHMREALTIME shows 0.49 for all eligible months by the cutoff, resolve NO.

question: Between Oct 1 and Dec 31, 2025 (UTC), will an official closing announcement state that TikTok has completed a transaction transferring operational control of its U.S. application to a majority U.S.-owned joint venture, with Oracle as security provider, consistent with the White House’s Sep 25, 2025 framework?
background:
Status quo as of Oct 1, 2025:
- TikTok is a short-form video social media service owned by ByteDance, operating a U.S. service distinct from Douyin.
- On Sep 25, 2025, the White House published a fact sheet outlining a framework for a U.S.-based joint venture (JV) to operate TikTok’s U.S. application. Key elements include: the JV will be majority-owned by U.S. investors; Oracle will act as TikTok’s security provider and independently monitor and assure the safety of U.S. operations; the JV will control the operation of the algorithm, code, and content moderation decisions for the U.S. application; U.S. user data will be stored in a secure cloud environment in the U.S. run by Oracle; ByteDance will hold less than 20% of the stock, have only one of seven board seats, and be excluded from the security committee; and the Attorney General is directed not to enforce the Act for 120 days to allow the divestiture to be completed.
- Separately, on Sep 16, 2025, a presidential action further extended the enforcement delay for the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act until Dec 16, 2025.
- Oracle Corporation is a U.S.-based public technology company headquartered in Austin, Texas.
- Definitions used in this question: a joint venture (JV) is a business entity formed by two or more parties with shared ownership, returns/risks, and governance, typically a separate legal entity in many jurisdictions ; “U.S. person” means any U.S. citizen, permanent resident alien, entity organized under U.S. law (including foreign branches), or any person in the United States.

Why this question: Whether the parties can finalize closing and transfer operational control by year-end 2025 remains uncertain due to deal mechanics, governance, regulatory approvals, and financing considerations. The enforcement delay through Dec 16, 2025 sets a timeline pressure point, but closing could occur either before or after that date. The White House framework provides concrete elements that can be used to unambiguously verify the nature of any closing.
resolution_criteria:
Eligible period and time zone:
- Eligible events must occur between 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Definitions and thresholds:
- Joint venture (JV): As used here, a JV is a business entity formed by two or more parties characterized by shared ownership, returns/risks, and governance, typically as a separate legal entity. The JV must be organized under the laws of the United States (i.e., incorporated/formed in a U.S. jurisdiction), as indicated in the White House framework.
- Majority U.S.-owned: More than 50% of the outstanding voting equity interests of the JV are owned, directly or indirectly, by “U.S. persons,” where “U.S. person” has the meaning in 31 CFR 560.314 (any U.S. citizen, permanent resident alien, entity organized under U.S. law including foreign branches, or any person in the United States). Ownership may be confirmed across one or more acceptable sources.
- TikTok’s “U.S. application/operations”: The TikTok service offered in the United States (distinct from Douyin), including operational control over the algorithm, code, and content moderation decisions applied to the U.S. service, as described in the White House framework.
- “Official closing announcement”: A public communication by an involved entity (ByteDance, TikTok, Oracle, the JV entity, or named JV investors) or a U.S. government announcement (White House or U.S. Department of Justice) stating that the transaction “has closed,” “has completed,” “closing has occurred,” or “is effective” as of a specific date. Examples of acceptable forms include company press releases and SEC filings (e.g., Form 8-K), or official White House/DOJ releases. The announcement must be accessible on an official corporate or government website or an official investor relations/SEC filing repository.

What must be verified for a YES resolution:
Resolve YES if, by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, there is an official closing announcement (as defined above) and, based on the announcement and any accompanying official documentation, all of the following can be verified:
1) The transaction has closed (or equivalent language) and transfers operational control of TikTok’s U.S. application to a JV organized under U.S. law.
2) The JV is majority U.S.-owned under the definition above (i.e., >50% voting equity interests held by U.S. persons/entities). Evidence may consist of ownership breakdown statements within press releases, SEC filings, or official government releases; it is acceptable to aggregate information across these official sources.
3) Oracle is named as TikTok’s security provider for the U.S. application under the arrangement (e.g., providing secure U.S. cloud storage and/or overseeing security operations), consistent with the White House framework.
4) The JV is described as operating TikTok’s U.S. application, including at least one explicit proxy for operational control: control over the algorithm, code, or content moderation decisions for the U.S. service.

If any of conditions (1)–(4) cannot be verified from official sources by the deadline, resolve NO.

Acceptable sources for resolution:
- Official company press releases by ByteDance, TikTok, Oracle, the JV entity, or named JV investors.
- SEC filings (e.g., Form 8-K) by Oracle or any publicly listed JV participant or entity involved in the transaction.
- Official White House or U.S. Department of Justice publications.

Tiebreakers and clarifications:
- Time stamps are judged in UTC based on the publication time visible on the official source. If the publication time is ambiguous, use the earliest verifiable UTC time of the posting as shown on the source page or in the SEC’s EDGAR system.
- If official sources use synonymous language (“completed,” “effective,” “closing occurred”), these count as “has closed.”
- If the JV’s majority U.S.-ownership is implied via an explicit statement that ByteDance holds less than 20% and the remaining equity is held by named U.S. investors, this is sufficient to verify >50% U.S. ownership, provided the named investors qualify as U.S. persons/entities.
- Reports solely from non-official media sources (e.g., newspapers) are not sufficient to resolve; they may be used for context but not for verification.

Non-eligible events:
- Announcements lacking an explicit closing/completion/effective statement.
- Announcements of preliminary agreements, term sheets, MOUs, or regulatory approvals without closing.
- Announcements referring to arrangements materially inconsistent with the Sep 25, 2025 White House framework (e.g., lacking Oracle as security provider or lacking JV operational control over algorithm/code/moderation decisions).

question: Will the U.S. Treasury designate any economy a “currency manipulator” in its Q4 2025 semiannual FX report?
background:
Summary of what’s being forecast
- Event: Whether the U.S. Department of the Treasury will explicitly designate (determine) at least one economy as a “currency manipulator” under Section 3004 of the Omnibus Trade and Competitiveness Act of 1988 in its second (Q4) 2025 semiannual Report to Congress on Macroeconomic and Foreign Exchange Policies of Major Trading Partners of the United States (the “FX Report”), or in the accompanying Treasury press release, published between Oct 15 and Dec 31, 2025 (UTC).

Status quo (as of 2025-09-30)
- Treasury’s most recent FX Report and press release were published on June 5, 2025. Treasury concluded that “no major U.S. trading partner manipulated the rate of exchange between its currency and the U.S. dollar” during the four quarters through December 2024, and that no major trading partner met all three criteria for enhanced analysis under the 2015 law in that period. The June 2025 report covers the four quarters through December 2024.
- Treasury maintains a Monitoring List of economies whose currency practices and macroeconomic policies merit close attention. As of the June 2025 report, the Monitoring List comprised China, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Singapore, Vietnam, Germany, Ireland, and Switzerland.
- The FX Report is statutorily semiannual and reviews major U.S. trading partners; Treasury posts the reports and press releases on home.treasury.gov. The landing page for these reports is here: https://home.treasury.gov/policy-issues/international/macroeconomic-and-foreign-exchange-policies-of-major-trading-partners-of-the-united-states. In June 2025, Treasury noted that the report covered partners “comprising about 78 percent of U.S. foreign trade in goods and services”.

Definitions and framework a forecaster will need
- What counts as a “currency manipulator” designation? Under Section 3004 of the 1988 Act (22 U.S.C. § 5305), Treasury assesses “whether countries manipulate the rate of exchange between their currency and the United States dollar for purposes of preventing effective balance of payments adjustments or gaining unfair competitive advantage in international trade.” A designation for this question requires an explicit determination in Treasury’s own language that an economy manipulated its currency under this standard (e.g., “Treasury determines under the 1988 Act that [Economy] manipulated…” or “designates [Economy] a currency manipulator”). Treasury commonly uses phrasing such as “no major U.S. trading partner manipulated …” and “Treasury has not designated [Economy] as a currency manipulator” when discussing the outcome.
- Context on TFTEA (2015) criteria: Separately from the 1988 Act determination, Treasury evaluates three quantitative criteria under Section 701 of the Trade Facilitation and Trade Enforcement Act of 2015 (19 U.S.C. § 4421): (1) at least a $15B goods and services surplus with the U.S.; (2) a current account surplus of at least 3% of GDP; and (3) persistent, one-sided FX intervention: net purchases of foreign currency in at least 8 of 12 months totaling at least 2% of GDP over 12 months. Meeting two of three places an economy on the Monitoring List; meeting all three triggers enhanced analysis. These are not, by themselves, a “manipulator” designation under the 1988 Act.
- Plain-language definition: In U.S. policy usage, “currency manipulation” refers to government policies that interfere with market forces to intentionally push down the currency’s value to boost exports and gain an unfair trade advantage.

Why this is decision-relevant now
- Designations under the 1988 Act are rare, but Treasury explicitly left open in June 2025 that it could designate if evidence warranted. Forecasters must weigh macro developments (e.g., current account balances, FX interventions, bilateral balances), policy signals, and the likelihood of Treasury’s thresholds/interpretation changing or being applied differently in the Q4 2025 report.

Primary sources to monitor
- Treasury’s FX Report landing page (where the Q4 2025 report will be posted): https://home.treasury.gov/policy-issues/international/macroeconomic-and-foreign-exchange-policies-of-major-trading-partners-of-the-united-states.
- Example structure of a press release (June 5, 2025): https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0157.
resolution_criteria:
Question:
- Resolve “Yes” if, between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, the U.S. Department of the Treasury (a) publishes its second semiannual 2025 FX Report (the “Q4 2025 FX Report”) OR an official accompanying Treasury press release, and (b) that document explicitly states that at least one economy is determined/designated to have “manipulated” its currency under Section 3004 of the 1988 Act; otherwise resolve “No”.

Key definitions for resolution:
- “Q4 2025 FX Report” means the semiannual “Report to Congress on Macroeconomic and Foreign Exchange Policies of Major Trading Partners of the United States” that Treasury releases in the October–December 2025 window, regardless of whether its PDF title page says November or December (Treasury’s own landing page hosts these semiannual reports).
- “Explicitly states” means the Treasury-authored report or its official press release includes unambiguous language that an economy “manipulated” its currency under the 1988 Act (22 U.S.C. § 5305), e.g., phrases such as “Treasury determines under the 1988 Act that [Economy] manipulated …” or “Treasury designates [Economy] a currency manipulator.” Phrases explicitly stating the opposite (e.g., “no major U.S. trading partner manipulated …”) do not count as a designation.
- “Economy” (country) refers to any jurisdiction named by Treasury in the report/press release (e.g., sovereign states or distinct economies like Taiwan).

What does NOT count:
- Placement on (or removal from) the Monitoring List, meeting (or failing to meet) one or more TFTEA 2015 criteria, or initiation of “enhanced analysis/engagement,” absent an explicit 1988 Act manipulation determination, does not count as a “currency manipulator” designation for purposes of this question.

Primary resolution sources:
- The PDF of the Q4 2025 FX Report and the corresponding Treasury press release, as posted on home.treasury.gov (FX Report landing page: https://home.treasury.gov/policy-issues/international/macroeconomic-and-foreign-exchange-policies-of-major-trading-partners-of-the-united-states; example press release structure from June 5, 2025: https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0157).

Edge cases and tie-breakers:
- If multiple Treasury documents in the window provide conflicting statements, the latest-dated Treasury-authored document within the window governs.
- If Treasury issues a standalone press release within the window explicitly designating an economy as a manipulator under the 1988 Act, that counts even if the PDF report posts later (outside the window).
- If no relevant Treasury document meeting the above criteria is published within the window, resolve “No.”
- If home.treasury.gov is unavailable at resolution time, use an archived snapshot (e.g., Internet Archive) of the Treasury page(s) or, failing that, two or more credible newswires/newspapers (e.g., AP, Reuters, Bloomberg, WSJ) that directly quote the Treasury determination; the quoted language must meet the “explicitly states” standard above.

question: As of 23:59 China Standard Time on December 31, 2025, will China’s Ministry of Ecology and Environment have officially extended into 2026 the compliance deadline for 2024 emissions for any of the newly included steel, cement, or aluminum smelting sectors under the national ETS?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-09-30: China’s national Emissions Trading System (ETS) was officially expanded in March 2025 to include the steel, cement, and aluminum smelting industries, in addition to the power sector. The Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) released a Work Plan on March 26, 2025 that set the first compliance deadline for these newly included sectors at the end of 2025, covering 2024 emissions. The expansion brought approximately 1,500 additional companies into scope. For the first compliance year, free allocation for these sectors is equal to their verified 2024 emissions, and entities must surrender sufficient China Emission Allowances (CEAs) to meet their compliance obligations by the deadline. The MEE is the lead authority for the national ETS and routinely issues official notices regulating allowance surrender deadlines and compliance procedures; prior cycles for the power sector saw high compliance rates and were concluded by the end of 2023, with formal MEE notices governing surrender and verification processes.

Key definitions and context for forecasters:
- China’s national ETS: China’s national cap-and-trade style carbon market administered by the MEE (overview pages and news from ICAP and official MEE documents provide context). General background: https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/china-national-ets (context link; factual claims in this background are sourced to the cited documents).
- Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE): The national environmental regulator responsible for the ETS, including allocation, surrender, data verification, and market oversight. Official site: https://www.mee.gov.cn/
- China Emission Allowance (CEA): The tradable unit used to satisfy compliance obligations under the national ETS; CEAs are allocated annually per an MEE Quantification and Distribution Plan and must be surrendered by Key Covered Entities by the compliance deadline.
- Key Covered Entity: An enterprise designated by the MEE (via provincial lists) as subject to compliance obligations under the national ETS within specified sectors.
- Newly included sectors: The steel, cement, and aluminum smelting sectors as defined in MEE’s March 26, 2025 Work Plan expanding the ETS.
- Compliance deadline at issue: The date by which Key Covered Entities in the newly included sectors must surrender CEAs corresponding to their 2024 emissions—set at December 31, 2025 in the Work Plan.
- Official extension: Any formal MEE issuance (e.g., notice, circular, press release, policy document, or amendment) published on the MEE domain (mee.gov.cn) that moves the 2024 emissions compliance deadline for any of the newly included sectors into any date in 2026 (or later). MEE commonly uses official notices to set or adjust allowance surrender deadlines.
- Time zone: China Standard Time (CST), UTC+8.

Why this is forecastable and non-trivial: China has historically adjusted timelines in its ETS as implementation progresses, and the 2025 expansion is administratively complex, covering ~1,500 firms across energy-intensive industries. Whether the MEE will keep the original December 31, 2025 surrender deadline for 2024 emissions or officially extend any sector into 2026 remains uncertain. Forecasters should consider progress on verification, market readiness, and precedent for deadline adjustments described in MEE reporting.
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves based on the regulatory status at 23:59 China Standard Time (UTC+8) on December 31, 2025.

Resolution:
- Resolve YES if, on or before 23:59 CST on December 31, 2025, the Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) has published an official issuance on mee.gov.cn (e.g., notice, circular, press release, policy document, Q&A, or amendment) that extends the compliance deadline for surrendering CEAs for 2024 emissions for any of the newly included sectors (steel, cement, or aluminum smelting) into any date in 2026 or later. Examples of qualifying issuances include: a Notice on Allowance Surrender adjusting deadlines, an amendment to the March 26, 2025 Work Plan, or an MEE press release/FAQ that explicitly postpones the 2024 compliance deadline for any of these sectors into 2026.
- Resolve NO if, as of 23:59 CST on December 31, 2025, no such official MEE issuance exists and the latest applicable MEE communications still indicate that the compliance deadline for 2024 emissions in these sectors is December 31, 2025 as originally set in the Work Plan. In other words, the absence of an official extension into 2026 for any of the three sectors is sufficient for a NO outcome.

Scope clarifications:
- “Any of the newly included sectors” includes steel, cement, and aluminum smelting as covered by the MEE Work Plan released March 26, 2025. If the MEE extends the 2024 compliance deadline into 2026 for even one of these sectors (even if limited to certain provinces or a subset of enterprises within that sector), the outcome is YES.
- The evaluation considers MEE issuances published at any time prior to the resolution time; issuances before October 15, 2025 also qualify.
- Primary resolution source: the MEE official website (mee.gov.cn), including sections for policies/notices and press releases. If the MEE website is inaccessible at resolution, credible reporting by state media (e.g., Xinhua) or international wire services (e.g., Reuters) that cite and link to the relevant MEE issuance may be used as secondary confirmation. However, in the event of conflict, documents on mee.gov.cn take precedence.

Evidence to check:
1) The MEE Work Plan sets the original deadline at end-2025 for surrendering CEAs covering 2024 emissions in the newly included sectors.
2) MEE’s standard practice is to issue official notices governing allowance surrender and deadlines, which serve as the canonical source for any deadline changes.

All times are CST (UTC+8).

question: Will BEVs and PHEVs account for at least 30.0% of EU‑27 new passenger car registrations during Jan–Nov 2025?
background:
What is being forecast: Whether the combined market share of battery electric vehicles (BEVs) and plug‑in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs) in the European Union (EU‑27) will be at least 30.0% of new passenger car registrations over the period 2025‑01‑01 00:00:00 UTC through 2025‑11‑30 23:59:59 UTC.

Key definitions and scope:
- Battery electric vehicle (BEV): A type of electric vehicle propelled exclusively by one or more electric motors using energy stored in on‑board rechargeable batteries; no internal combustion engine. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battery_electric_vehicle
- Plug‑in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV): A hybrid electric vehicle with a rechargeable battery that can be charged by plugging into an external electricity source and that also has an internal combustion engine. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plug-in_hybrid
- EU‑27: The 27 member states of the European Union as listed here: https://european-union.europa.eu/principles-countries-history/eu-countries_en (the United Kingdom is not included).
- New passenger car registrations: First‑time registrations of M1 passenger cars as reported in ACEA statistics for the EU‑27 (see ACEA fuel‑type figure page: https://www.acea.auto/figure/fuel-types-of-new-passenger-cars-in-eu/).

Where forecasters track the data:
- ACEA monthly press releases for EU‑27 new passenger car registrations and fuel‑type market shares: https://www.acea.auto/press-release-calendar/
- ACEA “Fuel types of new passenger cars in the EU” figure page (monthly and YTD market shares): https://www.acea.auto/figure/fuel-types-of-new-passenger-cars-in-eu/
- EAFO EU‑27 Vehicles and Fleet dashboards (monthly BEV/PHEV registrations by powertrain): https://alternative-fuels-observatory.ec.europa.eu/transport-mode/road/european-union-eu27/vehicles-and-fleet

Context notes for forecasters (non‑exhaustive): OEM compliance strategies, consumer demand, charging infrastructure build‑out, and national incentive policies can all affect BEV/PHEV uptake. The European Commission’s light‑duty CO2 performance standards step‑up applies from 2025: https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/road-transport/light-duty-vehicles_en
resolution_criteria:
Resolution timeline and outcome: The question resolves on or before 2025‑12‑31 23:59:59 UTC.
- YES if the combined share of BEVs and PHEVs in EU‑27 new passenger car registrations during 2025‑01‑01 00:00:00 UTC through 2025‑11‑30 23:59:59 UTC is at least 30.0%.
- NO otherwise.

Primary resolution source and procedure:
1) Use ACEA’s November 2025 EU‑27 press release on new passenger car registrations (typically reporting Jan–Nov year‑to‑date fuel‑type market shares) from the ACEA statistics press release page: https://www.acea.auto/press-release-calendar/
   - If ACEA explicitly provides Jan–Nov 2025 YTD market shares for BEV and PHEV, compute Combined EV share = BEV share + PHEV share (in percentage points).
   - If ACEA explicitly reports a combined BEV+PHEV share, that value is used directly.

Fallbacks if the primary is unavailable by the resolution time:
2) ACEA “Fuel types of new passenger cars in the EU” figure: https://www.acea.auto/figure/fuel-types-of-new-passenger-cars-in-eu/ If it shows Jan–Nov 2025 YTD EU‑27 BEV and PHEV shares, sum them.
3) EAFO computation: https://alternative-fuels-observatory.ec.europa.eu/transport-mode/road/european-union-eu27/vehicles-and-fleet Sum monthly EU‑27 BEV and PHEV new registrations for Jan–Nov 2025 and divide by total EU‑27 new passenger car registrations over the same months. If EAFO does not provide the monthly total denominator, use ACEA’s monthly total EU‑27 registrations for the same months if available on the ACEA press release calendar.

Computation and rounding rules:
- Market share = 100% × (BEV registrations + PHEV registrations) / (Total new passenger car registrations) over the period Jan–Nov 2025 (EU‑27).
- Compare the resulting percentage to a threshold of 30.0%. If only rounded shares are available from the source, treat values reported as 30.0% or higher as meeting the threshold; values reported below 30.0% do not meet it. If unrounded values are available, 29.999% is considered below 30.0%.

Scope and exclusions:
- Geography: EU‑27 only; the United Kingdom is excluded.
- Vehicle scope: New M1 passenger cars only; BEVs and PHEVs count toward the numerator; non‑plug hybrids (HEVs) and fuel‑cell vehicles (FCEVs) do not.

Conflict resolution and publication cutoff:
- If figures conflict across sources, precedence is: ACEA November 2025 press release > ACEA Fuel‑types figure page > EAFO computation. As a last resort, if still irresolvable, use consensus from at least two major international newswires explicitly citing ACEA’s Jan–Nov 2025 BEV and PHEV EU‑27 shares.
- Data used must be publicly available by 2025‑12‑31 23:59:59 UTC.

question: Will the European Commission publicly announce at least one targeted support measure for EU wine exporters that explicitly references the 2025 U.S. tariffs between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01:
- A 15% U.S. import tariff on European Union (EU) wine and spirits took effect on August 1, 2025, under a U.S.–EU framework deal; EU officials indicated the rate would apply until a further agreement is reached, with talks expected to continue in the autumn.
- Italian wine exports to the U.S. showed early signs of strain in 2025: Jan–Jul value fell by 1.1% while volumes rose 6.1%; July 2025 export value was down 21.1% year-over-year, with average prices per liter declining, and trade press noted concern ahead of the August tariff impact.
- Italian agri-food exports to the U.S. overall lost approximately €600 million in value in the first seven months of 2025 compared to the prior year.
- As an example of prior support action (outside this question’s measurement window), the European Commission approved a €5 billion French state aid scheme in May 2025 to facilitate exports of wines and spirits to the U.S. ahead of tariffs, under EU state aid rules (valid May 8–July 8, 2025). This illustrates the type of targeted support that can exist but does not, by itself, resolve this question because it was announced before the start date specified below.

Definitions and scope:
- European Commission (EC): The executive branch of the European Union responsible for proposing legislation, implementing decisions, and managing the day-to-day business of the EU. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Commission.
- Tariff: A tax imposed by a government on imported or exported goods. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tariff.
- Wine: An alcoholic beverage made from fermented grapes; for EU sectoral context see: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wine and EU wine policy overview: https://agriculture.ec.europa.eu/farming/crop-productions-and-plant-based-products/wine_en.
- Wine exporter: For the purposes of this question, a business or entity that exports wine produced in the EU to foreign markets (here specifically the United States). See general concept of exporter: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Export.
- Publicly announced: Published on official EC channels (e.g., the EC Press Corner, Directorate-General websites, or the Official Journal of the European Union). EC Press Corner: https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/home/en. Official Journal: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/oj/direct-access.html.
- Targeted support measure (qualifying types include but are not limited to):
  - State aid measures approved by the EC that specifically facilitate or support EU wine exporters’ activity vis-à-vis the U.S. market in response to 2025 U.S. tariffs (e.g., export credit/reinsurance schemes, grants, guarantees, or cost-offsets), where the EC publication explicitly references the U.S. tariffs relating to wine or spirits.
  - EC-funded promotion or market access program (e.g., DG AGRI promotion calls, DG TRADE initiatives) explicitly aimed at EU wine exporters with the stated rationale of addressing the 2025 U.S. tariffs on wine/spirits.
  - Regulatory accommodations or administrative measures (e.g., temporary flexibilities or guidance) explicitly citing the 2025 U.S. tariffs as rationale and targeted to EU wine exporters.
- Explicit reference requirement: To qualify, the EC publication must clearly mention the United States and tariffs (e.g., “U.S. tariffs”, “15% duty”, “2025 U.S. tariffs on wine/spirits”) and indicate that the measure is targeted to wine exporters (wine and/or spirits; spirits may be included if the measure collectively targets the wine/spirits sector). Generic sectoral support that does not reference the U.S. tariffs does not qualify.

Why this is forecastable and non-trivial:
- There is active uncertainty regarding whether the EC will issue additional measures by year-end as negotiations with the U.S. continue and EU wine export performance evolves. Prior actions show precedent but occurred before the start date. Analysts can monitor Commission communications, trade press, and policy developments; reasonable forecasters may disagree on the likelihood of new EC actions in the specified window.

Additional context to aid forecasters:
- The U.S. tariff environment in 2025 has been dynamic and politically salient, with direct commercial exposure for EU wine producers, especially in Italy.
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves to Yes or No based on EC publications between the start and end dates below.

Measurement window:
- Start: 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC
- End: 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC

Resolution test (Yes):
- Yes if, during the measurement window, the European Commission publishes at least one qualifying targeted support measure for EU wine exporters that explicitly references the 2025 U.S. tariffs. Qualifying publications include:
  - EC Press Corner press releases, statements, or Q&As; EC Directorate-General pages (e.g., DG AGRI, DG TRADE) hosting official announcements or pages describing the measure; or entries in the Official Journal of the European Union.
  - The publication text must explicitly mention the United States and tariffs (e.g., “U.S. tariffs”, “15% duty”, “2025 U.S. tariffs on wine/spirits”) and indicate that the measure targets wine exporters (wine and/or spirits). Measures that target the broader agri-food sector only qualify if they explicitly include wine/spirits and the tariff reference as defined above.
  - Examples of qualifying measures (non-exhaustive): state aid approvals by the EC for schemes aiding wine/spirits exports to the U.S. (analogous in form to the French scheme approved in May 2025 , but announced within the measurement window); EC-funded promotional programs or calls explicitly addressing the U.S. tariff shock for EU wine/spirits; regulatory accommodations explicitly citing 2025 U.S. wine/spirits tariffs.

Resolution test (No):
- No if no such EC publication meeting all criteria appears during the measurement window.

Exclusions and clarifications:
- Exclude member state actions or industry initiatives unless they are approved/announced by the EC and published on EC channels as defined above.
- Exclude measures announced before 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC (e.g., the EC approval of the €5bn French scheme in May 2025 ) or after 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.
- Exclude generic EC sector-wide measures or statements that do not explicitly reference the 2025 U.S. tariffs on wine/spirits.
- Negotiation updates or political statements without an announced, concrete measure do not qualify.

Primary resolution sources:
- EC Press Corner: https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/home/en.
- Official Journal of the European Union (EUR-Lex): https://eur-lex.europa.eu/oj/direct-access.html.
- Relevant EC Directorate-General pages (DG AGRI: https://agriculture.ec.europa.eu; DG TRADE: https://policy.trade.ec.europa.eu).

Fallback (if needed to verify existence/absence):
- Credible wire-service or newspaper reporting that directly cites and links to the EC publication (e.g., Reuters, AP, Bloomberg, Financial Times). Example context on tariffs: Reuters coverage of the 15% U.S. tariffs effective August 1, 2025.

How to adjudicate in practice:
1) During January 1–December 31, 2025, but only counting announcements timestamped within the measurement window, search EC Press Corner and DG AGRI/DG TRADE sites for combinations of “wine” AND “United States” AND “tariff” or “duty” and review the text.
2) Verify the publication date/time in UTC (if only local time is provided, convert to UTC using Brussels local time as needed).
3) Confirm the text includes an explicit reference to the U.S. tariffs as defined and that the measure targets wine exporters (wine and/or spirits).
4) If at least one qualifying publication exists in the window, resolve Yes; otherwise, resolve No.

Rationale for the test and baseline context:
- The existence of the 15% U.S. tariff regime and its expected persistence pending further talks establishes a clear external shock.
- Documented 2025 export strains in the Italian wine sector provide relevant context on potential need for support.
- Prior EC action (the French scheme) demonstrates the type of EC-approved targeted support that can exist, helping adjudicators identify qualifying measures by analogy, while the start date ensures the outcome is not already known.

question: Will the EU add at least 10 unique new listings to its Iran nuclear/ballistic-related sanctions annexes between 00:00 UTC on Oct 15, 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on Dec 31, 2025?
background:
Context as of Oct 1, 2025:
- On Aug 28, 2025, France, Germany and the UK (the E3) notified the UN Security Council that Iran was in significant non-performance of its JCPOA commitments, initiating the snapback process. The EU subsequently reimposed nuclear-related restrictive measures on Sept 29, 2025. The Council press release lists and links the legal acts adopted that day, including Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1975, Council Implementing Regulations (EU) 2025/1980 and 2025/1982, Council Decision (CFSP) 2025/1972, Council Decision (CFSP) 2025/1978, and Council Implementing Decision (CFSP) 2025/1971.
- The EU’s Iran nuclear framework operates primarily via Council Decision 2010/413/CFSP (travel bans and listings in its Annex I) and Council Regulation (EU) No 267/2012 (asset freezes and listings in its Annex VIII for UN-designated and Annex IX for EU-designated persons/entities). Regulation 267/2012 specifies criteria including involvement in proliferation-sensitive nuclear activities or development of nuclear weapon delivery systems, and establishes that the Council adds listings via amendments to Annex VIII/IX.
- As part of the Sept 29, 2025 snapback package, the EU adopted implementing measures that added entries under headings including “A. Persons and entities involved in nuclear or ballistic missile activities,” “B. Entities owned, controlled, or acting on behalf of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps,” and “C. Entities owned, controlled, or acting on behalf of the Islamic Republic of Iran Shipping Lines (IRISL)” in Annex I to Decision 2010/413/CFSP and in Annex VIII to Regulation 267/2012. The implementing acts indicate these headings and that they amend the relevant annexes; they also state entry into force upon publication in the Official Journal. Based on the annexes, 43 natural persons and 78 entities (60 under heading A, 15 under heading B, 3 under heading C) were added—121 items total—on Sept 29, 2025.
- Other EU sanctions regimes also applicable to Iran exist (e.g., for human rights abuses, and for Iran’s military support to Russia and regional destabilization). These are distinct legal frameworks with their own legal bases and annexes (e.g., 2011/235/CFSP and Reg 359/2011 for human rights; 2014/145/CFSP and Reg 269/2014 for Russia/Ukraine), and are not part of the Iran nuclear/ballistic framework in Decision 2010/413/CFSP and Regulation 267/2012 [2d8a7].
- For resolution purposes, the Official Journal (OJ) entries on EUR-Lex are the authoritative publications. Implementing acts commonly specify that they enter into force on the date of OJ publication, and the publication date is displayed on EUR-Lex.

Implications for forecasters:
- After a large Sept 29 package, the EU could add further listings by year-end (e.g., follow-on implementation rounds, corrections, or additions). However, only additional names added to Annex I of Decision 2010/413/CFSP or Annex VIII/IX of Regulation 267/2012 published in the OJ within the specified window would count for this question.
resolution_criteria:
Outcome: Resolve Yes if 10 or more unique natural or legal persons are newly listed in the EU’s Iran nuclear/ballistic framework via Official Journal (OJ) acts published between 00:00 UTC on Oct 15, 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on Dec 31, 2025; otherwise resolve No.

Definitions and scope:
- Eligible legal bases (the “Iran nuclear/ballistic framework”):
  - Council Decision 2010/413/CFSP concerning restrictive measures against Iran—listings appear in Annex I (travel bans).
  - Council Regulation (EU) No 267/2012 concerning restrictive measures against Iran—listings appear in Annex VIII (UN-designated) and Annex IX (EU-designated) (asset freezes).
- Listing (or “newly listed”): The addition of a person or entity’s name to Annex I of Decision 2010/413/CFSP and/or to Annex VIII or Annex IX of Regulation 267/2012 by an EU legal act published in the OJ within the time window. Corrections to spellings/identifiers, updates to reasons, renewals without adding a new name, or delistings do not count. If a person/entity was not present in the relevant annex immediately prior to an OJ publication and is added by that act, that counts as a new listing (even if the person/entity had been listed historically at an earlier date).
- Unique counting: Count each person/entity at most once across all eligible annexes/acts in the period. If the same person/entity is added to both the Decision and the Regulation (common in parallel implementing acts), count as one. Deduplicate using the OJ entry’s name together with identifying details (e.g., date of birth, identifiers) when clearly referring to the same subject.
- Time window and timezone: Only OJ acts with publication dates between 00:00 UTC on Oct 15, 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on Dec 31, 2025 are eligible. The publication date is the date shown on the OJ entry on EUR-Lex; for acts that state entry into force on the date of publication, this date will appear on EUR-Lex (e.g., “This Regulation shall enter into force on the date of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union”).
- Exclusions: Listings under other EU regimes concerning Iran (e.g., human rights under Decision 2011/235/CFSP/Reg 359/2011; Russia/Ukraine or regional destabilization frameworks) do not count. Only listings to the annexes of Decision 2010/413/CFSP and Regulation 267/2012 are eligible [2d8a7, 55edd4].

Resolution procedure:
1) Identify all Council Implementing Decisions (CFSP) that amend Annex I of Decision 2010/413/CFSP and all Council Implementing Regulations that amend Annex VIII or Annex IX of Regulation 267/2012 with OJ publication dates within the time window. The Sept 29, 2025 acts are before the window and are provided here only as background.
2) For each eligible act, read the annex and extract all names added by that act to the relevant annex(es). Ignore corrections/updates that do not add names or that remove names.
3) Deduplicate across acts using names and identifying details to produce a set of unique persons/entities newly listed during the window.
4) If the total unique count is ≥ 10, resolve Yes; otherwise No.

Primary sources of truth:
- EUR-Lex Official Journal entries for acts amending Decision 2010/413/CFSP Annex I and Regulation 267/2012 Annex VIII/IX published in the period. For legal architecture and examples of implementing language and publication/entry-into-force, see Council Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1982 and Council Implementing Decision (CFSP) 2025/1971.

Notes:
- The Sept 29, 2025 reimposition package demonstrates the headings used and the scale of recent listings (121 items), but those do not count for this question because they predate the start of the time window.

question: Ecuador: Will the referendum question eliminating mandatory state budget financing for political organizations be nationally approved on November 16, 2025?
background: Status quo as of 2025-10-01: Ecuador will hold a combined nationwide vote on Sunday, 2025-11-16, consisting of two partial constitutional referendum questions and one national consulta popular (popular consultation). The National Electoral Council (Consejo Nacional Electoral, CNE) officially initiated the electoral process on 2025-09-25 following a favorable ruling by the Constitutional Court, and unified the referendum and consulta for the same date. Multiple reputable outlets list the three ballot questions and confirm the date. The two referendum questions include: (1) a proposal to eliminate the constitutional prohibition on foreign military bases; and (2) a proposal to eliminate the State’s obligation to allocate resources from the General State Budget to political organizations. The consulta popular asks whether to convene and install a Constituent Assembly subject to an attached statute and later referendum approval. The referendum question relevant to this forecast is: “¿Está usted de acuerdo con que se elimine la obligación del Estado de asignar recursos del Presupuesto General del Estado a las organizaciones políticas, reformando parcialmente la Constitución de conformidad con el anexo de la pregunta?”. Approval of a referendum proposal in Ecuador requires a simple majority of valid votes (more than half of valid votes cast), with final results proclaimed by the CNE and published thereafter.
