Primicias further reports the CNE’s formal convocation and logistics for the unified vote on 2025-11-16 , and provides context that these questions have been validated for the ballot. El Universo and other outlets reproduce the same wording of the questions and the unified election date. For general concept definitions: - Referendum: a direct vote by the electorate on a specific proposal (see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Referendum). - Consulta popular: a popular consultation instrument in Ecuador used for policy questions that may not modify the Constitution; the 2025 consulta concerns convening a Constituent Assembly. - CNE (Consejo Nacional Electoral): Ecuador’s electoral authority that conducts elections and proclaims official results (see https://www.cne.gob.ec/). - Valid votes: votes counted toward the proposal outcome, excluding null/spoiled and blank ballots; “votos válidos” are referenced by Ecuadorian practice, with approval requiring a simple majority of valid votes. For clarity, null/spoiled votes (see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spoilt_vote) and blank votes (see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blank_vote) do not count toward “valid vote” totals when determining approval in Ecuador’s referendum practice. Additional context: the CNE has planned oversight and logistics for the unified vote; media report a combined budget and observer presence for these processes. Forecasters should track campaigning dynamics, legal challenges, turnout expectations, and historical vote patterns for similar governance-related referendum questions in Ecuador. Key official source for resolution: the CNE’s national tally and proclamation for the 2025 Referéndum y Consulta Popular, which is expected to be accessible via the CNE’s official website and formal proclamations.
resolution_criteria: This question concerns the referendum proposal specifically about eliminating the obligation of the State to allocate resources from the General State Budget to political organizations, as worded on the official 2025 ballot: “¿Está usted de acuerdo con que se elimine la obligación del Estado de asignar recursos del Presupuesto General del Estado a las organizaciones políticas, reformando parcialmente la Constitución de conformidad con el anexo de la pregunta?”. Definitions: - Approving option: the ballot option that indicates agreement with the above proposal (i.e., “Sí/Yes”) versus the opposing option (“No”). - Nationally approved: the approving option receives more valid votes than the opposing option in the nationwide aggregation reported by the CNE (i.e., a simple majority of valid votes nationally). - Valid votes: votes counted toward the proposal outcome, excluding null/spoiled and blank ballots (“votos válidos”). - National results: the CNE’s official aggregation of votes across all eligible Ecuadorian voters, including domestic and abroad where applicable, as presented in the CNE’s official results and proclamation. Timeframe and timezone: - Eligible events for resolution occur between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. - The referendum is scheduled on 2025-11-16, but the resolution uses the national tally as of 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. How to resolve: - Resolve “Yes” if, by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, the CNE’s official national results (or official proclamation) show that the approving option (agreement with the proposal) has more valid votes than the opposing option; otherwise resolve “No”. - Primary source: CNE’s official national results and proclamation for the Referéndum y Consulta Popular 2025. If the CNE website is temporarily inaccessible, use credible reporting that directly cites the CNE’s proclaimed national results (e.g., Primicias, El Universo) as a fallback, provided it clearly states the official national outcome. Notes: - This question only evaluates the referendum proposal on financing political organizations. The other referendum proposal (foreign military bases) and the consulta popular (Constituent Assembly) are out of scope. - If results are under legal dispute but the CNE has not proclaimed a final national outcome by the deadline, use the latest official CNE national tally posted as of 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

question: Between 2025-10-15 and 2025-12-31 (UTC), will BOTAŞ announce it has signed an additional long‑term (≥10 years) U.S.-origin LNG supply agreement with a counterparty other than Mercuria?
background: Context as of 2025-09-30: Türkiye’s state-owned natural gas company BOTAŞ (BOTAŞ Petroleum Pipeline Corporation) is responsible for the country’s natural gas transmission and trading operations. Liquefied natural gas (LNG) is natural gas cooled to a liquid state for transport and storage, typically loaded at LNG export terminals onto specialized tankers. On 2025-09-24, BOTAŞ signed a 20‑year agreement with Mercuria to purchase U.S.-sourced LNG, equivalent to about 4 bcm per year starting in 2026; the deal totals roughly 70 bcm over its term and was announced in New York during President Erdoğan’s visit. Türkiye’s Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources also described the agreement’s purpose as enhancing supply security and diversifying sources. Separately, around the same time BOTAŞ and Woodside announced a nine‑year preliminary LNG agreement starting in 2030, primarily linked to Woodside’s Louisiana (U.S.) LNG project; reporting indicates this was a preliminary agreement rather than a finalized long‑term SPA and its term is under 10 years. Trade press likewise summarized BOTAŞ having two agreements, the Mercuria 20‑year U.S.-sourced LNG deal starting in 2026 and a nine‑year Woodside arrangement starting in 2030. Definitions for this market: long‑term LNG sales are typically documented via binding Sales and Purchase Agreements (SPAs), historically running 15–25+ years and remaining the standard instrument for international LNG trade. By contrast, Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) or Heads of Agreement are generally non‑binding expressions of intent in business contexts. For “U.S.-origin LNG,” a practical, verifiable proxy is LNG loaded at U.S. LNG export terminals, per EIA’s characterization of LNG export operations. Given BOTAŞ’s recent U.S.-focused LNG activity and diversification push, the likelihood of an additional U.S.-origin long‑term agreement before year‑end 2025 is uncertain but plausible.
resolution_criteria:
Question: Resolve whether, between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, BOTAŞ publicly announces that it has signed a new, additional binding long‑term (≥10 years) LNG supply contract for U.S.-origin LNG with a counterparty other than Mercuria.

Definitions and requirements:
- BOTAŞ: Türkiye’s state-owned natural gas company, BOTAŞ Petroleum Pipeline Corporation.
- LNG: Liquefied natural gas; natural gas cooled to a liquid for transport.
- U.S.-origin LNG: LNG that is explicitly stated to be sourced from, or loaded at, U.S. LNG export terminals (i.e., cargoes loaded in the United States).
- Long‑term: A fixed contractual term length of at least 10 years (inclusive) from the contract’s effective start date; consistent with long‑term LNG SPA practice.
- Binding LNG supply contract: A signed Sales and Purchase Agreement (SPA) or equivalent binding LNG supply contract creating enforceable obligations to deliver/receive LNG over the stated term; non‑binding instruments (e.g., MoU/HoA/LoI) do not qualify.
- Additional and distinct counterparty: The announced contract must be separate from, and not an amendment to, the 2025 Mercuria agreement , and the counterparty must be an entity other than Mercuria (Mercuria Energy Group Ltd.).
- Publicly announces: BOTAŞ, Türkiye’s Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources, or a major reputable newswire/outlet (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg) publishes an announcement/report stating that a qualifying contract has been signed, with the publication timestamp within the resolution window.

Resolution:
- Yes: If, within the UTC window above, there is a public announcement meeting all of the following: (1) identifies BOTAŞ as a party; (2) states that a binding LNG supply contract has been signed; (3) specifies a contractual term of ≥10 years; (4) specifies that LNG is U.S.-origin (as defined); and (5) identifies a counterparty other than Mercuria. Acceptable sources include an official BOTAŞ or Ministry press release, or credible reporting by major outlets such as Reuters or Bloomberg with explicit details.
- No: If no such qualifying announcement is published within the window.

Clarifications:
- The volume or start year of deliveries are not required for resolution, provided the term length and U.S.-origin are explicitly stated.
- If an earlier preliminary announcement (e.g., MoU/HoA) is later finalized into a signed binding contract within the window and meets all criteria (including ≥10 years), it counts.
- The 2025 Mercuria agreement itself does not count, nor do amendments/extensions to it.
- Announcements outside the window are not eligible, even if the contract is signed earlier/later.

Primary resolution sources to check on/after 2025-12-31 (UTC):
- Official Ministry news page (for press releases) [ab6b48 as example of official announcements].
- Major wire services (e.g., Reuters) which previously reported the Mercuria deal with sufficient detail.

question: Will Spain’s 2026 General State Budget (PGE) be promulgated and published in the BOE by December 31, 2025?
background:
Overview and status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- Constitutional framework: Article 134 of Spain’s 1978 Constitution establishes that the Government must present the General State Budget (Presupuestos Generales del Estado, PGE) to the Congress of Deputies at least three months before the expiration of the previous year’s budget (i.e., by September 30 for the following fiscal year). If the Budget Law is not approved before the first day of the fiscal year, the previous year’s budget is automatically extended until new ones are approved.
- What the PGE are: The Presupuestos Generales del Estado are Spain’s annual public budget, enacted as a law after parliamentary approval, royal sanction, and publication in the Boletín Oficial del Estado (BOE). They include all state public sector revenues and expenditures and are published in the BOE with the rank of ordinary law.
- BOE role: The Boletín Oficial del Estado (BOE) is Spain’s official gazette. Publication in the BOE is the authoritative and authentic text of laws and binding acts; it guarantees the publicity of norms under the Constitution. For this question, BOE publication is the single source of truth for whether the 2026 Budget Law is in force and the date of its publication.
- Current political/legislative status: As of late September 2025, Spain missed the constitutional deadline to present the 2026 Budget Bill to Congress for the third consecutive year. Reporting noted that the Council of Ministers had not approved the non-financial spending limit (techo de gasto) nor the fiscal/stability path (senda de déficit/estabilidad), key steps preceding budget submission. Coalition arithmetic is fragile, with Junts signaling they would withhold support absent concessions. The government continues operating under the extended 2023 accounts (prórroga) due to lack of new approved budgets.
- Official budget information portal: Spain’s Ministry of Finance (Hacienda) maintains a comprehensive PGE portal with documentation, links to BOE publications, and historical materials. While informative, the BOE publication is the primary resolution source for this question.

Why this question is forecastable and non-trivial:
- Two-sided risk: Despite renewed efforts, calendar compression, coalition dynamics, and prior rejection of key fiscal path votes create genuine uncertainty about completing all parliamentary stages and promulgation before year-end.
- Clear resolution event: BOE publication of the 2026 Budget Law is binary and uniquely identifiable.
resolution_criteria:
Question:
Will the Spanish “Ley de Presupuestos Generales del Estado para 2026” be promulgated and published in the Boletín Oficial del Estado (BOE) between 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC?

Definitions (all terms clearly specified):
- Presupuestos Generales del Estado (PGE): Spain’s annual public budget enacted as a law, covering all state public sector revenues and expenditures. After approval by the Cortes Generales, it is sanctioned by the King and published in the BOE. For 2026, the relevant law will explicitly be titled “Ley de Presupuestos Generales del Estado para 2026” (or equivalent wording clearly indicating it is the Budget Law for fiscal year 2026). Source: https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presupuestos_Generales_del_Estado.
- Boletín Oficial del Estado (BOE): Spain’s official gazette; publication here constitutes the official and authentic text of laws. Source: https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolet%C3%ADn_Oficial_del_Estado (and BOE’s own legal description).
- Promulgated and published: For the purposes of this question, “promulgated and published” is satisfied only when the Budget Law text appears as a law in the BOE (with law number/year and full text), which is the authoritative publication event. Parliamentary votes or royal sanction without BOE publication do not count as “published”.
- Date used for resolution: The date of publication is the calendar date displayed by the BOE on the law’s publication page/issue. The comparison to “on or before December 31, 2025” will be made against that BOE date. The eligibility window for this question is the publication occurring between 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC; practically, we rely on BOE’s displayed publication date for Yes/No determination.

Resolution:
- Resolve YES if a law explicitly constituting the “Ley de Presupuestos Generales del Estado para 2026” is published in the BOE with a BOE publication date of December 31, 2025 or earlier.
- Resolve NO otherwise (including cases where Parliament has approved the law but BOE publication occurs after December 31, 2025, or where only drafts, press releases, ministerial orders, or other non-law documents exist).

Primary resolution source:
- BOE official site (daily issues and law publication pages). The resolver will verify publication by locating the Budget Law’s BOE entry and reading the displayed publication date. Start from: https://www.boe.es (navigate to Diario BOE and search for “Presupuestos Generales del Estado 2026”). BOE publication is official and authentic under Spanish law.

Secondary confirmation (if needed):
- Spain’s Ministry of Finance PGE portal may link or reference the BOE entry for the law: https://www.hacienda.gob.es/es-ES/Areas%20Tematicas/Presupuestos%20Generales%20del%20Estado/Paginas/Presupuestos.aspx.

Context notes for forecasters:
- Constitutional deadlines and the automatic extension (prórroga) mechanism are defined in Article 134 of the Spanish Constitution.
- Recent reporting (late Sep 2025) indicates the constitutional deadline to present the bill was missed, key preliminary steps (techo de gasto, senda de estabilidad) were not approved, and the legislature is operating on extended 2023 accounts amid fragile coalition dynamics.

Start and end dates:
- Eligible publication window: From 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC through 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.
- Timezone: Dates stated in UTC for the eligibility window; the BOE publication date shown on the law’s page/issue will be used as the authoritative calendar date for Yes/No determination.

Ambiguity handling and edge cases:
- Drafts or preliminary budget documents (e.g., projectos, press materials, ministerial orders) do not count; only the enacted Budget Law published in BOE counts.
- If multiple BOE entries reference the 2026 PGE (e.g., corrections/errata), the first publication of the law itself determines the resolution date.
- If the law’s title or wording varies slightly but unambiguously identifies the General State Budget for 2026 (e.g., “Ley X/2025, de [fecha], de Presupuestos Generales del Estado para el año 2026”), it counts as the 2026 Budget Law.

question: Will ONDC total transactions in November 2025 be at least 20.0 million?
background:
Definition and scope: The Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) is a public technology initiative by India’s Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), designed as a set of specifications enabling open interchange among shoppers, platforms, and retailers. ONDC publishes network metrics derived from participant API logs; order/transaction metrics are computed using counts of On_confirm API calls and other processed metrics per ONDC’s Network Observability specification. For forecasting purposes, “total transactions” refers to ONDC’s monthly total count across domains as displayed on ONDC’s official Open Data dashboards (Mobility, Logistics, Retail) or an official ONDC-published aggregate, and is conceptually the sum of confirmed orders/rides across these domains as per ONDC’s processed metrics definitions.

Status quo as of 2025-10-01: According to Moneycontrol’s read of ONDC’s open data, ONDC recorded 17.94 million total transactions in August 2025, up 2.7% from July, with a breakdown of Mobility 11.81M, Logistics 2.35M, and Retail 3.76M. Broader trends in 2025 include strong growth in Mobility and softer Retail: Economic Times reported ONDC Mobility transactions at 8.1 million in February 2025 (vs. 5.5 million in October 2024), while Retail orders fell to 4.6 million in February 2025 from a peak of 6.5 million in October 2024; Logistics were ~2 million in February 2025. ONDC’s Q1 FY25 quarterly update reported 26.2 million network transactions for the quarter, with 11.3 million mobility rides facilitated and monthly category counts in several domains reaching the “One Million Club”.

Why 20.0 million and November: August 2025’s total (17.94M) suggests a plausible path to ≥20.0M under seasonal uplift and continued mobility strength, while ongoing retail softness adds downside risk, making 20.0M a non-trivial, high-entropy threshold. November is chosen to ensure the question can be resolved before December 31, 2025, while still capturing late-year dynamics.

Useful links: ONDC Open Data dashboards (official resolution source): https://opendata.ondc.org/; ONDC website: https://ondc.org/. Time zone reference: India Standard Time (IST, UTC+5:30) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Standard_Time (for defining calendar-month boundaries).
resolution_criteria:
Event window and time zone: “November 2025” means the calendar month from 2025-11-01 00:00:00 IST to 2025-11-30 23:59:59 IST (IST = UTC+5:30).

Definitions:
- Total transactions: The aggregate count for November 2025 across ONDC domains as published by ONDC. This is either (a) a single ONDC-published monthly aggregate labeled as total transactions/orders/rides for November 2025 (e.g., “Number of Transactions”), or (b) the sum of ONDC’s November 2025 monthly counts shown on its official Open Data dashboards for Mobility, Logistics, and Retail. ONDC’s processed metric for orders/transactions is derived from counts of On_confirm API calls from Network Participants , and ONDC reports domain-level monthly order/rides counts (e.g., mobility rides, retail orders, logistics orders) in official updates.
- Sources qualifying as “official ONDC communication”: ONDC’s Open Data dashboards (https://opendata.ondc.org/), official publications/updates posted on ondc.org, or official ONDC documents/press releases.

Resolution procedure (by 2025-12-31 23:59 UTC):
1) Primary: Check ONDC’s official Open Data dashboards and/or an official ONDC publication (e.g., a monthly or quarterly update) for the November 2025 monthly total. If ONDC publishes a single “Number of Transactions” for November 2025, use that figure. If only domain dashboards show November monthly totals, sum November 2025 counts for Mobility, Logistics, and Retail to obtain the total.
2) Secondary (fallback if Primary is unavailable by the resolution deadline): Use credible reporting that explicitly cites ONDC’s open data or official communication and provides November 2025 totals or a domain breakdown sufficient to compute the total. Examples of acceptable outlets include Moneycontrol and the Economic Times, both of which regularly report ONDC monthly counts and breakdowns based on ONDC open data.
3) Numeric interpretation: The threshold is 20,000,000 exactly. Use the integer figures as published. If only million-level rounding is available from credible reporting, treat “≥20.0 million” as met if the reported figure is at least 20.0 million when expressed with one decimal place. If conflicting figures exist, prefer the most authoritative ONDC source (Open Data or official ONDC publication) over media reporting.

Outcome:
- Resolves Yes if the official ONDC sources (or, failing that, credible reporting citing ONDC data) show total ONDC transactions in November 2025 ≥ 20,000,000 by 2025-12-31 23:59 UTC.
- Resolves No otherwise.

Auditability: All counts should be verifiable on ONDC’s Open Data site (https://opendata.ondc.org/) or via official ONDC publications; media fallbacks must explicitly attribute figures to ONDC open data or official communication.

question: Will the European Commission publish at least one DMA Article 29 non-compliance decision against any gatekeeper other than Apple or Meta between 00:00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01:
- The EU’s Digital Markets Act (DMA) is Regulation (EU) 2022/1925. Under Article 29, the European Commission may adopt a “non-compliance decision” when it finds a gatekeeper failed to comply with obligations in Articles 5–7 or certain related measures; such decisions order the gatekeeper to cease and desist the non-compliance within an appropriate deadline and to explain how it will comply.
- Designated gatekeepers under the DMA currently include Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, ByteDance, Meta, Microsoft, and Booking (for Booking.com). Booking was designated on May 13, 2024. A “gatekeeper” is defined and designated by the Commission under Article 3 of the DMA based on criteria including significant impact on the internal market, providing important gateway core platform services, and entrenched/foreseeable durable position; presumptions and thresholds are set in Article 3(2).
- On April 23, 2025, the Commission adopted and announced non-compliance decisions under the DMA against Apple and Meta, imposing fines of €500 million and €200 million, respectively. The official materials describe them as “Non-compliance decision on Apple’s steering terms” and “Non-compliance decision on Meta’s ‘consent or pay’ model”.
- The Commission opened non-compliance investigations on March 25, 2024 into Alphabet (Google Play steering; Google Search self-preferencing), Apple (App Store steering; browser choice screen), and Meta (“pay or consent” model). The Commission stated it intends to conclude such proceedings within 12 months. On March 19, 2025, the Commission sent preliminary findings to Alphabet regarding Google Search self-preferencing and Google Play anti-steering; the document explicitly notes preliminary findings do not prejudge the outcome and are not final decisions.
- As of the Commission’s “Latest news on the DMA” page consulted above, the only non-compliance decisions publicly noted are those against Apple and Meta; no additional gatekeepers have final non-compliance decisions recorded through mid/late 2025.
Definitions and scope for this question:
- Digital Markets Act (DMA): Regulation (EU) 2022/1925 establishing rules for designated “gatekeepers” providing core platform services in the EU. Authoritative text at EUR-Lex (link provided below).
- Gatekeeper: Any undertaking designated by the European Commission under Article 3 DMA. For practical identification and current list, see the Commission’s “Gatekeepers” page and Booking designation page (links provided below).
- Non-compliance decision: An implementing act adopted by the Commission under Article 29 DMA that sets out a finding of non-compliance and orders the gatekeeper to cease and desist within an appropriate deadline and provide explanations on compliance. Fines may be imposed under Articles 30–31, but the presence of fines is not required for an event to count; what matters is the adoption/publication of a non-compliance decision itself.
- Preliminary findings, opening/closing of investigations, workshops, commitments, or other procedural steps do not count as “non-compliance decisions” unless the Commission explicitly adopts and publishes a decision pursuant to Article 29.
Useful official links for forecasters:
- EUR-Lex DMA text: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32022R1925 
- Commission “Gatekeepers” page: https://digital-markets-act.ec.europa.eu/gatekeepers_en and Booking designation: https://digital-markets-act.ec.europa.eu/commission-designates-booking-gatekeeper-and-opens-market-investigation-x-2024-05-13_en 
- Commission press release and news on Apple/Meta decisions (example language): https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/ip_25_1085 and https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/commission-finds-apple-and-meta-breach-digital-markets-act 
- Preliminary findings to Alphabet: https://digital-markets-act.ec.europa.eu/commission-sends-preliminary-findings-alphabet-under-digital-markets-act-2025-03-19_en 
- Latest news on the DMA: https://digital-markets-act.ec.europa.eu/latest-news_en
resolution_criteria:
Time window: Eligible events must occur between 00:00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, inclusive.

Condition to resolve “Yes”: The European Commission publishes at least one non-compliance decision under Article 29 of the DMA against any designated gatekeeper other than Apple or Meta during the time window. “Publishes” means an official European Commission communication (press release, official decision page, or news item) on Commission web properties (e.g., PressCorner or the Digital Markets Act site) where the decision is explicitly described as a “non-compliance decision” under the DMA or references Article 29 and identifies the gatekeeper concerned. Examples of acceptable source locations include:
- Commission PressCorner (news/press releases): https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner
- “Latest news on the DMA” page: https://digital-markets-act.ec.europa.eu/latest-news_en 

Condition to resolve “No”: If no such publication is present by 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025.

Clarifications:
- Eligible gatekeepers include any undertaking designated by the Commission under Article 3 DMA at the time of decision adoption (current list includes Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, ByteDance, Meta, Microsoft, and Booking; Apple and Meta are explicitly excluded for the purposes of this question).
- Only non-compliance decisions adopted and publicly posted by the Commission count. The following do NOT count: preliminary findings, opening of investigations, workshop announcements, commitments, de-designations, specification decisions under Article 8(2) unless accompanied by an Article 29 non-compliance decision, or court judgments unrelated to an Article 29 Commission decision.
- If multiple qualifying decisions are published in the window, “Yes” still resolves; only one is required.
- If a decision is adopted on or before the deadline but is not publicly posted on Commission web properties until after the deadline, it does not count; publication time governs resolution for this question. This aligns with using public, verifiable sources that can be checked within minutes.

Verification steps for resolver: Check the Commission’s PressCorner and the “Latest news on the DMA” page for any items dated in the time window that explicitly state “non-compliance decision” against Alphabet, Amazon, ByteDance, Microsoft, Booking, or any other designated gatekeeper except Apple or Meta. Confirm the item references the DMA and, ideally, Article 29 language (cease-and-desist order), consistent with the legal definition.

question: Between September 26, 2025 and December 31, 2025 (UTC), will any state or federal financial-crime charge tied to the misuse of Franz or Theresia Kraus’s Social Security benefits be filed against Lorenz F. Kraus?
background:
Status quo as of September 30, 2025: Lorenz F. Kraus (age 53) was arrested after a televised interview in which he described killing his parents years earlier; investigators had been looking into Social Security-related fraud when they discovered human remains at the family’s Albany, NY home. At arraignment in Albany City Court, Kraus pleaded not guilty to multiple counts of second-degree murder and concealment of a human corpse; no financial-crime counts were included at that time. Reporting indicates the probe was triggered by a Social Security Administration (SSA) wellness check, and that Social Security payments continued to be deposited into the parents’ accounts after their disappearance around 2017; the SSA Office of Inspector General was among the agencies involved. Local authorities described the matter as primarily a financial-crimes investigation early on, with the benefits angle central to the inquiry.

Definitions and clarifications for forecasters:
- Social Security benefits: Benefits administered by the U.S. Social Security Administration (SSA) under the Social Security Act, typically retirement, disability, or survivor benefits. See SSA overview: https://www.ssa.gov/benefits/ and Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_Security_(United_States).
- Criminal complaint, information, indictment: Formal charging instruments initiating or continuing a criminal case. See Cornell LII/Wex: complaint (https://www.law.cornell.edu/wex/criminal_complaint), indictment (https://www.law.cornell.edu/wex/indictment), information (https://www.law.cornell.edu/wex/information) and Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure Rule 3 (complaint) and Rule 7 (indictment/information): https://www.law.cornell.edu/rules/frcrmp/rule_3 and https://www.law.cornell.edu/rules/frcrmp/rule_7.
- Financial-crime charge tied to the parents’ SSA benefits: Any charge in a state or federal charging instrument that alleges theft, fraud, conversion, identity theft, or other unlawful receipt or misappropriation of SSA benefits payable to Franz K. Kraus or Theresia Kraus (or funds derived therefrom). Examples include charges under 42 U.S.C. § 408 (Social Security fraud), 18 U.S.C. § 641 (theft of government property), 18 U.S.C. § 1028/1028A (identity theft/aggravated identity theft) when used to obtain or continue SSA benefits, or New York Penal Law larceny/welfare-fraud statutes where the charging language explicitly ties the alleged conduct to the parents’ SSA benefits. Charges that involve other financial misconduct not tied to SSA benefits for Franz or Theresia Kraus do not count.
- Name scope: Charges against “Lorenz F. Kraus” or “Lorenz Kraus” are counted; if necessary, match by case context (Albany, NY case involving Franz and Theresia Kraus) and birth year/age as reported.

Why this is non-trivial: As of the most recent reporting, murder and concealment charges are filed but financial-crime charges have not been brought, despite an investigation centered on continued SSA payments and suspected misuse over several years. It is plausible that state or federal prosecutors add financial counts based on ongoing investigations, but it is not certain they will do so before year-end 2025.

Useful sources to monitor for resolution:
- USAO Northern District of New York press releases: https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndny/pr
- SSA Office of Inspector General newsroom: https://oig.ssa.gov/newsroom/
- Albany County District Attorney press office: https://www.albanycountyny.gov/government/albany-county-district-attorney/press-office
- New York State Unified Court System portals (availability varies by court for criminal dockets): https://www.nycourts.gov/
- Credible reporting from outlets such as the Times Union (Albany), AP, Reuters, NYT (e.g., Times Union coverage of the SSA-triggered probe ; NYT overview ).
resolution_criteria:
Time window and timezone: Evaluate filings dated between 2025-09-26 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Resolve Yes if, within this window, at least one qualifying financial-crime count (as defined above) is included in any new state or federal charging instrument against Lorenz F. Kraus. Qualifying charging instruments include: criminal complaint, information, indictment, superseding indictment/information, or a separate case’s charging document. “Filed” means the document bears a court clerk’s filing date or an official docket entry date on or before 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC; if only a local date is available (without time), treat that calendar date as determinative.

Resolve No if no such qualifying charge has been filed within the window.

Evidence hierarchy and acceptable sources:
- Primary: official court docket entries or copies of charging instruments from New York state courts or U.S. federal courts.
- Secondary: official agency press releases (USAO NDNY; SSA OIG; Albany County DA) that clearly state such charges were filed and identify their nexus to the parents’ SSA benefits.
- Tertiary: corroborated reporting from reputable outlets (e.g., Times Union, NYT, AP, Reuters) that quotes or reproduces charging language or official confirmation.

Disambiguations and exclusions:
- Charges that involve financial misconduct but do not explicitly tie to SSA benefits owed to Franz or Theresia Kraus (e.g., unrelated tax offenses) do not count.
- If charges are filed under seal and not publicly acknowledged by an official source before the deadline, they do not count.
- If both state and federal charges are filed, count either; if multiple instruments are filed, any single qualifying count is sufficient for Yes.

Baseline reference for “additional”: At baseline (arraignment), Kraus faced murder and concealment charges and no financial-crime counts; thus any qualifying financial-crime count filed in the window is “additional”. The investigation’s origin and focus on Social Security benefits is documented.
